docs.title: When you need it
docs.text: Before creating resources or choosing a deployment identity.

docs.title: What to edit
docs.text:
Use an existing workspace, catalog and schema you are allowed to use. The deployment identity needs rights to manage the generated jobs. The jobs' Run-as identity needs source reads, output/metadata writes, model registry and MLflow access, plus rights to start downstream jobs. Monitoring has its own store and reference permissions. Configure these in deployment/targets.yml and deployment/variables.yml; a successful local preview does not test them.

Use an authenticated Databricks CLI and a Core release matching the template. Generated jobs install deployment/requirements.txt; see runtime packaging.

docs.title: The command
docs.text:
databricks version
databricks auth describe --profile YOUR_PROFILE

docs.title: What you should see
docs.text: The profile resolves to your intended workspace and identity. Avoid copying access tokens into project configuration.

docs.title: Common errors and fixes
docs.text: A different host or principal means the wrong profile is active. Fix authentication before deployment; do not treat local package installation as proof of cloud permissions.

docs.title: 2. Create the project
docs.text: Detailed reference: Setup modes, generated files and preview.

docs.title: When you need it
docs.text: Once per new project. Quick and detailed setup generate the same project for the same answers.

docs.title: What to edit
docs.text: The answer file below selects single_model, regression and the source used in chapter 3. Quick setup is the default. Without an answer file, the wizard asks essential applicable questions; select detailed for model/candidate/branch, search, compute and deployment choices. Defaults remain editable in generated YAML. Competition compares candidates for one target; multi-target trains separate targets and packages one coherent model set.

docs.title: The command
docs.text:
From the Skyulf checkout, save this as quick-init.json. Omitting setup_mode selects quick setup; the explicit answers avoid prompting:

{
  "project_name": "claim_demo",
  "catalog": "workspace",
  "schema": "skyulf_demo",
  "training_layout": "single_model",
  "task": "regression",
  "source_table_name": "customer_observations",
  "record_key_columns": "customer_id",
  "input_columns": "income, age",
  "target_column": "claim_amount"
}

databricks bundle init skyulf-core/templates/databricks --config-file quick-init.json --output-dir ./generated
cd generated/claim_demo
uv pip install -r deployment/train-requirements.txt

docs.title: What you should see
docs.text: A generated/claim_demo directory containing configuration, jobs, Python extensions and topic guides. No tables, models or endpoints are created by initialization.

docs.title: Common errors and fixes
docs.text: Run later commands from generated/claim_demo. Do not add a second workflow.json or Python model declaration beside the generated YAML owners.

docs.title: 3. Supply data, directly or through feature groups
docs.text: Detailed reference: Feature tables and merge contracts.

docs.title: When you need it
docs.text: Before training or scoring can read real rows.

docs.title: What to edit
docs.text:
For this tutorial keep config/features.yml at groups: {}. There is no feature job and no merged table: training and scoring read customer_observations directly. The catalog/schema must already exist. Create the example table once below, or use a table with the same schema and update the source name in both configurations.

If your inputs must first be assembled, follow the feature-table tutorial: each group reads its own source, calls a Spark transform and writes a feature table; the merge joins those tables onto the base observations. Then explicitly set the merged table as training_table and score_source_table. Feature groups do not change those sources automatically. This optional path is separate from fitted preprocessing and online feature lookup.

docs.title: The command
docs.text:
This example predicts a numeric claim_amount from income and age, keyed by customer_id. Use an existing authorized Delta table with those columns, or create the following demonstration table in a schema you own. Run this SQL once in Databricks; substitute your catalog/schema in both the SQL and the bindings below. CREATE TABLE deliberately fails if the name is already in use.

CREATE TABLE workspace.skyulf_demo.customer_observations
USING DELTA
TBLPROPERTIES ('delta.enableChangeDataFeed' = 'true')
AS SELECT
  id AS customer_id,
  CAST(20000 + id * 350 AS DOUBLE) AS income,
  CAST(20 + id % 45 AS DOUBLE) AS age,
  CAST(50 + id * 7 + id % 3 AS DOUBLE) AS claim_amount
FROM range(120);

Expected: 120 unique BIGINT keys, two DOUBLE inputs and a DOUBLE label. This is an execution example, not a realistic business benchmark. Record keys identify requests; keep them out of input_columns unless they are genuine features. The rules for record keys, labels and source windows are in training data.

docs.title: What you should see
docs.text: The source has 120 distinct nonmissing BIGINT customer_id values. income, age and claim_amount are DOUBLE columns. Record keys identify outputs and stay outside model inputs.

docs.title: Common errors and fixes
docs.text: An existing table name makes CREATE TABLE fail deliberately. Choose a new owned name rather than replacing data. Enable CDF before new scoring changes arrive. A timestamp can be a feature-join key but is not a supported single-model prediction record key; use a stable STRING or BIGINT ID. See prepare the source table.

docs.title: 4. Choose training data, model and policy
docs.text: Detailed reference: Training rows and holdout, model catalog, search strategies and decision thresholds.

docs.title: When you need it
docs.text: Before each new fit when changing data selection, evaluation, estimator or recipe.

docs.title: What to edit
docs.text:
Edit config/training.yml. The generated table bindings and model entry already match the answer file. Merge this fragment into defaults; keep the other generated settings and the models mapping:

defaults:
  input_columns: [income, age]
  target_column: claim_amount
  pre_split_recipe: known_income
  preprocessing_recipe: claim_inputs
  save_preprocessing_diagnostics: true

The defaults use linear regression with a bounded search. Keep them for this run, or remove the model's tuning block to fit fixed parameters. The training field tables explain all accepted settings, types, defaults, inheritance and layout restrictions. Use that page's complete three-layout files when changing layout. For another algorithm, use the model catalog: each card has its parameters, default search space and YAML selection. The search and ensemble guide explains strategy controls, CV, budgets and how to configure voting or stacking members.

docs.title: The command
docs.text: There is no cloud action in this chapter. Complete the next two recipe files before running python src/tools/preview.py --action train in chapter 7.

docs.title: Training data flow
docs.text:
The job pins a Delta source version, selects the configured window and eligible sample, applies fixed training filters, creates the final split, and then fits preprocessing/model parameters inside training folds. Holdout rows stay outside search and fitting. Label availability filtering is independent of observation time and split policy.

Review training_window_mode, optional training_sample_rows, split_strategy and cv separately. Random splitting needs no event dates. Temporal splitting requires the configured time column and boundaries. Null training_table_version resolves latest once at invocation; a concrete version pins that snapshot. A rolling window changes at invocation, while a fixed window keeps its boundaries.

docs.title: Three independent decisions
docs.text:
Setting Location Meaning promotion_policy Training policy, or inference model_set policy manual_approval waits for an operator; automatic applies saved quality gates score_model_selection config/inference.yml Resolve the controlled champion or use a pinned model_version follow_champion config/inference.yml true starts scoring after a successful champion transition; false leaves scoring to its own trigger

Manual approval does not imply manual scoring. A pinned scorer keeps using its pinned version even after champion changes. Rejection and training without a champion transition do not trigger score handoff.

docs.title: Common errors and fixes
docs.text: Quick setup's manual policy leaves quality_threshold unset. This allows candidate registration and pinned scoring, but first-champion approval needs an absolute quality limit chosen before training. To exercise approval in this synthetic example, add quality_threshold: 5.0 under defaults; heldout RMSE must then be at most 5.0. Choose a meaningful business limit for real data. Editing it after the fit does not replace the candidate's saved policy.

docs.title: 5. Set fixed pre-split eligibility
docs.text: Detailed reference: Custom pre-split filters and executed examples.

docs.title: When you need it
docs.text: When fixed cleanup or eligibility rules must run before holdout and CV splitting.

docs.title: What to edit
docs.text:
Replace config/pre_split.yml with the complete file below. The previous chapter already selects known_income. It converts -999 to missing income and excludes those observations. It learns no means, quantiles or category vocabularies.

If another recipe filters missing claim_amount, set skip_target_pre_split_steps: true in config/scoring.yml before preview when you intend scoring to skip that label-dependent filter. Preview checks the decision even for training. This tutorial's income-only filter needs no such switch; actual labels are not required for prediction.

docs.title: The command
docs.text:
For example, normalize a sentinel before testing training eligibility:

version: 1
recipes:
  default: []
  known_income:
    - name: income_sentinel
      transformer: ValueReplacement
      params: {columns: [income], to_replace: -999, value: null}
    - name: known_income
      transformer: DropMissingRows
      params: {subset: [income]}

Place this in config/pre_split.yml and select pre_split_recipe: known_income. Do not repeat the same normalization in preprocessing. With the generated mode: pre_split, scoring normalizes the sentinel, then excludes that row under known_income. The response retains its key with a missing prediction, scoring_status="excluded" and exclusion_reason="pre_split:known_income". The estimator receives only eligible rows. To predict for missing income, change the saved scoring eligibility/mode deliberately and include a fitted imputer, then train/package a new version; adding an imputer alone does not override this eligibility rule. Keep learned statistics after splitting.

docs.title: What you should see
docs.text: All 120 demo rows pass the filter. A future row with income -999 retains its key in scoring output, with no estimate and the explicit exclusion status described above.

docs.title: Common errors and fixes
docs.text: Keep learned imputers/scalers/encoders in preprocessing. Pre-split supports only the eight admitted built-ins and declared fixed filters. Deduplication does not repair duplicate record IDs and does not remember earlier scoring batches. Separate target-reading and feature-only filters if the latter must remain active at scoring time.

docs.title: When you need it
docs.text: When inputs need learned filling, scaling, encoding or other model transformations.

docs.title: What to edit
docs.text:
Replace config/preprocessing.yml with this complete file. claim_inputs is selected by chapter 4. The income filter is already in pre-split; this recipe fills missing age and scales the two numeric inputs.

version: 1
recipes:
  default: []
  claim_inputs:
    - name: age_fill
      transformer: SimpleImputer
      params: {columns: [age], strategy: median}
    - name: numeric_scale
      transformer: StandardScaler
      params: {columns: [income, age]}

The catalog gives each transform's parameters, defaults, minimal YAML, common mistake and saved-state behavior. Its customer classification example additionally covers group imputation and unseen categories.

docs.title: The command
docs.text:
After both recipe files exist, inspect their resolved definitions:

python src/tools/preview.py --list-preprocessors

docs.title: What you should see
docs.text: The selected order is age imputation, then scaling. Preview resolves declarations; only training learns medians and scale statistics. Each CV fold fits its own state; holdout and prediction reuse saved state.

docs.title: Common errors and fixes
docs.text: Adding a YAML step does not alter an already registered model. Train a new version. Do not include record IDs or the target in scaler columns, and do not define the same phase in YAML and a Python builder.

docs.title: 7. Check locally and deploy
docs.text: Detailed reference: Deployment identities, permissions and compute.

docs.title: When you need it
docs.text: After configuration changes and before any job run.

docs.title: What to edit
docs.text: Set workspace, namespace, identity and paused schedule bindings for the shared test target. Keep the package pin matched to this template.

docs.title: The command
docs.text:
For this example use shared target test. In deployment/targets.yml, set its workspace.host to your workspace URL. In deployment/variables.yml, set test_catalog to workspace and test_input_schema, test_output_schema and test_metadata_schema to your approved skyulf_demo schema. The target root must be a directory your deployment identity controls. Replace YOUR_PROFILE below with the authenticated CLI profile for that workspace.

Install the generated training requirements in your local preview environment. There is no project-wheel or dist/ build step. Run:

uv pip install -r deployment/train-requirements.txt
python src/tools/smoke.py
python src/tools/preview.py
python src/tools/preview.py --action train
python src/tools/preview.py --action score

Use the local tools reference for preview's binding flags, defaults and scope; the generated src/tools/README.md keeps the same short reference beside the scripts. Then validate and deploy from the generated directory:

databricks bundle validate --strict -t test --profile YOUR_PROFILE
databricks bundle deploy -t test --profile YOUR_PROFILE

Choose manual schedules while learning the workflow. A scheduled job can start after deployment when its pause status is UNPAUSED.

docs.title: What you should see
docs.text: Smoke and train/score preview succeed. Strict validation resolves the resources. Deployment creates claim_demo_train, claim_demo_score and claim_demo_monitoring; it does not fit a model. No feature job appears with empty groups.

docs.title: Common errors and fixes
docs.text: Resolve every REPLACE_* value. A source field error belongs to configuration; a missing import belongs to the generated dependency files. Preview executes trusted project factories but does not read Delta rows. See exact-message fixes.

docs.title: 8. Train, inspect and decide
docs.text: Detailed reference: Training reports, approve, reject and roll back, interrupted alias recovery.

docs.title: When you need it
docs.text: When you want a new candidate or an evidence-based activation decision.

docs.title: What to edit
docs.text: The reviewed YAML and source snapshot define this training run. Keep manual promotion for the first exercise; a registered candidate is usable by pinned scoring without becoming champion.

docs.title: The command
docs.text:
databricks bundle run train -t test --profile YOUR_PROFILE

Open Workflows > train run > training_report > Output. The training reports guide explains the task graph, the notebook output and the saved input evidence. Chapter 4 turned on save_preprocessing_diagnostics; preprocessing diagnostics explains where its report is and how to read it.

The report lists the next actions with their exact parameters. Run them on the same train job; they reuse the saved candidate and do not fit a new model. For the first candidate of a new model, the expected champion is none. For example, only when the report actually returns candidate 1 and expected champion none:

databricks bundle run train -t test --profile YOUR_PROFILE --params lifecycle_action=approve,candidate_version=1,expected_champion_version=none

Operator actions explains every parameter, the comparison digest and the promotion receipt. To reject a candidate or undo a promotion, follow reject or roll back.

docs.title: What you should see
docs.text: The report shows the candidate version, protected holdout metrics, the quality decision and the next actions. After approval it shows the promotion receipt and the new champion. Keep that receipt for a later rollback. If score handoff is enabled, follow the child score run and inspect its publication separately; an approval result does not imply a score run occurred.

docs.title: Common errors and fixes
docs.text:
A failed quality gate or a changed champion stops an approval. Inspect the current aliases and the new report before deciding again; do not start another fit only to approve. Copy concrete versions from the report; do not type an alias where a version is requested.

If a training task fails, open that task and its MLflow run. training_snapshot.json records the pinned source and the input, split and budget settings; training_pipeline_config.json records the original pipeline input and saved project source. Keep source Delta history and the recorded dependencies available for replay. A direct SDK replay rebuilds TrainingSpec from the snapshot and passes the original pipeline configuration to train_candidate. Do not substitute pipeline_config.json, which can already contain projected pre-split transformations. Restore the matching YAML and Python in a separate copy; do not overwrite newer project source to inspect a failed run.

docs.title: When you need it
docs.text: After a concrete candidate exists, and whenever new source rows are ready.

docs.title: What to edit
docs.text: In config/inference.yml, keep score_model_selection: pinned_version and set model_version to the actual result. The default is version "1". Redeploy changes before running. See scoring for the complete graph, business rules and layout differences.

docs.title: Score and inspect the demonstration rows
docs.text:
Quick setup defaults to score_model_selection: pinned_version and writes model_version: "1" into config/inference.yml. Replace that version with the actual registered result and redeploy if necessary. A pinned scorer can run a registered candidate without promoting it; choosing champion requires the successful activation described above.

databricks bundle run score -t test --profile YOUR_PROFILE

Open Jobs & Pipelines > claim_demo_score > latest run > score > Output. Inspect its concrete model version, source version, prediction table, counts and commit receipt. Default projects have no scoring_report task; that final report appears when optional CDF expiry recovery is enabled.

With the example's shared test bindings, inspect the named output:

SELECT COUNT(*) AS predictions,
       COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS distinct_keys
FROM workspace.skyulf_demo.claim_demo_predictions;

SELECT * FROM workspace.skyulf_demo.claim_demo_predictions
ORDER BY customer_id LIMIT 5;

For the initial unchanged 120-row source, both counts should be 120. This checks publication, not holdout quality: the final holdout metrics come from training. Repeat score without changing the source; expect a no-op with the same 120 stored rows. For incremental acceptance, append new unique keys to the CDF source, run score again and verify that only those keys add rows.

docs.title: What happens to existing predictions?
docs.text: Changing a model alias does not itself rewrite a prediction table. Score resolves one concrete model/set version and applies the configured change policy. Append mode preserves older rows and their provenance; a configured model-change full rebuild recomputes the current snapshot into a versioned generation and switches the stable prediction view only after success. The previous generation remains. Schema changes need a compatible destination. Model changes involving carried temporal history require rebuilding the corresponding history, not mixing states.

docs.title: Aliases and results to inspect
docs.text: Inspect the concrete registered candidate, champion, challenger, preserved previous aliases and promotion/rejection receipts. A registered version can exist after a later failure without having become champion. A scoring result should identify source watermark, model/version, row counts, no-op/rebuild outcome and Delta commit receipt. Match outputs by record keys.

docs.title: Recovery and schedules
docs.text:
After a scoring failure, inspect the target receipt before retrying. The writer can recognize an acknowledged or uncertain prior commit; deleting state or inventing a new watermark can duplicate work. Recovery options are explicit and do not convert arbitrary source updates/deletes into incremental inserts.

Train and score schedules are independent in deployment variables. A paused schedule prevents clock triggers, not already queued or manually started runs. Both jobs serialize their own active runs; protect registry and output ownership from outside writers too. A successful no-op score is different from a queued job.

docs.title: Configure independent clocks and training data
docs.text: Use training schedule settings for when to attempt fitting, scoring schedule settings for when to inspect new input, and training-window settings for which observations are eligible. The cron timezone does not define the source timestamp timezone. Preview rolling boundaries and result availability cutoffs before activating a schedule. See source windows for the detailed contract.

docs.title: 10. Observe and evaluate retraining
docs.text: Detailed reference: Store setup, enrollment and references, delayed labels, drift, performance loss, retraining guards and dashboard interpretation.

docs.title: When you need it
docs.text: After scoring has committed, or when delayed labels make a later observation useful.

docs.title: What to edit
docs.text: Configure the shared monitoring catalog/schema and optional label source in deployment variables. Keep schedules paused until references are prepared. The monitoring overview covers store setup, reference preparation, label joins, drift/performance policies and the dashboard. A first pinned candidate that was never activated can need reference preparation after scoring enrollment.

docs.title: The command
docs.text:
When an enrolled identity lacks its reference, prepare it explicitly:

databricks bundle run monitoring -t test --profile YOUR_PROFILE --params monitoring_action=prepare_references

Then retry the same score run to finish its monitoring handoff, or run the separate monitoring job with its ordinary observe action. Do not delete committed predictions.

docs.title: Inspect the separate monitoring run
docs.text:
Open the score run's monitor_model child link when monitoring is enabled. In the separate monitoring job, inspect monitor_model, monitoring_report and evaluate_retraining. The last task can legitimately decide not to retrain. An initial inventory needs the project's central store and reference setup; follow store setup before unpausing its schedule.

Without a label source, drift may be available while observed performance is unavailable. Without configured performance policies there is no policy decision. Dashboard refresh reads stored observations; it does not create measurements. Use model/version/context filters to inspect the newly enrolled identity.

docs.title: Common errors and fixes
docs.text: If scoring committed but the monitoring child failed, inspect both stages. Spark reference is not prepared; run prepare_spark_monitoring_reference first. means the reference setup above is missing, not that the predictions disappeared. Retries must retain the saved source/model identity and receipt. No labels means performance is unavailable. Dashboard refresh rereads stored observations and cannot create absent measurements. Retraining needs its explicit policy and freshness, coverage and cooldown guards; it still passes normal model-quality gates.

docs.title: 11. Optionally serve online and increase traffic
docs.text: Detailed reference: Endpoint and SQL queries, online features, daily rollout and serving observations.

docs.title: When you need it
docs.text: Only when consumers need an HTTP/SQL endpoint rather than a Delta prediction table.

docs.title: What to edit
docs.text: Follow the project's SERVING.md for concrete model selection and endpoint creation. Online feature lookup adds key-based retrieval; gradual rollout controls traffic between served versions. These are separate choices. Online publication syncs Delta features to the selected online store; it does not send prediction requests. Lakebase provisioning is explicit, not a side effect of selecting serving.

docs.title: The command
docs.text:
Use the named setup/run commands in those guides after completing their configuration. Validate and deploy their generated resources with the same target:

databricks bundle validate --strict -t test --profile YOUR_PROFILE
databricks bundle deploy -t test --profile YOUR_PROFILE

Deployment alone is not a request test. Send the documented request only after the endpoint and, when used, online publication report ready.

docs.title: What you should see
docs.text: A request identifies the concrete served model and returns its prediction. The rollout controller advances traffic only with sufficient passing evidence; missing checks hold traffic. Final champion promotion follows the configured full-traffic observation period.

docs.title: Common errors and fixes
docs.text: Daily traffic rollout does not apply to batch, incremental Delta scoring or Spark worker inference. Missing/stale online features obey the selected lookup policy. Do not infer endpoint readiness from a successful training or publication job. This optional endpoint path is not executed by the baseline tutorial.

docs.title: 12. Upgrade an existing generated project
docs.text: Detailed reference: Project upgrade and migration.

docs.title: When you need it
docs.text: When adopting a newer Core/template release.

docs.title: What to edit
docs.text: Follow the upgrade guide. It lists the release notes to read, the files to compare and the Core pin to change.

docs.title: The command
docs.text:
uv pip install -r deployment/train-requirements.txt
python src/tools/smoke.py
python src/tools/preview.py --action train
python src/tools/preview.py --action score
databricks bundle validate --strict -t test --profile YOUR_PROFILE

Deploy to your test target, exercise the affected fit/load/score path, and review receipts before upgrading other targets.

docs.title: What you should see
docs.text: The new runtime, generated graph and saved artifact requirements agree. See what you should see.

docs.title: Common errors and fixes
docs.text: An old deployed graph and a new runtime fail a workflow-contract check. Deploy the matching files together; see the upgrade errors.

docs.title: Choose a project shape
docs.text: Three questions decide most of a new Databricks project. Answer them before databricks bundle init; each answer links to the page that owns the details. The closest NYC taxi example is named where one exists.

docs.title: Single model, competition or model set?
docs.text:
You have Choose Closest example Details One target and one model you already picked single_model taxi_fare Training configuration One target and 2-8 candidate algorithms to compare model_competition: CV picks one winner taxi_high_fare Training configuration 2-8 targets approved and scored together multi_target: one versioned model set taxi_trips Model sets One candidate that combines several learners A voting or stacking model in any layout none Ensembles

A competition winner that fails its holdout gate does not promote the runner-up. The layout shapes the generated train job, so choose it at bundle init; see layouts and setup modes.

docs.title: Local batch, Spark batch, REST or ai_query?
docs.text:
Who reads the predictions Choose Closest example Details A scheduled job writing a Delta table within max_rows/max_input_mb score job, batch_compute: single_node (default) taxi_high_fare Scoring A scheduled job on a table too large for one Python process score job, batch_compute: spark taxi_fare Spark scoring An application sending raw feature values REST serving endpoint taxi_fare_endpoint Serving SQL users, SQL jobs and dashboards SQL function calling the endpoint with ai_query taxi_fare_endpoint SQL function Requests that send only an entity key Endpoint with online feature lookup taxi_fare_online Online features

The batch job never calls an endpoint, and an endpoint never writes the prediction table. Models packaged with feature lookup score in batch only with batch_compute: spark. Runtime and cost per path are compared in how predictions are produced.

For rows excluded by preprocessing at scoring, start with taxi_fare_robust. Its Spark and raw-input endpoint examples retain row identity and explain excluded status, null predictions and the resulting monitoring coverage.

For endpoint delivery without a batch prediction table, copy taxi_fare_endpoint. Its serving job follows champion and enrolls the endpoint's telemetry logs for monitoring. Its guide includes a SQL request and the Online serving dashboard.

docs.title: Which steps run on Spark workers and endpoints?
docs.text:
Spark workers and serving endpoints both run the saved pandas pipeline on independent batches, so the same admission applies to both.

Part On Spark workers and endpoints Details Training, tuning and CV Never distributed: one bounded pandas or Polars process Spark scoring Built-in models Reviewed linear/logistic/tree models and XGBRegressor; additional models and voting/stacking with matching training probe evidence Support table Built-in preprocessing steps Reviewed steps (including median imputers), plus eligible row-preserving recipes with matching training probe evidence Recipe boundaries Your column_step and fitted_step functions, saved scoring rules Admitted when training lints and probes them When the probe fails Steps that need other rows (group, window, global), custom_step classes Rejected; keep batch_compute: single_node Custom steps

A single-model or competition Spark project rejects an unsupported model or step before registration, so the failure appears in the train job, not in the first score run. A model set is checked when it is activated and again at scoring.

docs.title: When you need it
docs.text:
Use a custom pre-split filter when a fixed eligibility rule must run before the holdout and CV split, and the admitted built-in pre-split steps cannot express it. A filter keeps or removes whole rows. It learns nothing and changes no values. Learned transformations belong in config/preprocessing.yml; see custom steps for those.

A generated project already ships three filter factories in src/features/pre_split.py: pre_split.minimum_completeness, pre_split.value_range and pre_split.allowed_values. Their parameters are in the ready functions catalog. Select the factory with custom: in config/pre_split.yml, not the callback that takes df.

docs.title: The filter contract
docs.text:
filter_step builds a RowFilterFunction step:

filter_step(name, function, *, columns, params=None, inference_context=None)
Callback you write Required return When Skyulf calls it function(df); with nonempty params, function(df, params) A pandas Boolean Series with exactly one non-null True/False per row, aligned to df.index Generated pre-split eligibility before train/holdout splitting; optionally reused by the saved scoring policy before prediction

df is a private pandas copy, also for Polars models. columns declares the columns the filter reads; they are read automatically and need not be model inputs. Decide missing values explicitly, for example (df["x"] > 0).fillna(False). Use only data known at the observation cutoff; eligibility must not depend on future information.

Custom pre-split steps remain declared fixed filters: they preserve survivor values and order and cannot learn statistics. The generated config/scoring.yml defaults to mode: pre_split, which reuses the saved filters on unlabeled score input. Filters reading the target require an explicit skip choice, shown below.

The shipped completeness filter treats null/NaN as missing; blank strings and infinity count as values. With three selected fields and min_present=2, rows with two or three observed values survive without any value or order changes.

docs.title: Example: an adult-only filter
docs.text:
For this example, start with a single regression model, engine: pandas, with numeric inputs age and income, target claim_amount, and record_id as the record key. Keep the key outside model inputs. The fixed business rule is age at least 18; missing ages are ineligible.

Create src/features/eligibility_rules.py. The callback receives rows; the factory receives only the YAML parameters and returns one step.

# src/features/eligibility_rules.py
from skyulf.preprocessing import filter_step


def adult_rows(df, params):
    """Keep rows meeting a fixed age limit; reject missing ages."""
    return (df[params["column"]] >= params["minimum"]).fillna(False)


def adults_only(column, minimum=18):
    """Build a fixed eligibility filter without learning from the data."""
    return filter_step(
        "adult_only",
        adult_rows,
        columns=[column],
        params={"column": column, "minimum": minimum},
    )


def target_present(df, params):
    """Keep training rows whose actual target is known."""
    return df[params["column"]].notna()


def known_target(column):
    """Declare target usage so scoring can require an explicit skip choice."""
    return filter_step(
        f"known_{column}",
        target_present,
        columns=[column],
        params={"column": column},
    )

Replace config/pre_split.yml with the following recipes, or merge the two named recipes into the existing recipes mapping. Keep one default recipe.

version: 1
recipes:
  default: []
  none: []
  adult_custom:
    - custom: eligibility_rules.adults_only
      params: {column: age, minimum: 18}
  adult_labeled:
    - custom: eligibility_rules.adults_only
      params: {column: age, minimum: 18}
    - custom: eligibility_rules.known_target
      params: {column: claim_amount}

Here eligibility_rules.adults_only resolves to src/features/eligibility_rules.py and calls adults_only(column="age", minimum=18). Activate adult_custom by merging these fields into the existing config/training.yml. Retain its generated table, model, split, quality and resource settings. The generated config/preprocessing.yml already has an empty none recipe.

defaults:
  input_columns: [age, income]
  target_column: claim_amount
  pre_split_recipe: adult_custom
  preprocessing_recipe: none

docs.title: The command
docs.text:
Run from the generated project directory:

python src/tools/smoke.py
python src/tools/preview.py --action train
python src/tools/preview.py --action score

Smoke should return "status": "passed" with "project_hooks_executed": false: it checks syntax and declarations. Training preview resolves adult_custom to the adult_only step. Score preview validates the configured scoring workflow; previews make no remote reads and do not apply filters to rows. The new filter must appear in the training preview before training a new model.

docs.title: What you should see
docs.text:
For example, these training inputs retain record IDs 102, 103, 104, 105, in that order, with all survivor values unchanged. These small samples illustrate the filter; use a source large enough for the configured train/holdout split and CV when training a Bundle model:

record_id,age,income,claim_amount
101,17.0,10.0,1.0
102,18.0,20.0,2.0
103,30.0,30.0,3.0
104,50.0,40.0,4.0
105,70.0,50.0,5.0
106,,60.0,6.0

After training, the default mode: pre_split uses the saved filter on unlabeled rows. For these model inputs (supply record keys separately when running the Bundle batch job):

age,income
17.0,10.0
18.0,20.0
30.0,30.0
,60.0

The four result rows have scoring_status [excluded, predicted, predicted, excluded]. Excluded rows remain in the result with an empty prediction and exclusion_reason: pre_split:adult_only; only the two survivors reach the model.

docs.title: Filters that read the target
docs.text:
To also require a known training label, select pre_split_recipe: adult_labeled. For example, if record 104 above has a missing claim_amount, the two filters retain 102, 103, 105. Because the target is unavailable at scoring time, the default skip setting makes training preview stop with:

Pre-split step 'known_claim_amount' reads target 'claim_amount'. Set SKIP_TARGET_PRE_SPLIT_STEPS=True or SCORING_MODE='custom'.

If the intended scoring population is adults regardless of label availability, replace config/scoring.yml before training:

version: 1
mode: pre_split
skip_target_pre_split_steps: true
eligibility: []
outputs: []
combined: []

Rerun smoke and both previews. Training still applies both filters; scoring skips known_claim_amount and keeps adult_only, so the unlabeled scoring example has the same four outcomes. The choice is saved with each new model version; editing the file does not change an already trained model.

This switch skips an entire target-reading filter. Keep feature eligibility and target checks in separate steps if the feature rule must remain active. mode: custom instead uses only the separately configured scoring rules; merely switching modes does not activate any commented examples. See scoring eligibility.

docs.title: Common errors and fixes
docs.text: Symptom Fix A custom factory cannot be resolved Use a path relative to src/features/, ending in the factory name; retain __init__.py in subpackages. A target-reading filter prevents unlabeled scoring Decide whether it is training-only and set skip_target_pre_split_steps in scoring.yml explicitly before training. See troubleshooting. Filter function must return a boolean Series with one value per row. Return a pandas Series aligned to df.index, one value per row. Filter function must return only True/False values, e.g. df['age'] >= 18. Fill missing comparisons explicitly, for example with .fillna(False). A filter needs learned statistics Move the rule to fitted preprocessing; pre-split filters stay fixed. Edits do not alter an existing model Train a new version; saved source and filter declarations are immutable inputs to scoring.

docs.title: When you need it
docs.text:
Use a custom factory when the built-in preprocessing catalog does not express your calculation. This page covers fixed and learned column transformations in config/preprocessing.yml. Fixed row filters that run before the split have their own page: write your own pre-split filter.

Shipped factories live in src/features/preprocessing.py and are selected as preprocessing.<factory>, for example preprocessing.frequency_encoding. Add your own factory to that file, or keep a larger group in its own module under src/features/ and select it as <file>.<factory>. For example, factory clip_outliers in src/features/income_rules.py is income_rules.clip_outliers. Paths are relative to src/features; preprocessing, pre_split, scoring and groups are the generated modules.

flowchart LR
    A["Raw training rows"] --> B["Fixed pre-split filters"]
    B --> C["Training fold"]
    C --> D["learn: saved state"]
    C --> E["apply: transformed training rows"]
    D --> E
    D --> F["apply: validation or scoring rows"]

A column_step applies a fixed function without learning state. A fitted_step learns separately inside each fold and reuses that state during apply. A filter_step supplies the fixed mask before splitting; see pre-split filters.

docs.title: Custom preprocessing recipes
docs.text:
Select per-step columns when mixing numeric and categorical features. Generated projects contain custom Python examples in src/features/. The YAML files own the ordered recipe lists; Python owns only the selected functions/factories:

File Owns config/pre_split.yml Fixed eligibility recipes config/preprocessing.yml Learned preprocessing recipes src/features/preprocessing.py Shipped transformation factories, selected as preprocessing.<factory> src/features/pre_split.py Shipped filter factories, selected as pre_split.<factory> src/features/<file>.py Your own module of factories, selected as <file>.<factory>

For example, select the shipped frequency encoder in config/preprocessing.yml:

version: 1
recipes:
  default:
    - custom: preprocessing.frequency_encoding
      params: {columns: [category]}

Select preprocessing_recipe: default for the model. To add a built-in node, add its name, transformer and params entry to that same ordered list. Customize the Python factory when the calculation itself must change. The generated PREPROCESSING.md explains factory names, assets and advanced class examples.

Frequency encoding learns count / training_rows per observed string category. For training values ["A", "A", "B", null], scoring ["A", "B", "NEW", null] produces [0.5, 0.25, 0.0, 0.0]. It replaces selected columns in place, preserving other columns and row order. Each CV fold learns its own mapping; saved-model inference never recomputes frequencies on the score batch. Missing/unseen values map to zero. Cast numeric category identifiers to strings upstream if needed. Select these columns in workflow input_columns, excluding target/record keys.

python src/tools/preview.py --action train

See the local tools reference or the generated src/tools/README.md for preview flags, defaults and scope.

docs.title: Writing your own step
docs.text:
The function helpers build ordinary Core steps: column_step produces ColumnFunction, fitted_step produces FittedFunction, and filter_step produces RowFilterFunction. The YAML factory receives keyword parameters and returns one step dictionary; Skyulf invokes the callbacks later with the rows.

For scikit-learn users: learn is fit, apply is transform, and the saved state dictionary contains the fitted attributes. Keep these public helper names; the descriptive callback names below explain the calculation without changing the API used by existing projects.

docs.title: Function signatures and execution
docs.text:
These are the helper signatures. Optional inference_context declares row, group, window or global dependence for diagnostics. Alone it does not grant Spark or REST serving admission: training lints and probes your steps first, and "row" is optional there while group, window and global stay rejected. See Admit your own row steps and, when a step is rejected, When the probe fails.

column_step(name, function, *, output, replace=False, params=None, inference_context=None)
fitted_step(name, learn, apply, *, output, replace=False, params=None, inference_context=None)
filter_step(name, function, *, columns, params=None, inference_context=None)
Helper Callback signatures you write Required return When Skyulf calls it column_step function(df); with nonempty params, function(df, params) Series, DataFrame, NumPy array or list, with one value per input row per output column Transform training rows in each CV fold/final fit, validation rows and scoring rows; no statistics are learned fitted_step learning learn(df, y); with nonempty params, learn(df, y, params) A JSON-compatible dict with string keys, no NaN or infinity Each CV training fold and final training fit; never refit on validation or scoring rows fitted_step applying apply(df, state); with nonempty params, apply(df, state, params) The same column-return contract as column_step Transform training/validation/scoring rows with that fit's saved state filter_step function(df); with nonempty params, function(df, params) A pandas Boolean Series with exactly one non-null True/False per row, aligned to df.index Generated pre-split eligibility before train/holdout splitting; optionally reused by the saved scoring policy before prediction

df is a private pandas DataFrame copy even for a Polars pipeline. Column/fitted callbacks do not see the target column in df; y is a private training target passed to learn (or None if no target is supplied). state is exactly the learned dictionary restored from the artifact. params is the helper's saved user-configuration dictionary, passed as the last positional argument only when nonempty. With params=None or {}, omit that argument in your callback signature or give it a default. YAML params first configures the factory; the factory explicitly passes its callback parameters into the helper.

For column outputs, preserve row count/order and any pandas index; return as many columns as output declares. A Series names one output; a DataFrame/array supplies outputs in the declared order. output supplies the final column names. Use replace=True only when replacing existing columns; a callback must not replace the target. Filter callbacks instead may read declared target columns when explicitly configured, but remain fixed row-local rules with no learning: see target-reading filters for the saved scoring skip choice. Filters preserve every retained value and row order.

docs.title: One output: the shipped log feature
docs.text:
This is the generated src/features/preprocessing.py example. It adds a column and leaves income unchanged. Its callback has nothing to learn.

import numpy as np

from skyulf.preprocessing import column_step


def log1p_value(df, params):
    """Return log(1 + value); negative values count as 0."""
    return np.log1p(df[params["column"]].clip(lower=0))


def log_feature(column):
    """Add log_<column> next to the original column."""
    return column_step(
        f"log_{column}", log1p_value, output=f"log_{column}", params={"column": column}
    )

version: 1
recipes:
  default: []
  with_log:
    - custom: preprocessing.log_feature
      params: {column: income}

Select preprocessing_recipe: with_log and include income in input_columns. For income [-2, 0, 3, null], log_income is [0, 0, 1.3862943611, NaN]: negative values are clipped to zero and missing values stay missing. A model that cannot accept missing values needs a later imputation step in its recipe.

docs.title: Two outputs: a custom budget calculation
docs.text:
Create src/features/budget.py. This example adds a net amount and an expense ratio. Zero or missing income makes the ratio missing; this example does not invent a denominator or fill that value.

import pandas as pd

from skyulf.preprocessing import column_step


def budget_values(df, params):
    """Return net income and expense share in the original row order."""
    income = df[params["income"]]
    expenses = df[params["expenses"]]
    denominator = income.where(income.ne(0))
    return pd.DataFrame(
        {"net_income": income - expenses, "expense_share": expenses / denominator}
    )


def budget_columns(income="income", expenses="expenses"):
    """Add two fixed calculations without learning population statistics."""
    return column_step(
        "budget_columns",
        budget_values,
        output=["net_income", "expense_share"],
        params={"income": income, "expenses": expenses},
    )

version: 1
recipes:
  default: []
  with_budget:
    - custom: budget.budget_columns
      params: {income: income, expenses: expenses}

Select preprocessing_recipe: with_budget and input columns income, expenses. Rows (income, expenses) of (100, 25), (80, 40), (0, 10) and (null, 5) produce (net_income, expense_share) of (75, 0.25), (40, 0.5), (-10, NaN) and (NaN, NaN). The two original columns and row order remain unchanged. Add appropriate missing-value handling before an estimator that requires finite inputs.

docs.title: Learned mapping: the shipped frequency encoder
docs.text:
These are the actual generated preprocessing.py callbacks and factory. The factory connects learning and applying; its columns list is saved as callback params. You normally select the existing factory instead of copying it elsewhere.

import pandas as pd

from skyulf.preprocessing import fitted_step


def learn_frequencies(df, y, params):
    """Learn: share of training rows per category (null is not a category)."""
    if len(df) == 0:
        raise ValueError("Frequency encoding requires nonempty training rows.")
    return {column: (df[column].value_counts() / len(df)).to_dict() for column in params["columns"]}


def apply_frequencies(df, state, params):
    """Apply: look up the saved share; unseen or null categories get 0."""
    return pd.DataFrame(
        {
            column: df[column].map(state[column]).astype(float).fillna(0.0)
            for column in params["columns"]
        }
    )


def frequency_encoding(columns):
    """Replace string category columns with their training frequency."""
    if not isinstance(columns, (list, tuple)) or not columns:
        raise ValueError("Frequency columns must be a nonempty list of column names.")
    if any(not isinstance(column, str) or not column for column in columns):
        raise ValueError("Frequency columns must be nonempty column names.")
    if len(set(columns)) != len(columns):
        raise ValueError("Frequency columns must be unique.")
    columns = list(columns)
    return fitted_step(
        "frequency_encoding",
        learn_frequencies,
        apply_frequencies,
        output=columns,
        replace=True,
        params={"columns": columns},
    )

version: 1
recipes:
  default: []
  with_frequency:
    - custom: preprocessing.frequency_encoding
      params: {columns: [category]}

Select preprocessing_recipe: with_frequency with category as a raw input. Training on ['A', 'A', 'B', null] learns {'category': {'A': 0.5, 'B': 0.25}}. The denominator includes all four training rows, while null is not a category. Applying to ['A', 'B', 'NEW', null] returns [0.5, 0.25, 0.0, 0.0]. Repeated or differently sized score batches reuse those same fractions. Saved-model loading restores the mapping and Python source; it does not count the incoming categories again. Use string category values so the learned dictionary has valid string keys.

docs.title: Learned category groups: learn and apply without numeric encoding
docs.text:
The generated rare_categories example separates the same two phases but keeps text. It is useful before a numeric encoder when rare and unseen categories should share a deliberate fallback value.

from skyulf.preprocessing import fitted_step


def learn_common_categories(df, y, params):
    """Learn: categories that cover at least min_share of the training rows."""
    shares = df[params["column"]].value_counts() / len(df)
    common = shares[shares >= params["min_share"]].index
    return {"keep": sorted(str(category) for category in common)}


def apply_common_categories(df, state, params):
    """Apply: keep learned categories and nulls; everything else becomes `other`."""
    values = df[params["column"]].astype(object)  # object: "Other" is allowed as a value
    keep = values.isna() | values.astype(str).isin(state["keep"])
    return values.where(keep, params["other"])


def rare_categories(column, min_share=0.05, other="Other"):
    """Replace categories seen in less than min_share of training rows with `other`."""
    if not 0 < min_share < 1:
        raise ValueError("min_share must be between 0 and 1, e.g. 0.05 for 5%.")
    params = {"column": column, "min_share": min_share, "other": other}
    return fitted_step(
        f"rare_{column}",
        learn_common_categories,
        apply_common_categories,
        output=column,
        replace=True,
        params=params,
    )

version: 1
recipes:
  default: []
  grouped_categories:
    - custom: preprocessing.rare_categories
      params: {column: city, min_share: 0.3, other: Other}
    - custom: preprocessing.frequency_encoding
      params: {columns: [city]}

Select preprocessing_recipe: grouped_categories and include city in the raw inputs. With training cities ['London', 'London', 'London', 'Paris', 'Oslo'], learn_common_categories saves {'keep': ['London']} at min_share: 0.3. Applying the rare-category step to ['London', 'Paris', 'Tokyo', null] gives ['London', 'Other', 'Other', null]; null stays null and the unseen city uses Other. In the complete recipe, the following frequency step learns from the transformed training rows, so the final four values are [0.6, 0.4, 0.4, 0.0]. This demonstrates ordered steps; neither mapping is relearned during scoring.

For fixed row eligibility, the pre-split filter page shows the third helper. The shipped alternatives are pre_split.value_range, pre_split.allowed_values and pre_split.minimum_completeness: select the factory with custom: in config/pre_split.yml, not the callback that takes df.

docs.title: Learning from the target: a small category-mean example
docs.text:
Create src/features/target_mean.py. This educational example uses the training y to learn a mean per string category. Its apply function receives no target; missing or unseen categories use the saved global training mean.

import pandas as pd

from skyulf.preprocessing import fitted_step


def learn_target_means(df, y, params):
    """Learn category means and a fallback from this training fold's targets."""
    if y is None:
        raise ValueError("Target-mean encoding requires training targets.")
    labels = pd.Series(y, index=df.index, dtype=float)
    means = labels.groupby(df[params["column"]]).mean().to_dict()
    return {"means": means, "fallback": float(labels.mean())}


def apply_target_means(df, state, params):
    """Use saved means without reading or requiring scoring targets."""
    return df[params["column"]].map(state["means"]).fillna(state["fallback"])


def target_mean(column):
    """Replace a string category with its learned target mean."""
    return fitted_step(
        f"target_mean_{column}",
        learn_target_means,
        apply_target_means,
        output=column,
        replace=True,
        params={"column": column},
    )

version: 1
recipes:
  default: []
  with_target_mean:
    - custom: target_mean.target_mean
      params: {column: category}

Select preprocessing_recipe: with_target_mean with input category and your normal target column. For categories ['A', 'A', 'B', 'B'] with targets [0, 1, 2, 3], the state is {'means': {'A': 0.5, 'B': 2.5}, 'fallback': 1.5}. Applying to ['A', 'B', 'NEW', null] without y returns [0.5, 2.5, 1.5, 1.5].

Cross-validation learns from each fold's training rows, so that mapping does not read validation targets. This does not make a naive target encoder universally leakage-safe: transforming its own training rows with their fitted category mean can overfit, especially for singleton categories. This tiny helper has no internal out-of-fold encoding, smoothing or time-aware exclusion. Use an appropriately validated target-encoding recipe and splitting policy for real target-dependent feature engineering. Never build this mapping on the entire dataset before splitting.

docs.title: Clipping with learned bounds
docs.text:
The next example creates a new fitted factory rather than selecting a shipped one.

# src/features/income_rules.py
from skyulf.preprocessing import fitted_step


def learn_bounds(df, y, params):
    """Learn clip limits from the training fold only."""
    values = df[params["column"]]
    return {"low": float(values.quantile(0.01)), "high": float(values.quantile(0.99))}


def clip_values(df, state, params):
    """Clip every later batch with the saved training limits."""
    return df[params["column"]].clip(state["low"], state["high"])


def clip_outliers(column):
    """Replace column with its value clipped to training 1%-99% quantiles."""
    params = {"column": column}
    return fitted_step(f"clip_{column}", learn_bounds, clip_values,
                       output=column, replace=True, params=params)

Select that factory in config/preprocessing.yml:

version: 1
recipes:
  default: []
  custom_clip:
    - custom: income_rules.clip_outliers
      params: {column: income}

The dotted path starts at src/features/: income_rules means src/features/income_rules.py, and clip_outliers is the top-level factory in that file. The loader calls clip_outliers(column="income"); it does not pass rows to the factory. A module in a subfolder also needs that folder's __init__.py.

Set preprocessing_recipe: custom_clip under defaults or the selected model in config/training.yml, and include income in input_columns. The empty default recipe does not activate custom_clip; neither does merely creating the Python file. After saving both files, run these commands from the generated project:

python src/tools/smoke.py
python src/tools/preview.py --action train
python src/tools/preview.py --action score

Smoke checks syntax and declarations without executing the factory. Training preview resolves the selected clip_income step; score preview checks the configured scoring workflow. Neither command fits quantiles or predicts rows. For training incomes [10, 20, 30, 40], the fitted bounds are 10.3 and 39.7; later incomes [-1000, 1000] clip to those saved bounds.

learn runs on the training rows of every CV fold and of the final fit; its dict is saved with the model and apply reuses it for validation and scoring rows; validation/scoring rows do not fit those quantiles. y is the training target; the target column is removed from df in both functions, so apply can never depend on it. Rules:

  • Use top-level def functions, not lambdas or nested functions.
  • df is a pandas copy, also for Polars models; changing it has no effect.
  • Return one value per row in the same order. Filters return True/False per row; decide missing values explicitly, e.g. (df["x"] > 0).fillna(False).
  • Learned dicts must be JSON-like: string keys and no NaN. NumPy numbers are converted automatically.
  • Nonempty params={...} is passed to every function as its last argument; empty params are omitted from the callback call.
  • Use replace=True to overwrite existing columns; otherwise outputs must be new.

Errors name the failing function, e.g. Project function ...:learn_bounds failed: KeyError: 'income'.

Most former Calculator/Applier pairs fit in these helpers. The advanced custom_step factory below instead connects Calculator.fit(X, y, config) to Applier.apply(X, y, state). Choose that class pair only when the learned state is not a small dict (for example a fitted scikit-learn object), the step changes the number of rows during preprocessing, or it needs native Polars/Spark code for performance. These helper steps are project code only: the web canvas and backend API reject them, because a graph must never name an arbitrary server function.

docs.title: Advanced: a Calculator/Applier class pair
docs.text:
This is the shipped preprocessing.rare_categories step written as a class pair. The class version receives pandas or Polars (X.to_native()), rebuilds the whole table itself and can keep native Polars code. Prefer fitted_step unless you need that, a learned state that is not a small dict, or a step that removes columns or rows.

# src/features/rare_class_step.py
import polars as pl

from skyulf.inference.project_code import custom_step
from skyulf.preprocessing.base import BaseApplier, BaseCalculator, apply_method, fit_method


class RareCategoryCalculator(BaseCalculator):
    """fit(): runs on the training rows of every CV fold and returns what it learned."""

    @fit_method
    def fit(self, X, y, config):
        """Learn the categories covering at least min_share of the training rows."""
        native = X.to_native() if hasattr(X, "to_native") else X
        values = native[config["column"]]
        values = values.to_pandas() if isinstance(values, pl.Series) else values
        shares = values.value_counts() / len(values)
        common = shares[shares >= config["min_share"]].index
        return {
            "column": config["column"],
            "other": config["other"],
            "keep": sorted(str(category) for category in common),
        }


class RareCategoryApplier(BaseApplier):
    """apply(): runs on train, test and scoring rows using only the saved fit() result."""

    @apply_method
    def apply(self, X, y, state):
        """Replace categories not in the saved list with `other`; nulls stay null."""
        native = X.to_native() if hasattr(X, "to_native") else X
        if isinstance(native, pl.DataFrame):
            return _apply_polars(native, state)
        return _apply_pandas(native, state)


def _apply_polars(frame, state):
    """Native Polars expression: no conversion to pandas."""
    column = pl.col(state["column"])
    keep = column.is_null() | column.cast(pl.Utf8).is_in(state["keep"])
    replaced = pl.when(keep).then(column.cast(pl.Utf8)).otherwise(pl.lit(state["other"]))
    return frame.with_columns(replaced.alias(state["column"]))


def _apply_pandas(frame, state):
    """Pandas version; returns a copy so the caller's table is never changed."""
    values = frame[state["column"]].astype(object)
    keep = values.isna() | values.astype(str).isin(state["keep"])
    result = frame.copy()
    result[state["column"]] = values.where(keep, state["other"])
    return result


def class_rare_categories(column, min_share=0.05, other="Other"):
    """Build the step: replace rare categories in column with `other`."""
    if not 0 < min_share < 1:
        raise ValueError("min_share must be between 0 and 1, e.g. 0.05 for 5%.")
    return custom_step(
        f"class_rare_{column}",
        RareCategoryCalculator,
        RareCategoryApplier,
        params={"column": column, "min_share": min_share, "other": other},
    )

Select it in config/preprocessing.yml:

version: 1
recipes:
  default: []
  rare_city_class:
    - custom: rare_class_step.class_rare_categories
      params: {column: city, min_share: 0.05}

Training saves the exact Python source with the fitted artifact. Both local and MLflow loading restore this saved source, including custom classes. Changing the project file affects future training; score, approve and rollback continue using saved model code/state. Different source versions use distinct package identities. All Python files under src/features/ are captured in a bounded 64 KiB snapshot, excluding root groups/ producers. Use relative imports and an __init__.py in every subpackage. Declared assets can be captured as described below; third-party dependencies must be installed explicitly in both training and scoring environments. Keep job entrypoints outside the feature package. Only load trusted code/models, as with existing pickle artifacts. Historical feature context and post-prediction business rules have their own configuration.

docs.title: Pre-split filters
docs.text: Fixed row filters built with filter_step have their own page: write your own pre-split filter.

docs.title: Does custom: work for every custom function?
docs.text:
It is a general selector, not a special case for log_feature. The example calls src/features/preprocessing.py -> log_feature(column="income") to build one step. That factory returns column_step(...); Skyulf later calls its calculation function with the actual rows. YAML does not pass a DataFrame into the factory.

Custom work Factory returns Selected from Fixed formula producing one or more columns column_step(...) preprocessing.yml Transformation learning state from training rows fitted_step(...) preprocessing.yml Fixed row eligibility mask filter_step(...) pre_split.yml Advanced Calculator/Applier pair custom_step(...) Its supported phase; see a class pair Spark aggregation producing a feature table Spark DataFrame features.yml -> groups, using file.py:function

The factory must be a top-level function defined in the referenced captured project module, accept the YAML params as keyword arguments, and return one valid Core step dictionary. Select multiple factories as separate YAML entries. A raw def transform(df) returning a DataFrame, a sklearn transformer instance, a list of steps or a lambda is not a valid custom: factory. Wrap the calculation using the matching helper; do not rewrite its business logic inside the loader.

Calculation functions used by the helpers must also be saved top-level functions. column_step/fitted_step preserve rows and return one value per row per declared output; their callbacks receive pandas frames. A fitted step separates learning from applying a saved, JSON-compatible state dictionary. filter_step returns one non-null Boolean per input row, uses fixed row-local rules and changes no values. Pre-split is not a place to fit a scaler or learn population statistics. Declare external dependencies in the project's deployment requirements and package declared assets; YAML does not install packages or capture live services.

These custom examples work in the local pipeline. Spark batch and REST serving require a supported fitted pipeline; an arbitrary custom function is not automatically admitted for those runtimes. Check the scope in feature tables and serving.

Keep named recipes under recipes in each phase YAML file and select one per model using preprocessing_recipe. Competition can select different preprocessing recipes per candidate while sharing pre-split eligibility. Independent-target projects can select preprocessing and pre-split recipes per model. Both YAML files require version: 1 and a default recipe; none means no steps. Recipes prefixed example_ remain inactive until selected. Do not add Python build_preprocessing or build_pre_split_steps builders for a phase owned by YAML. Existing Python-only projects continue to work without these YAML files.

Check the resolved project before training:

python src/tools/smoke.py
python src/tools/preview.py --action train
python src/tools/preview.py --list-preprocessors

Smoke validates the declarations without calling custom factories; preview resolves the selected recipes and executes trusted factories. Keep I/O out of module imports and factories.

The saved model contains resolved steps, fitted state, captured YAML declarations and project Python. Prediction does not re-read current recipe files or fit new means. Edits apply to newly trained model versions. Upstream Spark feature jobs are separate: a model trained on a merged table still needs those input features; it does not automatically execute the upstream joins from a raw table.

docs.title: The command
docs.text:
From the generated project directory, with its pinned dependencies installed:

python src/tools/smoke.py
python src/tools/preview.py --action train
python src/tools/preview.py --action score

Smoke parses the package; preview resolves trusted factories. A real training run is needed to learn and save state. Follow training and reports for that step.

docs.title: Try the callbacks locally before training
docs.text:
Smoke and preview check declarations and resolve factories; they do not run learn or apply on rows. After creating the clipping file above, run this literal example from the generated project root with its pinned dependencies. It uses the shipped frequency encoder and your income_rules.py factory. fit_transform returns the transformed training frame and metrics; transform returns only the transformed scoring frame.

import sys
from pathlib import Path

import pandas as pd

from skyulf.preprocessing import FeatureEngineer

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path("src/features").resolve()))
from preprocessing import frequency_encoding
from income_rules import clip_outliers

engineer = FeatureEngineer([frequency_encoding(["city"]), clip_outliers("income")])
training = pd.DataFrame(
    {"city": ["A", "A", "B", None], "income": [10.0, 20.0, 30.0, 40.0]}
)
transformed_train, _ = engineer.fit_transform(training)
scoring = pd.DataFrame(
    {"city": ["A", "NEW", None, "B"], "income": [-1000.0, 1000.0, 25.0, None]}
)
transformed_score = engineer.transform(scoring)
print(transformed_score)

Expected city values are [0.5, 0.0, 0.0, 0.25]; expected income values are [10.3, 39.7, 25.0, NaN]. These are the training frequencies and saved quantile bounds, not statistics recomputed from the scoring frame. This local exercise runs real callbacks, but does not register a model, contact Databricks or certify Spark/REST execution. The generated training workflow captures the project source when it later trains and saves the actual model.

For a fixed lookup file or third-party package, follow captured source, assets and dependencies. Use inference_context="row", "group" or "window" only when it accurately describes your callback's input dependence; the declaration is metadata, not a worker or serving certificate. See inference context for the separate admission boundary.

docs.title: What you should see
docs.text: The examples above show expected outputs, saved learned state and clipping bounds. After reload, predictions use the captured recipe and source, even if the editable project has changed.

docs.title: Captured source, assets and dependencies
docs.text:
Training freezes src/features/, excluding the root groups/ directory, as a versioned 64 KiB package snapshot. Spark producers in groups/ execute separately in the feature job. Keep custom model functions in their phase modules; do not import producers from model recipes. See feature tables for the stage boundary. Declare bounded data files in src/features/assets.json as files: [...] (the file itself uses JSON), and read them with read_project_asset from skyulf.inference.project_package. Paths stay inside the package; symlinks are rejected. Code, captured recipe declarations, assets and exact dependency pins share the snapshot budget. Use distribution==version in src/features/requirements.txt and install those versions in training/scoring environments; loading verifies them without installing.

YAML and Python edits apply to the next training load. Saved models retain resolved settings, recipe declarations, fitted preprocessing and frozen source; scoring and lifecycle replay do not reread editable YAML or Python. Changing rules/assets/pins requires a new model.

python src/tools/smoke.py
python src/tools/preview.py --action train

docs.title: Common errors and fixes
docs.text:
Symptom Fix A custom factory cannot be resolved Use a path relative to src/features/, ending in the factory name; retain __init__.py in subpackages. A target-reading filter prevents unlabeled scoring See pre-split filters. A helper changes row count or ordering Return one value per input row, or a fixed filter mask. Use supported advanced contracts for other transformations. Edits do not alter an existing model Train a new version; saved source and fitted state are immutable inputs to scoring. Reload rejects dependencies or the source package Keep exact pins, package-local asset paths and the snapshot budget; installing packages is an explicit environment step.

See context and diagnostics for group/window operations and feature tables for Spark producers that run before the model pipeline.

docs.title: When you need it
docs.text: Use a decision threshold when a classifier's saved class decision should differ from its native prediction. This affects class labels, not probability calibration. It is independent of promotion quality_threshold and of business output bands. New projects leave this policy off.

docs.title: What to edit
docs.text:
Merge this fragment into an existing classification config/training.yml, keeping its model, inputs, source, split and other settings. A named model can override defaults.decision_threshold:

defaults:
  decision_threshold:
    mode: auto
    metric: balanced_accuracy
    validation_fraction: 0.2
    random_state: 42

New projects keep decision thresholds off. Configure decision_threshold on a named model entry in config/training.yml. These Python mappings illustrate the corresponding Core pipeline value; use the equivalent YAML mapping in a Bundle model entry:

# Native classifier decisions; no calibration partition is reserved.
DECISION_THRESHOLD = {"mode": "off"}

# Binary: predict "churn" when its probability is >= 0.7, including exact ties.
DECISION_THRESHOLD = {"mode": "manual", "positive_class": "churn", "value": 0.7}

# Multiclass: exactly one class wins argmax(probability / class value).
DECISION_THRESHOLD = {
    "mode": "manual",
    "thresholds": [
        {"class": "low", "value": 0.5},
        {"class": "medium", "value": 0.3},
        {"class": "high", "value": 0.2},
    ],
}

# Binary or multiclass: select thresholds on a reserved part of training data.
DECISION_THRESHOLD = {
    "mode": "auto",
    "metric": "balanced_accuracy",
    "validation_fraction": 0.2,
    "random_state": 42,
}

Use original target labels, preserving their types (e.g. integer 1 versus string "1"), even when preprocessing encodes the target. The fitted encoder chain maps these labels to the model's probability columns. Saved local models return original labels and record them in manifest.classes; evaluation uses the same mapping. This covers LabelEncoder and OrdinalEncoder, including explicit category order and repeated encoding around resampling. Feature-only encoders do not change target labels. Multiclass entries must cover every class exactly once, with positive finite values; they are relative decision weights, not minimum confidence requirements. The result always has one class, even if all probabilities are low. Binary manual cutoffs permit both endpoints, zero and one.

Automatic mode reserves 20% of the training partition by default, before fitting preprocessing or selecting model parameters. It fits the model on the remaining rows, selects thresholds on calibration rows, and saves that fitted model without refitting on the calibration population. Final holdout labels never select an estimator, preprocessing state or threshold. Random calibration is stratified; group CV keeps groups separate; temporal workflows use a chronological calibration tail and honor the configured CV gap. Every class must occur in both partitions, otherwise training fails with an actionable error. Small datasets can therefore require a different split or manual mode.

For random row splitting, validation_fraction: 0.25 fits the saved model on approximately 75% of the training rows and uses the remainder only to choose its decision threshold. With group splitting, the fraction selects groups, not rows: unequal group sizes can produce very different row proportions. Whole groups stay together; inspect fitting_rows and calibration_rows in the threshold evidence for the actual populations. There is no final full-training refit in this mode. off and manual do not reserve this extra calibration population. Full-data refitting is a different policy and can change the probabilities to which a selected threshold applies.

Supported automatic objectives are balanced_accuracy, binary f1, f1_macro, f1_weighted, and matthews_corrcoef. For binary selection, positive_class is optional and defaults to the fitted model's second class. The existing heldout binary precision/recall/F1 and probability metrics retain that second-class reporting convention, even when a different label owns the decision cutoff. Sample weights affect estimator fitting, but calibration objectives and their reported scores remain unweighted, as do the other evaluation metrics. f1_weighted means class-support averaging, not row-weighted scoring. Automatic threshold selection has no row-cost/sample-weight objective option; it should not be interpreted as optimizing weighted business costs. Thresholds change class predictions; they do not calibrate or alter probabilities. An improved calibration score does not guarantee a better independent holdout score.

CV and competition independently refit the complete model-and-threshold policy inside every outer training fold. Parameter searches also run inside those folds; their extra work counts toward competition_max_trials. The original model-search scores in tuning.json describe base-model selection, while cross_validation.json and competition_evaluation.json evaluate the final decision policy. decision_threshold.json records fitting/calibration counts, selected values, the positive class and calibration scores. Model reload, registry evaluation, batch prediction preserve the saved decision rule. For an additional standalone inference bundle export, pass use_tuned_thresholds=True to build_bundle. That separate portable format retains its existing supported-node restrictions; target-encoder pipelines use the full local artifact saved by the Bundle.

Prediction columns retain stable positional names: probability_0 belongs to manifest.classes[0], probability_1 to manifest.classes[1], and so on. For example, manifest.classes = ["no", "yes"] maps probability_1 to "yes". This mapping uses the original labels even when the target was encoded. Do not infer a class from its spelling or assume the positive class always has index 1 when explicitly configuring a different positive_class.

Regression and classifiers without predict_proba cannot enable thresholds. The separate nested-CV binary search modeling.tune_threshold is accepted; do not enable it alongside manual or auto. An explicit off policy leaves that independently requested search intact. Promotion quality_threshold remains a separate acceptance gate.

Use your configured target/profile. Preview checks configuration; only fitting can verify class support and the actual calibration population. Inspect the new saved version before selecting it for scoring.

docs.title: What you should see
docs.text: Open the training run's Artifacts > decision_threshold.json for selected values, positive class, fitting/calibration counts and calibration scores. cross_validation.json and competition_evaluation.json evaluate the complete policy; tuning.json describes base-model selection. See training reports for the job tasks and MLflow locations, and search and cross-validation for fold controls. Check the saved manifest.classes before interpreting probability_0, probability_1 or later columns. Saved predictions use the selected rule and original label types after reload. Holdout metrics remain independent evidence.

docs.title: Common errors and fixes
docs.text: Symptom Check and fix Too few classes in fit/calibration Supply more representative data, change the split, or choose manual/off mode. Both partitions must contain every class. Manual class is not found Use the original target label and type, and cover every multiclass label exactly once. An auto threshold consumes more rows than expected The calibration population is reserved before fitting. With groups, validation_fraction counts groups, not rows. Inspect the saved counts. Probability values did not change Expected: thresholds change class decisions, not probability estimates. Regression or a classifier without predict_proba is rejected Keep threshold mode off or use a supported probabilistic classifier. tune_threshold conflicts with manual/auto Choose one policy; explicit off leaves a separately requested nested search intact. Better calibration score, worse holdout score Calibration optimization is not a promise of better independent model quality. Retain the holdout gate.
