Inspect each group task's receipt_json and the merge output for table/version, row count and reuse evidence. Initialization records source versions and transform hashes. Expected results for the sample inputs are four rows in each group output and four rows in the merged table:

SELECT observation_id, company_id, observed_at, employee_count,
       monthly_amount, transaction_count, churn
FROM workspace.demo.company_merged
ORDER BY observation_id;
observation_id company_id observed_at employee_count monthly_amount transaction_count churn 101 1 2026-01-31 10 100.0 2 0 102 1 2026-02-28 12 150.0 1 1 103 2 2026-01-31 20 20.0 1 0 104 2 2026-02-28 21 70.0 1 1

This table is the expected result of the shown joins. January company 1 receives the January 25 activity total, not the later February 25 total. The merge keeps all base columns, including observation_id and churn; it adds only the declared features. Every join checks row count. Duplicate/null join keys, overlapping feature names, inconsistent key/time types, or missing required matches stop publication.

Missing output tables are created as Delta with CDF enabled. Later runs upsert changed keys and retain older observations; they do not propagate source deletes or evolve output schemas implicitly. Existing outputs need matching schema and CDF. A source correction can therefore produce UPDATE events in the merged scoring source: apply the scoring source-change policy intentionally rather than assuming every feature refresh is append-only.

docs.title: 5. Point training and scoring at the result
docs.text:
Merge this fragment into the existing classification config/training.yml, retaining its model, registry, split, quality and resource settings:

defaults:
  training_table: workspace.demo.company_merged
  record_key_columns: [observation_id]
  input_columns: [employee_count, monthly_amount, transaction_count]
  target_column: churn

In config/inference.yml, update these two fields, retaining the other settings:

score_source_table: workspace.demo.company_merged
prediction_table: "{catalog}.{output_schema}.company_predictions{resource_suffix}"

Once there are enough representative rows for the configured split/CV, run the normal training workflow and approve/select a saved version before scoring. For independent-target layouts, check model-level input/target overrides as well as defaults. The merged table may contain labels; labels are not model inputs. A separate unlabeled observation/merge table can be the scoring source.

Choose one owner for each transformation. Do not scale or impute from the whole merged population and then repeat it in the saved model. Add learned missing value handling to config/preprocessing.yml. See the training field reference for split, sampling, limits and per-model settings.

To add a domain, create src/features/groups/balances.py with compute_features(frame), add groups.balances with its source, destination, transform and distinct feature names, then refresh and redeploy. Do not add this upstream folder to src/features/__init__.py or import it from model recipes.

docs.title: Refresh selected groups and repair a failed run
docs.text:
To recompute activity while reusing the currently stored company features:

databricks bundle run features -t test --profile YOUR_PROFILE --params selected_groups=activity

selected_groups=* is the default and computes every group. A comma-separated list chooses groups; an empty selection reuses all group outputs. Reused tables must already exist. Initialization pins their versions, and merge uses those pinned versions. An unknown group name fails.

If a group task fails, inspect its input version, transform hash and exception. Repair only when the saved graph/code/input evidence still applies. Changed configuration or transform code needs a new run; retrying a stale receipt is not a way to accept a new calculation. A completed group output can exist even when a later group or merge fails, so inspect the receipts instead of assuming all writes form one multi-table transaction. In Repair run, rerun the failed group and dependent merge while keeping the original pinned inputs. External writes to the feature destinations are unsupported; serialized job runs do not lock unrelated producers.

Each new run also pins the output table identities and records a publication generation. A newer run that starts publishing any group or the merged output supersedes an older run. Repairing that older run then fails before it can overwrite newer values; start a fresh run instead. This includes newer runs that failed partway through publication. Old saved mutation snapshots without generation evidence must also restart from initialization.

Retrying the same current snapshot is supported after a lost write response, provided its transforms are deterministic. Keep one owning, serialized producer for these tables. The generation check detects stale repairs; it is not a distributed lock against simultaneous external writers. Existing outputs receive a publication-intent table property before the merge, which can add a metadata-only Delta history version even when no rows change.

docs.title: Bind existing UC features instead of materializing a merge
docs.text:
Use feature_lookup when the model should retain native lookup lineage. The following training defaults fragment uses an existing base table containing observation_id, company_id, observed_at and churn, but not the fetched features:

engine: pandas
training_table: "{catalog}.{input_schema}.company_observations"
record_key_columns: [observation_id]
input_columns: [monthly_amount, transaction_count]
target_column: churn
feature_lookup:
  lookups:
    - table_name: "{catalog}.{input_schema}.company_activity_history"
      lookup_key: [company_id]
      feature_names: [monthly_amount, transaction_count]
      timestamp_lookup_key: observed_at
      timestamp_type: date
      lookback_seconds: 2678400

Set batch_compute: spark in config/inference.yml for this offline batch route and score from the corresponding observation table. The example's lookback is 31 days. For a non-temporal exact lookup, omit timestamp and lookback fields. Any direct model inputs not fetched must be present in the base table. Fetched features must be listed in input_columns and must not also exist there.

The feature table must already be a valid UC feature table with declared primary keys; historical lookup additionally needs the appropriate TIMESERIES key. The ordinary group output above does not add those catalog constraints. Install the matching Feature Engineering dependency in deployment/requirements.txt (the generated feature-store integration pins databricks-feature-engineering==0.18.1). Native lookup uses the saved model's feature binding and score_batch, not the ordinary merged-table pyfunc route.

The saved training_snapshot binding records feature-table IDs/versions. When a feature table advances, scoring accepts it only if its identity and schema still match and a distributed comparison proves both retained snapshots contain exactly the same rows, including duplicates. This permits data-preserving maintenance such as compaction. Actual data or schema changes require refreshed training and an explicit rebuild/new prediction target. Missing historical snapshots fail validation; retain the training versions needed for this check.

The equality proof can scan both complete feature-table snapshots. It is repeated on later scoring calls while the current version differs from the saved training version; there is no persistent proof cache. Plan for this cost on large feature tables. Before/after version checks detect concurrent writes; they do not lock the tables: the SDK provides no lookup versionAsOf argument. Keep those tables stable during training/scoring. Nullable integer/Boolean transport needing the post-lookup encoder is not admitted by this adapter. Driver training limits still apply even though lookup and batch scoring use Spark.

Preparation records the base Delta version and every feature table's ID/version, then validates actual null/duplicate keys and matching key/timestamp types before SDK joins. Splitting retains record/time/weight metadata, which is excluded from the logged model's inputs. Separate tasks reconstruct native TrainingSet lineage from the same frozen declaration; scoring reuses fitted preprocessing. Single-model and competition winners retain that lineage. A set combines only compatible component lookups: conflicting versions, key/time semantics or direct/fetched input meanings fail. Scoring validates the complete package, exact named prediction schema and record-key/cardinality preservation. Spark batch monitoring reconstructs the scored keys' feature values using the same saved lookup evidence; native-feature monitoring supports Spark batch only. Keep feature tables stable during monitoring as well as training/scoring.

The library's optional feature-store extra requires SDK 0.18.1 or later within major version zero; the chosen runtime must support that SDK. Match active MLflow tracking/registry URIs to the project's explicit URIs before native scoring. The SDK downloads the concrete model URI in that context; aliases resolve first. For distributed estimator admission, worker budgets and declarative weighted composition, see distributed scoring.

For latest-value endpoint lookup, follow online feature setup. That path adds explicit required-feature/freshness guards, publication into an existing online store and endpoint admission. Current generated online policy transport supports pandas single-model/competition training and non-temporal lookup; it is not a historical asof endpoint or a multi-target online flow.

docs.title: Common errors and fixes
docs.text:
Symptom Check and fix No features job after init Empty groups deliberately disables it. Configure groups and run refresh_feature_graph. Graph digest mismatch Refresh locally after configuration changes, then redeploy matching resources. Feature key/timestamp not unique Correct the producer's grain; do not silently discard observations to make a join pass. Missing observation match Check exact/asof choice, dates and key types. Set allow_missing only if null features are acceptable. Feature column overlaps base/group Give each output feature one owner or rename it explicitly upstream. Scoring rejects observed_at as a record key Keep date/time for feature joins; use the stable BIGINT observation_id for scoring. Updated feature rows make scoring fail Ordinary single-model scoring rejects source updates/deletes; review correction/rebuild behavior before publishing changed historical inputs. A saved model cannot import a group function Groups are upstream code, excluded from the model recipe snapshot. Move model callbacks to the captured phase/custom modules.

Platform details: point-in-time lookup, task dependencies, repairing tasks, Delta upserts, and Feature Engineering compatibility.

docs.title: Databricks project glossary
docs.text: Use these meanings when reading the project walkthrough. The file/action column tells you where to make a decision or inspect its evidence in a generated project. Configuration names describe this checkout; use the matching Core release/build for your project revision.

docs.title: Data and preprocessing
docs.text:
Term Plain meaning File or action Record key Stable columns identifying a source record and its published result. These are data identity, not a DataFrame's temporary row index. Set record_key_columns in config/training.yml; verify uniqueness in the source. Target / label The actual outcome the estimator learns to predict, such as observed revenue or whether a customer churned. A prediction is not an actual label. Set target_column in config/training.yml; maintain real outcomes upstream. Pre-split Fixed edits and eligibility filters applied before dividing labeled rows into training and holdout populations. They must not learn values from the complete dataset. Select pre_split_recipe from config/pre_split.yml; decide target-filter reuse in config/scoring.yml before preview. Fitted preprocessing Transformations whose learned state, such as imputation means or scaling statistics, is fitted on training rows and reused for evaluation and prediction. Define recipes in config/preprocessing.yml, select preprocessing_recipe in training.yml, then train a new version after edits. Holdout Rows reserved from model fitting for the final evaluation. They are distinct from the validation folds used during tuning. Set split/window fields in config/training.yml; inspect the saved split membership and held-out metrics in training_report. Cross-validation (CV) Repeated train/validation splits within the training population, used to estimate or select model settings. It does not replace the final holdout. Set cv_enabled, cv_type and related fields in config/training.yml; inspect saved fold reports. Training window The source time range eligible for a training run, before the final holdout boundary and other eligibility rules are applied. Set training_window_mode, event/date parsing and window fields in config/training.yml. Observation window The prediction or request-time interval measured by monitoring. A completed performance window may wait for actual outcomes before assessment. Set window_hours and label_delay_hours in monitoring_performance_policies; inspect monitoring reports. This differs from the training window and the job schedule. Recipe A named, ordered list of steps in config/pre_split.yml or config/preprocessing.yml. Only the selected recipe runs. Select pre_split_recipe and preprocessing_recipe in config/training.yml. See the recipe catalog. Preprocessing probe An optional check that replays the saved preprocessing on up to 256 holdout rows, whole, repeated, in chunks and reversed. It does not refit or block promotion. Set save_preprocessing_diagnostics: true; read preprocessing diagnostics. Row, group, window and global context What a step needs at prediction time: one row and saved state (row), all rows of a group (group), ordered earlier rows (window) or the whole batch (global). Read what context means. Outcome availability When a real label became available for use. This can be later than the underlying event or prediction. Configure result_available_at_column and cutoff rules for training; configure monitoring_result_available_at_column for monitoring labels.

Read the recipe catalog, training field reference and context-dependent preprocessing guide. For the target-reading filter error, see troubleshooting.

docs.title: Model lifecycle and scoring
docs.text:
Term Plain meaning File or action Candidate A fitted, registered model version with saved evaluation evidence. Registration alone does not make it active. Run the train job, then inspect training_report and its concrete version. Champion The active model version selected through the lifecycle's champion alias. The alias can move; the concrete version identifies one saved artifact. Use the approved activation action and inspect its receipt. score_model_selection: champion resolves the active version for scoring. Challenger A candidate staged for comparison or an approval decision. Its existence does not route production requests or replace the champion. Inspect the challenger alias and saved candidate report; use approve/reject according to policy. Alias A named pointer such as champion or challenger to a registered version. It is mutable, unlike a concrete version number. Inspect registry aliases and lifecycle receipts. Use score_model_selection: pinned_version with model_version when a fixed score version is required. Promotion / activation A guarded decision to make a candidate active. A passing training task or deployment alone is insufficient. Set promotion_policy, metric and quality thresholds in config/training.yml; inspect the activation receipt. Competition Several estimators compete for one target under shared data, split and selection rules. Only the activated winner becomes the production model. Use training_layout: model_competition and candidate entries in config/training.yml. Model set / multi-target One coordinated release containing independent models for several targets, such as revenue and cost. It is not a competition for one winner. Use training_layout: multi_target; define branches in config/training.yml, and set activation/publication policy in config/inference.yml. See model sets and its replacement rule. Scoring eligibility Rules determining whether an input receives a prediction. Excluded rows remain in the result with their status and reason. Configure mode, target-step skipping and rules in config/scoring.yml before fitting the version. Publication Committing predictions and their metadata to the output Delta table, optionally exposing selected model-set views. This does not promote a registry version. Set output and publication policy in config/inference.yml; inspect the score task and committed output. Change Data Feed (CDF) Delta's record of source inserts, updates and deletes over retained versions. Incremental scoring uses it to discover source changes after a saved checkpoint. Enable CDF on the configured source upstream. Ordinary single/competition scoring accepts inserts; only model sets expose model_set.on_source_change in config/inference.yml for readable corrections. Use the documented recovery action if required history expires. Full rebuild Recompute the configured prediction population under the selected model rather than only processing changes since a checkpoint. Review model/source change policy and the explicit recovery action in config/inference.yml; inspect the resulting output generation. Expected champion and none The champion version an operator action expects to replace. The action fails if the alias moved. none means no champion exists yet. Copy it from the report's next actions. See operator actions. previous_champion / previous_challenger History aliases. Promotion moves the old champion to previous_champion; a new candidate moves the displaced challenger to previous_challenger. Inspect registry aliases. See challenger history. next_actions Ready-to-copy parameters in the training report for the next approve, reject or rollback run. Open training_report > Output. See operator actions. lifecycle_action The train job's Run now parameter: train, approve, reject or rollback. Only train fits a model. Set it with Run now with different parameters. See operator actions. Comparison digest A SHA-256 hash of the reviewed candidate, data, metric policy and expected champion. Approval checks it instead of reevaluating. Usually resolved from the candidate's saved evidence. See approve without training. Promotion receipt The saved record of a completed alias change. Rollback needs it to restore the prior champion. Copy promotion_receipt_json from the report. See reject or roll back. Prediction receipt The saved record of a committed scoring write: source identity, versions and output. Recovery reads it before any retry. Inspect the score task output. See scoring. Watermark The last committed source Delta version. The next score run reads changes after it. Never edit it by hand. See how new rows are discovered. Batch follow_champion Whether a successful champion change starts the score job (true) or not (false). It is fixed at deployment. Set it in config/inference.yml, then redeploy. See operator actions. Serving follow_champion Whether a successful champion change starts the serving endpoint job, in shared and personal development targets alike (true) or leaves it to a manual run (false). It is read from YAML at run time. Set serving_endpoint.follow_champion in config/serving.yml and deploy the updated file; no job-parameter change is needed. See the serving job. Handoff A saved request from one job to another, such as activation requesting scoring or serving, or scoring requesting monitoring. It carries concrete evidence rather than leaving the child to guess the current alias. Set the relevant follow_champion in config/inference.yml or config/serving.yml; follow the native child job in the run graph.

Read registry actions, scoring and recovery and training policy fields.

docs.title: Features and online requests
docs.text:
Term Plain meaning File or action Feature group An optional upstream job unit that reads one source, runs the configured transform, and writes its own feature output table. Add a group in config/features.yml and its transform under src/features/groups/; refresh the feature graph, deploy and run the feature job. Merged table The optional output obtained by joining the configured base table with feature-group outputs using declared keys and timestamp rules. It is a source for training/scoring only when you select it. Configure the merge in config/features.yml, then point training_table and score_source_table to its output. Empty groups: {} creates neither a feature job nor a merged table. Feature lookup Retrieval of explicitly named features from a Unity Catalog feature table by entity keys and optional time rules. It is separate from the template's feature-group merge job. Configure feature_lookup in config/training.yml; verify key/feature metadata and input columns. Point-in-time lookup A lookup that selects historical features according to each observation's timestamp and configured lookback, avoiding the use of later values. Configure timestamp lookup settings in feature_lookup; inspect saved training lookup/snapshot evidence. Online publication / synchronization Copying eligible feature data into the configured online feature service so an endpoint can retrieve it. Publishing features does not train a model or deploy an endpoint. Configure and run the optional publication/sync steps in the online feature guide and generated SERVING.md. Online lookup A live entity-key lookup made while handling a prediction request. Missing or stale required features can reject the request. Configure the model's online_features required columns/freshness rules and the serving feature lookup contract. Inspect the endpoint response and logs. Pinned endpoint A serving endpoint tied to a concrete registered model version and inspected input/output contract. Use the pinned serving helpers and generated SERVING.md; keep the endpoint, version and inference-log identity together. Rollout A separate, guarded process controlling serving traffic or stage progression. A champion alias update alone does not establish that traffic changed. Configure the optional config/serving.yml rollout and inspect saved health/decision evidence.

Read feature groups and merged tables, online features and serving rollout.

docs.title: Runtime, engine and operations
docs.text:
Term Plain meaning File or action Engine The DataFrame execution implementation selected for fitted Core preprocessing, such as pandas or Polars. It is not a package version or cluster size. Set engine in config/training.yml; follow the supported engine/route combinations in the inference reference. Runtime The installed Python, Skyulf and dependency environment required to load and execute a saved artifact. A different engine or compute target does not make incompatible dependencies safe. Inspect deployment/*requirements.txt, the saved artifact manifest and job environment. Install the matching release/build. Inference mode The route that applies a saved model, such as local scoring or the supported Spark UDF route. Spark inference does not turn training into Spark-native fitting. Set batch_compute and Spark UDF options in config/inference.yml; verify the selected artifact's support boundary. Admission / certified package Spark workers score only a saved MLflow package with a safety certificate. Admission rechecks it and rejects unsupported steps. Log a new certified version if admission fails. See distributed inference. workflow_contract A version marker on the generated job tasks. The runtime rejects a deployed graph and project that disagree. Deploy the matching files together. See project upgrade. Production-mode target The shared test, syst and prod targets. Only they enroll models in the shared monitoring store; development targets can opt in to their own separate store. Select the target with -t. See deployment. Monitoring enrollment The shared inventory entry binding a project/model/version to its prediction evidence, labels and policy. It is separate from a dashboard display. Inspect activation register_monitor and the score-to-monitor handoff; configure monitoring target variables. Dashboard refresh Rerunning the dashboard's published datasets over saved monitoring evidence. It neither computes a new observation nor retrains the model. Configure the native refresh task per target in deployment/monitoring.yml; inspect the monitoring job separately. Drift A measured change in feature distributions or declared schema checks. It is not automatically a loss in predictive quality. Inspect the saved monitoring report and drift thresholds; enable guarded retraining separately if desired. Performance degradation A measured worsening against a matching baseline under an explicit metric, tolerance, window and label-coverage policy. Missing labels are unavailable evidence. Configure monitoring_performance_policies; read the saved window and baseline evidence before interpreting its verdict.

Read inference artifacts and runtime checks, Spark execution boundaries and the monitoring overview.

docs.title: Approve, reject and roll back model versions
When you need it
docs.text:
A registered candidate is not automatically the production champion. Use the serialized train job to apply the saved quality policy and record an operator decision. Daily serving traffic rollout is a separate endpoint operation.

flowchart LR
    A["Train and evaluate"] --> B["Registered challenger"]
    B --> C["training_report: available actions"]
    C --> D["Approve: quality gates pass"]
    C --> E["Reject: retain decision evidence"]
    D --> F["Champion and promotion receipt"]
    F --> G["Optional rollback to prior champion"]

This shows manual approval. Automatic policy applies the same saved quality gates without an operator approval run. First-champion initialization has no prior champion to restore.

docs.title: Independent scoring and promotion policies
docs.text:
Generated Bundles and direct run_action callers separate these decisions:

score_model_selection promotion_policy Behavior pinned_version manual_approval Register/evaluate the contender; score keeps the configured version pinned_version automatic Apply promotion gates; score still keeps the configured version champion manual_approval Register/evaluate the contender; score follows the existing champion champion automatic Apply promotion gates; the next score follows the resulting champion

For example, a library configuration containing model_version: "2", score_model_selection: "pinned_version" and promotion_policy: "automatic" continues scoring with v2 after a successful promotion of v4. Selecting champion instead resolves the controlled alias once per score run. A missing champion fails before output preparation; there is no fallback to latest.

Set both fields together; a partial configuration fails before training or scoring. Generated projects also require follow_champion. Automatic promotion requires quality_threshold, including when scoring is pinned. Scoring never updates the caller's configured version. Moving from the single model_selection_mode field is covered in project upgrades.

docs.title: Additional quality gates
docs.text:
Keep one selection metric. Optionally add quality_gates directly to config/training.yml defaults; no extra initializer question is needed. For example, merge these regression policy fields into your existing configuration:

{
  "metric": "heldout_rmse",
  "quality_threshold": 5.0,
  "min_improvement": 0.2,
  "quality_gates": {"heldout_mae": 3.0, "heldout_r2": 0.7}
}

These illustrative bounds require RMSE <= 5, MAE <= 3 and R2 >= 0.7. Choose bounds appropriate to your target's units and business requirements; generated projects keep the quality threshold unset. Every bound must pass. For later champions, RMSE must additionally improve by at least 0.2 absolute units on the same holdout. A tie never qualifies, even with minimum improvement 0. The first champion still needs an explicit selection-metric quality threshold.

For classification, a policy might select heldout_f1 with threshold 0.8 and add {"heldout_recall": 0.9, "heldout_log_loss": 0.5}. Classification score bounds are in [0, 1], except Matthews correlation [-1, 1]; error/loss bounds are nonnegative, while R2/explained variance may be negative but cannot exceed 1. The existing metric definition determines whether a lower or higher value wins. Use weighted metrics for multiclass models. An unavailable metric, such as binary ROC AUC on a one-class holdout, fails its gate; it is never silently ignored. These bounds do not set classification probability decision thresholds or tune them.

The comparison/final notebook reports show each bound, observed value and failure reason. MLflow retains the policy in candidate_comparison.json, all gate outcomes in quality_gates.json, and per-gate version tags. Version tags identify their event; use quality_gate_event to distinguish current gates from retained older outcomes. Approval requires the saved policy unchanged and re-evaluates it before changing aliases. Omitting quality_gates preserves the single-gate policy and historical receipt digests. SDK callers should use the returned comparison_sha256; when explicitly serializing a report for evidence, use comparison_payload/comparison_digest from skyulf.integrations.mlflow.lifecycle.validation instead of hashing dataclasses.asdict.

In both modes, registration nominates @challenger before comparison. A tied or worse candidate retains that alias with validation_status=rejected and a reason; comparison errors retain it with validation_status=error. New contenders replace the pointer without deleting earlier version evidence. Manual approval records these results without automatically promoting the candidate. Training resolves the current champion; a stale explicit champion_version fails before fit. Generic Core training remains alias-free unless a caller supplies the explicit on_registered lifecycle callback.

docs.title: Models that exclude rows
docs.text:
Fitted outlier steps (IQR, ZScore, EllipticEnvelope, ManualBounds) and PowerTransformer can leave a holdout row without a prediction (see rows that are not scored). For such a model, training computes every metric on the scored rows only and records how many rows that is:

Metric Meaning heldout_total_rows Holdout rows given to the model heldout_scored_rows Rows that received a prediction heldout_excluded_rows Rows excluded by an outlier or invalid-value step heldout_scored_fraction heldout_scored_rows / heldout_total_rows

A model that skips difficult rows can look better than it is, so two coverage rules apply by default. Both are policy fields in config/training.yml, next to min_improvement:

min_scored_fraction: 0.90   # null turns this rule off
max_coverage_drop: 0.05     # 0.05 = five percentage points; null turns it off
  1. Minimum coverage (min_scored_fraction). At least this fraction of the holdout rows must be scored. A candidate below it is rejected, even if its metrics pass. The default is 0.90.
  2. No large drop against the champion (max_coverage_drop). The candidate's coverage may be at most this much lower than the champion's. With a champion at 99% coverage and the default 0.05, a candidate at 96% can be compared, but one at 93% is rejected even though it passes the 90% rule.

Both values accept a number from 0 to 1, or null to turn the rule off. They sit wherever min_improvement is set: once for a single model or a competition, and separately for each multi-target branch. Generation writes the defaults; to change them before generation, put min_scored_fraction and max_coverage_drop (or branch_N_min_scored_fraction and branch_N_max_coverage_drop for branch N) in the answer file. The setup wizard does not ask for them. A quality_gates entry for heldout_scored_fraction remains possible as an additional bound; the stricter of the two applies. Models without an excluding step always score 100% of the rows, so these rules never reject them.

When both rules pass, the candidate and the champion are compared on the holdout rows that both scored. Refitted outlier bounds move slightly with every retraining, so the two models rarely exclude exactly the same rows; comparing only the shared rows keeps the comparison fair. Each model's own coverage is checked separately against the two rules above, never on the shared rows. A model without any excluding step has a coverage of 100%, so replacing it with one that excludes rows is limited by the same 5-point margin.

Training runs and model versions share readable metadata: train_data_version, test_data_version, train_data_destination, test_data_destination, model_type, candidate_date_tag, and engine. Optional risk_category is editable in config/training.yml defaults. Since fit and evaluation split one Delta snapshot, their table names and versions match; train_start, test_start, and data_end explain the split. The exact dataset identity is saved in training_data.json. Run tags use task=training.

Validation reasons use plain English. Technical event tags retain unique IDs and evidence hashes for rollback/recovery; their JSON fields are action, from_version, proof, parent, state, and previous. from_version identifies the version previously held by the affected alias, not necessarily the previous champion. These are audit records, not settings to edit. Earlier compact receipts remain supported.

docs.title: Set quality and activation
docs.text: A multi_target project approves, rejects and rolls back the complete model set, not one component. The set has its own promotion_policy in config/inference.yml > model_set; branch policies stay manual. A replacement set needs every branch to pass its absolute gates, no branch to regress and at least one branch to improve by its min_improvement. The model set guide owns the rule, the set aliases and set scoring.

docs.title: Operator actions through Run now
docs.text:
The existing train job is the serialized lifecycle writer. Use this same procedure for a single model, the competition winner or a complete model set. A model set shows the same blocks in training_report > Output; its candidate_version is the set version.

  1. Open Workflows > Jobs > your project's train job > the finished run > training_report > Output. Review the comparison and decision first.
  2. Find Available action: approve, Available action: reject, or If rollback is needed. For rollback, expand Show parameters only if you want to roll back. Copy the displayed parameter values, including the complete promotion_receipt_json when present.
  3. On the same train job, choose Run now with different parameters (called Run with different settings in the report). Set the listed lifecycle_action and evidence values. Clear unrelated operator fields; for reject, enter your own rejection_reason. Leave the other job parameters empty; the five lifecycle fields are the only job parameters.
  4. Open the new run's training_report > Output to inspect the action result, receipt and any next action. A failed gate or stale champion stops the action; starting an approval run does not guarantee promotion.

For reference, these are the fields the report provides:

Action Required job parameters train No operator evidence; leave other parameters empty approve candidate_version, expected_champion_version; comparison proof resolves automatically reject Same as approve, plus rejection_reason rollback promotion_receipt_json, expected_champion_version approve over an unloadable champion As approve, plus allow_unloadable_champion=true; only when the report offers it

For a single model or competition winner, manual training returns copyable next_actions.approve and next_actions.reject fields. A model set's next_actions field is a list of sentences; copy its values from the report blocks. Review the comparison and copy its exact values; add a reason for rejection. expected_champion_version=none explicitly selects first-champion initialization; an empty value fails. Configure the metric and absolute quality threshold before training so saved evidence matches the approval policy. A completed single-model promotion returns next_actions.rollback, including its complete receipt JSON; a set shows it in the rollback block. Copy that receipt rather than reconstructing it from alias names. These operator actions reuse the existing candidate; they do not fit a model.

For rollback, Required current champion and expected_champion_version are a safety check: the alias must still point to that version. Restore version is the prior version recorded inside the promotion receipt. For example, a receipt for v2 -> v4 expects current champion v4 and restores v2. Do not put v2 in expected_champion_version.

docs.title: Champion from an older Core release
docs.text:
A saved model loads only under the exact runtime that produced it (Skyulf Core, scikit-learn, numpy, pandas and the other pinned packages). After a Core upgrade the comparison cannot score the old champion, so it reports reason: champion_runtime_unavailable instead of failing. Automatic promotion holds, and the report shows an approve block with allow_unloadable_champion: true and the warning The champion was not compared.

Run the train job with those values only after reviewing the candidate's own metrics. The override is accepted only for approve, only as the exact value true, only while the champion still cannot be loaded, and only when the candidate passes a configured quality_threshold and any quality_gates. The saved comparison records that the champion was not measured. It works under either promotion policy. Model sets support the same explicit approval path; every candidate component must pass its own absolute quality gates. See Upgrading Core with model sets for the retained component versions and rollback requirements.

For a single model, rolling back to a champion from the older release restores its alias, but the current score job cannot load it; keep that release's runtime if you need it.

Batch follow_champion is a deploy-time setting in config/inference.yml, not a Run now parameter. Changing it needs the matching deployed job parameters and a redeploy; see schedules and handoff. true requests the existing score job after a successful initialization, promotion or rollback. false leaves scoring to an explicit score run or its schedule. Rejection and training without a champion transition never trigger score. Handoff preserves the score selector: a pinned scorer still uses its configured version even after champion changes.

The project has separate train, score and monitoring jobs. The train graph runs the lifecycle phases, then scoring_requested checks the verified handoff and run_batch_scoring conditionally invokes the score job. Train and score queue runs with max_concurrent_runs: 1. Score's fixed notebook role ignores inherited lifecycle parameters and cannot dispatch alias actions; this is input isolation, not a replacement for exclusive registry write permissions. A failed/uncertain alias action never publishes a successful score request. If the alias change succeeded but score failed, retry score directly; no retraining is needed.

The score entrypoint filters inherited parent-job evidence before dispatching score. Validate permissions and compute dependencies in each deployment target.

docs.title: Approve an existing candidate without training
docs.text:
Use an explicit manual policy and the comparison returned by the earlier training job. Review that saved result before passing its version and digest:

from skyulf.integrations.databricks.lifecycle.workflow import run_action

# candidate is the result of an earlier training job; no training runs here.
comparison_sha256 = candidate.comparison_sha256
receipt = run_action(
    spark,
    config,  # promotion_policy="manual_approval" and both independent fields
    "approve",
    candidate_version=candidate.model_version,
    comparison_sha256=comparison_sha256,
    expected_champion_version=candidate.comparison.champion_version,
)

Approval downloads candidate_comparison.json and candidate_training_spec.json from the run associated with that registered version. It verifies the digest, current metric policy, expected champion and controlled challenger receipt. It then reads the original Delta version and evaluation window and rechecks quality using the existing Core comparison/promotion services. The original engine is preserved; current read budgets may tighten the saved limits.

The action does not train, register or upload a model, rewrite model_version, or publish predictions. A later score run follows the configured selector. Retrying an unchanged successful approval returns its original committed receipt; changed champion, pending writes or incompatible evidence fail. A training run without a saved candidate_training_spec.json cannot be approved this way; there is no fallback to current training dates. Use the same externally serialized lifecycle writer as training. The Bundle train job provides that path; its score handoff follows the deployed setting.

docs.title: Reject a candidate or roll back a promotion
docs.text:
To decline the candidate above, use the same version and evidence digest with an explicit manual policy. This is an alternative to approving that candidate:

decision = run_action(
    spark,
    config,
    "reject",
    candidate_version=candidate.model_version,
    comparison_sha256=comparison_sha256,
    expected_champion_version=candidate.comparison.champion_version,
    rejection_reason="Business review requires another candidate",
)

Rejection retains both aliases and the evaluation metrics/status. It records approval_status=rejected and the human-readable approval_reason separately. The reason must be nonempty and at most 256 UTF-8 bytes. A rejected version cannot be implicitly approved, restaged, renominated or made the first champion. There is no reopen action; a later training run creates a new candidate. Neither rejection nor rollback reads training rows, fits or registers a model.

To undo an earlier completed promotion, pass that promotion's receipt:

reversal = run_action(
    spark,
    config,
    "rollback",
    promotion_receipt=receipt,  # kind="promotion", not first-champion initialization
    expected_champion_version=receipt.new_version,
)

Rollback is available under either promotion policy. It restores the previous champion only when the saved transition still matches controlled registry state. A separately verified challenger is retained. Repeating an unchanged rejection or rollback returns the same committed receipt; incompatible evidence, conflicting alias state and unresolved writes stop the action.

All lifecycle actions must use the same externally serialized writer as training. No additional control table is created. Direct run_action calls do not launch score or rewrite its version pin; the Bundle adapter can request score afterward. A later champion score follows the restored alias; a pinned_version score continues using its configured version. Rollback does not undo predictions already written; scoring's model-change policy still applies.

docs.title: Recent challenger history
docs.text:
The Core lifecycle keeps the last displaced contender as previous_challenger:

Action Champion Challenger Previous challenger Starting state v2 v3 unset Nominate v4 v2 v4 v3 Repeat nomination of v4 v2 v4 v3 Promote v4 v4 unset v3

Only replacing an existing contender rotates this pointer. Evaluation and promotion retain it, and promotion still puts the old champion in previous_champion. If the historical version becomes champion through rollback, or becomes challenger again, its history alias is cleared. The version and its earlier event records remain available.

This alias is neither a complete history nor a scoring fallback. It creates no table or job. History changes share the lifecycle's pending-event checks and writer ownership; manual alias/receipt disagreement stops further actions, including retries. Partial writes require reconciliation before proceeding.

With score_model_selection=champion, score resolves the alias once to a concrete version per run, under either promotion policy. Only the serialized train job identity may write this model's aliases; other alias-write grants must be removed before training. Alias promotion and Delta scoring are separate transactions. If scoring fails after promotion, the last successful prediction output remains and the score job must be retried. Unknown alias outcomes need receipt reconciliation. Skyulf marks an alias transition as pending before writing it; automatic training and scoring stop until that pending event is reconciled. An existing champion alias set outside this controlled lifecycle also needs reconciliation before controlled champion scoring or promotion can use it. For a failed controlled operation, use the alias recovery procedure with the original destination version, pending event ID and shared admission. It completes fully applied changes or aborts untouched changes; mixed roles remain blocked for operator inspection. It does not change serving traffic or prediction tables, and it cannot adopt an uncontrolled alias automatically.

For example, a regression project using legacy workflow.json can select its gate with these internal field names:

{
  "engine": "polars",
  "score_model_selection": "champion",
  "promotion_policy": "automatic",
  "score_handoff": "after_alias_change",
  "metric": "heldout_rmse",
  "min_improvement": 0.1,
  "quality_threshold": 5.0,
  "model_change_mode": "incremental_append"
}

These example values mean RMSE must be at most 5.0; a later candidate must reduce champion's RMSE by at least 0.1 on the same holdout. Improvement is an absolute metric difference, not a percentage. Skyulf derives the direction from the metric: RMSE/MAE/log loss are minimized, while R-squared/accuracy/F1 are maximized. Use a metric supported by the configured model task. The first comparison reports reason=no_champion and eligible=false because no baseline exists; successful bootstrap is recorded separately as result.alias_change.kind=initial in the Bundle output after the absolute gate passes.

If promotion succeeds but scoring fails, the train job reports a failed dependent score task. Correct the scoring problem and run score again; retraining is unnecessary. Full-rebuild output continues to expose the last successfully activated generation during this recovery.

docs.title: Common errors and fixes
docs.text:
Symptom Fix First approval lacks a quality threshold Set an absolute bound before training; saved policy cannot be replaced by editing YAML afterwards. Champion changed since review Inspect a fresh comparison; the expected champion must match current controlled state. Alias write outcome is uncertain Reconcile the original pending event before another lifecycle action. Promotion succeeded but scoring failed Correct and retry score; no new training is required. A rejected candidate cannot be approved Train a new candidate; rejection is not a temporary hold.

Direct SDK snippets above assume existing spark, validated config and the returned training candidate. Use its returned comparison digest; a generic dataclass hash can differ from the saved canonical evidence.

docs.title: Recover an interrupted model alias operation
When you need it
docs.text:
Looking for a normal rollback after a completed promotion? Follow the training_report and Run now steps.

An AliasOutcomeUnknownError or a pending alias event means a registry write may have succeeded before its response was received. Further controlled training, promotion and champion scoring can remain blocked until that event is reconciled. This procedure concerns registry aliases; a failed score or dashboard refresh after a confirmed promotion does not by itself require alias recovery.

flowchart LR
    A["Stop every alias writer"] --> B["reconcile_alias_change"]
    B --> C["Read all four roles and saved intent"]
    C --> D["committed: finish metadata"]
    C --> E["aborted: nothing changed"]
    C --> F["AliasConflictError: inspect"]

docs.title: What to edit
docs.text:
First stop every job and manual operation that can write the model's aliases. Confirm the original run has terminated and cannot retry. Preserve its inputs, logs, model/version tags and all four role assignments: champion, challenger, previous_champion, previous_challenger.

Obtain the original destination version and event ID from the failed operation's logs, pending_alias_event and promotion_<event_id>. New operations save their intent in alias_intent plus numbered chunks before publishing the pending marker. Run recovery with the same Skyulf Core version as the jobs that wrote the intent. Use the same admission authority as the original writers; do not invent a new lock or clear the pending marker just to make a job run.

docs.title: The command
docs.text:
The MLflow registry recovery procedure contains the SDK call with its required admission, destination version and event ID. Run that call from an authorized operator environment while writers remain stopped. There is no Bundle lifecycle_action=recover convenience action. The recovery API validates observed state against the saved intent; it does not set or delete aliases for you.

For a normal candidate decision whose outcome is known, use the train job's approve/reject/rollback actions. Do not substitute rollback for reconciliation of an unknown outcome.

docs.title: What you should see
docs.text:
Result Meaning Next step committed Intended role changes already exist; metadata is completed and verified, then this pending marker is cleared. Read the controlled champion and resume the appropriate downstream operation. aborted Roles and owned metadata still match their starting values; no promotion is completed. Review and retry the original business operation with fresh checks if still wanted. AliasConflictError Mixed roles, unexpected changes or contradictory metadata prevent automatic reconciliation. Keep writers stopped and inspect the complete intent and observed state.

An unchanged retry of an already completed repair returns the same outcome. Unchanged aliases alone do not prove completion of metadata-only actions such as rejection. Recovery does not undo prediction rows, endpoint traffic or tables.

docs.title: Common errors and fixes
docs.text:
Symptom Fix Another writer still owns admission Verify that exact owner's run state; follow the registry guide's conditional recovery procedure. Never release a different owner's claim. Only some roles changed Compare every role and marker with the saved plan under exclusive operator control; follow the documented manual procedure before retrying reconciliation. Alias intent digest differs from its stored chunks and the alias_intent manifest shows "encoding":"json-framed-v1" The operator environment runs an older Core that cannot read framed chunks. This is a version mismatch, not corruption. Install the writers' Core version and retry. An old event has no complete intent Automatic recovery is unavailable. Restore from verified original evidence with the platform owner; keep the model blocked if that evidence is insufficient. An old intent was replaced by a newer operation The latest snapshot cannot repair the earlier event. Use the original durable evidence. A tag budget error occurs Preserve current control receipts and pending evidence; review the registry guide before retiring obsolete audit tags.

Return to model lifecycle decisions only after reading back a consistent controlled state.

docs.title: Databricks model catalog
docs.text:
Choose a model by its behavior, then copy one of its models: entries into config/training.yml. This catalog covers all 16 regression and 18 classification choices in the project wizard, including voting and stacking.

Keep the surrounding version: 1, defaults: and your existing data, target, validation and layout settings from the training reference. Each example below replaces the models: mapping; do not concatenate the tuned and untuned mappings. In a competition, give candidates distinct names. In a multi-target project, retain each branch's target and feature settings.

The untuned example fixes the estimator configuration. The tuned example uses a deliberately small explicit grid to demonstrate valid YAML; it is not the full automatic search space. Validation/CV comes from defaults, not from a tuning.cv field. Read search strategies and ensembles for all strategy fields, nested CV, budgets, member parameters and wizard questions.

docs.title: Reading defaults and search spaces
docs.text:
The parameter tables are generated from the same Core hyperparameter registry used by the wizard's build_model_spaces.py. They show key supported controls, not every parameter accepted by an upstream estimator. Core catalog default is the registered control value, not a promise about an omitted YAML field. The adjacent column is generated from the calculator's actual constructor settings. Library/resolver means the calculator delegates that default to the installed estimator or its composite resolver. For example, Logistic Regression registers max_iter=100 in the catalog but an omitted YAML value runs with Core's max_iter=1000. Random Forest has similar explicit Core overrides. Supply a parameter explicitly when reproducing a catalog setting matters. Core also injects its deterministic seed into compatible estimators when no seed is given.

Table literals use JSON notation (null, true, false); the explicit constructor column preserves Python source (None, True, False). Use YAML null, true, false in configuration. A table's default does not imply that all combinations of its controls are valid; solver/penalty pairs and estimator capabilities are still checked.

Grid and halving-grid use the compact grid column. Random, halving-random and Optuna use the richer finite-choice column when the wizard supplies its automatic space. The wizard writes these axes into the generated configuration. A missing or empty YAML search_space also asks the runtime to derive the Core space for the selected model, respecting its fixed parameters and ensemble members. For halving, the default resource is n_samples; a resource parameter cannot also appear in its search space. The strategy guide explains minimum/maximum resources and how to limit the full Cartesian grid. Large automatic grids, especially ensembles with several members, can exceed max_candidates before fitting. Use a bounded explicit space such as the examples below, or a random strategy with an explicit trial budget.

docs.title: Weights, optional packages and execution boundaries
docs.text:
weight_column is a training workflow setting, not a constructor parameter. The column is removed from model features; weights must be finite, nonnegative, and have a positive sum in every fitted fold. Neighbor models do not accept row weights. Ensembles require every selected base model and the final estimator to support them. Metrics and threshold selection remain unweighted. An ensemble's weights controls member averaging and is a separate concept.

Every card's Spark/serving note describes the current admission policy, not proof that a particular saved artifact will pass it. Training these estimators uses local pandas/Polars data within the configured row/byte bounds; choosing Spark inference does not turn fitting into Spark ML training. Spark worker and pinned serving admission inspect a complete pandas-fitted artifact, exact model classes, preprocessing, schemas, runtime and saved state. An otherwise eligible model can still be rejected by its preprocessing or custom scoring rules. See Spark execution and serving rollout.

Optional XGBoost/LightGBM packages must be installed in training and inference environments. Installing a package does not extend the admission allowlist. Local fit/predict examples do not establish Spark, REST, or ai_query acceptance.

docs.title: ridge_regression
docs.text:
Ridge regression. Task: regression. A linear baseline with L2 shrinkage, useful when numeric predictors are correlated or there are many modest signals. Scale numeric features before comparing alpha values.

Sample weights: Yes; configure the workflow weight_column.

Optional package: None beyond the standard Core scikit-learn runtime.

Spark workers / serving: Not admitted by the current Spark-worker/pinned-serving model allowlist; use local inference.

docs.title: Parameters and defaults
docs.text: Parameter Core catalog default Explicit Core constructor default Meaning alpha 1.0 1.0 Regularization strength; must be a positive float. solver "auto" 'auto' Solver to use in the computational routines. fit_intercept true Library/resolver Whether to calculate the intercept for this model. random_state 42 Library/resolver Seed used by the stochastic sag/saga solvers.

docs.title: Default search spaces
docs.text:
Axis Grid / halving_grid Random / halving_random / Optuna alpha [0.01, 0.1, 1.0, 10.0, 100.0] [0.01, 0.1, 1.0, 10.0, 100.0] fit_intercept [true, false] [true, false] max_iter [2000] [1000, 2000, 5000] solver ["auto", "saga"] ["auto", "svd", "cholesky", "lsqr", "sparse_cg", "sag", "saga"]

Halving resource: n_samples (the wizard default). This model has no top-level n_estimators resource. Use n_samples in the wizard; another estimator parameter needs an explicit compatible configuration.

docs.title: Minimal training entries
docs.text:
Untuned:

models:
  candidate:
    model:
      type: ridge_regression
      params: {}

Tuned (small explicit grid):

models:
  candidate:
    model:
      type: ridge_regression
      params: {}
    tuning:
      strategy: grid
      metric: r2
      max_candidates: 4
      search_space:
        alpha: [0.01, 0.1]

Common mistake: Assuming the same alpha has the same effect before and after feature scaling.

docs.title: linear_regression
docs.text:
Ordinary least squares. Task: regression. A transparent baseline when a numeric target changes approximately linearly with the features. Coefficients are useful for understanding direction, provided the features have meaningful units.

Sample weights: Yes; configure the workflow weight_column.

Optional package: None beyond the standard Core scikit-learn runtime.

Spark workers / serving: Eligible exact model family, subject to complete artifact admission.

docs.title: Parameters and defaults
docs.text: Parameter Core catalog default Explicit Core constructor default Meaning fit_intercept true True Whether to calculate the intercept for this model. copy_X Not a catalog control True Core constructor setting. n_jobs Not a catalog control -1 Core constructor setting.

docs.title: Default search spaces
docs.text:
Axis Grid / halving_grid Random / halving_random / Optuna fit_intercept [true, false] [true, false]

Halving resource: n_samples (the wizard default). This model has no top-level n_estimators resource. Use n_samples in the wizard; another estimator parameter needs an explicit compatible configuration.

docs.title: Minimal training entries
docs.text:
Untuned:

models:
  candidate:
    model:
      type: linear_regression
      params: {}

Tuned (small explicit grid):

models:
  candidate:
    model:
      type: linear_regression
      params: {}
    tuning:
      strategy: grid
      metric: r2
      max_candidates: 4
      search_space:
        fit_intercept: [true, false]

Common mistake: Treating correlated coefficients as independent causal effects; remove redundant features or compare Ridge.

docs.title: adaboost_regressor
docs.text:
AdaBoost regression. Task: regression. Sequentially reweights the learning problem to focus later learners on difficult examples. A compact boosting baseline when simple weak learners capture useful signal.

Sample weights: Yes; configure the workflow weight_column.

Optional package: None beyond the standard Core scikit-learn runtime.

Spark workers / serving: Not admitted by the current Spark-worker/pinned-serving model allowlist; use local inference.

docs.title: Parameters and defaults
docs.text: Parameter Core catalog default Explicit Core constructor default Meaning n_estimators 50 50 The maximum number of estimators at which boosting is terminated. learning_rate 1.0 1.0 Weight applied to each classifier at each boosting iteration. random_state 42 Library/resolver Seed passed to the base estimator's randomness, if it has any.

docs.title: Default search spaces
docs.text:
Axis Grid / halving_grid Random / halving_random / Optuna learning_rate [0.1, 0.5, 1.0] [0.01, 0.1, 1.0, 1.5] n_estimators [50, 100, 200] [50, 100, 200, 500]

Halving resource: n_samples (the wizard default). This model also exposes n_estimators; selecting it requires explicit max_resources and removing that axis from the search space.

docs.title: Minimal training entries
docs.text:
Untuned:

models:
  candidate:
    model:
      type: adaboost_regressor

Stacking ensemble regression. Task: regression. Learns a final estimator from out-of-fold base predictions. Its internal cv prevents the final learner from training on overoptimistic in-sample predictions; passthrough also includes original features.

docs.text: Parameter Core catalog default Explicit Core constructor default Meaning base_estimators ["random_forest", "gradient_boosting", "ridge"] Library/resolver Base learners combined by the ensemble. final_estimator "ridge" Library/resolver Meta-learner trained on the base models' out-of-fold predictions. cv 5 5 Cross-validation folds used to generate out-of-fold predictions for the final estimator. Keep small (e.g. 3) when also running an outer hyperparameter search to limit nested-CV cost. passthrough false Library/resolver When on, the final estimator sees the original input features alongside the base models' predictions instead of the predictions alone. docs.title: stacking_classifier
docs.text:
Stacking ensemble classification. Task: classification. Learns a final estimator from out-of-fold base predictions. Its internal cv prevents the final learner from training on overoptimistic in-sample predictions; passthrough also includes original features.

Sample weights: Yes for the default configuration; every selected child and final estimator must support it.

Optional package: None beyond the standard Core scikit-learn runtime; add xgboost or lightgbm when selected as a member.

Spark workers / serving: Not admitted by the current Spark-worker/pinned-serving model allowlist; use local inference.

docs.title: Parameters and defaults
docs.text: Parameter Core catalog default Explicit Core constructor default Meaning base_estimators ["random_forest", "gradient_boosting", "svc"] Library/resolver Base learners combined by the ensemble. final_estimator "logistic_regression" Library/resolver Meta-learner trained on the base models' out-of-fold predictions. cv 5 5 Cross-validation folds used to generate out-of-fold predictions for the final estimator. Keep small (e.g. 3) when also running an outer hyperparameter search to limit nested-CV cost. passthrough false Library/resolver When on, the final estimator sees the original input features alongside the base models' predictions instead of the predictions alone. Can help when the base learners miss signal in the raw data. n_jobs 1 Library/resolver Number of base models fit in parallel. 1 = sequential, -1 = use all CPU cores. Speeds up fitting when you have several independent base learners. calibrate_base_models false Library/resolver Wrap each base classifier in CalibratedClassifierCV so its predicted probabilities are well-calibrated. Improves soft voting and stacking when base models give over/under-confident probabilities. calibration_method "sigmoid" Library/resolver Sigmoid (Platt scaling) is robust on small data; isotonic is more flexible but needs more samples to avoid overfitting. calibration_cv 3 Library/resolver Cross-validation folds used to fit each base model's calibrator.

docs.title: Keeping this catalog current
docs.text:
The explanatory text and examples are maintained here; marked parameter/search regions are regenerated from Core. From a repository checkout, run:

python skyulf-core/templates/databricks/build_model_catalog.py
python skyulf-core/templates/databricks/build_model_catalog.py --check

The generator needs only Python's standard library. Its check and the model-card coverage/example tests detect drift without needing workspace credentials.

docs.title: Train, approve and score a multi-target model set
When you need it
docs.text:
Use a model set when one project trains several models for different targets and you want to approve, roll back and score them together. A customer dataset can, for example, train a purchase classifier, a spending regressor and a visit-count ensemble. Each model stays useful on its own. Different targets have different metrics, so their scores are never ranked against each other.

Choose training_layout=multi_target when you generate the project. The single_model and model_competition layouts do not create a set.

A set is one registered model whose version holds every component's exact fitted artifact. It records each component's model name, version and digest. It also captures src/features/, the combined rules and the typed record keys. Scoring and approval load these saved assets, so editing project files cannot change an existing set. Packaging changed rules creates a new set candidate.

flowchart LR
    A["train_name: each branch"] --> B["register_model_set"]
    B --> C["evaluate_model_set"]
    C --> D["model_decision"]
    D --> E["training_report"]
    E --> F["run_batch_scoring"]
    F --> G["score job: score_models.py"]

train_name stands for each concrete train_<name> task. run_batch_scoring starts the score job only when follow_champion requests it after a set alias change. See training reports for the notebook behind each task.

docs.title: Configure the branches
docs.text:
Each branch is a named entry under models in config/training.yml. Shared source, keys and budgets belong under defaults. A branch can override its target, input columns, preprocessing recipe, estimator, search/CV, split and quality settings. It registers its own component model.

The train job resolves one Delta table version before training starts. Branches read that same snapshot within their own row/byte budgets. Missing labels are excluded per target before sampling and splitting, so a missing spending label cannot remove a labeled purchase example. Every target column is forbidden as a model input to prevent cross-target leakage. Learned preprocessing is fitted inside the training folds and the final holdout stays separate.

All branches are required. If one fails, the run stops and earlier component versions remain available for inspection. MLflow records a parent run and a linked child run for each branch. Branches keep promotion_policy=manual_approval and follow_champion: false; the set has its own promotion policy.

Select recipes per branch. Declare named lists under recipes in config/preprocessing.yml and config/pre_split.yml. Keep custom factories in src/features/preprocessing.py and src/features/pre_split.py:

models:
  revenue:
    preprocessing_recipe: revenue_features
    pre_split_recipe: complete_inputs

Branches can share one recipe and still learn separate fitted state. Missing names and duplicate configuration owners fail before data is read. Do not define the same recipe in both Python and YAML.

After adding, removing or renaming entries in models, run python src/tools/refresh_training_graph.py and redeploy. An old deployed graph with a changed model list is rejected before any model is trained.

docs.title: Set the model_set block
docs.text:
config/inference.yml > model_set declares the set. Detailed setup asks model_set_name, model_set_table_name, model_set_output_mode and model_set_promotion_policy; quick setup writes editable defaults.

Field Default Effect model_name <project_name>_set in the metadata schema Registered set identity. Required. prediction_table <project_name>_set_scores in the output schema Physical result table. Required. promotion_policy manual_approval manual_approval or automatic set activation. combined_rules_path ../features Feature package; captures combined rules from adjacent config/scoring.yml or legacy Python hooks with the next set. composition_config Absent Declarative alternative to combined_rules_path; the two cannot coexist. on_source_change stop stop or rescore_all for source updates and deletes. publication mode: all Output mode and optional views.

Names gain the target catalog, schema and deployment suffix. Unknown fields are rejected.

docs.title: Choose the output mode
docs.text:
publication.mode Stored values Consumer access all (default) Every component output and combined rule result One prediction table combined_only Combined results, keys, rule outcomes and set provenance One prediction table; needs saved combined rules separate_views All results, written once Component views and an optional combined view

combined_only still computes every component; it only stores the combined results. An empty rule list fails. Changing between combined_only and a full schema needs a fresh table.

For separate_views, setup also asks model_view_prefix and combined_view_name. Blank names give <project_name>_predictions_<branch> and <project_name>_business_results. To pick names per branch, merge this fragment into model_set:

publication:
  mode: separate_views
  model_views:
    revenue: "{catalog}.{output_schema}.revenue_predictions{resource_suffix}"
    cost: "{catalog}.{output_schema}.cost_predictions{resource_suffix}"
  combined_view: "{catalog}.{output_schema}.profit_results{resource_suffix}"

Replace revenue and cost with real branch names. Omitted model_views creates a view for every branch; {} creates none. A combined view exists only when the saved set has combined rules. Views are projections of one Delta table, not separate copies. They keep record keys, status/output fields and set provenance. View setup runs before the data write, so a failure can leave views over empty or previous data, but no partial new result. Existing views must match their recorded projection; use new names to change them. Removing configuration does not delete catalog objects, and unrelated objects are never replaced.

docs.title: Write combined rules
docs.text:
In config/scoring.yml, eligibility and outputs configure each component; combined configures calculations across component results. The default lists are empty. Top-level mode: combined means pre-split plus model eligibility; it does not itself enable cross-model calculations.

For example, add this entry to the combined list, keeping the other top-level scoring.yml fields:

combined:
  - name: profit
    version: "1"
    custom: scoring.profit
    params: {}
    columns: [{name: profit, dtype: float64}]
    required_components: [revenue, cost]

The optional helper in src/features/scoring.py subtracts cost__prediction from revenue__prediction. Its declaration and source are captured with the set.

A combined rule declares a function, rule version, parameters, output column types and required_components. The function receives (inputs, predictions, params) and returns a pandas DataFrame with exactly the declared columns. inputs holds only the set's keys and component input columns. Component results are named like revenue__prediction. An excluded required component makes the rule ineligible for that row; an unrelated component's exclusion does not. Missing predictions are never replaced with zero. A rule exception fails the job before new results are published.

Declare rule dependencies as exact pins in src/features/requirements.txt. The saved set includes them and rejects pins that conflict with a component.

The same combined list supports declarative operations: weighted_sum and weighted_mean over named numeric component outputs, with finite weights and one float64 output column. weighted_mean needs nonnegative weights with a positive sum. Keep combined_rules_path: ../features and put this in config/scoring.yml:

combined:
  - name: combined_score
    version: '1'
    operation: weighted_mean
    params:
      inputs: [revenue__prediction, value__prediction]
      weights: [0.7, 0.3]
    columns:
      - name: combined_score
        dtype: float64
    required_components: [revenue, value]

Older projects can still place an outputs mapping under model_set.composition_config instead when no config/scoring.yml exists, removing combined_rules_path as well. An existing scoring.yml, even with an empty combined list, conflicts with inline composition_config. Choose one owner. Python-only feature packages without scoring.yml retain build_combined_rules().

With config/scoring.yml present, combined_rules_path must select a direct child package of src, normally ../features. A nested package would miss the canonical YAML and is rejected before import; move its helpers into the selected package. Older Python-only projects without scoring.yml can retain nested packages.

Weights do not convert units. Check that the combination has a business meaning.

docs.title: Quality policy and replacement rule
docs.text:
Set each branch's metric, quality_threshold, optional quality_gates and min_improvement in its models entry. Every branch needs a primary quality_threshold before a set can be activated:

models:
  revenue:
    metric: heldout_rmse
    quality_threshold: 10.0  # RMSE must be <= 10.
    quality_gates:
      heldout_r2: 0.8       # R2 must also be >= 0.8.
    min_improvement: 0.0

A classifier can use metric: heldout_f1 with quality_threshold: 0.8. Ensembles use the same policy fields. These limits are examples, not advice.

  • First set: every branch must pass its absolute gates.
  • Replacement: every branch must still pass its absolute gates. No branch may regress on its selected metric against its counterpart in the pinned champion set. At least one branch must improve by its min_improvement, with a positive gain even when the minimum is zero. Tied branches are allowed.
  • All tied: the set stays challenger.

For example, lower revenue RMSE with unchanged risk accuracy can promote the complete set. Components are evaluated on their saved holdout rows. Policies, comparison digests and the expected set champion are frozen into the package, so editing training.yml cannot relax a registered candidate. A replacement needs the same branch names and registered component names; use a new set for a changed layout. Independent component aliases cannot change the baseline.

With promotion_policy: automatic, gates are checked after packaging. A passing set becomes champion. A failed gate leaves the champion unchanged; the report and model_set_quality/.../decision.json list the failed components. Missing evidence, changed baselines and execution errors fail the job.

docs.title: Approve, reject or roll back a set
docs.text:
Use the same procedure as a single model: open the train run's training_report > Output, copy the values from Available action: approve, Available action: reject or If rollback is needed, and start the same train job with Run now with different parameters. The operator steps give each click and field.

Action Set-specific behavior approve Offered for a pending manual_approval set whose quality passed. Runs every component and rule on a bounded scoring-source snapshot, requires at least one result from each, then rechecks saved quality. reject Offered for a pending manual_approval set, even when quality failed. Needs rejection_reason. Runs no training or scoring. rollback Offered after a set promotion, not after the first activation or a rollback. Restores the complete prior set.

candidate_version is the set version, not a component version. expected_champion_version is the set champion recorded at evaluation, or none for the first set. The set's next_actions field is a list of sentences; copy parameter values from the report blocks. Decision details (JSON) below the blocks shows per-component quality.

Aliases belong to the set; component aliases stay unchanged:

  • Every completed candidate becomes the set's challenger. A newer candidate moves the displaced one to previous_challenger.
  • Approval removes the promoted version's challenger alias and keeps the old champion as previous_champion.
  • A rejected set stays challenger until a newer candidate replaces it. Its approval_status=rejected blocks later approval. An identical repeat reuses the receipt; a changed reason, candidate or champion fails.
  • Rollback restores the whole prior set and keeps an unrelated current challenger. A stale or manually changed alias blocks it.

docs.title: Score the set
docs.text:
The score job runs src/jobs/score_models.py. It resolves the set champion once per run, or uses score_model_version as a concrete set version. Do not try to replace one component through that parameter.

Components and rules join on unique, non-null integer, string or boolean keys. One Delta commit holds the complete result with set provenance. A component or rule exception fails before the commit, and earlier output stays intact. Train and score use max_concurrent_runs: 1 and must own set alias changes and prediction-table writes exclusively.

  • Append keeps older rows with their original set version.
  • Full rebuild replaces the compatible output table when the selected set changes, even without new input. Changes that involve temporal carry history require full rebuild.
  • on_source_change: rescore_all: when CDF shows an update or delete, the selected set rescores all current rows, recomputes rules and resets temporal history. Deleted records disappear. New inserts alone still append. The full snapshot must fit the row/byte limits. Receipts record the internal source_change_policy, source_rebuilt and write_mode.

Single-model scoring has no rescore_all source option; it rejects source updates and deletes. See source changes.

docs.title: Spark scoring
docs.text: With batch_compute: spark, every component must pass Spark admission. Admission runs at activation (manual approval or automatic promotion) and again at scoring. Independent outputs and composition_config with weighted_sum/weighted_mean are admitted. Function rules from scoring.yml and legacy Python hooks are admitted when training linted and probed them: packaging probes each combined rule on up to 256 rows of the set's training source, changing one row's inputs and component predictions at a time, and seals the evidence in the set. A failing rule stops packaging with a message naming the rule and check. Reused pre-split eligibility stays rejected. See the Spark support table and When the probe fails.

docs.title: Train branches from the Python SDK
docs.text:
TrainingBranch binds a TrainingSpec, pipeline, registered model, metric and gates. train_branches trains the branches in order and returns a BranchTrainingResult with parent_run_id, pinned source identity, components and plan_sha256.
