From a Skyulf checkout, save these selections as online-init.json. This answer-file command takes missing answers from their defaults; it does not ask for missing table or target names. Replace the explicit example identities with your own before generating:

{
  "project_name": "customer_online",
  "catalog": "features",
  "schema": "customer",
  "source_table_name": "customer_observations",
  "target_column": "next_month_spend",
  "engine": "pandas",
  "training_layout": "single_model",
  "task": "regression",
  "input_columns": "total_spend, feature_updated_at",
  "record_key_columns": "customer_id",
  "include_online_feature_lookup": "true",
  "include_online_publication": "false",
  "include_daily_rollout": "false",
  "score_follow_champion": "false",
  "scoring_mode": "manual",
  "promotion_policy": "manual_approval"
}

databricks bundle init ./skyulf-core/templates/databricks --config-file online-init.json --output-dir ./generated
cd generated/customer_online

The three serving selections are independent and default to "false". Only detailed setup asks them; quick setup keeps "false", so use detailed setup or an answer file like the one above. include_online_feature_lookup adds an unscheduled online_feature_lookup_setup job and its notebook. It installs the native Feature Engineering dependency for training even when another project owns publication. Initialization creates files only. With include_online_publication: "true", detailed setup asks for online_publication_mode; an answer file can set it directly: TRIGGERED (default) keeps the paused hourly job; CONTINUOUS generates explicit start/status/stop/restart controls without a periodic schedule. The mode is independent of online serving and rollout.

Complete the generated placeholders under defaults: in config/training.yml, retaining the source, label, split and model settings for your project. Both mappings belong under defaults:; a top-level feature_lookup is rejected. For example:

defaults:
  # ... keep the generated source, keys, target and model settings ...
  feature_lookup:
    lookups:
      - table_name: "{catalog}.{input_schema}.customer_features"
        lookup_key: [customer_id]
        feature_names: [total_spend, feature_updated_at]
  online_features:
    required_features: [total_spend, feature_updated_at]
    freshness:
      - column: feature_updated_at
        max_age_seconds: 3600.0

All lookup features must be declared in input_columns; the required features must cover them exactly. Choose a maximum age for each lookup's freshness field. Empty generated placeholders fail validation. The policy is frozen into the training specification and carried through prepare, fit, log and registration. The original feature-table snapshot binding and fitted preprocessing remain enforced. This generated flow supports pandas single-model and competition training; multi-target policy transport and temporal feature lookups are rejected. No Spark scoring job or batch prediction table needs to run or exist.

Keep the generated Core release pinned in deployment/requirements.txt and complete your Bundle target and ordinary training settings. Change only this requirement's version to upgrade Core and redeploy. The optional online jobs inherit this pin through serving-requirements.txt, which also installs the pinned feature-engineering SDK. Validate saved-model runtime compatibility before upgrading production; see runtime packaging. Provision and publish the feature source as described below, or use an existing publication maintained externally. Then validate, deploy and train:

databricks bundle validate --strict -t test
databricks bundle deploy -t test
databricks bundle run train -t test

Continue with online endpoint setup using the concrete version from training. The setup verifies publication binding and first-sync evidence; it does not provision the store or publish features.

docs.title: Create a latest-value source and an online store
docs.text:
Use a Unity Catalog Delta feature table containing one current row per entity. Declare its primary key columns NOT NULL, enable Change Data Feed, and include a DOUBLE feature timestamp containing UTC Unix seconds. The timestamp records when that entity's values were produced; a recent table synchronization is not a substitute for a recent feature timestamp.

Provision an online store explicitly with the native Feature Engineering client and wait until it is AVAILABLE. Store provisioning is never a side effect of Skyulf prediction. Install deployment/serving-requirements.txt with uv pip install in a compatible Databricks environment. Packaging and serving must use the same Core release and source runtime.

Choose the store name and capacity when provisioning it in your selected workspace. Databricks manages the underlying Lakebase infrastructure. Bundle initialization does not create that infrastructure: online_store in config/serving.yml refers to this existing store. source_table identifies the Delta source, while online_table names the destination as catalog.schema.table; prepare that destination catalog and schema first.

from databricks.feature_engineering import FeatureEngineeringClient

features = FeatureEngineeringClient()
# Run provisioning once with a new name and an appropriate capacity.
features.create_online_store(name="customer-features", capacity="CU_1")

Prepare the destination catalog and schema before publication. Keep one online publication per source when exact store selection matters: native lookup can choose the oldest online copy if the same source has several publications. The model's lookup contract identifies its source features, not a chosen online table replica.

Inspect provisioning before publishing; creation is not a readiness signal:

store = features.get_online_store(name="customer-features")
print(store.name, store.state, store.capacity)

Continue when the platform reports AVAILABLE. For the following publisher example, use features.customer.customer_features with customer_id BIGINT NOT NULL, total_spend DOUBLE and feature_updated_at DOUBLE, a primary key on customer_id, and CDF enabled. Keep the training observation table separate: it contains entity keys and labels, while the lookup supplies the selected feature values. Source and online destination are different objects.

docs.title: Publish and inspect a sync
docs.text:
from databricks.sdk import WorkspaceClient
from skyulf.integrations.databricks.data.admission import SingleWriterAdmission
from skyulf.integrations.databricks.feature_store import (
    OnlinePublicationSpec,
    online_publication_status,
    publish_online_features,
)

source = "features.customer.customer_features"
detail = spark.sql(f"DESCRIBE DETAIL {source}").first()
publication = OnlinePublicationSpec(
    source_table=source,
    online_table="features.online.customer_features",
    online_store="customer-features",
    source_table_id=detail["id"],
    publish_mode="TRIGGERED", # Default; choose CONTINUOUS to start a native stream.
)
receipt = publish_online_features(
    spark,
    publication,
    feature_client=features,
    admission=SingleWriterAdmission(),
)
print(receipt)

This validates the source table identity, CDF, key declarations and actual key rows before requesting a TRIGGERED sync. Source and publication writers must share the declared exclusive ownership; the adapter does not lock outside writers or change the source schema for you. It publishes all source columns. Temporal source tables remain unsupported. CONTINUOUS starts native feature synchronization and releases the writer admission after submission, allowing subsequent source writes. No caller process needs to keep running.

Inspect status later without submitting another sync:

workspace = WorkspaceClient()
status = online_publication_status(workspace, receipt)
print(status["status"], status.get("update_id"))

SUBMITTED and PENDING are not completion. SYNCED requires a native pipeline update that started after submission and completed; FAILED identifies a failed or canceled update. Keep the receipt and update ID for inspection. The recorded source version is the version checked during preflight, not a guarantee that native latest-value publication copied precisely that snapshot. Verify an actual endpoint lookup when testing propagation.

docs.title: Operate continuous feature publication
docs.text:
Select online_publication_mode: "CONTINUOUS" together with include_online_publication: "true" in the Bundle initialization answers. Complete the generated publisher configuration with the actual resources:

online_publication:
  enabled: true
  exclusive_writer: true
  publish_mode: CONTINUOUS
  source_table: features.customer.customer_features
  source_table_id: "REPLACE_WITH_DESCRIBE_DETAIL_ID"
  online_table: features.online.customer_features
  online_store: customer-features

After configuring exclusive source/publication ownership and deploying the Bundle, run one explicit operation at a time:

databricks bundle validate --strict -t test
databricks bundle deploy -t test
databricks bundle run online_publication -t test --params publication_action=start
databricks bundle run online_publication -t test --params publication_action=status
databricks bundle run online_publication -t test --params publication_action=stop
databricks bundle run online_publication -t test --params publication_action=status
# Wait until pipeline_state is IDLE or FAILED, then explicitly restart:
databricks bundle run online_publication -t test --params publication_action=restart

RUNNING describes pipeline activity, including resource provisioning; it is not first-sync completion or entity freshness. Inspect pipeline_state, update_id, update_state, synchronization_state, first_sync_completed and last_sync_end_timestamp separately. A failed update or synchronization is reported by the inspected status command as FAILED even if the pipeline still reports running during recovery. STOP_REQUESTED is a submitted stop; check again for STOPPING or STOPPED. Restart requires native pipeline_state to be IDLE or FAILED. Overall status=FAILED can coexist with a RUNNING or STOPPING pipeline; stop active compute first and inspect its pipeline state. A restart receipt keeps its new update ID and reports PENDING until that update appears in native metadata. Earlier update/synchronization failures do not establish failure of that attempt. Once its acknowledged update appears, that update/pipeline activity decides the attempt status; synchronization failure labels remain separately visible because they can lag an intentional cancellation or restart. An intentionally stopped pipeline can therefore report native pipeline_state=IDLE alongside overall status=FAILED and update_state=CANCELED from the last operation. The model's saved missing/stale guard still validates every prediction request.

A repeated continuous start inspects and reuses the active pipeline without submitting another update. Restart uses the same pipeline after a confirmed stop or failure. Calls that time out or lose a response are not retried automatically; inspect native status before another action. Changing publish_mode on an existing publication is rejected. Stop and inspect the existing pipeline, then explicitly plan the new publication and model-routing migration with its resource owner; this adapter never drops or recreates an online table.

With TRIGGERED, the same start command requests one sync and the generated hourly schedule remains PAUSED until you deliberately enable it. status inspects the latest native update; SYNCED does not attest entity freshness. Continuous stop/restart controls require a continuous publication. If online serving uses an external publication, set its online_feature_lookup.publications[].publish_mode to that publication's actual mode before setup.

The SDK exposes the same operations without a Bundle:

from skyulf.integrations.databricks.feature_store import (
    publication_receipt,
    restart_online_publication,
    stop_online_publication,
)

# publication is an OnlinePublicationSpec with publish_mode="CONTINUOUS".
receipt = publication_receipt(workspace, publication)
print(online_publication_status(workspace, receipt))
print(stop_online_publication(workspace, receipt, admission=SingleWriterAdmission()))
# Inspect status in a later cell; restart only when pipeline_state is IDLE or FAILED.
receipt = restart_online_publication(
    spark, receipt, client=workspace, feature_client=features,
    admission=SingleWriterAdmission(),
)

If the source was dropped, replaced or became inaccessible, the guarded SDK control fails closed during binding checks, even for stop. The resource owner must inspect permissions, the saved receipt, online table source/store properties and native pipeline identity before stopping through the native API. For example, after that ownership review, verify the remaining publication metadata:

saved = receipt["spec"]
online = workspace.tables.get(saved["online_table"])
synced = workspace.database.get_synced_database_table(name=saved["online_table"])
pipeline_id = receipt["pipeline_id"]
assert online.pipeline_id == synced.data_synchronization_status.pipeline_id == pipeline_id
assert (online.properties or {}).get("source_table") == saved["source_table"]
assert synced.spec.source_table_full_name == saved["source_table"]
assert synced.effective_database_instance_name == saved["online_store"]
print(workspace.pipelines.get(pipeline_id=pipeline_id))
# Resource owner only: after confirming this saved pipeline is the intended resource.
workspace.pipelines.stop(pipeline_id=pipeline_id)

This recovery stops pipeline compute and does not alter the source table or publication. If metadata or ownership cannot be confirmed, resolve that with the resource owner before any mutation. Inspect native pipeline state after the stop request. Restart still requires restored, valid source identity/access and all normal source preflight checks.

docs.title: Save the freshness policy with the model
docs.text:
The Bundle training path above saves this policy for you. The next snippet is the equivalent SDK packaging stage, continuing an existing fitted model and native training set; its named objects are prerequisites, not standalone inputs.

Build the native training set with explicit lookup fields and train from its load_df() result, retaining that same native training-set object for packaging. The freshness field must already be a fitted raw float64/double input and a selected lookup feature. Each lookup table needs its own freshness field.

from skyulf.integrations.databricks.feature_store import OnlineFeaturePolicy
from skyulf.integrations.mlflow.models.feature_model import log_feature_pipeline_model

online_policy = OnlineFeaturePolicy(
    required_features=("total_spend", "feature_updated_at"),
    freshness=(("feature_updated_at", 3600.0),),
)

# fitted_path, training_set, lookup_spec and lookup_binding come from training.
# run_id identifies the explicit MLflow run that owns this package.
model_uri = log_feature_pipeline_model(
    fitted_path,
    training_set=training_set,
    lookup_spec=lookup_spec,
    lookup_binding=lookup_binding,
    run_id=run_id,
    artifact_path="model",
    client=features,
    tracking_uri="databricks",
    online_policy=online_policy,
)

lookup_binding is the saved binding for that training set: its lookup spec and training_snapshot evidence identify the feature table IDs and Delta versions used during training. Retain that binding with the fitted artifact; do not replace it with a new snapshot when packaging an already fitted model.

Choose the maximum age for your domain. The example's one-hour limit is not a universal default. All fetched features are required and non-null. Every request uses one real UTC clock reading; nonfinite, future or over-age timestamps fail before fitted preprocessing. Callers cannot pass another clock to the saved model. The policy is checked across saved model metadata, configuration and serialized state when the package is loaded.

The timestamp is an actual fitted input: adding it only at packaging time is rejected. If it should not affect the estimator, remove it through a supported fitted preprocessing step and verify that step's serving certificate. Do not drop or transform inputs outside the saved preprocessing and expect Databricks lookup to repeat those transformations. log_feature_model_set also accepts online_policy; its raw saved guard covers the model-set request before its components run.

docs.title: Next: create the endpoint
docs.text: Continue with endpoint admission and requests. That page owns endpoint creation, readiness and the inspected request schema; the publication and saved freshness policy above are prerequisites.

docs.title: Schedule publication and test updates
docs.text:
Generate a Bundle project with include_online_publication: "true". Fill online_publication in config/serving.yml with the explicit source table ID, source and online table names, and store name. Establish exclusive source/sync writer ownership before setting exclusive_writer: true and enabled: true. The hourly job starts PAUSED; deploy, inspect a manual run and its pipeline status, then unpause it. Its result may be PENDING while the native pipeline continues. A later run should not be used to blindly retry an ambiguous native failure; inspect its pipeline and receipt first.

For acceptance, compare an endpoint prediction with the saved fitted artifact, change a source feature and its timestamp, publish, and verify that the same key-only request reflects the new value. Check that an absent entity and an expired timestamp produce the intended feature error. A successful local model load or native batch score_batch call does not establish online endpoint lookup.

docs.title: Repeat the same request after a feature update
docs.text:
Continue the publication examples above and the endpoint SDK example with their workspace, features, publication, plan and receipt. Use an isolated demonstration source, with an existing customer_id=42, a one-hour saved freshness limit and a model whose output depends on total_spend. This sequence uses TRIGGERED publication. Supply any additional fields required by plan.input_schema; the illustrated model accepts only the entity key.

assert tuple(plan.input_columns) == ("customer_id",)
assert spark.table(publication.source_table).where("customer_id = 42").count() == 1
records = [{"customer_id": 42}]
before = query_named_records(
    workspace, plan, records, client_request_id="feature-demo-before",
)
print("Before:", before.as_dict())

spark.sql(f"""
UPDATE {publication.source_table}
SET total_spend = total_spend + 100.0,
    feature_updated_at = CAST(unix_timestamp() AS DOUBLE)
WHERE customer_id = 42
""")
receipt = publish_online_features(
    spark, publication, feature_client=features,
    admission=SingleWriterAdmission(),
)
print(receipt)

Do not query immediately and treat an unchanged response as a failure. In a later cell, inspect the submitted synchronization:

status = online_publication_status(workspace, receipt)
print(status)
assert status["status"] == "SYNCED", "Wait for this submitted sync; inspect FAILED separately"
after = query_named_records(
    workspace, plan, records, client_request_id="feature-demo-after",
)
print("After:", after.as_dict())

The request and model version are unchanged. Compare the response with a local prediction from the same fitted artifact using the new feature values. For a simple model prediction = 2 * total_spend, a change from 50 to 150 should change the prediction from 100 to 300. That arithmetic illustrates the acceptance check; it is not an expected value for an arbitrary trained model. A classifier label may remain unchanged even when its probabilities change.

For CONTINUOUS, update the source once, inspect the existing publication and observe propagation; do not resubmit publish_online_features on every write. An active pipeline alone does not prove that a particular row reached the store.

docs.title: Check missing and stale features
docs.text:
First use a key absent from the demonstration source. The following call should raise a native model-evaluation error, not return an imputed prediction:

assert spark.table(publication.source_table).where("customer_id = 999999").count() == 0
query_named_records(
    workspace, plan, [{"customer_id": 999999}],
    client_request_id="feature-demo-missing",
)

Then change the existing entity's freshness field to two hours ago:

spark.sql(f"""
UPDATE {publication.source_table}
SET feature_updated_at = CAST(unix_timestamp() - 7200 AS DOUBLE)
WHERE customer_id = 42
""")
receipt = publish_online_features(
    spark, publication, feature_client=features,
    admission=SingleWriterAdmission(),
)

Wait for this receipt's SYNCED status as above, then repeat records with client_request_id="feature-demo-stale". A model saved with the one-hour limit must reject it. Inspect the matched request's model log for the freshness error; an unrelated network/authentication error does not pass this check. Afterwards restore the entity's real feature values and a current production timestamp, synchronize again and verify a successful request. Do not leave a shared entity with intentionally stale test features.

The native Feature Engineering wrapper replaces every model error with a generic one, so the REST caller only sees Encountered an unexpected error while evaluating the model. ... Error ''. Read the reason from the served model's logs:

databricks serving-endpoints logs <endpoint-name> <served-model-name> --profile <profile>

The served model name is in databricks serving-endpoints get <endpoint-name> (config.served_entities[].name, for example customer_model-1). Look for one of:

Online required features have no value in 1 of 1 rows (first row 0): total_spend, feature_updated_at. The lookup key has no row in the online table, or the published value is null.
Online freshness feature 'feature_updated_at' is stale in 1 of 1 rows: oldest age 7200s exceeds 3600s (max_age_seconds). Refresh and republish the feature table.

Check that the traceback belongs to the rejected request; a generic HTTP error alone does not establish that the freshness policy ran.

The latest-value policy does not replace historical evaluation evidence. New feature-bound candidates save their enriched holdout in lifecycle/data/holdout.parquet; later champion promotion verifies that saved artifact and the original source identities. Advancing a feature table's version is allowed on this path; dropping/recreating a table or altering the saved holdout blocks it. A candidate without a saved holdout uses strict snapshot reconstruction, so a feature-source advance blocks it. Train a new candidate with the matching runtime rather than replacing historical values with today's online features.

docs.title: When you need it
docs.text:
Use a performance policy when you need to decide whether measured prediction quality has worsened enough to investigate or request training. Drift measures input changes and can exist without performance loss, or vice versa. Start with report mode and configure actual outcomes.

Performance policy is disabled by default. Each producer sets an independent JSON mapping keyed by the exact fully qualified enrolled model name. The example policy under What to edit reports a weighted F1 drop of at least 0.05 across three distinct, completed windows for version 2.

flowchart LR
    W["Mature UTC window with labels"] --> B["Compare metric with baseline and tolerance"]
    B --> S["Count consecutive failing windows"]
    S --> R["mode: report: record the verdict"]
    S --> T["mode: retrain: evaluate_retraining guards"]
    T --> J["One guarded train job request"]

docs.title: What to edit
docs.text:
Detailed setup offers a simple initial policy through these answers:

{
  "monitoring_catalog": "workspace",
  "monitoring_schema": "skyulf_monitoring",
  "label_table_name": "outcomes",
  "label_available_at_column": "available_at",
  "performance_policy_mode": "report",
  "performance_regression_metric": "wape",
  "performance_classification_metric": "accuracy",
  "performance_tolerance_mode": "relative",
  "performance_tolerance": "0.2",
  "performance_baseline_version": "1"
}

The default is off. Enabling report or retrain requires both an outcome binding and a monitoring store. Setup writes monitoring_performance_policies in deployment/variables.yml: one entry for a single model or competition winner, and one entry per component in a model set. Regression and classification components use their respective metric answer and the correct loss direction. The initial policy uses 24-hour windows, a six-hour label delay, at least 20 labeled rows, 80% coverage and two consecutive failing windows for retraining. These are editable policy fields, not additional hidden runtime rules.

Verify the concrete baseline version before activation. Different model-set components may need different versions: edit their JSON entries independently. Changing the baseline is an explicit policy change; promoting a new champion does not automatically advance the baseline. report can show a degraded first window but never requests training.

For a more specific classification policy, set a target override:

monitoring_label_table: labels.production.outcomes
monitoring_result_available_at_column: available_at
monitoring_performance_policies: >-
  {"models.risk.churn":{
    "mode":"report",
    "metric":"f1_weighted",
    "direction":"higher",
    "baseline":{"kind":"training_holdout","model_version":"2"},
    "tolerance":0.05,
    "tolerance_mode":"absolute",
    "window_hours":24,
    "label_delay_hours":6,
    "minimum_labeled_rows":20,
    "minimum_label_coverage":0.8,
    "consecutive_windows":3}}

These are example values, not production defaults. Put them under the producer Bundle's targets.<target>.variables in deployment/targets.yml, alongside the monitoring destination. Replace the model and label table names with your own fully qualified names.

Labels match saved record keys and the saved target; their UTC available_at must say when the actual outcome became available. For serving, match request ID and row index instead; label matching has the full contract.

Setting Meaning in this example monitoring_label_table Actual outcomes joined to original predictions by stable record keys. Predictions are never used as actual outcomes. monitoring_result_available_at_column Outcome availability timestamp used to exclude labels unavailable at the observation cutoff. models.risk.churn Exact enrolled model name; a component model name for a model-set. mode: report Persist and display the performance decision without requesting training. metric: f1_weighted Class-support-weighted F1 over eligible prediction/label pairs; this does not enable training sample weights. direction: higher A decrease is worse. Regression MAE uses lower, where an increase is worse. baseline Saved training holdout for concrete model version 2; production-window references are also supported. tolerance: 0.05, absolute A baseline of 0.84 is degraded at 0.79 or below: five percentage points, not a five-percent relative drop. window_hours: 24 Measure each completed, fixed UTC day independently. label_delay_hours: 6 Wait six hours after the window ends before assessing it. This is independent of the job schedule. minimum_labeled_rows: 20 Require at least 20 eligible labeled predictions in that window. minimum_label_coverage: 0.8 Require eligible labels for at least 80 percent of the window's prediction population; both minimums must pass. consecutive_windows: 3 Require three adjacent eligible failing windows for trigger eligibility; replaying one window does not count again.

An individual window can already be reported as degraded before the required streak is reached. report never requests training, even after three failures. With retrain, reaching the streak only makes the performance trigger eligible; fresh training data, cooldown, active-run and duplicate-request guards still apply.

Policy reports retain the required window count even when labels, a baseline or a source snapshot are unavailable. For example, a three-window policy reports 0 / 3 after a failed observation; that failure does not count as measured degradation. Older reports without a saved required count show Unavailable in the notebook's failure-streak denominator instead of an invented zero.

Project layout Policy scope Single One policy for the active concrete model version. Competition Policy for the activated winner; losing candidates are not production monitors. Model-set / multi-target A separate mapping entry and matching baseline for each component model; each keeps its own target, metric and version.

The producer's label table must contain the target columns needed by its enrolled components. A retraining request runs the configured project train job; it does not introduce selective retraining of just one model-set branch.

Use mode: "retrain" in the JSON policy to request guarded automatic training, or {"mode":"off"} for an explicitly disabled model. An active policy needs the label table and UTC availability column shown above. Select a training_holdout baseline or pin an existing production observation with {"kind":"production_window","model_version":"2","report_id":"<64 hex characters>"}. The baseline version must match the observed version; a mismatch is unavailable and cannot request training. No metric, direction, tolerance or baseline is inferred. Fixed UTC windows wait label_delay_hours after their end, then count only labels available at the cutoff. A 00:00–24:00 UTC window with a six-hour delay can first be evaluated at 06:00 UTC the next day. Replays do not advance the consecutive-window count; missing and immature labels remain unavailable. Distribution drift remains controlled separately by on_drift. Its cooldown and minimum new labeled training-row settings are shared request guards for either retraining trigger. Model evaluation and approval rules still apply.

An active policy requires every policy field in the example; there are no default metric, direction, baseline or tolerance values. tolerance_mode accepts absolute or relative.

For relative tolerance, the permitted degradation is tolerance * abs(baseline). A zero baseline makes relative tolerance unavailable. Boundary equality counts as degradation (with the evaluator's small floating-point comparison tolerance). Active tolerances and window lengths must be positive finite numbers; label delay is nonnegative, minimum rows is an integer at least 2, coverage is from 0 to 1, and consecutive windows is an integer from 1 to 100.

Policy metrics with lower direction are mae, mse, rmse, mape, wape. Metrics with higher direction are r2, explained_variance, accuracy, balanced_accuracy, precision_weighted, recall_weighted, f1_weighted, matthews_corrcoef, g_score. Observed reports can contain additional probability metrics; their presence does not make them supported policy metrics.

docs.title: WAPE when actual values can be zero
docs.text:
wape is sum(abs(actual - prediction)) / sum(abs(actual)). It is a ratio: 0.10 means 10%, and lower is better. Like the other reported regression metrics, it uses unweighted evaluation rows; training sample weights are not reused for holdout or monitoring observations. It is calculated from saved predictions and available labels, excluding rows the model did not score.

For actual values [0, 10, 20] and predictions [5, 12, 18], total absolute error is 9 and total absolute actual value is 30: WAPE = 0.30. MAPE instead divides each row's error by that row's actual magnitude. Its near-zero denominator makes the zero-actual row dominate. The taxi example's February labels include three zero fares, so MAPE can be extremely large even while most errors are small. Both metrics remain available; inspect WAPE alongside MAE, RMSE and label coverage.

When every actual value is zero, WAPE is undefined, including for perfect zero predictions. Core evaluation omits wape from its finite metric dictionary; monitoring records value: null, status: unavailable. A WAPE policy cannot act on that window. No epsilon or invented zero score disguises the missing denominator. A nonfinite result is also unavailable.

Use metric: wape with direction: lower in a performance policy, retaining all the other required policy fields shown above. For registered-model holdout comparison or an additional quality gate, use heldout_wape; its direction is minimize. A missing holdout WAPE fails the gate. This does not add a WAPE scorer to tuning or cross-validation model competitions.

For example, this regression policy reports a WAPE increase of at least 20% relative to version 3's training holdout in each eligible completed daily window. It counts adjacent failing windows; consecutive_windows: 2 would gate trigger eligibility in retrain mode, but does not delay reports in report mode:

monitoring_performance_policies: >-
  {"models.sales.revenue":{
    "mode":"report",
    "metric":"wape",
    "direction":"lower",
    "baseline":{"kind":"training_holdout","model_version":"3"},
    "tolerance":0.2,
    "tolerance_mode":"relative",
    "window_hours":24,
    "label_delay_hours":6,
    "minimum_labeled_rows":20,
    "minimum_label_coverage":0.8,
    "consecutive_windows":2}}

Replace the model name and version with your enrolled identity and keep the label table/availability settings from the complete example above. With baseline WAPE 0.05, the limit is 0.06: this is a 20% relative increase, not 20 percentage points. WAPE suits this example when actual values can be zero because it uses the whole population's absolute actual total; MAPE divides by each individual actual. report never requests training. Spark monitoring reads cached holdout metrics from its prepared reference; an older cache without WAPE produces unavailable policy evidence until a compatible reference exists. The in-memory path measures the verified holdout with the fitted model. Neither path rewrites historical training-run metrics.

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from skyulf.modeling._evaluation.metrics import calculate_regression_metrics

truth = np.array([0.0, 10.0, 20.0])
values = calculate_regression_metrics(
    None, pd.DataFrame(), truth,
    X_np=np.empty((3, 0)), y_np=truth,
    predictions=np.array([5.0, 12.0, 18.0]),
)
assert values["wape"] == 0.3

WAPE gives larger-magnitude actuals more influence and is undefined for all-zero populations. It does not replace per-segment inspection or establish business acceptability. A lower aggregate value can still conceal a poorly served segment.

docs.title: The command
docs.text:
To enable performance-driven retraining, change only the relevant model's policy from "mode":"report" to "mode":"retrain" in the producer target variables, retain its metric, matching baseline and evidence requirements, then validate and deploy that producer Bundle. Run activation registration or successful scoring to update enrollment, then run monitoring to evaluate the next eligible window. This is a job configuration change; there is no dashboard switch that starts training. A policy change does not turn an old report into a new eligible request or bypass consecutive-window requirements.

Run these cloud commands from the generated project after updating target variables. Between deployment and observation, use normal activation or successful scoring to refresh enrollment.

databricks bundle validate --strict -t test --profile YOUR_PROFILE
databricks bundle deploy -t test --profile YOUR_PROFILE
databricks bundle run monitoring -t test --profile YOUR_PROFILE

There is no literal enforce mode: report records a decision, retrain enables guarded request eligibility, and off disables the policy. For online enrollments, both the inline policy and the job-level gate must be configured as described in retraining.

docs.title: What you should see
docs.text: monitoring_report reads the saved observation instead of recalculating it. Its output includes Open monitoring dashboard when the shared HTTPS monitoring_dashboard_url is configured. It displays feature drift, observed prediction/outcome metrics and the separate performance-loss policy. A measured RMSE or F1 value alone does not establish degradation: the policy also requires a valid baseline, completed window, label coverage and configured tolerance. The policy population can differ from the exact scoring batch shown under observed performance. healthy means the selected metric has not degraded beyond its configured tolerance; it does not establish that the model meets an absolute quality goal.

docs.title: Observed metrics and policy decisions
docs.text:
Local performance reuses skyulf.modeling._evaluation.metrics. Classification includes G-score, accuracy, balanced accuracy, MCC and precision/recall/F1; probabilities also enable log-loss, ROC-AUC and PR-AUC variants. Regression includes MAE, MSE, RMSE, R2, MAPE, WAPE and explained variance. The job installs Core's optional G-score dependency and compatibility pin. Local feature drift uses Core DriftCalculator; Spark enrollments use distributed metric and drift aggregations.

Performance metrics appear as dynamic pivot columns, so selecting a regression model shows its regression metrics, while classification shows its available metrics, including G-score and AUC. Same-time reports get deterministic observation suffixes so the pivot cannot merge distinct reports/monitors. Blank cells remain unavailable, never zero. Latest prediction coverage by model replaces the three shared counters with one row per model/version/context. Each row shows predictions, matched outcomes and label coverage from that identity's latest full observation. A failed latest measurement clears its counts rather than reviving an older success. Counts and coverage are never aggregated across models, contexts or observation windows.

The performance page starts with matching identities, then policy results and policy history. Prediction coverage and observed metrics follow below. Latest policy result for every model gives each identity its own row with metric, baseline, current score, allowed limit, improvement direction, result, explanation and training action. Accuracy, F1 and RMSE policies can coexist, with separate model/metric chart panels and independent scales. The policy charts use each identity's latest saved policy metric; selecting MAE in Chart metric does not hide an RMSE policy. Current is the observed metric, Baseline is its reference value, and Tolerance boundary is the permitted limit. An accuracy baseline of 0.96 with an absolute tolerance of 0.10 gives a lower limit of 0.86. For an error metric, exceeding the upper limit indicates loss. Missing scores are unavailable and must not be interpreted as zero. The latest policy summary ranks by window end before measurement time for each identity: a late historical degradation cannot replace a newer unavailable window. Disabled policies are explicitly labeled disabled, and identities without a saved check show No policy evidence. The Performance checks table is the history of those per-window comparisons. Performance result means Within tolerance, Performance loss, Insufficient evidence or Policy disabled. Training action is separate: loss can be report-only, awaiting further checks, skipped or actually requested. Eligible is not already submitted. Full reasons, source references and request IDs remain in performance_history and the job's saved reports. Classification matrix availability appears below the confusion matrix; the full metric matrix follows below.

Performance pairs a latest-observation metric table with time series in separate model/version/context and metric panels. Each panel keeps its own units and scale; legends identify whether higher or lower is better. The table identifies each metric, value, target and window even when only one observation exists. A latest unavailable measurement stays blank, rather than falling back to an older measured value. The metric selector defaults to an available MAE, weighted F1, accuracy or other saved metric independently for each matching context. Selecting a metric narrows the observed table and time chart to identities with that metric. A single observation does not establish a trend. The charts never combine different monitor identities or windows. Metric selection does not remove columns from the full metric-history table.

Filters never select an older observation; see latest observations and page filters. Metric selection does not change the configured policy metric.

Each saved performance value is a point. Missing values have no point and are not joined by a line. The time axis and date filters use Data window end (UTC), while Calculated at records the separate execution time.

The scoring-volume chart uses one stacked bar per full observation: labeled rows and rows not labeled at measurement add up to scored rows. Gray identifies observations without measured label coverage. The tooltip shows coverage as a percentage. Counts absent from the original report stay blank even if an older store row defaulted them to zero. Failed and policy-only reports never invent scoring counts; bars from different or overlapping windows must not be added.

The policy-margin comparison uses each identity's latest saved policy window, independently of the chart metric and history date filters. Remaining tolerance is the direction-aware distance from the saved limit divided by the absolute baseline-to-limit distance: 1 is at baseline, 0 is at the limit and negative values are beyond it. Bar color follows the saved policy verdict, including boundary equality rules. Unavailable, disabled or zero-tolerance policies stay in the policy table without a bar. Accuracy and error metrics can therefore share this normalized comparison without mixing their original units. The Policy status legend distinguishes blue Within tolerance from red Performance loss. Rows without a calculable margin remain in the policy table and are excluded from this chart and its legend.

The confusion-matrix pivot separates model/version/context first, then shows actual classes on rows and predictions on columns from each identity's latest report. Counts from different identities are never combined. Numeric class indices preserve identity when display labels collide. Measured zeros are real counts; unavailable classification, regression and historical reports without a stored matrix show an explicit status. The matrix is independent of history date and target filters.

docs.title: Common errors and fixes
docs.text:
Symptom Fix active policy has missing or unknown fields. Keep every field from the complete example, with no invented fields; off accepts only its mode. Baseline unavailable or wrong version Pin the observed concrete version and its saved training holdout or a compatible production report ID. Do not substitute another version. A raw RMSE or F1 exists but the policy is unavailable Check its own window, matching baseline, minimum labeled rows, label coverage and maturity. Observed batch and policy populations may differ. The same failing window was retried but the streak did not grow Distinct adjacent eligible windows are required; retries and backfills do not create extra windows. A performance loss did not start training report never submits; request_eligible still needs the shared retraining guards. Dashboard refresh is not a training command. Logging errors coexist with a policy verdict Usable records can still provide evidence; inspect the partial-population warning. Missing usable labels leave the policy unavailable.

An unavailable newest window remains newest; historical success or degradation does not replace it. Policy reports retain the required streak denominator even after failed observations. Delayed and insufficient labels are evidence limits, not zero accuracy.

docs.title: Create and preview a Databricks project
When you need it
docs.text: Create an editable project before its first deployment. For a complete example with source rows, follow the end-to-end guide. Initialization is offline and does not inspect your tables.

docs.title: Start from the closest example
docs.text:
Copying a finished project is usually faster than answering the setup wizard. Six NYC taxi projects on samples.nyctaxi.trips cover the main shapes:

Your project Copy Notes One model, scored on Spark workers taxi_fare Promotes automatically and scores after promotion REST/SQL serving and monitoring without batch output taxi_fare_endpoint Automatic endpoint after promotion, ai_query and captured-request monitoring; no score job or prediction table Preprocessing exclusions with Spark and raw-input serving taxi_fare_robust Reuses pre-split preparation; IQR, PowerTransformer and imputer handling; REST/ai_query examples and labels for monitoring One model behind an online endpoint taxi_fare_online Needs a billable Lakebase online store; no batch scoring One target, several candidate algorithms taxi_high_fare Competition with custom steps and manual approval Several targets approved together taxi_trips Model set with a combined scoring rule
  1. Copy the project folder out of examples/nyctaxi.
  2. Run load_nyctaxi.sql in the Databricks SQL editor with catalog set to workspace (or yours) and schema set to the project name. It creates the source tables and never overwrites one.
  3. In deployment/targets.yml, replace https://replace-test.example.invalid with your workspace URL. If your catalog is not workspace, change test_catalog and monitoring_catalog in deployment/variables.yml.
  4. Run databricks bundle deploy -t test --profile <profile>, then databricks bundle run train -t test --profile <profile>.

Three more projects in examples/real_data use public UCI data, loaded by its load_data.py notebook with pinned archive hashes. air_quality_no2 is the most complete one: built-in and custom pre-split filters, custom and built-in preprocessing (missing-value markers, IQR exclusion, Yeo-Johnson, imputation, encoding), combined scoring rules, SHAP, evaluation charts and monitoring on a later season with real drift and a report-only WAPE policy. diagnostic_single and bike_demand_set add serving endpoints and a model set.

Then swap the taxi tables, columns and recipes for your own. The examples README owns the complete steps, approval and serving. Not sure which shape fits? See choose a project shape.

docs.title: Generate a project with the wizard
docs.text:
When no example is close, generate the project:

flowchart LR
    A["databricks bundle init"] --> B["Edit config/*.yml and deployment/"]
    B --> C["src/tools/smoke.py"]
    C --> D["src/tools/preview.py"]
    D --> E["bundle validate --strict"]
    E --> F["bundle deploy"]

Smoke and preview run locally. Validate and deploy use the workspace; see deployment.

docs.title: Choose a layout and setup mode
docs.text:
Choice Use it when Result single_model One target and one chosen model One fitted pipeline and registered candidate model_competition One target, several candidate algorithms Comparable candidate runs and one selected winner multi_target Several independently defined targets One fitted component per target and a versioned model set setup_mode=quick (default) You want a working starting configuration Choose source arrangement, tables, keys, targets, input columns and monitoring destination; accept editable defaults setup_mode=detailed You want to choose model, search, schedules and compute before generation Ask applicable settings, including competition candidates and each active branch

Quick mode still supports all three layouts. Its defaults include bounded pandas training, whole-frame inference, manual schedules, a random split, manual promotion and pinned-version scoring. Inspect the generated values before the first run; accepting a default does not inspect the table or infer suitable columns. Detailed mode also has hidden advanced defaults; offline preview shows the effective configuration.

The manual quick default leaves quality_threshold unset. Pinned scoring can use a registered version, but first-champion initialization requires an absolute quality bound chosen before training. Set that field in training defaults or the model entry if you intend to approve the first candidate; see the worked run.

docs.title: Files you edit
docs.text:
File Owns Example change config/training.yml Shared defaults and each model's fit/evaluation policy Inputs, target, row/byte limits, model, search, CV, recipes config/pre_split.yml Fixed cleanup and eligibility recipes Convert a declared sentinel, filter missing labels config/preprocessing.yml Learned or fixed feature steps Fit an imputer and encoder on training folds config/inference.yml Saved-model selection and prediction publication Pinned version/champion, source, output, model-change policy config/features.yml Optional upstream feature domains Transform and merge Delta inputs config/serving.yml (optional) Publication, endpoint setup and rollout Existing store/table identity, concrete version, health policy deployment/targets.yml, variables.yml Workspace, UC namespaces, identities, compute and schedules Bind test to an authorized workspace and schema deployment/*requirements.txt Core and optional runtime dependencies Change a published Core pin; add the selected estimator's package src/features/ Trusted custom Python factories Register a custom step referenced from YAML

Built-in steps and their full parameter cards are in the Preprocessing YAML catalog. For every accepted training field, its default and complete examples of all three layouts, use the training configuration reference. Generated START_HERE.md, PREPROCESSING.md, SERVING.md and deployment/monitoring READMEs travel with the project and document its template revision.

docs.title: What a configuration change requires
docs.text:
Change Preview/redeploy Fit a new model Feature steps, training columns, estimator, search or split Yes Yes; scoring keeps the old fitted state until you select the new version Pinned scoring version, output destination or change policy Yes No, but check artifact/output compatibility Cron, pause status, identity or compute binding Validate and redeploy No; verify access and runtime compatibility Published feature values Run/observe publication No for latest-value requests; historical evaluation retains its saved evidence Core/dependency upgrade Follow release migration steps, validate and redeploy When saved-artifact runtime checks require it

Targets are test, syst and prod, with optional paired test_development, syst_development and prod_development targets. There is no standalone dev target. Personal schedules start paused. Input catalogs/schemas and tables must exist; template generation and deployment do not provision them.

Quick setup asks for the training layout, project name, task, source arrangement, tables, record keys (including composite keys), target and input columns, and the monitoring destination. Detailed setup also asks for split strategy, applicable date parsing, model, CV, scoring/promotion policies, compute and deployment choices. Serverless is the default. Answer-file examples are in skyulf-core/templates/databricks/examples/. The generated project has its own databricks.yml; Skyulf's root has no Bundle config.

New projects use YAML as the authoritative configuration. Edit shared settings under defaults and named model settings under models in config/training.yml:

Layout Training configuration single_model One model entry, normally models.main model_competition One entry per candidate, sharing target/split/quality defaults multi_target One entry per independent target, with its own inputs, model and policy

For multiple targets, config/inference.yml has a model_set mapping for the registered set, activation policy and scoring destinations. Put business output functions in src/features/scoring.py. For example, revenue and cost model entries can activate together and expose a saved profit rule. See model sets.

version: 1
defaults:
  training_layout: single_model
  engine: pandas
  save_preprocessing_diagnostics: false
models:
  main:
    model:
      type: linear_regression
      params: {}

This is a configuration excerpt; keep the generated source, keys, target, limits and quality settings. Model entries inherit complete values from defaults; nested mappings replace rather than deep-merge. Use YAML true, false, null. Do not add competing Python model files or workflow.json beside these files; each setting has one owner. Place shared training values in YAML defaults, model/tuning values in the named models entry, and scoring values in config/inference.yml.

Regression starts with Core linear_regression and heldout_rmse; classification starts with logistic_regression and heldout_accuracy. The pipeline remains editable: add registered Core preprocessing nodes and choose a task-compatible model. Model parameters are editable too:

models:
  main:
    model:
      type: random_forest_regressor
      params: {n_estimators: 100, max_depth: 8, random_state: 42}

A default model ID or an empty parameter object uses Core defaults.

In a JSON answer file, max_rows and max_input_mb are positive integer strings; the generated config/training.yml stores them as numbers. Enter record_key_columns as customer_id, observation_id and input_columns as income, age, with no brackets or quotes; the generated YAML stores ordered lists. Answer files use task-specific regression_model/classification_model and regression_metric/classification_metric.

docs.title: The command
docs.text:
Initialize a project from a Skyulf checkout:

databricks bundle init skyulf-core/templates/databricks --output-dir ./generated

docs.title: Guided setup and offline preview
docs.text:
Setup follows your answers; it does not inspect source tables or sample rows. Random full-snapshot training hides observation-date questions. Result-availability questions appear when you enable that filter; separate_outcomes enables it using the selected outcome availability timestamp. Schedule and policy-cluster details likewise appear only when selected.

setup_mode chooses how much to answer now. The default, quick, asks for the training layout, project name, task, source arrangement, record keys and target/input columns, and for the monitoring destination. It also asks for optional outcome-table and availability-column names. separate_all asks for a distinct scoring source. Both modes ask include_source_sql, default false: keep it off when your tables already exist and use preview.py --action sources to check them. Choose true only if you need an editable CREATE TABLE starter for tables that do not exist yet. In a JSON answer file this is "include_source_sql": "true" (a string). The starter is config/sources.sql; replace its namespace and type placeholders before running it yourself. Setup and deployment never execute it. SOURCES.md and the read-only source check remain available with either choice. A model set asks for the task and columns of each active branch. It accepts documented defaults for the remaining settings. Choose detailed to inspect model choices, competition candidates, branch recipes, search and deployment settings as they become relevant. Every list starts with its default, so Enter accepts it. Both modes produce the same files for the same answers. Explicit answer-file values are honored even for prompts hidden in quick mode; edit the generated config/*.yml and deployment/ files to change them afterwards.

docs.title: Monitoring destination
docs.text:
Both setup modes ask the monitoring questions after the deployment questions:

Question Answer Result monitoring true or false monitoring_enabled; monitoring_catalog defaults to each target's catalog (deployment/variables.yml) monitoring_schema Shared schema; omitted or blank uses skyulf_monitoring monitoring_schema in deployment/variables.yml development_monitoring (with personal development targets) true or false Development targets monitor into their own schema (deployment/monitoring.yml) development_monitoring_schema Any schema except the shared one development_monitoring_schema in deployment/variables.yml monitoring_dashboard none, create or connect The test dashboard block in deployment/monitoring.yml

Give every project the same schema, reserved for monitoring (for example skyulf_monitoring), not the project's own schema: all models then appear in one store and one dashboard. Every monitoring table and view is created in that one schema. Only one project creates the dashboard; the others connect to it, see the shared dashboard. Tables in your workspace lists every table the jobs create and where each one belongs.

monitoring: "true" sets monitoring_enabled to "true": train and score enroll models and run monitoring. monitoring: "false" sets it to "false": train and score run without monitoring. A user-selected schema is preserved, including an existing store. To use a central catalog instead of each target's own, set monitoring_catalog in deployment/variables.yml or per target in deployment/monitoring.yml. The schema is created on first use if the run-as identity may create schemas. Personal development targets set monitoring_enabled to "false" unless development_monitoring is "true"; then they monitor into their own separate store (see development monitoring).

Configured projects also include an independent weekly monitoring_cleanup job. It defaults to Sunday 04:00 UTC, confirmed cleanup and a 90-day minimum reference age. Its cron, confirmation and pause controls are editable per target; personal development keeps it paused. Review reference retention before deployment. Setup does not move or delete tables in an existing store.

To turn monitoring on later, set monitoring_catalog, monitoring_schema and monitoring_enabled: "true" in deployment/variables.yml, or per target under targets.<name>.variables, then redeploy. See monitoring store setup.

Before raising a project's Core pin, follow the Upgrade steps for generated Databricks projects listed under each release in the changelog.

Some settings are never asked, in either mode. Set them with --config-file using an existing example, or edit the generated config/training.yml before running preview:

Never asked Default test_size, random_state, stratify 0.2, 42, false training_sample_seed 42 min_improvement 0.0 risk_category Empty: the key is omitted from config/training.yml catalog, schema REPLACE_TEST_CATALOG, REPLACE_TEST_SCHEMA; prefill the test bindings in deployment/variables.yml and the preview/smoke defaults

Quick setup also skips the settings below. Detailed setup asks them when they apply to the chosen layout and earlier answers:

Asked only in detailed setup Quick default training_table_version (not asked for single_model) null: pin the latest snapshot at run start training_window_mode auto: full snapshot for random, rolling calendar for temporal cv_enabled, then cv_folds, cv_type, cv_shuffle, cv_random_state CV off; 5, k_fold, true, 42 max_rows, max_input_mb 10000, 64 training_sample_rows (per branch for model sets) null: read all rows within the limits; this never samples predictions save_preprocessing_diagnostics false: enable to check fitted preprocessing on a bounded holdout sample performance_policy_mode, task-specific metric, tolerance and baseline version off; when enabled, require outcomes and a monitoring store. See performance policy.

Most answer-file values are strings, including "true", "42" and "null"; min_improvement is a JSON number. The generated config/training.yml uses native YAML booleans and numbers, and omits keys whose value is null. Nonempty values under known removed answer names, including inference_mode, score_handoff, model_change_mode, auto_rebuild_on_cdf_expiry, preprocessing_probe, admit_probed_custom_steps and monitoring_catalog, now fail initialization instead of silently selecting defaults. Use the current names in the examples and generated schema. For monitoring, initialize with monitoring: "true"; monitoring_catalog remains an editable deployment variable. The Databricks CLI can still discard other unknown answer keys before the template sees them, so check the generated configuration when editing an answer file. This is an upstream CLI behavior, not a general unknown-key validation guarantee.

For fixed dates, start from random-window-init.example.json or temporal-delayed-results-init.example.json. For stratified CV and sampling, use guided-classification-init.example.json. From the Skyulf checkout, for example:

databricks bundle init skyulf-core/templates/databricks --config-file skyulf-core/templates/databricks/examples/guided-classification-init.example.json --output-dir ./generated

Review table and feature names in the example first. If you edit the generated config/training.yml, use full_snapshot, fixed_window, rolling_calendar or rolling_days for training_window_mode; auto is resolved during initialization. Run python src/tools/preview.py --action train from the generated project to validate the resulting combination.

For each date column you actually use, declare how it is stored:

Your answer Follow-up questions timestamp: database timestamp representing an instant No text format, source timezone or date-only question local_timestamp: database clock time without a timezone Which timezone this clock belongs to date: day with no clock time Source timezone, then whether to treat the day as midnight or reject it text: dates stored as strings Whether the text contains a date only, local date/time, or date/time with an offset; then its format and only the applicable timezone/date-only questions

For example, date-only text 2026-08-10 asks for its format, timezone and permission to use 00:00. Text 2026-08-10T14:30:00+02:00 asks for its format but not another timezone or midnight rule. Initialization fields event_time_kind/result_time_kind and event_text_kind/result_text_kind control these questions only; the generated config/training.yml stores only the resulting event_time_parsing/result_time_parsing rules. Runtime still validates actual values against your declared rules.

The project has two input table references. source_table_name contains the training observations. Targets may be embedded or joined from explicitly selected outcomes. score_source_table_name contains records to predict; blank reuses the training input. Neither is the output. Choose the result name through prediction_table_name, for example customer_predictions. It becomes prediction_table in the configured output schema, with any target resource suffix. Blank uses <project_name>_predictions.

Both modes ask source_layout: single_table uses embedded training targets; separate_outcomes joins actual targets into training and shares one feature source with scoring; separate_all uses distinct training and scoring sources. The separate layouts require label_table_name and label_available_at_column. Only separate_all prompts for score_source_table_name; explicit answer-file overrides in older projects are preserved. Quick setup keeps the default prediction_table_name; detailed setup asks for it for a single model or competition. See source contracts and validation. A multi_target project sets its scoring outputs in config/inference.yml.

Setting Meaning and example Training version A saved Delta table snapshot from the table's History, such as version 12. This pins input data, not model v12. null or missing resolves latest once at run start; an explicit nonnegative integer pins that snapshot for manual and scheduled runs. Source selection full_snapshot: use all eligible rows from that snapshot. fixed_window: use observation dates between your boundaries. rolling_calendar: derive recent complete months at every invocation. rolling_days: read the last lookback_days elapsed UTC days before every invocation. auto: full snapshot for random splitting, rolling calendar for temporal splitting. Result availability column A column such as claim_confirmed_at, recording when that row's answer became known. Only needed if availability filtering is enabled. Result cutoff Keep answers known by this instant, including equality. For a cutoff of September 15, an answer confirmed September 20 is excluded even if the observation occurred in August. An explicit cutoff is honored in every run; null derives invocation time minus result_availability_lag_hours. Date format For a text value 10/08/2026 14:30, use %d/%m/%Y %H:%M (day/month/year hour:minute). For 2026-08-10, use %Y-%m-%d. Database timestamp/date columns do not need a text format. Source timezone For values such as 2026-08-10 14:30 with no offset, specify where that clock time belongs, e.g. Europe/Copenhagen. Offset-bearing values such as 2026-08-10T14:30:00+02:00 identify their offset already. Date-only policy reject stops on values without clock time. midnight interprets 2026-08-10 as 00:00 in the explicitly selected source timezone. Training sample 10000 selects up to 10,000 eligible rows before splitting; with a 20% test split this usually means 8,000 train and 2,000 test. null uses all eligible rows within read limits. Prediction never samples. CV With five folds, score each search candidate using five training folds. Learned preprocessing is fitted within each fold. The final test set remains separate. Cron timezone The timezone of the job clock. A 03:00 schedule with Europe/Copenhagen uses Copenhagen time, including daylight saving. This does not interpret source dates or change the selected data window.

For training every six months on January 1 and July 1 at 03:00, choose scheduled and enter 0 0 3 1 1,7 ?. The cron is the schedule; nothing overrides it with a second monthly timer. Manual and scheduled runs use the same train action with identical snapshot/window selection rules. monthly_lookback_months separately controls how many complete months a rolling_calendar window reads; lookback_days does the same for rolling_days. Scoring has its own independent job schedule.

Detailed setup groups its questions into these sections. Quick setup asks only the task, source table, keys and columns from the first one.

Section What you choose Basics/data Engine/task, source and output tables, keys/features/target, split strategy, snapshot and window, availability/date parsing and input limits; sampling uses config Model A menu containing only models for the selected regression/classification task; defaults remain editable in the generated file Evaluation CV Enable evaluation with fold-local preprocessing; select folds, method, shuffle and seed Lifecycle Metric/gates, manual/automatic promotion, score selector/handoff and enabled retraining cron Compute Serverless or approved policy cluster and cost tags

Edit the ordered recipe in config/preprocessing.yml. Put fixed eligibility rules in config/pre_split.yml. Custom Python factories stay in the corresponding src/features/ modules. For example:

version: 1
recipes:
  default:
    - name: impute
      transformer: SimpleImputer
      params: {columns: [income, age], strategy: mean}
    - name: scale
      transformer: StandardScaler
      params: {columns: [income, age]}

Select preprocessing_recipe: default in the model's training configuration.

docs.title: Smoke result
docs.text:
smoke.py validates YAML, model configuration and Python syntax without executing editable hooks. Present src/features/ and src/composition/ packages also pass training's snapshot checks: package boundaries, declared assets, exact pins and saved-source size limits. Success JSON lists project_packages; a failure exits with code 1 and names its file/package and reason. Syntax errors include file, line and column. Dependencies are neither imported nor installed by this check.

Smoke does not prove data access, runtime dependency compatibility, model fit or deployment permission. Preview executes trusted builders; keep I/O out of imports and factories. A training sample is a real training input, not a no-write smoke mode.

docs.title: Generated files and preview output
docs.text:
Directory Responsibility src/jobs/ Databricks notebook entrypoints referenced by generated job resources src/features/ Custom Python factories, helpers and scoring rules referenced from YAML config/ Authoritative YAML, including the recipes in pre_split.yml and preprocessing.yml src/tools/ Preview, smoke checks and local graph/dashboard setup; see its README.md

To move an existing project to this layout, follow project upgrades.

docs.title: Local tools and preview
docs.text:
The generated src/tools/README.md is the short reference beside the scripts. Run commands from the project root with the matching Core package installed:

python src/tools/preview.py
python src/tools/preview.py --list-models
python src/tools/preview.py --list-preprocessors
python src/tools/preview.py --action train
python src/tools/preview.py --action score
Option Effect and default --action train\|score Inspect training or scoring; default: score. Training checks job preflight, including configured source/window selection. --list-models List installed Core model metadata for the configured task. A multi_target project lists both regression and classification models. --list-preprocessors List installed Core preprocessing metadata and configuration defaults. --catalog Override the local catalog binding; default is the initialization catalog value. --input-schema Override the input schema; default is the initialization schema value. --output-schema Override the output schema; default is the initialization schema value. --metadata-schema Override the registry/metadata schema; default is the initialization schema value. --resource-suffix Override the resource suffix; default is empty. --help Show the available command-line options.

Preview executes the trusted Python recipe to resolve its steps. Keep data access and training out of module-level code and build_preprocessing(). The preview shows the actual pipeline, input selection, final holdout, CV and score/promotion policies. Competition prints a Candidate: section for each candidate; model sets print a Branch: section for each branch. The same training rules apply to manual and scheduled runs. Preview starts no cloud job, reads no Delta rows, fits no model and does not execute save_preprocessing_diagnostics. A preview-resolution ValueError prints Configuration error: and exits with code 2; fix the reported setting before deployment. File/parsing failures that happen before resolution may raise directly.

This check does not test data values, parameter combinations, permissions or worker dependencies. Model/node metadata comes from the installed Core registry; availability depends on local packages and the selected options.

Preview uses its local default bindings. To inspect a deployment target, pass --catalog, --input-schema, --output-schema, --metadata-schema and --resource-suffix matching that target's resolved Bundle variables. Preview does not resolve target YAML or workspace ${...} substitutions. Run the real Bundle's validate --strict as well before deployment.

If initialization did not supply catalog/schema, these defaults remain the generated REPLACE_TEST_* placeholders. Editing Bundle target YAML does not update the preview script's defaults.

Other tool When to use it and command smoke.py Check YAML, Python syntax and package snapshots without running editable hooks: python src/tools/smoke.py. It accepts preview's five binding flags; see smoke result for status and exit codes. refresh_feature_graph.py After editing feature groups or merges: python src/tools/refresh_feature_graph.py. refresh_training_graph.py After editing competition candidates or model-set branch names/count: python src/tools/refresh_training_graph.py. Single-model projects remain unchanged.

Graph tools change local resource YAML. Validate and redeploy before running the updated job. They do not start a cloud job by themselves.

The answer-file examples include guided-classification-init.example.json (Polars, random forest, stratified CV and explicit sample) and random-window-init.example.json (random holdout inside an observation window, separate Copenhagen event and Vilnius result parsing). Replace example table/column names and snapshot pins with real values.

docs.title: Common errors and fixes
docs.text:
Symptom Fix Preview resolves the wrong schema Pass the target's --catalog, --input-schema, --output-schema, --metadata-schema and --resource-suffix. Preview does not read target YAML. An init example names columns absent from your table Edit its source, keys, inputs and targets; initialization never validates source rows. A quick setup did not ask about a model or search Edit config/training.yml, or choose detailed setup. Quick mode retains editable defaults. A newly enabled task has no notebook Generate a separate comparison project and transfer the required notebook, dependencies and graph together. Monitoring appears in a different schema than expected A catalog with an omitted or blank schema uses skyulf_monitoring. Set the existing store's schema explicitly in target variables; setup never migrates tables. Train or score fails with Set both monitoring_catalog and monitoring_schema. monitoring_enabled is "true", or only one destination value is set. Set both values for that target and redeploy, or set monitoring_enabled: "false" and clear both.

Continue with deployment and access, or upgrade an existing project.

docs.title: When you need it
docs.text:
Upgrade the Core pin, adopt a newer template graph, or add notebooks that were omitted during original setup. Compare a freshly initialized project in a separate directory; regeneration is not an in-place upgrade.

Public documentation describes the current revision. Read Upgrade steps for generated Databricks projects for every intervening release in the 0.9.x changelog. Keep the project pin and release-specific contracts together.

docs.title: What to edit
docs.text: Keep bundle identity, target resource keys, workspace root, output/state paths and edited recipes stable. Transfer reviewed changes to notebooks, dependencies and graphs as one compatible set.

docs.title: Configuration validation and migration
docs.text:
New projects declare config_version: 1 and task. The notebook validates the resolved configuration before training, registry access or output writes: resource names, distinct columns, reserved metadata names, budgets, model/task compatibility, metric/threshold domains and action-specific snapshot inputs. Actual source schema, keys and artifact compatibility are checked by the existing data-read and scoring services against the real data.

python src/tools/preview.py --action train (or --action score) runs the same check locally, without Spark or registry access, for every layout. For another action in a single_model project, run this from the project root:

from pathlib import Path

from skyulf.integrations.databricks.lifecycle.workflow import resolve_target_config
from skyulf.integrations.databricks.projects.project import load_project_workflow
from skyulf.integrations.databricks.projects.workflow_config import validate_workflow_config
from skyulf.integrations.databricks.projects.yaml_config import (
    project_config_path,
    read_workflow_config,
)

root = Path.cwd()
config = read_workflow_config(project_config_path(root))
loaded = load_project_workflow(config, root / "src/features")
resolved = resolve_target_config(loaded, {
    "catalog": "workspace",
    "input_schema": "my_inputs",
    "output_schema": "my_outputs",
    "metadata_schema": "my_models",
    "resource_suffix": "",
})
validate_workflow_config(resolved, action="approve")  # Or train, score, etc.

load_project_workflow adds the recipes and code from src/features; validating the raw YAML without it fails with pipeline.modeling.type must identify a registered Core model. Competition and multi_target projects load their candidates or branches differently; use preview.py for them.

For an older project's loaded JSON, migrate explicitly:

from skyulf.integrations.databricks.projects.workflow_config import migrate_workflow_config

updated = migrate_workflow_config(
    config, task="regression", score_handoff="after_alias_change"
)

Review/save updated, regenerate the affected job definitions and entrypoints, then validate and redeploy together. Migration returns a copy; it does not upload files, invent training dates, or change aliases. Legacy auto_champion maps to champion/automatic; legacy pinned_version maps to pinned/manual approval. Mixed policies, unknown config versions and contradictory existing task or handoff settings are rejected. The notebook checks the deployed workflow_contract and deployed_score_handoff markers against the JSON. These detect stale generated definitions; they are not workspace permissions or a complete audit of manually edited Jobs settings.

test, syst and prod have placeholder workspace and catalog bindings. Optional personal targets are test_development, syst_development and prod_development; there is no standalone dev target. Edit each target's host, catalog and input/output/metadata schema bindings, then validate with its designated profile. Replace the placeholders with your approved workspace values. Policy-backed compute uses the policy name, runtime, node type and cost tag supplied at initialization. Serverless compute needs none of those fields.

For a company policy requiring PayingRegNo, select that value as cost_tag_key and supply the approved registration number as cost_tag_value. The paying-reg-no-init.example.json example demonstrates both settings; the generic default remains CostCenter. This tag applies to policy-cluster compute. Selecting it does not assign a model risk category.

Advanced configuration accepts an optional risk_category, such as Low, Medium, or High. Leave it blank to omit the tag. The value remains editable in config/training.yml defaults and is recorded on future training runs and model versions; it does not change promotion gates or relabel existing versions.

docs.title: The command
docs.text:
uv pip install -r deployment/train-requirements.txt
python src/tools/smoke.py
python src/tools/preview.py --action train
python src/tools/preview.py --action score
databricks bundle validate --strict -t test --profile YOUR_PROFILE

These checks precede deployment. Verify saved-artifact runtime compatibility and the monitoring store upgrade before redeploying in your target.

docs.title: What you should see
docs.text:
Imports do not create a Spark session or cloud resource.

Regenerate and deploy notebooks, graph and the matching Core package together for graph contract 3. Existing graph-2 bundles retain their legacy runtime path; changing only a contract marker does not migrate a bundle. The workflow configuration schema remains version 1.

Notebook entrypoints are explicit: generated src/jobs/score.py calls job_runtime.run_score_notebook; lifecycle notebooks call job_runtime.run_lifecycle_notebook with a fixed phase. Deploy new entrypoints with the matching Core package. Existing direct run_notebook(task_role=...) callers remain supported: score delegates to the score entrypoint, while lifecycle keeps its sequential behavior and does not acquire durable phase/retry semantics. run_bundle_action, run_action and train_candidate retain their APIs.
