Edit recipe lists in config/preprocessing.yml, custom calculations in src/features/preprocessing.py, model settings in config/training.yml, and scoring/publication settings in config/inference.yml. These remain project choices; common workflow fixes ship in the Skyulf wheel instead of requiring edits to every generated notebook.

The library's skyulf.integrations.databricks modules are grouped under jobs, training, scoring, observability, model_sets, projects, data and lifecycle, with cross-domain contracts in shared. Crowded groups have smaller subpackages: jobs/{training,monitoring,lifecycle,shared}, training/{fitting,competition,tuning,thresholds,weights,shared} and scoring/{batch,incremental,shared}. Monitoring lives in observability/monitoring, with spark, performance and serving subpackages; charts and reports have their own folders. For example, notebook adapters import skyulf.integrations.databricks.jobs.shared.job_runtime. Use these paths directly. The old local_* integration modules and renamed APIs have been removed; update existing imports and model packages as described in upgrade integration code. The generated project's src/jobs directory remains unchanged.

The related MLflow library follows the same organization: skyulf.integrations.mlflow.{models,spark,lifecycle,registration,runs,shared}. Use models.pipeline_model and models.feature_model for fitted-pipeline adapters. Package import leaves MLflow optional; pyfunc adapters load it when selected. Worker source snapshots and certificates continue to cover the entire Skyulf package after the files move.

docs.title: Changes to adopt from earlier releases
Selection and promotion policy fields
docs.text: Earlier projects used one model_selection_mode. Generated projects use score_model_selection and promotion_policy together, plus follow_champion. Remove model_selection_mode when adding the two fields; mixed or partial configurations fail before training or scoring. Migrate the configuration, all notebook entrypoints and the job graph together; changing only a configuration file is not enough. Direct Core callers can still pass the legacy value with a deprecation warning; migrate_workflow_config above shows how each value maps.

docs.title: Final report links
docs.text:
The Where to look table needs two additions in a project generated before they existed:

  1. In resources/train.job.yml, add workspace_host: ${workspace.host} to the base_parameters of the training_report task. Generated files carry it in both layout branches. Without it, the table renders but every link is plain text.
  2. In src/jobs/training_report.py (or src/jobs/models_report.py for multi_target), pass display_html=globals().get("displayHTML") to the runtime call. Without it, the task prints a plain text summary and no table.

Compare both files with a freshly generated project, then validate and redeploy.

docs.title: Replacing a champion produced by the previous release
docs.text: Models load only under their producing runtime, so the first training after an upgrade cannot compare its candidate with the old champion. Review the candidate and approve it with allow_unloadable_champion=true; see champion from an older Core release. Until then, scoring the old champion needs the old runtime. Model sets must be replaced with the release that produced their champion set.

docs.title: Lifecycle tags and alias recovery
docs.text:
Run every job that reads or writes lifecycle tags for one registered model on the same Core version, and upgrade them together.

  • promotion_<event_id> tags carry an at timestamp. Older Core readers reject it, so downgrading a job after such a tag exists makes its lifecycle checks fail. Current readers still accept tags without at; old tags are not backfilled.
  • Alias recovery intent is stored as framed chunks with "encoding":"json-framed-v1". Current readers also read the earlier unframed intent. An older reader cannot recover a framed intent and reports Alias intent digest differs from its stored chunks. Upgrade the operator environment that runs recovery as well.

docs.title: Model sets
docs.text:
• Sets registered before quality evidence was saved remain scoreable. Retrain and package them before approving through the Bundle. The low-level SDK keeps an explicit functional-only approval for those packages.
  • model_set_<branch>_* version tags exist only on sets registered after they were introduced; older versions are not backfilled.
  • Projects configured through src/modeling/model_set.py, a src/composition/ package or Python recipe builders remain readable through their original loader. Do not define the same set or recipe in both Python and YAML.
  • New tuning and fitted-configuration parameters appear only on training runs made with the updated Core; existing runs are not backfilled.

docs.title: Spark scoring changes
docs.text: A whole-frame MLflow package logged without a Spark safety certificate cannot use batch_compute: spark. Log a new certified version. Configurations without batch_compute keep whole-frame scoring.

docs.title: Project layout and configuration files
docs.text:
• Projects configured through older Python or JSON files remain readable. Keep one owner per setting; do not define it in both the old file and YAML.
  • To adopt the current layout, initialize a separate project, transfer values into its YAML files and copy custom functions into src/features/. Model versions already registered keep their saved source snapshot.
  • resources/workflow.jobs.yml became train.job.yml and score.job.yml. Keep the train/score resource keys, bundle name and root so jobs are updated in place.
  • The standalone dev target became test/syst/prod development pairs with their own roots and personal schema bindings. Generate the new layout separately, keep the old root during the change and never delete old jobs or tables as part of it.
  • Answer files use plain-text key/input fields and task-specific regression_*/classification_* model and metric fields. Regenerate old answer files; their older names are still accepted.
  • max_bytes became max_input_mb, and earlier key/result-time names became record_key_columns and result_available_at_column. Neither has an alias: regenerate and retrain.
  • Temporal configurations must name their window mode explicitly.
  • New projects have no src/features/custom/ package. Scoring callbacks live at the end of scoring.py (scoring.<function>). Existing projects may keep custom/; custom.<file>.<factory> references still resolve.
  • Training evidence from experimental releases, and candidates saved without sampling evidence, must be recreated before approval.

docs.title: Monitoring and serving changes
docs.text:
• New projects ask for the monitoring catalog and schema and start with monitoring_enabled: "false" when they are blank. Existing projects keep monitoring_enabled: "true" in deployment/variables.yml; with a blank destination their train and score jobs stop with Set both monitoring_catalog and monitoring_schema. Set both names, or set monitoring_enabled: "false", then redeploy.
  • Older monitoring stores need the owner to rerun store initialization, which adds retraining_requests and serializable isolation, before producers without CREATE privileges upgrade.
  • Deploy train, score and monitoring jobs with the same Core so the development-target monitoring guard and activation-order metadata apply together.
  • The score graph runs prepare_monitoring -> monitoring_ready -> monitor_model. The asynchronous monitoring_invocation_id and the drift_report.py / retrain_on_drift.py wrappers were removed; update projects that still call them.
  • Upgrade every inventory reader before the first serving enrollment; older runtimes reject the serving field. Serving latency classes and logging-error counts appear only in reports recorded after the upgrade.
  • Rollout health.maximum_latency_ms limits p99 execution time when it is recorded, with the maximum as fallback; earlier controllers checked the maximum. Review configured limits before upgrading the rollout job.
  • Add bundle_target: ${bundle.target} to the daily_rollout task parameters so rollout evidence names the target that ran it instead of monitoring.environment.
  • If your CI/CD passes --var pipeline_owner or requires target permissions, add a pipeline_owner variable and each target's permissions list as in a newly generated project; see job access.

docs.title: Upgrade integration code
docs.text:
Use the purpose-based module, class and function names from the Python SDK guide. The previous fitted-pipeline and integration names containing local have been removed, including their forwarding modules. Update those imports and call sites.

Replace runtime="local" with runtime="standalone"; local is not a valid runtime value. Choose engine="pandas" or "polars" separately, and use runtime="databricks" for UC Delta publication.

Saved pickle or MLflow packages that reference removed module or class names may fail to load. Rebuild and log those model packages with the updated imports before upgrading their consumers.

Persisted values such as kind="local_pipeline", mode="local_pipeline" and execution_scope="whole_frame_local" are unchanged. Keep these artifact-format values; Python naming does not change execution admission, payload checks or resource budgets. Portable bundles continue to use predict_local.

docs.title: Common errors and fixes
docs.text:
Symptom Fix Alias intent digest differs from its stored chunks The recovery environment runs an older Core; install the writers' version. It does not mean the evidence is corrupt. Report links are plain text Add workspace_host: ${workspace.host} to the training_report task. Graph contract mismatch Deploy matching notebooks, graph and Core; changing a marker alone is not migration. A notebook is absent after toggling a feature Copy that feature's generated notebook, resource and dependency changes from the comparison project. Saved model rejects its runtime Use the producer-compatible environment or retrain; changing a requirements pin does not migrate artifacts. Monitoring view is missing a new column Run the documented store upgrade before refreshing the dashboard; refresh does not change SQL definitions.

The validation snippet loads the project's own files. The migration snippet assumes an already loaded config. Both return data to review and do not perform a cloud deployment.

docs.title: When you need it
docs.text:
Enable automatic training only after drift or performance-loss reporting is understood and the project training source is maintained with real targets. The new candidate still follows normal evaluation, promotion and approval.

Eligible signal Retraining decision Neither drift nor performance loss No training request. Drift only, with on_drift: retrain One request, subject to shared guards. Performance loss only, with policy mode: retrain One request, subject to shared guards. Both signals eligible One combined request, not two training jobs. Missing labels, unavailable metrics or policy mode: report No performance-driven training request; drift remains independently eligible.

The two retraining opt-ins form an OR decision, not an AND requirement: on_drift: retrain enables drift; a model's performance policy mode: retrain enables performance loss. Setting only one leaves the other disabled. For performance, eligible labels, a matching baseline, tolerance and the configured consecutive-window count must pass first. Missing labels, an unavailable metric, mode: report, or a historical backfill cannot independently start training. Both eligible signals are combined into one idempotent project training request. The resulting candidate still goes through the existing evaluation, promotion and approval rules; detecting a change does not itself approve a new model.

flowchart LR
    A["monitor_model"] --> B["monitoring_report"]
    B --> C["evaluate_retraining"]
    C --> D["Shared guards: fresh rows, cooldown, no active run"]
    D --> E["One request to the train job"]
    E --> F["Normal evaluation and approval"]

docs.title: What to edit
docs.text:
Set these variables under targets.<target>.variables in deployment/targets.yml to request this project's existing train job:

on_drift: "retrain" # Default: disabled
on_drift_cooldown_hours: "24"
on_drift_min_new_training_rows: "20"

These cooldown and fresh labeled training-row controls are shared by drift and performance retraining requests. Set a model's performance policy to mode: "retrain" inside the JSON mapping to enable its performance trigger; on_drift remains an independent setting. Either trigger uses the same guarded train job request. Neither trigger bypasses model evaluation or approval.

Set training_table_version: null. Maintain the configured training features upstream. Targets may be embedded in that table or read through an explicit training_label_table join. With the join, use training_label_table_version: null for fresh runs: new eligible outcomes can count as changed training data even when feature rows are unchanged. Monitoring's optional label binding alone does not enable the training join or write outcomes back to a source table. Freshness means eligible training values changed relative to the active model; it does not require their arrival time to be after the drift report. The request records the assessed Delta version and content digest. The train run independently pins its input snapshot at initialization; inspect its saved training specification and membership evidence to establish what was actually used if data changed again. Predictions are never substituted for real targets. Random splitting includes some new eligible rows in training; merely reshuffling old rows does not qualify. Temporal rows qualify once they enter the training side of the time boundary. Changing the table, column roles, split strategy or engine needs an explicit training run before automatic retraining can assess the new contract.

A scheduled training job with training_window_mode: fixed_window repeats the same date interval. The project preview warns but permits this intentional combination. Use rolling_days or rolling_calendar to advance the interval. This warning does not alter automatic retraining's freshness and cooldown checks.

New data has to reach the training read before any trigger can pass the fresh-rows guard:

flowchart TD
    N["New measurements inserted"] --> TT[("Training source")]
    O["Actual outcomes inserted"] --> OT[("Outcomes table")]
    TT --> J["Training read: pinned versions"]
    OT -. "only with training_label_table" .-> J
    J --> F{"New eligible labelled rows since the active model?"}
    F -- "no" --> X["No request"]
    F -- "yes" --> G{"Cooldown passed and no active train run?"}
    G -- "no" --> X
    G -- "yes" --> R["Request recorded as intent, then submitted with its run"]
    R --> E["Train run: normal evaluation, promotion and approval"]

If new outcomes exist only in the monitoring label table, they do not reach training without training_label_table, so they cannot satisfy the fresh-rows guard. Training rows that already contain actual targets still work without a join. Predictions are never used as targets on either path.

For a daily rolling window, configure defaults or a model entry in config/training.yml:

training_window_mode: rolling_days
split_strategy: temporal
event_column: transaction_time
lookback_days: 90
holdout_days: 14

transaction_time must be a real selected source column, using the existing date parsing settings. Each run selects the preceding 90 elapsed UTC days; temporal holds out the latest 14 days. For random use holdout_days: null and test_size. Random with full_snapshot needs no event column. Advancing a window does not guarantee new training data or better performance.

docs.title: Serving performance needs both gates
docs.text:
Set the online enrollment's inline performance_policy.mode to retrain, and add a mode: retrain policy for that same fully qualified model in the job deployment variable monitoring_performance_policies, then redeploy the monitoring job. The inline policy determines the measured online verdict; the job-level mapping enables evaluation of guarded training requests. Only changing the inline policy leaves automatic requests disabled when on_drift is disabled and the job mapping remains {}. Existing ownership, freshness, cooldown and promotion checks still apply; retraining does not update an endpoint.

Requests are stored in the owned retraining_requests Delta table of the monitoring store, with job claims, request evidence and run IDs. Store bootstrap creates that table with the other store objects. The monitoring identity needs SELECT/MODIFY on it and CAN MANAGE RUN on the train job, in addition to monitoring's read permissions. Keep train max_concurrent_runs: 1. Ambiguous API failures retain the pending claim; repair the monitoring job's evaluate_retraining task to retry the same idempotency token. An unresolved request blocks other automatic requests instead of guessing that submission failed. The independent monitoring job revisits delayed labels and can submit guarded training requests. All project layouts use the same store and shared dashboard.

docs.title: The command
docs.text:
Validate and redeploy after changing target variables. Update enrollment through activation/scoring, or resubmit the online enrollment after changing its inline policy. Then observe:

databricks bundle validate --strict -t test --profile YOUR_PROFILE
databricks bundle deploy -t test --profile YOUR_PROFILE
databricks bundle run monitoring -t test --profile YOUR_PROFILE

The evaluate_retraining task reads saved evidence after monitoring_report. To use the recurring path, unpause the verified monitoring schedule. No dashboard switch enables training.

docs.title: What you should see
docs.text:
The independent Spark monitoring job runs monitor_model -> monitoring_report -> evaluate_retraining after a score request or on its unpaused schedule. The scoring job's native Run Job task provides the exact validated receipt and exposes the child run directly in the graph. The check reads the saved observation, checks the current enrolled version, and compares actual eligible training rows with the saved model's training data. Feature quality/schema problems, incomplete drift checks, stale observations, unchanged training data, active training and cooldown prevent a new request. The checks do not claim a request until submission; the request path repeats them before claiming, so a concurrent run or data change cannot bypass guards. One request starts the complete single, competition or model-set train job. Spark monitoring and scoring do not wait for that train run or alter its quality/approval policy. The trigger resolves the unique deployed ${bundle.name}_train job name at run time, preserving the actual scoring job's development prefix and avoiding a Bundle dependency cycle with training's scoring handoff.

Shared guards still require usable input, fresh training data, cooldown and no active or duplicate request. Earlier run graphs keep the task names they ran with; open the current job or a new run to see monitoring_report and evaluate_retraining.

A submission records the request identity and training run ID; a skip records why its guard did not pass. Performance action receipts are kept in performance_actions and presented through performance_history. Read the training action separately from the performance verdict: request_eligible does not mean a run was submitted.

An active performance policy that is report-only never requests training. Missing labels or an unavailable performance baseline do not disable an independently eligible drift trigger. Both eligible triggers share a single idempotent project request.

docs.title: Common errors and fixes
docs.text: Why no new train run appeared Fix or interpretation Neither trigger opted in on_drift and per-model mode: retrain are independent switches. Enable only the intended policy. Feature quality/schema problems or incomplete checks Resolve the data problem; a detected drift flag alone does not bypass quality guards. Stale evidence or changed enrolled version Observe the current concrete enrollment again. Unchanged or insufficient new labeled training rows Maintain the configured training source with eligible true targets; a label table alone or reshuffling old rows does not qualify. Changed table, roles, split or engine Run an explicit training job to establish the new contract first. Cooldown, active train run or duplicate/pending request Inspect request receipts and run history; keep max_concurrent_runs: 1. Ambiguous submission response Repair the same evaluate_retraining task and idempotency token; an unresolved claim intentionally blocks another automatic request. Loss recorded only in a historical backfill Backfilled evidence remains visible but cannot independently submit training. A new trained candidate did not move endpoint traffic Retraining preserves lifecycle approval and does not reconfigure serving; use the serving workflow.

docs.title: Score saved models and publish Delta predictions
docs.text:
The generated score job loads a saved model, finds eligible source records, produces predictions, and commits them with source/model provenance. It does not train a model. Use this guide after training and selecting a version. For a complete project sequence, start with the Databricks walkthrough.

The example below scores customer churn from a separate unlabeled Delta table. It shows exactly where to configure the source, version, eligibility and output. Workspace SQL and job results are labeled expected; local configuration and callback checks do not establish a deployed prediction run.

docs.title: 1. Choose the source and saved model
docs.text:
Keep these responsibilities separate:

File Scoring responsibility config/training.yml Model identity, record keys, feature columns, training recipe and local row/byte limits. config/inference.yml Scoring source, prediction destination, version selection and change/recovery policies. config/scoring.yml Rules captured with the next model version: reuse pre-split, eligibility, business outputs and combined rules. src/features/scoring.py Optional custom callbacks selected with custom: scoring.<function>. resources/score.job.yml, deployment/ Deployed task graph, compute, schedule, identity, timeouts and retries.

For the customer preprocessing example, use these training defaults fields, retaining the rest of the generated classification configuration:

record_key_columns: [customer_id]
input_columns: [age, income, tenure, segment]
target_column: churn

The record key must identify one source observation, be unique/nonmissing, and remain outside model inputs. Use BIGINT or STRING for the generated single-model prediction publisher. A date/timestamp is not a supported record key; a historical customer table usually needs a separate observation ID.

Create the following new scoring source in Databricks, replacing the schema with your own. The churn label is intentionally absent. Match these input types to the training model's saved schema; changing the source names alone cannot change a saved model's input contract. For this example, load the training columns age, income and tenure as DOUBLE too, before fitting; keep customer_id as BIGINT, segment as STRING and churn as BIGINT. This permits nullable numeric scoring inputs under the same saved schema. If an existing model was fitted with integer age/tenure, align the source to that contract or fit a new version using this explicit schema. Preview does not inspect table dtypes.

CREATE TABLE workspace.demo.customer_score (
  customer_id BIGINT,
  age DOUBLE,
  income DOUBLE,
  tenure DOUBLE,
  segment STRING
) USING DELTA TBLPROPERTIES ('delta.enableChangeDataFeed' = 'true');

INSERT INTO workspace.demo.customer_score VALUES
  (101, 35.0, 2500.0, 3.0, 'A'),
  (102, -1.0, 4000.0, 4.0, 'B'),
  (103, NULL, 1500.0, 2.0, 'A'),
  (104, 60.0, NULL, 5.0, 'NEW');

CDF must be enabled before incremental scoring starts. The source and output must be different Delta objects. The job identity needs source read/CDF access, model access and prediction-output write permissions. Do not prefill the output with arbitrary predictions: first-run bootstrap requires a compatible empty output or a new output provisioned by the workflow.

For a single model or competition winner, replace config/inference.yml with this complete local-scoring example. Replace version 1 with the concrete version you inspected in training evidence:

version: 1
batch_compute: single_node
initial_scoring: full_snapshot
score_source_table: workspace.demo.customer_score
prediction_table: "{catalog}.{output_schema}.customer_scores{resource_suffix}"
score_model_selection: pinned_version
model_version: "1"
on_model_change: score_new_rows
rescore_when_history_expires: false
follow_champion: false

local means bounded whole-frame prediction, including on Databricks compute. It is not a choice of workstation versus cloud. max_rows and max_input_mb remain in training.yml and bound each local scoring materialization. The first run can read the entire source, so budget for it as well as later increments.

Selection Single model / competition Independent-target model set Normal run pinned_version uses the positive string model_version; champion resolves the controlled champion for that run. Uses the controlled champion of model_set.model_name; approve a set champion first. The ordinary top-level pinned selector is not the set selector. One-run override score_model_version selects a concrete model version. The same parameter selects a concrete set version, not one component's version. Training score handoff After a successful alias change, uses the configured scoring selector. After an approved set alias change, uses the set selection.

Selecting a pinned version does not approve it, change aliases, or retrain it. Changing to champion selection does not by itself make an unapproved candidate the champion. A model set carries its saved component versions; do not try to replace one component through the score job's version parameter.

Training and scoring reference the same existing input table by default; neither reference creates it. Separate them when labeled training data and new scoring data have different lifecycles. With the default full_snapshot, the first score includes all existing rows, including historical labeled observations; confirm that population before running. Choose a table layout compares one shared table with separate measurement and outcome tables.

docs.title: Start with new records only
docs.text:
Set this in config/inference.yml before the first score run when existing rows are training history and should not receive production predictions:

initial_scoring: from_now

Quick and detailed setup both ask for this choice. The default is full_snapshot for every layout. It applies to single models, competition winners and model sets, using local pandas/Polars or supported Spark UDF scoring. It does not change training selection or serving endpoint requests.

For example, suppose the source has 50,000 rows at Delta version 12:

Run Source Result with from_now First score Version 12, 50,000 old rows Records version 12 in the prediction receipt; writes zero predictions. Repeat without changes Still version 12 No-op; the checkpoint stays unchanged. Next score Version 13 inserts 100 new keys Scores those 100 rows. The 50,000 old rows remain excluded. Model changes with rescore_all Current source snapshot Recomputes eligible rows added after version 12; keeps the original exclusion boundary.

The first score succeeds and can complete a training-to-scoring handoff even with zero predictions. Monitoring has no production predictions to evaluate yet; this is not a zero error rate or a measured performance score. An append after the pinned version, including one arriving during the first run, belongs to a later scoring run.

The receipt fixes initial_scoring and scoring_start_version. Changing the choice on an existing prediction target fails; use a new target for a separate scoring history. Existing projects and historical receipts continue to use full_snapshot unless a new target explicitly selects from_now.

Retention and keys: record keys must be immutable and never reused. Normal increments need only the CDF interval since the last successful score. A normal model-change or model-set source-correction rebuild uses keys in the last committed prediction snapshot (including excluded rows), plus new inserts after its source watermark, joined to the current source snapshot. Keep that prediction checkpoint and the recent CDF interval readable. It does not need the original starting snapshot, even when months have passed.

Approved CDF-expiry recovery cannot reconstruct missing insert history this way. It needs the source snapshot at the original starting version to exclude its keys. Retain that snapshot and its data files if you require this recovery option. If it has expired or been removed by VACUUM, recovery fails; it never silently expands to all historical rows. Restore the snapshot or choose a new prediction target and explicitly establish a new starting policy. Source updates/deletes still follow the separate source-change policy.

docs.title: 2. Decide eligibility before training the version
docs.text: Scoring rules are saved with the model. Configure them before training and packaging the version you will score. Editing today's scoring.yml or scoring.py does not rewrite an already registered version.

docs.title: The three scoring sections
docs.text:
config/scoring.yml has three rule sections. Each runs at a different moment:

Section Runs Does Example eligibility Before the model Decides whether a row may get a prediction. The hour is missing, so this record gets no prediction. outputs After the model Adds columns computed from the prediction and inputs. Probability 0.85 adds risk_band: high. combined After all models of a model set Computes one result from several models. Revenue prediction minus cost prediction gives profit.

A row rejected by eligibility is not deleted. It stays in the result with scoring_status: excluded, its exclusion_reason and an empty prediction. Outputs run only on predicted rows and keep the raw prediction unchanged.

The bike demand example uses all three:

  1. Eligibility: a row without hr is excluded with the reason missing_hour.
  2. Outputs: each model adds nonnegative_demand. A raw prediction of -2 gives 0 in the new column; the raw prediction is kept.
  3. Combined: total_demand adds the nonnegative_demand columns of the casual and registered models. If either model excluded the row, no total is produced; a missing prediction is never counted as zero.

Two settings with similar names do different things:

  • mode: combined applies the saved pre-split filters, then the eligibility rules, then the outputs.
  • The combined: list defines cross-model rules. A single model does not use it.

Choose mode: custom to use only your own eligibility and output rules, and mode: pre_split to reuse only the pre-split filters.

mode in scoring.yml What runs pre_split (default) Saved pre-split eligibility; empty recipe leaves the ordinary prediction schema. custom Custom eligibility, model prediction, then custom output rules. combined Saved pre-split eligibility, custom eligibility on its survivors, model prediction, custom outputs.

With pre_split/combined, a filter reading the target needs an explicit decision: skip_target_pre_split_steps: true skips those filters because scoring has no actual label. The default false rejects that recipe, including during training preview. It does not invent labels. A mixed filter reading both target and features is skipped as a whole, so split the rules when the feature check should remain. Custom mode rejects a true skip flag because it does not reuse pre-split.

Pre-split replay uses a copy to decide membership; the saved model applies its fixed feature normalization once to the original accepted inputs. Combined custom callbacks also receive those original accepted inputs. A filter's input must be available in input_columns; it can later be dropped in preprocessing if it is not a model feature. Deduplication compares the current batch, not all records ever scored.

If pre-split excludes every row, neither custom callbacks nor the model runs. An empty recipe in combined mode still runs its custom sections. The target-skip switch does not change the target or synthesize a label; fixed target/feature normalization is projected onto features for saved inference. Preview lists the retained and skipped step names. Empty pre-split mode retains ordinary output columns when there is no active scoring policy.

The generated config/scoring.yml starts with version: 1, mode: pre_split, skip_target_pre_split_steps: false and empty eligibility, outputs and combined lists. Changing mode alone does not activate sample rules. Nonempty eligibility/output lists require custom or combined mode. combined is a separate cross-model list, described in the model set guide.

docs.title: A complete YAML rule example
docs.text:
Replace config/scoring.yml with this document. It selects custom mode, so the reasons come from these eligibility rules. No Python edits are needed:

version: 1
mode: custom
skip_target_pre_split_steps: false
eligibility:
  - name: observed_age
    check: required_values
    params: {columns: [age]}
  - name: adult_age
    check: value_range
    params: {column: age, minimum: 18.0, maximum: 120.0}
outputs:
  - name: churn_risk_band
    version: "1"
    rule: prediction_band
    params:
      column: probability_1
      thresholds: [0.3, 0.7]
      labels: [low, medium, high]
      output: risk_band
    columns: [{name: risk_band, dtype: string}]
combined: []

Each rule has a unique name and a string version (default "1"). Required-values checks take params.columns; range checks take a column and at least one finite inclusive minimum/maximum. Range checks reject missing, nonnumeric and infinite values; required-values checks report missing fields in the declared order. Bands require increasing finite thresholds and one more label than threshold. Their single declared column must match params.output (default band), dtype string. Unknown fields, duplicate YAML keys and invalid parameters fail during preparation.

For project-specific logic, replace check/rule with custom: scoring.<function> and keep params and declared columns. Eligibility receives (frame, params); outputs receive (frame, predictions, params). Implement the named helper in src/features/scoring.py, with relative imports for adjacent project modules. Custom references select captured project code, not external import paths or YAML expressions. Per-component eligibility/output callbacks receive only that model's saved input columns; shared callbacks must read columns available to every component. Cross-model combined callbacks instead receive the set's union of component input columns and keys, plus the component prediction results.

Older Python-only projects still use exported build_model_rules() or legacy build_scoring() (the former takes precedence), plus build_combined_rules(). A project containing scoring.yml must not also define/export those builders: remove them after moving declarations to YAML, retaining custom helper functions. Previously saved model versions continue to replay their saved policy and code.

The probability rule assumes the saved class order is [0, 1] and the classifier exports probability_1 for churn. Check the saved output/class schema; the suffix is a class position, not a promise about every target's label. If the estimator has no probability output, choose an available output or remove this rule. The bands are business thresholds, separate from the model's decision threshold.

Eligibility rules return one reason per row: null means accepted, text means excluded. They do not drop rows. The first exclusion reason wins. Output rules run only for accepted rows and return exactly their declared new columns. Callbacks receive pandas frames on both supported model engines, with an ordered RangeIndex that must be preserved. The rule name, version, function path, parameters and output dtype are captured with the model. Keep callbacks deterministic and independent of mutable network, clock or filesystem state; use captured assets for lookup data. Eligibility runs before temporal preprocessing: excluded rows do not enter lag/rolling history, and an all-excluded batch retains the previous tail. Input schema validation still applies to every request.

With the shown source, the expected eligibility is:

customer_id Expected status Reason Prediction/business output 101 predicted null Saved model result; risk_band follows its probability. 102 excluded outside_range:age Null. 103 excluded missing:age Null. 104 predicted null Saved preprocessing fills income and handles NEW; band depends on the fitted model.

The band callback itself maps probabilities [0.2, 0.3, 0.7] to [low, medium, high]; values on a threshold enter the upper band. This is a fixed callback example, not a measured model prediction. A rule exception fails the batch; it does not turn an implementation error into an exclusion reason.

docs.title: 3. Preview, train and score
docs.text:
After editing the future model's rules, run from the project root:

python src/tools/smoke.py
python src/tools/preview.py --action train
python src/tools/preview.py --action score

Smoke checks structure; preview resolves the editable declarations and trusted factories. Neither reads the source table, loads a UC model, runs Spark workers or validates cloud permissions. Train and inspect the new version using the training workflow, then update model_version or approve/select the desired champion. Use a fresh prediction-table name when introducing scoring-status/business columns into a deployment with an older output schema.

Deploy matching configuration and code, then score:

databricks bundle validate --strict -t test --profile YOUR_PROFILE
databricks bundle deploy -t test --profile YOUR_PROFILE
databricks bundle run score -t test --profile YOUR_PROFILE

To select a version only for this run, replace 7 with a real version:

databricks bundle run score -t test --profile YOUR_PROFILE --params score_model_version=7

The override belongs to the score job. It is not a train-job parameter and does not mutate inference.yml. A saved-model run uses its captured preprocessing and scoring rules, even if the editable project now contains different functions.

docs.title: 4. Open the correct task and inspect the output
docs.text:
All three layouts use the same default score task keys. The notebook differs: single_model and model_competition call src/jobs/score.py; multi_target calls src/jobs/score_models.py.

Generated graph Task keys / where to inspect Default recovery flag false score, monitoring_allowed, prepare_monitoring, monitoring_ready, monitor_model. Open score for prediction results; there is no scoring_report task. Recovery flag true Adds recovery_needed, recover_predictions, scoring_report. Open scoring_report for the ordinary-or-recovery final result. Monitoring tail monitoring_allowed permits the shared production deployment path; development runs skip that tail. prepare_monitoring validates scoring evidence; monitoring_ready controls the separate monitoring-job handoff.

The result summary reports the selected concrete model, source end version, input/output counts, prediction table Delta version and no-op/write status. When scoring policy metadata is present, the committed manifest also reports predicted_count and excluded_count. Monitoring failure after publication does not undo a committed prediction write. For a first pinned candidate, enrollment may require monitoring_action=prepare_references; follow monitor enrollment and retry the original score identity rather than deleting predictions or inventing a watermark. A no-op may show the previous write's model provenance alongside this run's selected model; those are not interchangeable.

For the single-model example, query the resolved output name shown in the job. This SQL assumes no resource suffix; substitute the actual table otherwise:

SELECT customer_id, prediction, probability_1, risk_band,
       scoring_status, exclusion_reason, model_name, model_version, run_id
FROM workspace.demo.customer_scores
ORDER BY customer_id;

Expected: four outcome rows, two predicted and two excluded. Exact estimates and bands depend on the saved fitted model. Excluded rows have null prediction and business columns; retaining their keys records that the source observation was processed. The first successful write's receipt binds the source identity/end version and prediction output. An all-excluded increment still commits its outcomes and advances the watermark. A failed rule or write advances neither.

docs.title: Inference settings reference
docs.text:
These fields belong in config/inference.yml. Defaults below are the values project generation writes. The model_set mapping exists only in multi_target projects.

Field Type / generated default Allowed values and effect version Integer 1 Companion-file format; distinct from deployed workflow_contract. batch_compute String single_node single_node or spark; selects whole-frame or admitted distributed batch scoring. score_source_table Three-part name; training source by default Delta input; deployment table placeholders are expanded. prediction_table Three-part name; project predictions name Single-model/competition output, with the generated resource suffix. score_model_selection String pinned_version pinned_version or champion for single-model/competition scoring. model_version Positive version string; generated "1" when pinned Required concrete pin for pinned single-model selection; replace with an inspected version. on_model_change String score_new_rows score_new_rows or rescore_all; controls behavior when model/set selection changes. rescore_when_history_expires Boolean false Opt into the matching deployed recovery graph for recognized expiry only. follow_champion Boolean false true or false; must match deployed graph parameters. spark_udf_env_manager String; generated only for Spark local on serverless or virtualenv on the generated job-cluster route; must match supported compute/dependencies. spark_udf_prediction_batch_rows Integer 10000 for Spark 1 to 100000 rows per model prediction call, not a whole-source limit. model_set Mapping; multi_target only Set identity, destination, rules, publication and promotion policy. See the model set fields.

docs.title: How new rows are discovered
docs.text:
The first successful run scores a pinned snapshot of the source. Later runs use the committed source Delta watermark and read CDF from the next version through a pinned upper version. They do not use MAX(customer_id) or an application clock to guess which records are new. Keys identify outcomes; Delta versions identify the source change window.

For example, after the first four rows have been committed:

INSERT INTO workspace.demo.customer_score VALUES
  (105, 45.0, 3500.0, 4.0, 'B');

Run score again. Expected: one new outcome for 105. With no further source changes, another run is a no-op and does not append duplicates. Keep the source and output under their declared ownership: replacing the source table changes its identity, and manually rewriting the prediction target can invalidate its receipt. The workflow rejects those changes rather than guessing a watermark.

docs.title: Source changes are separate from model changes
docs.text:
Event Default behavior Explicit alternative New source INSERT Score and append that observation. No special setting required. Selected model version changes score_new_rows leaves old predictions intact and uses the selected version for new inserts. on_model_change: rescore_all starts a versioned generation, preserving the initial scoring boundary. Readable source UPDATE/DELETE Ordinary single-model/competition insert scorer rejects it; model sets also default to reject. Model sets alone support model_set.on_source_change: rescore_all. Required CDF history expired Fail with history-loss evidence. Deploy the optional recognized-expiry recovery graph described below.

With score_new_rows, one target can contain predictions from several model versions. Use stored provenance when comparing rows. Merely choosing a different version with no new source rows does not rescore the old population.

With rescore_all, the logical prediction name is a managed view over a physical <prediction_table>_v<version> generation. A new version scores the eligible snapshot and switches the view after successful publication; older generation tables remain. Repeated runs for that generation can continue incrementally. With full_snapshot, every current source row is eligible. With from_now, the rebuild uses keys already in the previous prediction generation plus new CDF inserts after its source watermark; pre-start history remains excluded. A version-specific physical table records the model name, version and artifact digest. Scoring rejects a table at that name when its saved model provenance differs. A different registered model sharing the same numeric version needs a different logical prediction name or a new model version. Do not switch an existing physical append table to a full-rebuild view under the same name; choose a fresh logical destination and plan the consumer change. Full rebuild is a model-selection policy, not a blanket permission to accept updates in the current generation.

For a multi_target project, merge this fragment into its existing model_set mapping, keeping its registered set and destination settings:

model_set:
  on_source_change: rescore_all

When CDF contains UPDATE/DELETE, that policy rebuilds the eligible current source with the selected set, preserving any from_now boundary. Deleted observations disappear and corrected values, business outputs and temporal history are recomputed. Even if append mode had mixed earlier versions, the source-triggered rebuild uses the selected set for all eligible rows. It does not retrain. The selected local snapshot must fit row/byte limits. Do not add on_source_change at the top level or to a single-model project expecting the same behavior.

docs.title: Model-set outputs and business views
docs.text: A multi_target score loads one saved set with its component versions. Component rules run first; combined rules then use named results such as revenue__prediction. model_set.publication.mode chooses all, combined_only or separate_views. The model set guide owns the modes, view names and combined rules.

docs.title: Recover recognized CDF expiry
docs.text:
rescore_when_history_expires: true is opt-in and changes the generated task graph. Generate/deploy a matching project with recovery enabled; changing inference.yml alone is rejected because deployed_auto_rebuild_on_cdf_expiry in the job must agree in both job definitions. Leave recovery disabled until those tasks are deployed. Keep workflow_contract: "3" fixed; it is not the YAML version.

The score task recognizes a supported missing-history condition and emits a recovery request. recovery_needed selects recover_predictions, which scores the pinned eligible source snapshot with the same concrete model/set selection. For from_now, recovery excludes keys in the original starting snapshot. That snapshot must still be readable; if its history or files have expired, recovery stops rather than scoring pre-start history. Normal model-change rebuilds use the saved prediction keys and recent CDF instead. A successful replacement verifies source/output identities and the expected output version, then atomically retains the output table identity, grants and named views, then ordinary incremental scoring resumes at the new watermark. Older model-version generations remain available; rollback inside the rebuilt generation depends on Delta history retention. An exact committed recovery retry is a no-op. Open scoring_report for the completed result; the initial score output saying recovery was requested is not proof that replacement finished.

This mechanism handles history expiry, not permissions, connectivity, disabled CDF, source-table replacement, schema mismatch or readable UPDATE/DELETE events. Those retain their existing failure behavior. Recovery can read the full source, so keep capacity limits appropriate. It does not retrain or change aliases. If scoring fails after a successful promotion, repair/retry scoring separately; do not rerun a lifecycle action whose alias effects may already have committed.

docs.title: Schedules, handoff and execution engines
docs.text:
follow_champion: false is the default. true starts the score job after successful champion initialization/promotion/rollback. Pending review, failed quality gates and rejection do not trigger it. It is a deploy-time setting, not a Run now parameter. To change it, edit inference.yml and the matching deployed_score_handoff value in every resources/*.job.yml that carries it (train, score and monitoring), then redeploy. Changing inference.yml alone is rejected as a mismatch. The setup's scoring_mode chooses manual or scheduled job execution; it is separate from mode in config/scoring.yml, which chooses eligibility.

Inspect the handoff child score run before launching another score; a separate invocation is only needed for new rows or recovery.

Schedule, timezone, pause status, score retries, task/job time limits and notifications live under deployment configuration. Generated defaults do not add recipients or retries. Keep one owning writer for each prediction target; job serialization is not a lock against unrelated external writers.

docs.title: Distributed inference settings
docs.text: Without batch_compute, scoring is whole-frame (single_node). With batch_compute: spark, the Bundle uses mlflow.pyfunc.spark_udf to apply the saved preprocessing and model to pandas batches on Spark workers; it does not turn fitting or tuning into distributed training. Admission checks the exact fitted artifact, and a package logged without a certificate cannot use Spark. Score on Spark workers covers worker configuration, the support table, capacity and results.

docs.title: Training without publishing a prediction table
docs.text: The generated train and score jobs are separate. Set follow_champion: false in config/inference.yml to prevent automatic scoring after an alias change. Choose scoring_mode: manual during initialization to omit a score schedule. For an existing project, also update matching deployed_score_handoff parameters in resources/*.job.yml, remove any unwanted score schedule, and redeploy. The runtime rejects a YAML/job handoff mismatch. Merely configuring prediction_table does not create or populate it; training can still write its own dataset snapshots and lifecycle evidence. Endpoint callers can consume predictions without publishing a Delta prediction table.

docs.title: Common errors and fixes
docs.text: Symptom Action No champion / unknown version Inspect the concrete registered model or set and its approval evidence; use the intended selector/override. Preview rejects a target-reading filter Decide pre_split/combined skip behavior before training, or explicitly choose custom eligibility. Changing scoring.yml or scoring.py has no effect Train/package a new version; the selected model retains captured rules. No scoring_status columns Empty pre_split with no opted-in policy keeps ordinary outputs; select and package an actual policy. Expected scoring_report is missing Default graph has none; open score. scoring_report belongs to the recovery-enabled graph. UPDATE/DELETE causes failure Review source correction policy; model-set on_source_change: rescore_all is not a single-model option. Source is unchanged but a different model was selected Incremental append does not rewrite old rows; inspect selected model versus previous write provenance. Existing output schema differs Use a fresh compatible destination when adding policy/business fields or changing publication shape. Row/byte budget exceeded Size the first/rebuild population, not only daily inserts; adjust validated capacity or use an admitted distributed route. CDF recovery was requested but no new results appear Inspect recover_predictions and the final scoring_report; do not treat the request as success.

docs.title: Databricks Python SDK: fit, inspect and score
docs.text: Start here to fit a bounded pandas pipeline, save it and score two new rows in Python. Then choose only the cloud scenario you need from the index below. A Bundle is optional; the Python SDK does not submit Databricks jobs for you.

docs.title: Fit and score a small batch
docs.text:
Use Python 3.12+ and a writable working directory:

uv pip install skyulf-core
# Add tracking/registry support only when needed:
uv pip install "skyulf-core[mlflow]"

Pin a published Skyulf release and resolved dependencies for repeatable training and scoring. Newer integration features require their matching release/build; unpublished development validation uses the exact build on every participating runtime. Do not assume an editable install's version identifies its source revision.

This complete local example needs no account, Spark or MLflow:

import pandas as pd

from skyulf.data.dataset import SplitDataset
from skyulf.integrations.databricks import (
    InputSource, WorkflowConfig, ModelSelection, OutputSink,
    fit_workflow, prepare_workflow,
)

frame = pd.DataFrame({
    "x": [1., 2., 3., 4., 5., 6., 7., 8.],
    "target": [2., 4., 6., 8., 10., 12., 14., 16.],
})
training, heldout = frame.iloc[:6].copy(), frame.iloc[6:].copy()
pipeline_config = {"preprocessing": [], "modeling": {"type": "linear_regression"}}
artifact_path = "artifacts/customer-model"
artifact = fit_workflow(
    pipeline_config, SplitDataset(train=training, test=heldout),
    target_column="target", artifact_path=artifact_path,
    max_rows=100, max_bytes=1_000_000,
)
config = WorkflowConfig(
    runtime="standalone", engine="pandas",
    source=InputSource(kind="caller_frame", max_rows=100, max_bytes=1_000_000),
    model=ModelSelection(kind="local_pipeline", path=artifact_path),
    sink=OutputSink(kind="return_frame"),
)
prepared = prepare_workflow(config)
query = pd.DataFrame({"x": [9., 10.]})
predictions = prepared.predict(query)
assert prepared.preflight.ready
assert prepared.preflight.feature_order == ("x",)
assert (predictions["prediction"] - [18., 20.]).abs().max() < 1e-10
print(predictions)

Expect a prediction column containing approximately 18.0 and 20.0. artifacts/customer-model contains the saved fitted artifact, not a source project directory you must invent. Preflight verifies the recorded schema, engine, outputs and dependency versions before prediction. All rows remain in this Python process. The training/test split is explicit and test labels are not used to fit the model. Add normal Core steps to preprocessing; the recipe catalogue explains built-in nodes and parameters.

The same saved artifact can be logged/registered for separate jobs using MLflow model packaging and the registry walkthrough. A temporary driver path alone is not a cross-job model store.

docs.title: Choose your next scenario
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    A["fit_workflow: saved artifact"] --> B["log_pipeline_model and register_model"]
    T["train_candidate: fit and register"] --> R["Registered model version"]
    B --> R
    R --> C["prepare_workflow: preflight"]
    C --> D["predict: returned frame"]
    C --> E["run_frame_batch: one period"]
    C --> F["run_incremental_batch: new inserts"]

Fit, register and score are separate calls. The local example above skips registration and loads the saved artifact path. Only run_frame_batch and run_incremental_batch write a Delta table.

UC examples below run in a compatible Databricks notebook/task with authenticated spark, Delta support, model dependencies and access to the named resources. Replace example catalog/schema/table/version identities with your provisioned resources. A workstation needs separately configured compatible Databricks Connect; installing Skyulf alone does not create a session. Source reads require catalog/schema use and SELECT; model loading needs its own model permissions; publication needs target/control read-write permissions. Keep tokens outside configuration and authenticate through the runtime's credential provider.

docs.title: Preflight and custom pipelines
docs.text:
WorkflowConfig is frozen, serializable and has no implicit source snapshot, period or promotion decision. preflight(config, artifact=...) performs offline checks without a registry call, package load or job submission. It returns issues with a code, category and suggested fix. For a registry selection, offline preflight reports model_unresolved; call prepare_workflow when read-only registry access is allowed. That step loads the pinned package and performs full preflight before returning a predictor. local_issues, remote_issues and remote_checked keep the two stages visible. It may deserialize trusted pickle, but creates no cloud resource. If representative rows are available before submitting a job, pass probe_frame=sample to preflight or prepare_workflow. The probe runs the actual fitted FE and model and reports a prediction_probe_failed issue for an incompatible sample. A passing sample is evidence for that sample, not a guarantee about every later batch.

from skyulf.inference.fitted_pipeline import load_pipeline
from skyulf.integrations.databricks import preflight

artifact = load_pipeline("artifacts/customer-model")
report = preflight(config.model_copy(update={
    "model": ModelSelection(kind="local_pipeline", path="artifacts/customer-model")
}), artifact=artifact)
for issue in report.issues:
    print(issue.category, issue.code, issue.fix)

For custom feature engineering, edit the normal SkyulfPipeline preprocessing configuration, fit it on training data, save it, and compare predictions before and after loading. The SDK has no separate node or model allowlist: it restores the fitted SkyulfPipeline and calls its existing prediction path. Integration examples cover imputation, scaling, encoding, binning, linear and logistic regression, and a MinMaxScaler/random-forest combination on both DataFrame engines. Other library combinations remain governed by their own fitted inference behavior and should receive replay tests before production use. Saving a pipeline does not itself admit it to independent worker batches or single-row requests. Inspected pandas artifacts can use the separately certified Spark pyfunc route when their exact fitted recipe and model are supported. A portable InferenceBundle uses a different state format and its own predict_local/predict_spark paths; selecting the wrong package kind fails preflight. See preprocessing context for groups and history.

For example, an advanced pipeline may fit explicit binning followed by encoding before it is packaged; its saved edges and category positions are then replayed by the fitted artifact:

from skyulf.pipeline import SkyulfPipeline

pipeline = SkyulfPipeline({
    "preprocessing": [
        {"name": "bands", "transformer": "CustomBinning", "params": {
            "columns": ["x"], "bins": [0.0, 2.0, 4.0, 6.0],
            "output_suffix": "_band",
        }},
        {"name": "encode_bands", "transformer": "OneHotEncoder", "params": {
            "columns": ["x_band"], "drop_original": True,
            "handle_unknown": "ignore",
        }},
    ],
    "modeling": {"type": "linear_regression"},
})
# Pass this recipe and an explicit SplitDataset to fit_workflow, which saves it.

InputSource defaults to 100,000 rows and 128 MiB. Set tighter limits for each job. PreparedWorkflow.predict checks both before running FE and the model. It preserves the caller's input column order and rejects schema mismatches; it does not silently collect a Spark DataFrame. On Databricks, supply either a bounded caller-owned frame or the explicit pinned UC source adapter below.

docs.title: Evaluate the held-out split in the model run
docs.text:
Keep labeled test rows outside the fit split. After fitting and loading the artifact, evaluate_holdout calls the saved pipeline's normal prediction path on those raw test features. It returns heldout_mae, heldout_rmse and heldout_r2 for regression; classification returns heldout_accuracy and heldout_f1_weighted, plus heldout_f1 for binary models (the model's second class is positive). A negative R2 is a valid poor-generalization result, not a logging failure. The caller chooses the split and logs metrics to the same MLflow run ID that contains the model artifact:

# Continue the first local example: artifact, heldout and artifact_path.
from pathlib import Path
from skyulf.integrations.databricks import evaluate_holdout
from skyulf.integrations.mlflow import TrackingConfig, track_run
from skyulf.integrations.mlflow.models.pipeline_model import log_pipeline_model

tracking_uri = "sqlite:///" + (Path.cwd() / "sdk-demo.db").as_posix()
tracking = TrackingConfig(
    enabled=True, tracking_uri=tracking_uri, experiment_name="sdk-demo",
)
metrics = evaluate_holdout(artifact, heldout, target_column="target")
with track_run(tracking, run_name="customer-model") as run:
    run.log_params({"heldout_rows": len(heldout)})
    run.log_metrics(metrics)
    model_uri = log_pipeline_model(
        artifact_path, run_id=run.run_id,
        artifact_path="model", tracking_uri=tracking_uri,
    )
assert metrics["heldout_rmse"] < 1e-10
print(model_uri, metrics)

The held-out labels are used only for evaluation. Monthly scoring reads raw features without labels and applies the already fitted FE and model.

docs.title: Optional preprocessing probe
docs.text: Set TrainingSpec(..., preprocessing_probe=True) (default False) to check the saved and reloaded preprocessing on at most the first 256 holdout rows. The report is saved as preprocessing_probe.json on the candidate's MLflow training run. Preprocessing diagnostics explains what it checks and every status. The preflight prediction sample described above is a separate check that also calls the model.

docs.title: Train a candidate when labels are ready
docs.text:
Continue with pipeline_config from the first local example and the runtime-provided spark session. This scenario requires an existing Delta catalog.schema.labeled_events version 12 with unique event_id, numeric feature_a and feature_b, numeric target, and native Spark timestamp event_time/label_available_at. It also assumes an existing registered baseline version 7 with the same target/schema and experiment access. Omit champion_version when creating your first candidate. Replace these sample resource identities before running; the local first example does not create them.

train_candidate reads a specific Delta table version, filters a bounded event window in Spark when temporal splitting is selected. Random splitting uses Core DataSplitter on stable record-key order and needs no dates. Optional availability filtering excludes unknown results and those after the independent result_cutoff from both fit and holdout. For temporal splitting, the feature/model pipeline fits only on events before holdout_start; later eligible events are reserved for evaluation. The fit engine can be pandas or Polars. The run logs the Skyulf config, source and code identities, fitted model, held-out metrics and candidate_comparison.json. It registers a new concrete model version. By default it assigns neither @challenger nor @champion; an explicitly supplied on_registered callback can hand nomination to a separate lifecycle owner.

The model-producing run also exposes native MLflow Inputs for the actual training and holdout frames. These preserve the pinned source version and bounded split profiles; dataset_inputs.json links the source, sampling, split and optional feature lookup evidence. See training datasets in Inputs for the fields and the distinction between lineage metadata and saved data rows.

from datetime import UTC, datetime
from skyulf.integrations.databricks import TrainingSpec, train_candidate

spec = TrainingSpec(
    table="catalog.schema.labeled_events", version=12,
    split_strategy="temporal", filter_unavailable_results=True,
    result_cutoff=datetime(2026, 3, 15, tzinfo=UTC),
    start=datetime(2026, 1, 1, tzinfo=UTC),
    holdout_start=datetime(2026, 2, 1, tzinfo=UTC),
    cutoff=datetime(2026, 3, 1, tzinfo=UTC),
    event_column="event_time", result_available_at_column="label_available_at",
    record_key_columns=("event_id",), input_columns=("feature_a", "feature_b"),
    target_column="target", max_rows=10_000, max_bytes=32_000_000,
)
result = train_candidate(
    spark, spec, pipeline_config,
    model_name="catalog.schema.customer_model",
    tracking_uri="databricks", registry_uri="databricks-uc",
    experiment_name="/Shared/customer-model", run_name="candidate-2026-03",
    artifact_path="artifacts/customer-model", metric="heldout_rmse",
    min_improvement=0.05, engine="pandas",
    champion_version="7",  # Pin this concrete version before the job starts.
)
print(result.model_version, result.comparison.eligible)

The example uses native Spark timestamp instants; their stored instants are retained independently of the Spark session timezone. A missing or later label is not a training label, even if its target value is already present in the pinned table. The source must have unique nonnull row keys and distinct feature, target and timestamp columns. A nonempty training set and holdout of at least two rows each are required. The row and byte limits bound decoded rows and the local frame, not Spark's wire transfer size. The caller supplies a concrete champion_version; omit it for the first candidate. Review the comparison report, then use the separate guarded staging/promotion operations if a human approves a change. If fit, packaging, registration or comparison fails, no alias moves; a registered but unapproved candidate may remain for inspection. A scheduling policy is separate from this service.

For string, local-clock or date-only source columns, supply independent rules:

from dataclasses import replace
from skyulf.integrations.databricks import TrainingDateSpec

spec = replace(
    spec,
    event_time_parsing=TrainingDateSpec(
        format="%d/%m/%Y %H:%M:%S", timezone="Europe/Copenhagen"
    ),
    result_time_parsing=TrainingDateSpec(format="%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z"),
)

Leave the format unset for native timestamp columns. Naive local timestamps need an explicit source timezone; dates additionally require date_only="midnight". The default rejects date-only inputs. Ambiguous and nonexistent local times are rejected, and strings are never guessed. See the source-date contract for examples, boundaries, supported directives and distributed validation cost. candidate_training_spec.json retains both parsing rules for approval replay.

For a table without dates, create the same specification with no time fields:

spec = TrainingSpec(
    table="catalog.schema.labeled_customers", version=12,
    record_key_columns=("customer_id",), input_columns=("income", "age"),
    target_column="target", max_rows=10_000, max_bytes=32_000_000,
    split_strategy="random", test_size=0.2, random_state=42, stratify=False,
)

Pass this spec to the same train_candidate call above with either fit engine. All targets must be known. Enable filter_unavailable_results and set result_available_at_column plus result_cutoff if outcomes arrive later; random splitting still needs no observation timestamp. The returned candidate and saved spec record holdout membership evidence for approval replay. See the split/availability matrix for the four supported combinations.

docs.title: Candidate CV and sampling
docs.text:
Candidate training also accepts cv=CVSpec(enabled=True, folds=3) from skyulf.integrations.databricks.training.tuning.cv. It reuses Core CV on training rows, refits preprocessing per fold and logs a separate report to the candidate's MLflow run. Use method="stratified_k_fold" for classification; time-series CV requires an explicit event window and shuffle=False. The saved final pipeline and its protected holdout are independent of the fold fits.

TrainingSpec(training_sample_rows=10_000, training_sample_seed=42, ...) opts into seeded Spark-side selection before local transfer. The limit includes training and final holdout rows and cannot exceed max_rows. Sample membership is pinned for approval replay. Leaving it null preserves overflow-fail behavior. See Bundle CV, sampling and selection for full contracts and the Bundle's train calendar settings. The Bundle uses the same action for manual and scheduled runs: null source version resolves latest once, explicit version pins the snapshot, and rolling windows derive at invocation. The direct train_candidate API still takes a concrete TrainingSpec with its source version and any active date boundaries.

docs.title: Fit and score a pinned UC source
docs.text:
This is an independent Databricks scenario, run in a Python notebook/task with its authenticated spark session. Replace the example three-part names and versions with existing resources: version 12 of new_entities must contain entity_id keys, event_time as Spark timestamp, and amount/city with the exact raw schema of the pre-existing version 7 customer model. That model must have been fitted with Polars. These resources are not created by prepare_workflow. For a complete provision/train/register/monthly example, use the batch walkthrough.

fit_workflow requires an explicit SplitDataset; it bounds the total rows and in-memory bytes before fitting and saves the same trusted artifact as save_pipeline. Tracking and registration remain opt-in calls through track_run, log_pipeline_model and register_model. They do not move an alias.

from datetime import UTC, datetime

from skyulf.integrations.databricks import (
    InputSource, SourceSpec, WorkflowConfig, ModelSelection,
    OutputSink, prepare_workflow, score_source,
)

table = "catalog.schema.new_entities"
config = WorkflowConfig(
    runtime="databricks",
    engine="polars",  # must match the registered artifact's fit engine
    source=InputSource(kind="uc_table", table=table, version=12,
                       max_rows=10_000, max_bytes=32_000_000),
    model=ModelSelection(kind="local_pipeline",
                         name="catalog.schema.customer_model", version="7",
                         tracking_uri="databricks", registry_uri="databricks-uc"),
    sink=OutputSink(kind="return_frame"),
)
prepared = prepare_workflow(config)  # resolves a concrete model version
period = SourceSpec(
    table=table, version=12, record_key_columns=("entity_id",),
    input_columns=("amount", "city"),  # exact saved raw input order
    period_start=datetime(2026, 1, 1, tzinfo=UTC),
    period_end=datetime(2026, 2, 1, tzinfo=UTC),
    max_rows=10_000, max_bytes=32_000_000,
)
result = score_source(spark, period, prepared)
print(result.predictions, result.diagnostics)

The reader applies the pinned Delta version, half-open UTC period filter, column projection, deterministic row-key order and max_rows + 1 limit before iterating on the driver. It stops when decoded serialized rows or the resulting local frame exceed max_bytes, and rejects duplicate row keys. This byte guard measures decoded payload and local memory, not Spark's private wire framing; very wide individual rows should therefore be excluded or handled by a separately proven paged transport. The selected source and its limits must match the prepared workflow. The result keeps row keys outside the model input and records the source version, period, model digest and concrete model version. No prediction table is created here. Whole-frame FE retains local pandas or Polars behavior even though Spark performs the bounded UC read.

docs.title: Publish one scored month to a UC Delta table
docs.text:
This Databricks fragment assumes a pre-existing scoring_source version 12 with the same entity_id, event_time, amount and city contract as the previous scenario, a registered Polars model version 7, and provisioned output/admission tables. Use the complete batch walkthrough for table DDL, version discovery, unchanged retry, a second month and readback assertions.

run_frame_batch keeps feature engineering and model prediction in the saved pandas or Polars engine. Spark reads the pinned UC source and converts only the bounded final prediction rows to a DataFrame with the target's explicit schema. The guarded Delta writer then replaces exactly the requested half-open period. A second month therefore leaves the first month's predictions and run metadata unchanged; a backfill must explicitly name the earlier period.

Provision the source, prediction target and admission control table before the job. The source and target must be different Delta tables. The target must have the row-key columns with the same Spark types as the source (long or string), a timestamp period column, the saved model's output columns at their declared types, and three string columns: run_id, model_name and model_version. Here run_id identifies the prediction publication, not the MLflow training run; the incremental writer derives it from the source/model snapshot. Existing test targets with __skyulf_* columns retain their historical schema; create a new target with these names for the updated writer.

The control table has exactly one row, target_id STRING equal to the target Delta table ID and nullable owner STRING initially null. Every publisher of this target must use that same control table. The job identity needs read access to the source/model and write access to the target/control tables.

from datetime import UTC, datetime
from importlib.metadata import version

from skyulf.integrations.databricks import (
    BatchSpec, InputSource, SourceSpec, WorkflowConfig,
    ModelSelection, OutputSink, prepare_workflow, run_frame_batch,
)
from skyulf.integrations.databricks.data.delta_io.delta_admission import DeltaTableAdmission

source_table = "catalog.schema.scoring_source"
target_table = "catalog.schema.predictions"
control_table = "catalog.schema.prediction_admission"
source_version = 12
source = SourceSpec(
    table=source_table,
    version=source_version,
    period_start=datetime(2026, 1, 1, tzinfo=UTC),
    period_end=datetime(2026, 2, 1, tzinfo=UTC),
    record_key_columns=("entity_id",),
    input_columns=("amount", "city"),
    max_rows=10_000,
    max_bytes=32_000_000,
)
config = WorkflowConfig(
    runtime="databricks",
    engine="polars",
    source=InputSource(
        kind="uc_table", table=source_table, version=source_version,
        max_rows=source.max_rows, max_bytes=source.max_bytes,
    ),
    model=ModelSelection(
        kind="local_pipeline", name="catalog.schema.customer_model", version="7",
        tracking_uri="databricks", registry_uri="databricks-uc",
    ),
    sink=OutputSink(kind="uc_delta", table=target_table),
)
prepared = prepare_workflow(config)
spec = BatchSpec(
    period_start=source.period_start,
    period_end=source.period_end,
    as_of=datetime.now(UTC),  # capture after the selected source commit exists
    record_key_columns=source.record_key_columns,
    output_table=target_table,
    model_name=config.model.name,
    model_version=prepared.preflight.model_version,
    model_digest=prepared.preflight.model_digest,
    source_version=source_version,
    code_version=version("skyulf-core"),
    run_id="january-2026-v1",
    expected_target_version=0,  # read and pin before submission
    mode="local_pipeline",
)
result = run_frame_batch(
    spark, source, prepared, spec,
    admission=DeltaTableAdmission(spark, control_table),
)
print(result.commit_version, result.replayed, result.manifest)

Use a new logical run ID and the current target version for the next month's job. Retry an uncertain job with the identical spec, including its original run ID and expected target version; a successful replay returns the existing receipt. A new run with a stale expected version fails instead of overwriting newer results. An empty period fails unless allow_empty=True is explicit. The source snapshot must have been committed by as_of. The reader and result both enforce the configured local row and memory budgets; this does not measure Spark's private wire bytes. The control-row admission protocol protects participating writers only; do not let other jobs bypass it or manually clear an owner while a writer may still be active.

docs.title: Score newly inserted rows automatically
docs.text:
This independent Databricks scenario uses the runtime-provided spark session, a registered Polars model version 7, and an existing CDF-enabled new_records table whose raw feature columns match that model. event_id is the globally unique source key. The initially empty predictions target and prediction_admission control row must already be provisioned as described below. Choose a different target from a period-replacement job; incremental and period receipts are different contracts.

run_incremental_batch selects records by Delta source commits, not by calendar date. By default the first run scores the existing bounded snapshot. Set WorkflowConfig(initial_scoring="from_now", ...) to record an empty first checkpoint and skip existing rows. The choice is fixed in the target receipt; see starting boundaries and retention. On later runs it reads only inserts after the source version recorded in the last prediction-table commit. It appends predictions without replacing an older period. A source event_time column is optional; if you want to carry it into the target, set period_column="event_time" in the stable job configuration. It never filters rows by that column, including late arrivals.

Provision a distinct, initially empty Delta prediction table with the globally unique key, saved model output columns and run_id, model_name, model_version string columns. If carrying an event timestamp, add a matching Spark timestamp column to both tables. Enable Delta Change Data Feed on the source before any changes that the job must consume. Provision the same shared admission control table used by the explicit-period writer; all target writers must use that admission authority. The job identity needs source, model, target and control-table permissions.

from skyulf.integrations.databricks import (
    InputSource, WorkflowConfig, ModelSelection, OutputSink,
    prepare_workflow, run_incremental_batch,
)
from skyulf.integrations.databricks.data.delta_io.delta_admission import DeltaTableAdmission

config = WorkflowConfig(
    runtime="databricks",
    engine="polars",
    source=InputSource(
        kind="uc_table", table="catalog.schema.new_records",
        read_mode="incremental", max_rows=10_000, max_bytes=32_000_000,
    ),
    model=ModelSelection(
        kind="local_pipeline", name="catalog.schema.customer_model", version="7",
        tracking_uri="databricks", registry_uri="databricks-uc",
    ),
    sink=OutputSink(kind="uc_delta", table="catalog.schema.predictions"),
)
prepared = prepare_workflow(config)
result = run_incremental_batch(
    spark, prepared, record_key_columns=("event_id",),
    admission=DeltaTableAdmission(spark, "catalog.schema.prediction_admission"),
)
print(result.input_count, result.commit_version, result.noop)
