result = initialize_rollout(
    workspace,
    plan,
    store=store,
    policy=DailyRolloutPolicy.from_config(rollout_settings),
    admission=SingleWriterAdmission(),
    rollout_id=run.info.run_id,
    promotion=promotion,
)
print(result)
print("rollout run_id:", run.info.run_id)

The job checks these YAML values against the saved policy before reconciling the endpoint. To change a policy, initialize a new rollout on a settled 100/0 endpoint and configure its new run_id; editing YAML alone cannot shorten an active rollout. Missing timing fields use the 10-point/24-hour defaults. For an older run initialized with custom SDK values, add matching fields to its YAML.

SingleWriterAdmission is an explicit ownership contract, not a distributed lock. Restrict endpoint and alias mutation permissions to the controller's identity, serialize all its writers, and keep max_concurrent_runs: 1. Another job or UI writer must not modify those resources concurrently. Applications with multiple writers must supply a shared admission provider to the SDK operations. There is no native atomic compare-and-swap for an endpoint configuration.

docs.title: Enable the daily Bundle job
docs.text:
Generate the project with include_daily_rollout: "true" in the template init configuration. This adds resources/daily_rollout.job.yml, its notebook, config/serving.yml, and serving dependencies. To add it to an existing project, follow project upgrades. The job is initially PAUSED; its configuration is initially disabled.

Fill rollout in config/serving.yml:

  • Set run_id to the initialized rollout run and copy the comparison digest and exact approval settings used above.
  • Supply representative smoke_records matching the admitted request schema. The job calls both named served versions directly, including the version with zero routed traffic.
  • Configure minimum request and label counts, label coverage, maximum error rate and the latency limit (p99) in health.
  • Configure monitoring for the concrete challenger version and endpoint. source_table and prediction_table select its inference payload table. Use execution_engine: spark, an existing reference_namespace, and a label table with a result-availability timestamp.
  • monitoring.environment labels the saved observation only. The generated daily_rollout job passes bundle_target: ${bundle.target}, so evidence records the target that ran it; the YAML value (syst) is used only when that parameter is absent. It does not select tables or change rollout decisions.
  • Set enabled: true and exclusive_writer: true only after establishing the ownership contract. Deploy, test one run, and then unpause the schedule.

These fields are an excerpt of that generated block, not a replacement for the required approval, endpoint and monitoring identities:

rollout:
  enabled: true
  exclusive_writer: true
  run_id: "COPY_THE_INITIALIZED_ROLLOUT_RUN_ID"
  traffic_step_percent: 10
  stage_minimum_hours: 24.0
  evidence_max_age_hours: 24.0
  comparison_sha256: "COPY_THE_SAVED_COMPARISON_DIGEST"
  smoke_records:
    - income: 42000.0
      age: 38.0
  health:
    minimum_requests: 100
    maximum_error_rate: 0.01
    maximum_latency_ms: 1000.0
    minimum_labeled_rows: 30
    minimum_label_coverage: 0.8

Replace the smoke fields with the actual request schema; an online feature model may require keys and additional source fields instead. The three policy fields must match initialization; the health thresholds configure the job's observation. Preserve both deliberately.

From the configured generated project:

databricks bundle validate --strict -t test --profile YOUR_PROFILE
databricks bundle deploy -t test --profile YOUR_PROFILE
databricks bundle run daily_rollout -t test --profile YOUR_PROFILE

Open the resulting job task's Output, then compare the reported percentage and endpoint revision with the native endpoint configuration. Inspect the saved observation and reason before unpausing the daily schedule. Missing observations, missing latency, incomplete logs and immature labels are holds, not healthy passes.

Serving labels join on databricks_request_id and request_row_index; retain these identifiers when collecting outcomes. The adapter uses the actual served model identity from telemetry and evaluates the current stage's time interval. It does not recompute historical predictions. Late or missing outcomes hold the rollout until enough mature labels are available. Quality thresholds come from the saved comparison; the job does not accept a configurable PASS flag.

The job records the complete observation and verifies its MLflow artifact before changing traffic. Its output includes status, state.challenger_percentage, the decision and an observation digest. A successful final transition also includes the guarded promotion receipt.

docs.title: Decisions and timing
docs.text:
Observation Action Zero traffic, saved comparison and targeted requests pass Advance when the initial minimum stage has elapsed Enough fresh requests and mature labels; health and quality pass Increase by one configured step Too few requests or labels, stale evidence, or an incomplete stage Hold the current allocation Confirmed error-rate, latency, or quality regression Return traffic to the retained champion and stop the rollout 100% traffic completes its final passing stage Recheck the saved heldout evidence and automatically promote

A missed scheduled run does not cause several increases at once. Stage time starts when the new routing configuration is verified as ready. Endpoint traffic and registry aliases are separate: reaching 100% does not itself change an alias. The final approval also checks that the original champion, challenger, comparison digest and quality policy still match.

health.maximum_latency_ms bounds p99 model execution time, the duration at or below which approximately 99% of timed captured requests fall. A single unusually slow request can exceed the threshold without failing the stage. For example, p99 of 80 ms passes a 100 ms limit even if the maximum is 900 ms; p99 of 120 ms fails the same limit and requests rollback. This measures model execution, not total client/network response time.

If a saved summary has no latency_p99_ms, or it is null, the check uses latency_max_ms. Recorded zero is valid. An invalid non-null p99, or no usable latency in either field, holds the stage. Error-rate, minimum request and label counts, quality, stage duration and incomplete-log checks also apply.

For example, a verified 10% stage with insufficient mature labels stays at 10%. A confirmed health regression returns traffic to 0% challenger / 100% retained champion and ends that rollout. This traffic rollback does not promote the challenger or restore a registry alias from an unrelated promotion. At 100%, the challenger still needs its final complete passing stage before becoming champion. A day passing on the calendar is not sufficient evidence.

The evidence verdict and controller action are different fields:

Fresh, matching evidence Controller action Traffic and next invocation PASS, full stage elapsed, below 100% ADVANCE Add one configured step; start a new stage only after the endpoint is verified HOLD, missing evidence, or incomplete stage HOLD Keep the current share and original stage start; the next day evaluates that same stage with fresh evidence FAIL ROLLBACK Request 0% challenger / 100% retained champion immediately, even before 24 hours; verified rollback becomes terminal PASS at 100%, full stage elapsed COMPLETE Keep 100% and perform guarded final promotion

A label shortfall today does not reset the clock. The next invocation can advance once the complete stage has enough fresh, mature evidence; it never catches up by applying several missed daily increases. A terminal ROLLED_BACK run stays at 0% on subsequent invocations and cannot resume.

Too few requests, unavailable or inconsistent request counts, missing or invalid latency, stale/future observations, logging errors, too few mature labels and insufficient label coverage all hold. Logging errors mean capture is incomplete, not a measured prediction regression. Once usable evidence exists, an excessive error rate, excessive latency or failed quality gate yields FAIL. The controller first verifies evidence identity and freshness; stale or mismatched failure evidence cannot trigger rollback.

docs.title: Feature updates during a rollout
docs.text:
New feature-bound candidates save their enriched training-time holdout at lifecycle/data/holdout.parquet in the candidate's MLflow run. The saved comparison binds its hash, owner run, schema, row and memory limits, split membership and model identity. Lifecycle training reuses its prepared holdout; SDK training records the same bounded artifact when needed.

Final approval reloads those verified inputs and evaluates the fitted pipeline. Feature table versions may advance while the rollout runs: current feature values do not replace historical holdout values. The original source and feature table identities must still match. Missing or altered artifacts, changed split metadata, insufficient read budgets or a dropped and recreated table block approval. Retain the candidate run and its artifacts throughout the rollout and approval.

A candidate without this saved holdout uses strict snapshot reconstruction. If a feature table has advanced, approval explains that no frozen holdout is available and remains blocked. Train a new candidate with the updated runtime; do not edit comparison artifacts to bypass that check.

Online requests still use current published features and enforce their missing value and freshness policy. Historical holdout success does not replace fresh serving health, quality or final-stage observations. A shared feature failure can affect both versions; returning traffic to the champion does not repair that data. See online features for the serving freshness contract and supported request shape.

docs.title: Retry, stop and recovery
docs.text:
Before an endpoint update, the controller persists the exact intended request. After a timeout or interruption, rerun the job to reconcile that request. A reconciliation run does not immediately apply another traffic increase. The stage clock advances only after the expected endpoint revision and routes are verified.

New PREPARED receipts distinguish two submission states:

request.submission_state Recovery on the next invocation NOT_SUBMITTED Revalidate the endpoint and send the saved request once. OUTCOME_UNKNOWN, or absent in an older receipt Inspect the endpoint without resending. Commit the receipt only when the exact target revision, model pair and routes are ready.

The controller persists OUTCOME_UNKNOWN immediately before sending the request. A crash between those operations is therefore ambiguous even if the endpoint still has its old configuration. Repeated invocations hold that receipt; elapsed time alone does not prove that an update cannot still apply.

Inspect the saved intent and endpoint using the same clients and store as initialization:

receipt = store.load()
request = receipt.get("request", {})
endpoint = workspace.api_client.do(
    "GET", f"/api/2.0/serving-endpoints/{receipt['state']['endpoint_name']}"
)
print({
    "receipt_status": receipt["status"],
    "submission_state": request.get("submission_state", "OUTCOME_UNKNOWN"),
    "prior_revision": request.get("prior_config_version"),
    "target_revision": request.get("target_config_version"),
    "current_revision": endpoint.get("config", {}).get("config_version"),
    "pending_config": endpoint.get("pending_config"),
    "endpoint_state": endpoint.get("state"),
})

If the exact requested configuration has settled, rerun daily_rollout to reconcile it. A pending update must settle before proceeding. An unexpected endpoint ID, revision, model or routing setting stops automation rather than overwriting another writer's change.

There is no force-abort API for an ambiguous receipt. If the request cannot be resolved, pause the job, establish exclusive ownership and inspect the native endpoint operation with your workspace administrator. Retain the old run as evidence. Once no old update can still apply, explicitly restore an admitted, ready 100/0 endpoint and initialize a new rollout run using the sequence above; update rollout.run_id before resuming. Do not edit receipt artifacts or tags, reset the submission marker, or blindly resend an uncertain request.

Pause the scheduled job to stop further decisions. A verified regression rollback is terminal for that rollout; starting again requires a new explicit rollout. After a successful promotion, both concrete served entities remain available. Retiring the previous model or changing SQL pins is a separate operator action.

To restart after rollback, investigate the saved failure, correct its cause, and follow the explicit endpoint/initialization sequence with a new rollout run and an admitted model pair. Recheck the current champion, comparison and ownership; do not reuse or edit the terminal receipt to reset its state. Pausing a schedule only prevents new controller runs; it does not itself roll traffic back. A shared feature outage still needs its own repair.

docs.title: Check or create your source tables
When you need it
docs.text:
Read this page before the first training run, once you know which tables the project will read. Skyulf never creates or changes your data tables. It expects them to follow a small contract, and it gives you a read-only command to check that they do. You do not need to create anything when your tables already exist.

flowchart TD
    A{"Do the source tables exist?"} -- "yes" --> C["Run preview --action sources"]
    A -- "no" --> B["Create them, optionally from config/sources.sql"]
    B --> C
    C --> D{"Check passed?"}
    D -- "no" --> E["Fix the table or the configuration"]
    E --> C
    D -- "yes" --> F["Train, then score"]

A project reads data in up to three roles: training data, scoring input and actual outcomes. Choose a table layout explains the roles and the single_table, separate_outcomes and separate_all layouts. The generated SOURCES.md repeats the bindings for your project.

docs.title: What to edit
docs.text:
The check reads the table names from your configuration. Nothing else needs to change:

Role Setting Training data training_table in config/training.yml Training outcomes, when joined training_label_table in config/training.yml Scoring input score_source_table in config/inference.yml Actual outcomes for monitoring monitoring_label_table and monitoring_result_available_at_column in deployment/targets.yml

Every table must satisfy this contract:

  • Delta tables. Views and other formats are not accepted as sources.
  • Record keys. The record_key_columns exist in every table, are never null or non-finite, are unique within each table, and have exactly the same type in every table that is joined.
  • Inputs. The training data and the scoring input both contain every input column, with the same types.
  • Inserts only. The scoring input has Delta change data feed enabled, and rows are only appended. An UPDATE or DELETE stops incremental scoring; an outcome that arrives later goes into the outcomes table, not into an existing row.
  • Outcomes. An outcomes table holds the record keys, the target and the time the outcome became known. For monitoring this is a TIMESTAMP, or a string with an ISO timestamp and an explicit offset or Z. For training it must match result_time_parsing: a TIMESTAMP with the default parsing, a string with a format, a DATE with date_only: midnight and a timezone, or a TIMESTAMP_NTZ with a timezone only.

docs.title: If the tables do not exist yet
docs.text:
Choose include_source_sql: "true" during quick or detailed setup (or add "include_source_sql": "true" to the JSON answer file) to generate the starter. The default is "false"; SOURCES.md and source checks remain available in either case. If you already generated a project, render a separate folder with the option enabled and copy only the starter; do not overwrite your configuration.

config/sources.sql is an optional starter for that case. It contains one CREATE TABLE statement per input table that your layout needs: the training or feature table, a separate scoring input for separate_all, and the outcomes table when you named one. Columns come from your setup answers; every type is a TYPE_FOR_<column> placeholder except the availability column, which is TIMESTAMP. Change data feed is enabled on each table.

Replace {catalog}, {input_schema} and every placeholder with your real types, then run the statements yourself in Databricks SQL. Nothing in the Bundle runs this file. It does not copy data, and it uses CREATE TABLE without IF NOT EXISTS, so an existing table makes it fail instead of being changed. Skip the file entirely when your tables exist.

The jobs create the other tables themselves: the prediction table on the first score run, the monitoring store on the first enrollment, and the registered model on the first training run. See Tables in your workspace.

docs.title: The command
docs.text:
From the project root, with an existing SQL warehouse:

python src/tools/preview.py --action sources --profile YOUR_PROFILE --warehouse-id YOUR_WAREHOUSE_ID --catalog my_catalog --input-schema my_schema --output-schema my_schema --metadata-schema my_schema

Add --label-table and --label-available-at-column when the monitoring outcomes table differs from your setup answers. A short label table name resolves through the catalog and input schema you pass.

The command reads Delta metadata and runs bounded queries: DESCRIBE DETAIL, DESCRIBE TABLE, a probe for null keys and a probe for duplicate keys. The duplicate probe can scan the whole table. It never writes data, changes table properties or starts a job.

docs.title: What you should see
docs.text:
A JSON report per training configuration (main, or one entry per model-set branch):

{
  "main": {
    "status": "passed",
    "tables": {
      "workspace.air.observations": {"columns": {"record_id": "bigint", "...": "..."}, "change_data_feed": true}
    },
    "warnings": []
  }
}

Warnings do not fail the check. They name things that only the runtime can verify:

Warning Meaning Delta change data feed is off on <table>; ... Fine for a table that is never the scoring input. Initial scoring includes training history; ... Training and scoring share a table and use the default full_snapshot. Choose initial_scoring: from_now before the first score to skip existing rows. See Choose a table layout. Training availability values in ... are checked against result_time_parsing during training; ... The column type fits your parsing settings; individual values are validated when training reads them. Monitoring availability values in ... must be ISO timestamps with an explicit UTC offset or Z; ... A string availability column is accepted; monitoring rejects values without an offset. Feature lookup tables, point-in-time joins and fetched feature types are checked by training, ... Feature Store lookups are outside this raw-table check.

A passed check describes the tables as they are now, read with your identity. It cannot prove that future inserts keep the contract, that another run-as identity has the same access, or that the model's preprocessing accepts every value.

docs.title: Common errors and fixes
docs.text:
Errors are printed as Configuration error: <message> and the command exits with status 2.

Message Fix --action sources requires --profile and --warehouse-id. Pass both; the check needs a workspace and a running SQL warehouse. Source must be an existing Delta table: <table>. Create the table, check its name and schema, or convert it to Delta. Source is missing record key columns: <table>. Add the key columns, or correct record_key_columns. Source has null or nonfinite record keys: <table>. Remove or repair those rows upstream; keys identify one observation each. Source has duplicate record keys: <table>. Make the key unique, for example by adding a timestamp or observation id to record_key_columns. Source <table> is missing columns: [...] Add the columns, or remove them from input_columns and the other settings. Source column types differ: [...] Cast the columns so training, scoring and outcomes use exactly the same types. Enable Delta change data feed before incremental scoring: <table>. ALTER TABLE <table> SET TBLPROPERTIES ('delta.enableChangeDataFeed' = 'true'), before the first score run. An outcomes table requires an availability timestamp column. Set monitoring_result_available_at_column or result_available_at_column. Training outcome availability ... is incompatible with result_time_parsing; ... Change result_time_parsing to match the column type listed under What to edit, or change the column type. Monitoring outcome availability must use TIMESTAMP or offset ISO STRING: ... Use a TIMESTAMP column, or a string with an explicit offset. Source validation query did not complete: ... Start the warehouse, check your permissions on the tables and retry.

docs.title: Score on Spark workers
docs.text:
This page covers distributed scoring for a generated Databricks Bundle: batch_compute: spark worker configuration and admission, the table of what Spark scoring supports, worker capacity and environment settings, and how to read results and model-set composition. Read it when a saved model should score a Delta source in pandas batches on Spark workers instead of as one whole frame. Source selection, eligibility, watermarks and publication stay in the parent scoring guide.

Back to Score saved models and publish Delta predictions

Training fits one bounded pandas or Polars model in a Python process. Scoring can apply that fitted model to a whole frame or distribute admitted pandas prediction batches across Spark workers. Distributed inference does not turn the estimator's fit or tuning trials into distributed training.

flowchart LR
    A["Pinned Delta source"] --> B{"batch_compute"}
    B --> C["local: whole pandas/Polars frame"]
    B --> D["spark: admitted pandas worker batches"]
    C --> E["Saved preprocessing and model"]
    D --> E
    E --> F["Keyed predictions"]
    F --> G["Guarded Delta publication"]

Here batch_compute: single_node means whole-frame scoring, including on Databricks compute. It is separate from SDK runtime="standalone" versus runtime="databricks", which chooses the integration environment. UC Delta publication requires runtime="databricks". SDK runtime accepts standalone, databricks or spark; preflight rejects spark with runtime_unsupported because Spark scoring uses its separate batch runner. Monitoring already uses Spark and has no separate engine choice.

docs.title: Worker configuration and admission
docs.text:
Merge these fragments into the named files, keeping the remaining settings:

# config/training.yml
defaults:
  engine: pandas

# config/inference.yml
batch_compute: spark
spark_udf_env_manager: local
spark_udf_prediction_batch_rows: 10000

The Bundle uses mlflow.pyfunc.spark_udf; workers receive pandas batches and apply saved preprocessing without refitting. Explicit Spark with Polars is rejected. The library's predict_spark/mapInPandas API is a separate route. Without batch_compute, scoring is whole-frame (single_node).

docs.title: What Spark scoring supports
docs.text:
Admission checks the exact fitted artifact, not just its model-family name. The setup menus also serve whole-frame projects and therefore offer more choices than distributed scoring admits.

Part Admitted scope and important boundaries Linear models Exact LinearRegression and LogisticRegression. Tree models Exact DecisionTreeRegressor/Classifier, RandomForestRegressor/Classifier and ExtraTreesRegressor/Classifier; single-output fitted trees only. Custom subclasses or replaced inference methods are rejected. XGBoost Exact XGBRegressor with reviewed gbtree state and reg:squarederror or reg:logistic objective; no custom callbacks/objectives or DART. XGBClassifier instead needs sealed model probe evidence. Additional models AdaBoost, gradient boosting, histogram gradient boosting, nearest neighbours and LightGBM classifiers/regressors; Bernoulli/Gaussian/Multinomial Naive Bayes; calibrated classifier; ElasticNet, Lasso and Ridge regression; SGD classifier, SVC and SVR. Exact built-in classes and their saved configurations need sealed model probe evidence. Voting and stacking Classifiers and regressors need ensemble-level probe evidence. Every fitted member, calibration estimator and stacking final estimator must have an accepted exact identity. Replacing a member invalidates admission. Reviewed preprocessing SimpleImputer, StandardScaler, MinMaxScaler, ClipValues, GroupImputer, OneHotEncoder and FeatureInteraction. Each must pass its configuration/state checks and preserve rows. SimpleImputer supports mean, constant, most_frequent and median; GroupImputer supports mean, most_frequent and median. OneHotEncoder requires max_categories: null and include_missing: false; fixed string categories and column_names: slug retain these requirements and strict fitted-state inspection. Median uses saved training values through the pandas worker path; this does not add a native Spark median codec. Other built-in preprocessing Eligible row-preserving steps need sealed evidence for their actual saved state and recipe; see the table below. A successful probe cannot override a declared group/window/global context or row filtering. Skipped fitted row steps Deduplicate, DropMissingRows and RowFilterFunction (filter_step) are skipped by the prediction chain to preserve request rows. They do not filter each worker batch. Tuning and thresholds Reviewed fitted tuning wrappers are supported. Arbitrary tuned feature exclusions are rejected; recorded CV time/group metadata removal retains its existing contract. Tuned thresholds need a valid class-to-threshold mapping and a reviewed classifier or matching probed model evidence. SGD with hinge loss and SVC without probability support retain label-only outputs. Model sets Every component must pass admission, including its saved scoring rules and reused pre-split recipe. Independent outputs, declared numeric weighted_sum/weighted_mean composition and combined function rules selected in scoring.yml (or legacy build_combined_rules()) are supported; function rules need sealed training probe evidence (see below). Saved project scoring rules Eligibility and output rules are admitted when training linted and probed them (see below); Spark and online-feature projects do this automatically. The result columns (scoring_status, exclusion_reason and the declared outputs) travel through the Spark UDF and endpoints. Reused pre-split eligibility (mode: pre_split or mode: combined in scoring.yml) is admitted when its steps are row-local and probed: fixed built-in edits, DropMissingRows, ManualBounds and filter_step functions. Deduplicate and custom filter classes in the reuse are rejected; validate_model rejects them before registration. preview.py --action score prints Project scoring rules: disabled when none are saved. Custom/context-dependent code column_step/fitted_step steps are admitted when training linted and probed them (see below). An inference_context="row" declaration is optional. group, window and global declarations, custom classes from custom_step, unreviewed fitted states and temporal carry history are rejected. A passing preprocessing diagnostics report (save_preprocessing_diagnostics) alone grants no admission.

Models packaged with feature lookup require batch_compute: spark; whole-frame mode rejects them, including feature-backed model-set components. They score through the Feature Engineering score_batch route. Lookup does not relax the model/preprocessing checks.

docs.title: Built-in recipes and model evidence
docs.text:
The following additional steps can be admitted when the saved recipe preserves rows, declares row context and passes every probe check. Admission is per fitted recipe: a name in this table does not promise support for every parameter choice.

Purpose Candidate steps Cleaning and types AliasReplacement, Casting, InvalidValueReplacement, TextCleaning, ValueReplacement Missing data DropMissingColumns, MissingIndicator, KNNImputer, IterativeImputer Encoding DummyEncoder, HashEncoder, LabelEncoder, OrdinalEncoder, TargetEncoder, WOEEncoder Scaling and transformations MaxAbsScaler, RobustScaler, Winsorize, SimpleTransformation, GeneralTransformation, PowerTransformer Outlier exclusion IQR, ZScore, EllipticEnvelope, ManualBounds (see rows that are not scored) Binning CustomBinning, GeneralBinning, KBinsDiscretizer Feature generation FeatureGeneration, FeatureGenerationNode, FeatureMath, PolynomialFeatures, PolynomialFeaturesNode Feature selection CorrelationThreshold, ModelBasedSelection, UnivariateSelection, VarianceThreshold, feature_selection Dates and geography DateFeatures, GeoDistance, H3Index (requires its optional package) Text count_vectorizer, hashing_vectorizer, tfidf_vectorizer, tokenizer

Six of these steps needed a change before Spark and endpoints could use them, because their earlier behaviour let one row affect the others in its batch:

Step Earlier problem Behaviour now IQR, ZScore, EllipticEnvelope, ManualBounds They dropped the rows they flagged, so a request of 10 rows could return 8 predictions. The flagged row stays in the output without a prediction, marked excluded with reason outlier:<step name>. The bounds are learned at training, so each row is judged on its own values. PowerTransformer One value it could not transform, for example zero or a negative value with Box-Cox, left the whole batch untransformed. Each value is transformed on its own. A row with a value that cannot be transformed (zero or negative with Box-Cox, infinity, or a result too large to represent) is marked excluded with reason invalid:<step name>; the other rows are unaffected. A missing value is not invalid: it stays missing, so a later imputer can fill it. With Box-Cox, every row that has a zero or negative value is excluded, so use Yeo-Johnson for columns that contain zeros, such as counts. If more than 10% of the step's training rows would be excluded as invalid (missing values do not count), training stops with an error that names the share and suggests Yeo-Johnson or repairing those rows first. IterativeImputer When every value in a batch was missing, it skipped its learned rounds and returned only the initial fill. The learned rounds always run, so a row is filled the same way in any batch. Posterior sampling (sample_posterior: true) and unsupported estimators stay rejected.

Window steps, resampling, inspection nodes and sentence_embedder are not added by this admission path.

docs.title: Rows that are not scored
docs.text:
When an outlier step or PowerTransformer excludes a row, the output still has one row per input row. The excluded row has:

  • an empty (null) prediction and empty probability columns;
  • scoring_status = excluded (scored rows have predicted);
  • exclusion_reason naming the first step that excluded it, for example outlier:trip_distance_iqr or invalid:fare_power. A later step never overwrites it. The outlier: and invalid: prefixes separate a deliberate filter from a value the fitted step cannot handle, usually a data error.

The same rule applies to whole-frame scoring, Spark scoring and serving endpoints. During training the excluded rows are left out of model fitting; each step's rows_in and rows_out in the training result show how many were left out. Monitoring adds exclusion_rate (all excluded rows) and invalid_exclusion_rate (rows excluded by invalid: reasons) to the quality table, as shares of all stored prediction outcomes; a rising invalid_exclusion_rate usually means a data-quality problem upstream rather than model drift. Performance monitoring uses only the scored rows. Whatever reads the predictions must handle an empty prediction: decide in the consuming application whether to use a default value, send the row for review or show "not scored"; do not read an empty prediction as zero or as the negative class.

Adding one of these steps adds the scoring_status and exclusion_reason columns to the model's output, so a scoring table written by an earlier version has a different schema. Write the new version to a new table or migrate the existing one before switching. How training measures a model that excludes rows is described in models that exclude rows.

Admission is decided for your saved settings, not for the step name. The tests fit every listed step with one typical recipe; a different setting of the same step can behave differently, and training then stops with the failing check instead of registering a model that would score inconsistently. Typical cases:

  • Output type depends on the data. Casting to int64 turns a column into floats when a batch contains text it cannot parse, so a single bad row changes the dtype of its whole batch. Cast to the nullable Int64 instead; its dtype stays the same in every batch.
  • State saved in an older format. Some encoders (DummyEncoder, HashEncoder, LabelEncoder, OrdinalEncoder, WOEEncoder) saved by earlier versions render categories from the whole batch. Retrain to save the current per-row state.
  • Settings that read other rows. A few steps use other rows only for particular options. The error names the step and the check; see When a built-in step or model is rejected.

Spark and online-feature projects run the checks automatically. Endpoint-only projects enable the same training check with defaults.allow_tested_custom_steps: true in config/training.yml; despite its historical name, this setting also seals built-in and model evidence. Train and register a new version after enabling it. Editing an old artifact's flag does not create evidence.

Built-in code uses an exact calculator/applier identity check instead of project source lint. Its saved state and resolved recipe are fingerprinted; the replay check creates a fresh stateless applier over detached state. Model probes check predictions, supported probabilities and configured thresholds on transformed holdout rows. Nested estimator identities are checked too. Model fresh_module replays separately serialized state; it does not reload a third-party package. The model's empty check calls the saved prediction API and verifies its declared empty output schema without invoking the estimator. Nonempty comparisons follow the comparison rule described under floating-point rounding.

Each step and the model is checked on its own, and the complete prediction chain is checked once more end to end: the raw holdout rows are scored as a whole, again, and in batches of 1 and 7 rows, through every preprocessing step, the model and any saved scoring rules. This catches a rounding difference that a step's own check allows but that changes a label after the model, for example a value close to a tree's split point. At least 16 holdout rows must reach each step and at least 16 must receive a prediction at the end; rows excluded on the way do not count. A recipe that leaves fewer rows fails training with a message naming where the rows were lost.

Look at partition_probe.json in the training run: builtins contains the preprocessing evidence and model contains model evidence. The recomputed Spark/endpoint certificate records apply_probed_builtin and model_probed. No project source directory is required for a pipeline using only built-ins. Custom functions still require their captured source and lint checks. These bounded observations are evidence for the trained recipe, not proof for every future input or every library version. Workers need the same supported runtime and optional packages as the saved model.

XGBoost and LightGBM fingerprints now include their native learned trees. Artifacts with earlier fingerprints or probe evidence need fresh evidence and repackaging with the corrected runtime. Copying the old certificate into a new package is not supported.

docs.title: Admit your own row steps (opt-in)
docs.text:
Skyulf cannot prove that your apply function or scoring rule uses only its saved training state. A function that computes something from the batch, such as df["x"].mean(), would give different answers on each Spark worker batch. Training therefore checks your own code before it can run on Spark workers or endpoints:

  • In a project with batch_compute: spark or online_features, the check runs automatically whenever the model has a column_step, a fitted_step or saved scoring rules. No setting is needed.
  • Other projects, for example one that only serves an endpoint from config/serving.yml, or SDK training, opt in:
# config/training.yml
defaults:
  allow_tested_custom_steps: true

# src/features/preprocessing.py; inference_context="row" is optional
fitted_step("clip_duration", learn, apply, output="duration")

The check has two parts, and every step and rule must pass both:

  1. Lint. Training reads the saved source of apply() (or the rule) and the helpers it calls in the same file. It rejects whole-batch calls on the input frame, such as .mean(), .sum() or .max() without axis=1, .rank(), .shift(), .groupby(), .sort_values(), .value_counts(), .any(), len(df) and df.shape[0]. It also rejects writes to shared process state anywhere in the step's functions: module globals, class or function attributes, os.environ, mutated default arguments and globals(). learn() may use batch statistics: learning on the training rows is its job. Row-wise forms are fine: .str/.dt methods, axis=1 (or a positional 1), the column count df.shape[1], and any()/all()/len(df) == 0 used only in an if that raises or returns early for empty input. The lint is a heuristic: it does not see other modules or dynamic calls, so the probe still runs.
  2. Probe. On the first 256 holdout rows (at least 16 are required), each step or rule must give the same results (floating-point values within the rounding tolerance) on the whole sample, when scored again, in chunks of 1, 2 and 7 rows, in reverse order, with the row index renumbered, on an empty batch, and when one row's inputs change (other rows must not move). Spark gives each batch a fresh 0, 1, 2, ... index and can send an empty batch, so code that reads df.index, fails on empty input or returns a different dtype for it is rejected. A step must not change values in its module's globals while it is probed. Finally, the step runs from a freshly loaded copy of the project code (fresh_module) and must give the same results, as a new worker process would.

perturb moves numbers by half their size, staying inside small integer types such as uint8, flips booleans and replaces text with a value the sample does not contain. If the step raises on that text (for example a date or number stored as text), the row is retried with the text unchanged; a step that still raises is reported as raised on a changed input value.

Steps without a declaration that pass both are treated as row-local. Steps declared group, window or global stay rejected, as do custom classes from custom_step. Scoring rules run on the rows they really receive: eligibility on the raw request, output rules on up to 256 eligible holdout rows plus predictions. A reused pre-split recipe is probed as one eligibility rule bound to its saved steps; target-reading steps stay skipped with skip_target_pre_split_steps in scoring.yml. Model-set combined rules from scoring.yml or legacy build_combined_rules() read the same row's component predictions; they are probed on up to 256 rows of the set's training source (perturb changes one row's inputs and component predictions) and their evidence is sealed in the set.

Passing results are saved inside the model as evidence, tied to each step's saved state, each rule's version, function and parameters, and the project source. Spark scoring and endpoints admit the code only when that evidence matches; the certificate records steps as apply_probed and rules as rules_probed. The training report lists every probed step and rule with its passed checks (Spark and endpoint admission probe). The evidence is bound to the sealed model by its checksum. It does not authenticate who produced the model: a trusted SDK or job producer is trusted.

Spark output carries null rule results as SQL nulls. To do so it reserves the text value ␀null␀: a string output equal to it is rejected, as are nullable int64 outputs beyond 2**53, which float64 transport cannot hold exactly.

The probe is evidence, not proof. It checks at most 256 holdout rows, so it can miss:

  • logic that depends on the batch size, such as code that only runs above 300 rows;
  • batch statistics used only for rare values that the holdout does not contain;
  • module-level caches and globals that the lint cannot see. These are not allowed. The probe only detects plain JSON values that change while it runs.

Keep apply functions and rules to row-by-row arithmetic on the saved state.

docs.title: When the probe fails
docs.text:
Every failure names the step or rule, the check and one fix, and ends with a link to this section. A lint failure also gives the file, line and call:

Custom step 'fill_values' reads a batch statistic (preprocessing.py line 41:
df['x'].mean()). Compute it in learn() and read it from state in apply() ...

Pick one of three fixes:

  1. Make the function row-local. Move the batch statistic from apply() into learn() and read it from the saved state:
# Before: every Spark batch fills with its own mean.
def apply(df, state):
    return df["x"].fillna(df["x"].mean())

# After: learn() saves the training mean once; apply() only reads it.
def learn(df, y):
    return {"mean": float(df["x"].mean())}

def apply(df, state):
    return df["x"].fillna(state["mean"])
  1. The calculation really needs other rows. Move it upstream into a groups/ Spark producer that writes a feature column, or into a pre-split step if it only concerns training rows. Otherwise declare inference_context="group" or "window" and keep the project on batch_compute: single_node.
  2. Lint false alarm on a per-row call. Write the row axis explicitly, for example df[["a", "b"]].sum(axis=1). There is no switch to turn the lint off, by design.

Find failures on your laptop before a training job:

# Lint the selected recipes and rules (Spark and online-feature projects).
python src/tools/preview.py --action train
# Fit on a local labeled sample (CSV or Parquet, 16+ rows) and run lint and probe.
python src/tools/smoke.py --probe sample.csv

Get a real sample by exporting SELECT * FROM <training_table> LIMIT 256; its columns and dtypes must match input_columns plus the target. The local probe uses the sample as both training rows and holdout, so it shows how the code behaves on those rows only. Training on the real holdout makes the final decision.

docs.title: When a built-in step or model is rejected
docs.text:
Built-in steps and models run the same probe checks as your own code, without the lint. A rejection stops training before the model is registered and names the part and the check, for example:

Model partition probe failed chunks:1: output_mismatch. Partition parity
requires exact labels and the fixed floating tolerance; retrain with a
compatible configuration.

The check name tells you what differed:

Check What it compares Usual cause What to do repeat The same rows scored twice; must match exactly, with no rounding tolerance Randomness at prediction time Fix random_state; avoid estimators that sample when predicting. chunks:1, chunks:2, chunks:7 Batches of 1, 2 and 7 rows against the whole sample Output depends on the batch size beyond the rounding tolerance (below): a whole-batch fallback, or a dtype that follows the data Choose a setting from the step's table above, use stable dtypes, or replace the step. reverse, index_shift Reversed row order; renumbered index The step reads row order or the pandas index Use a step that only reads column values. empty A batch with no rows The step fails or changes dtypes on empty input Report it: built-in steps are expected to handle empty batches. perturb Change one row's inputs; the other rows must not move The step reads other rows' values, such as a whole-batch fallback, or fails on a value training never saw Use a setting that handles unseen values row by row, for example handle_unknown: ignore on OneHotEncoder. fresh_module Reload the saved state in a new process State that does not survive saving Retrain; report it if it persists.

Floating-point rounding. Floating-point results can differ in the last digits between batch sizes, because the numeric library chooses a different calculation path for each batch size. For example, a stacking model whose default logistic_regression final learner combines member outputs differs by about 2e-16 between a batch of one row and a larger batch. The probe therefore compares floating-point columns, such as probabilities, regression predictions and transformed numeric features, with a fixed tolerance: two values match when |a - b| <= 1e-12 + 1e-9 * |b|, and missing values must be in the same places. Everything else stays exact: predicted labels, integer, text and boolean values, column names, order and dtypes, the row index and the row count. A difference larger than the tolerance, or a single changed label, still rejects the model. Evidence saved before this rule (evidence version 1) is not accepted; retrain to create new evidence.

Change the rejected step's or model's settings, or remove it, and retrain.

docs.title: Capacity and worker environment
docs.text:
max_rows and max_input_mb bound local training, not the distributed scoring population. spark_udf_prediction_batch_rows accepts 1 through 100000 (default 10000) and slices each worker input into model calls. It does not limit every incoming Arrow allocation: the worker still needs memory for that frame, the fitted model and prediction slices. Databricks controls Arrow transport; serverless does not permit setting spark.sql.execution.arrow.maxRecordsPerBatch. There is no universal row threshold for choosing Spark and no fallback to collecting the source if distributed execution fails.

The template uses spark_udf_env_manager: local on serverless, reusing the declared task environment with the required wheel/dependencies. Here "local" describes environment reuse on the worker, not driver-side inference. Policy-cluster projects use virtualenv to install the packaged wheel and saved pins in an isolated worker environment; Core's direct API default is also virtualenv. Validate that environment on the chosen runtime: the tested serverless runtime rejects MLflow 3.16.1 virtualenv archives containing absolute interpreter symlinks. There is no automatic environment fallback.

Certified MLflow packages carry a safety certificate, exact source hash and Skyulf wheel. A package logged without a certificate cannot use Spark; log a new certified version. A pickle alone provides no Spark capability. Workers recheck loaded state and runtime versions. Nullable integer and Boolean transport is handled before Arrow conversion.

When a fitted artifact retains an XGBoost or LightGBM estimator, saving it automatically records that library's exact installed version. This includes members inside voting, stacking and calibrated models. MLflow packaging adds these pins to its requirements, and loading checks them before unpickling the model. A plain sklearn model does not require either native library merely because it was installed during training. Python must have the same major and minor version; a different patch version is accepted. The other recorded runtime dependencies must match exactly.

Re-export and repackage older native artifacts that lack these dependency pins. Native-model fingerprints and partition probe evidence created before the corrected native-state hashing must also be regenerated; changing only a manifest does not update or validate the saved model.

For a repeatable native/worker/Bundle comparison, see Measuring inference capacity. Its timings include a correctness aggregate and exclude Delta publication; they are not complete score-job latency. Benchmark resources are separate from project jobs and the shared dashboard. Measure executor memory and packaging on your actual target compute.

docs.title: Results and model-set composition
docs.text:
In Workflows > score job > score task, inspect the concrete version, row counts, source watermark and receipt. Spark receipts include inference mode, environment manager and prediction batch size. Snapshots, insert-only CDF, no-op replay, model-change policies and optional recover_predictions use the same guarded Delta publication lifecycle. Model-set outputs commit together; successful scoring retains the monitoring and dashboard-refresh handoff.

Spark admits model-set composition as declarative weighted_sum or weighted_mean rules in model_set.composition_config, and as function rules selected in scoring.yml or legacy build_combined_rules() when training sealed their probe evidence in the set. The model set guide shows the rule format.

docs.title: When you need it
docs.text:
Use this page to remove one target of a generated project, for example a finished test trial or a personal development target. databricks bundle destroy removes what the Bundle deployed. Data, models and monitoring evidence are Unity Catalog or workspace objects that the Bundle never managed, so they stay.

flowchart LR
    A["Pause monitoring enrollment"] --> B["Stop continuous publication"]
    B --> C["bundle destroy -t target"]
    C --> D["Check what survives"]
    D --> E["Owner decides on manual cleanup"]

docs.title: What to edit
docs.text:
Do these steps first, while the jobs still exist. After destroy you can no longer run them.

Step How Pause batch monitoring enrollments Set monitoring_enabled: "false" for the target, redeploy and run the score job once. The inventory then records a paused enrollment instead of a model that stops reporting. Pause serving enrollments Run the monitoring job with monitoring_action=enroll_serving and each entry resubmitted with enabled: false; see serving monitoring. Stop a continuous feature publication Run online_publication with publication_action=stop, then status; see online features. A native pipeline keeps running after the job is gone. Pause a traffic rollout Pause the daily_rollout schedule. Destroying the job does not change endpoint traffic. Keep training evidence you still need Approval, rollback and monitoring reference preparation read saved candidate runs. Export or keep them before removing the folder that holds the experiment (see below).

If this target owns the shared monitoring dashboard (created with --create-dashboard), other projects use its URL. Either keep the owner target deployed, or first create a new owner in another project with --create-dashboard and rerun the helper with the new --dashboard-url in every project that uses it. See the dashboard page.

docs.title: The command
docs.text:
From the generated project root, with the same target and profile used to deploy:

databricks bundle destroy -t test --profile YOUR_PROFILE

The CLI lists the jobs and the workspace folder it will delete and asks for confirmation. Read the list before you confirm. Repeat per target; destroying test does not touch syst or prod.

docs.title: What you should see
docs.text:
bundle destroy removes the resources in the Bundle state of that target:

Removed Source Jobs train, score, monitoring resources/*.job.yml Optional jobs online_feature_lookup_setup, online_publication, daily_rollout Present when selected at setup The features job resources/features.job.yml, when created by refresh_feature_graph.py The dashboard refresh task A target's block in deployment/monitoring.yml, part of the monitoring job The shared monitoring dashboard Only in a target whose deployment/monitoring.yml block uses create Job permissions managed by the Bundle permissions and manage_job_permissions settings Deployed files and Bundle state The target's root_path workspace folder

The training jobs log to the MLflow experiment <root_path>/experiment, inside that folder. Treat it as deleted with the folder unless you move or export it first. Registered model versions stay in Unity Catalog, but their links to those runs no longer open.

These stay, because the Bundle never created them as resources:

Survives Notes Training and scoring source tables Never created by the project Prediction tables, generation tables and model-set views Created by the score job at run time Feature group outputs and the merged feature table Created by the features job at run time Monitoring store tables and views model_inventory, monitoring_results, performance_actions, retraining_requests, the views, reference_cleanup_audit, monitor_ref_* references and shared monitor_src_* populations; shared with other projects Monitoring enrollment rows Stay in model_inventory; paused if you followed the steps above Registered models, versions, aliases and tags Unity Catalog objects Monitoring experiment named by monitoring_experiment_name Outside the project folder when set to a path such as /Shared/... Serving endpoints and UC SQL functions Created by the SDK or the online_feature_lookup_setup job, not by the Bundle Online stores, online tables and publication pipelines Created through Feature Engineering, not by the Bundle A dashboard reused by URL Owned by another project or created outside the Bundle

Tables in your workspace explains what each of these objects holds and which ones grow over time.

docs.title: Common errors and fixes
docs.text:
Check ownership before deleting anything by hand. The monitoring store, the dashboard, feature tables and online stores are often shared with other projects. Registered models and prediction tables can feed other consumers. Only the owner of an object should remove it, with that team's normal process.

Symptom Fix destroy wants to delete resources you did not expect Stop and check -t and --profile. Destroy works on the Bundle state of the selected target only. Other projects lost their dashboard The destroyed target owned it. Redeploying creates a new dashboard with a new ID, so create a new owner with --create-dashboard and rerun the helper with its --dashboard-url in every project that uses it. The dashboard still lists the removed model Its enrollment row stays in the shared inventory. Pause it before destroying, as shown above. An endpoint still serves the model Endpoints are not Bundle resources. Its owner removes it in Databricks Serving.

docs.title: Training YAML: fields and complete examples
docs.text:
Use config/training.yml to choose the data, target, estimator, evaluation and promotion policy for each model. This reference explains every accepted training, model and tuning field, then supplies a complete file for each layout. The result of training is a fitted registered candidate with source/split/quality evidence; activation and scoring remain separate decisions.

Use a Core package matching your generated project; see runtime packaging. These local configuration examples do not create Delta tables, contact Databricks or prove cloud permissions. For first deployment and operator actions, follow the Bundle walkthrough.

docs.title: File ownership and inheritance
docs.text:
File or section What belongs here training.yml > defaults Shared data, engine, split/CV, budgets, gates and optional model settings training.yml > models.<name> One model or candidate's explicit overrides pre_split.yml Fixed training eligibility and normalization before splitting preprocessing.yml Ordered fitted transformations; selected recipes fit inside training folds inference.yml Scoring source, version selector, publication/change policy and score handoff; model-set activation/publication deployment/variables.yml and target overrides Job compute, identities, schedules and environment bindings src/features/ Trusted custom functions and scoring policy selected before training

The tables below apply to shared defaults and individual model entries unless their conditions say otherwise. A model entry replaces the whole value of a shared field; nested mappings are not deep-merged. For example, overriding model replaces its type and entire params mapping. Repeat the parameters you still need. Do not define another Python model declaration or workflow.json beside these YAML owners.

Competition candidates share one source, target, split, CV and selection policy. Their entries can override only model, tuning, decision_threshold, preprocessing_recipe and explainability. Competition does not accept features_path or pre_split_recipe in its defaults; use the default pre-split recipe. Independent target models can have different labels, inputs, recipes, models and gates, but must share the exact source snapshot and record keys. Never include any sibling target in a branch's inputs.

docs.title: Root structure
docs.text:
Key Type/default Meaning version Integer; required 1 Version of this YAML document, independent of the runtime config version below. defaults Mapping; {} if omitted Fields inherited by every named model. Complete effective settings still need the required fields. models Nonempty mapping; required Safe names starting with a letter, at most 64 ASCII letters/digits/underscore/hyphen. Single layout has one entry; competition needs at least two. pipeline Optional mapping; usually omit Only empty preprocessing: [], empty modeling: {} and shared explainability are accepted. Recipe lists belong in their own files. Do not duplicate explainability here and in defaults/models.

YAML uses real numbers, booleans and null, rather than the string answers used by the init wizard. Quote dates such as "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z" so YAML does not turn them into timestamp objects. Unknown/duplicate keys, aliases, nonfinite numbers and documents larger than 64 KiB are rejected.

docs.title: Training fields
docs.text: Default means the generated quick-project value, or the runtime default where a field is omitted. Required fields must be present after inheritance. Inactive optional fields should be omitted or null, as specified. The last column identifies the corresponding init answer; YAML means edit the field directly. Detailed setup exposes more init answers than quick setup. Branch answers use the same question name with a branch_N_ prefix.

docs.title: Class and row weights
docs.text:
Set classifier class weights in model.params, for example params: {class_weight: balanced}. null disables them. Keep a class weight fixed by removing its search axis; to tune it, omit the fixed parameter and retain the axis under tuning.search_space. Supported classifiers may also use row weights.

Set weight_column: importance in defaults or a target entry. Omit it or use null for unweighted fitting. Competition uses one shared column. Every active fold requires finite nonnegative values with positive total weight. Weights are not normalized. Declared weight columns remain reserved across branches and cannot be features, targets, keys, group columns or timestamps.

Weights affect estimator fitting; selection, holdout and threshold metrics remain unweighted. Built-in row changes carry explicit row positions; unsupported custom row mapping fails. Synthetic sampling needs an explicit supported weight policy. Source snapshots preserve the training column and saved evidence records its aggregate statistics and ordered digest. Logs do not print raw weight vectors. Scoring uses the saved model and needs no weight column. Weight-only edits do not count as fresh labels for automatic retraining; train explicitly after such edits.

docs.title: Model and recipe fields
docs.text:
Field Type Default/required Choices and effect Init answer or owner model Mapping Required here or inherited type is a registered task-compatible Core model ID; params is an optional mapping. Omit tuning to fit this model once. regression_model / classification_model and model_params; branch/candidate variants tuning Mapping Omitted disables search; generated projects normally include it Wraps the model in the existing tuner. Fields below use native search metrics, not heldout_ names. Search questions and YAML preprocessing_recipe String default Named list in preprocessing.yml. Each candidate/branch learns its own fitted state even when sharing a recipe. preprocessing_recipe; YAML pre_split_recipe String default Named fixed eligibility list in pre_split.yml. Competition always uses recipes.default and rejects this field. pre_split_recipe; YAML features_path String Generated src/features Alternative project feature package; supported only for multi-target model entries. Its source, assets and exact dependency pins are captured. YAML decision_threshold Mapping {mode: off} Classification only: off, manual or auto. Changes hard-label decisions without changing probabilities; nested fields below. decision-threshold questions; YAML explainability Mapping Omitted disables it SHAP method and bounded sample/display limits below; packages and report task must be present. shap_enabled and SHAP limit questions

model.params uses the selected estimator's public parameters. For example, ridge_regression accepts alpha, while a random forest accepts n_estimators and max_depth. Parameters do not transfer automatically when model type changes. Use python src/tools/preview.py --list-models and the model catalog for parameters, default search spaces, weights and ready-to-use YAML for each model. class_weight belongs in the compatible classifier's params; it is distinct from a source weight_column.

docs.title: Tuning fields
docs.text:
These keys go inside models.<name>.tuning or a shared defaults.tuning. Deleting the entire mapping disables search. An empty mapping still requests a tuner and needs a compatible objective. Learned preprocessing is refitted within the training folds; neither search nor calibration can use the final holdout. The search and ensemble guide explains the five strategies, their additional controls, CV, competition budgets and complete examples.

Field Type Default/required Choices and effect Init answer or owner strategy String random grid, random, optuna, halving_grid, halving_random. Optuna needs the matching optional dependencies. search_strategy metric String Required; generated rmse / accuracy Native Core metric such as rmse, r2, accuracy or f1; not heldout_rmse. Must match task and competition objective where applicable. regression_search_metric / classification_search_metric n_trials Integer 10 1..1000; trial/candidate budget for the selected strategy. Grid enumeration additionally respects max_candidates. search_n_trials random_state Integer 42 0 through 2**32-1; search seed independent of final split/CV seeds. search_random_state max_candidates Integer 1000 1..10000; rejects exhaustive grids above this bound before fitting. search_max_candidates search_space Mapping {} Parameter to nonempty finite scalar candidate list; empty means registered default space with fixed params preserved. At most 128 axes, 100 values/axis and 64 KiB. search_space timeout Number or null Omitted/null Positive finite seconds, optuna only; not an overall job deadline. search_timeout strategy_params Mapping {} Optuna sampler/pruner/pruning or halving factor/resource/min/max controls below; nonempty rejected for grid/random. Advanced search questions tune_threshold Boolean false Binary-classification nested-CV threshold search only; incompatible with an active decision_threshold. Prefer an explicit decision_threshold. search_tune_threshold

For a fixed value use model.params, for searched values use candidate lists: search_space: {alpha: [0.1, 1.0, 10.0]}. A manual search axis cannot contradict a fixed parameter. Unknown parameter names fail instead of being silently ignored. The outer job's CPU/memory limits still apply; search uses one estimator worker to avoid nested parallel fits.
