docs.text:
Mapping Fields, defaults and valid choices Meaning event_time_parsing / result_time_parsing format: null, timezone: null, date_only: reject (or midnight) Native timestamps need no format. Naive local clocks need an IANA timezone; offset-bearing formats must not also set one. Date-only values require midnight plus timezone. DST gaps/overlaps are rejected. decision_threshold, mode off Only mode: off Keep the estimator's normal hard-label decision. decision_threshold, mode manual Binary: value in [0,1] plus typed positive_class; or thresholds: [{class: ..., value: ...}, ...] covering every class with positive values Bind original class labels, not probability column indexes. Per-class decisions use the saved threshold policy. decision_threshold, mode auto metric: balanced_accuracy (also f1, f1_macro, f1_weighted, matthews_corrcoef), validation_fraction: 0.2 strictly between 0 and 1, random_state: 42, optional positive_class Uses separate training-side calibration; temporal models retain chronological ordering. explainability Required method: shap; max_samples 100 (1..200), max_features 30 (positive integer, no fixed upper bound), max_display_samples min(10,max_samples) (0..50 and no larger than max_samples) Training explanation and report display bounded by the configured budgets. evaluation_charts Required boolean enabled; max_rows 2000 (2..10000), max_features 20 (1..50), max_classes 20 (2..50) Bounded saved holdout chart sample; does not change full holdout metrics. feature_lookup lookups list, each with table_name, lookup_key and feature_names; optional timestamp fields only on supported offline paths Declare every fetched feature in input_columns. Keep lookup controls/source identities explicit. See online guide for exact native contract. online_features required_features and freshness: [{column: ..., max_age_seconds: ...}] Cover all fetched features; each lookup needs its saved DOUBLE UTC-epoch freshness input. The age bound is an explicit domain choice, not an automatic default. tuning.strategy_params for optuna sampler: tpe (random, cmaes); pruner: median (hyperband, none); optional boolean pruning Configures the installed Optuna integration. tuning.strategy_params for halving factor: 3 (2..10); resource: n_samples; min_resources and max_resources depend on resource Custom estimator resource needs a compatible parameter and explicit positive maximum. Bounds and supported count strings are validated before fitting.

See online feature lookup, classification threshold policy and preprocessing context for their complete execution contracts. A valid field set does not certify a fitted recipe for Spark or serving.

docs.title: Three complete training files
docs.text:
Start with a newly generated project of the same layout. Keep its config/inference.yml, src/features/, tool scripts and resource graph. Replace only training.yml with the chosen complete block below, and use these companion recipes. Both files require a default recipe, even if it is empty.

In config/pre_split.yml:

version: 1
recipes:
  default: []

In config/preprocessing.yml:

version: 1
recipes:
  default:
    - name: fill_numeric
      transformer: SimpleImputer
      params: {columns: [income, age], strategy: mean}
    - name: scale_numeric
      transformer: StandardScaler
      params: {columns: [income, age]}

The examples use numeric regression targets to keep estimator/metric roles easy to compare. The source is an existing Delta table with nonnull unique BIGINT customer_id, DOUBLE income/age, and DOUBLE revenue/cost labels. For local fit verification you can create the following frame; it does not upload a table:

import pandas as pd

frame = pd.DataFrame({
    "customer_id": range(1, 41),
    "income": [float(i) for i in range(1, 41)],
    "age": [float(20 + i % 10) for i in range(1, 41)],
    "revenue": [float(2 * i + 5) for i in range(1, 41)],
    "cost": [float(i + 2) for i in range(1, 41)],
})
assert frame.customer_id.is_unique and frame.shape == (40, 5)

docs.title: One model for one target
docs.text:
Save this entire block as config/training.yml in a single_model project. The imputer/scaler are learned separately on training rows; the final 20% holdout does not fit them. The absolute RMSE gate is illustrative.

version: 1
defaults:
  config_version: 1
  training_layout: single_model
  engine: pandas
  task: regression
  training_table: "{catalog}.{input_schema}.customer_training"
  training_table_version: null             # Resolve latest once when invoked.
  record_key_columns: [customer_id]
  input_columns: [income, age]        # Keys and labels are not features.
  target_column: revenue
  model_name: "{catalog}.{metadata_schema}.revenue_model{resource_suffix}"
  split_strategy: random
  training_window_mode: full_snapshot # No event timestamps are needed.
  test_size: 0.2
  random_state: 42
  stratify: false
  filter_unavailable_results: false
  max_rows: 10000
  max_input_mb: 64
  cv_enabled: false
  metric: heldout_rmse
  min_improvement: 0.0
  quality_threshold: 5.0              # Needed for first-champion approval.
  promotion_policy: manual_approval
  preprocessing_recipe: default
  pre_split_recipe: default
models:
  revenue:
    model:
      type: ridge_regression
      params: {alpha: 1.0}

There is no tuning mapping, so this example fits the stated fixed ridge model. A generated wizard project normally includes tuning; remove that mapping deliberately if a single fixed fit is intended.

docs.title: Several algorithms competing for one target
docs.text:
Save this in a model_competition project. Candidates share final holdout and three-fold training CV. Candidate overrides change only model/search/recipe settings. The winner alone proceeds to final holdout comparison and registration.

version: 1
defaults:
  config_version: 1
  training_layout: model_competition
  engine: pandas
  task: regression
  training_table: "{catalog}.{input_schema}.customer_training"
  training_table_version: null
  record_key_columns: [customer_id]
  input_columns: [income, age]
  target_column: revenue
  model_name: "{catalog}.{metadata_schema}.revenue_competition{resource_suffix}"
  split_strategy: random
  training_window_mode: full_snapshot
  test_size: 0.2
  random_state: 42
  stratify: false
  filter_unavailable_results: false
  max_rows: 10000
  max_input_mb: 64
  cv_enabled: true                   # Required by competition.
  cv_type: k_fold
  cv_folds: 3
  cv_shuffle: true
  cv_random_state: 42
  competition_max_candidates: 8
  competition_max_trials: 100
  metric: heldout_rmse               # Shared objective, not training accuracy.
  min_improvement: 0.0
  quality_threshold: 5.0
  promotion_policy: manual_approval
  preprocessing_recipe: default
models:
  ridge:
    model: {type: ridge_regression, params: {alpha: 1.0}}
  forest:
    model:
      type: random_forest_regressor
      params: {n_estimators: 20, max_depth: 4, random_state: 42}

To search ridge alpha instead, remove fixed alpha from that candidate's params and add tuning: {strategy: grid, metric: rmse, max_candidates: 10, search_space: {alpha: [0.1, 1.0, 10.0]}}. Search metric is rmse; the final comparison metric remains heldout_rmse. Keep aggregate work inside the competition budget. Do not tune parameters against the final heldout rows.

docs.title: Independent models for two targets
docs.text:
Save this in a multi_target project. Both branches share one source snapshot and keys; each has its own target, model and model name. Missing labels are excluded per target. No branch uses the sibling label as a feature.

version: 1
defaults:
  config_version: 1
  training_layout: multi_target
  engine: pandas
  task: regression
  training_table: "{catalog}.{input_schema}.customer_training"
  training_table_version: null
  record_key_columns: [customer_id]
  input_columns: [income, age]
  split_strategy: random
  training_window_mode: full_snapshot
  test_size: 0.2
  random_state: 42
  stratify: false
  filter_unavailable_results: false
  max_rows: 10000
  max_input_mb: 64
  cv_enabled: false
  metric: heldout_rmse
  min_improvement: 0.0
  quality_threshold: 5.0
  promotion_policy: manual_approval    # Set activation is separate in inference.yml.
  preprocessing_recipe: default
  pre_split_recipe: default
models:
  revenue:
    target_column: revenue
    model_name: "{catalog}.{metadata_schema}.revenue_model{resource_suffix}"
    model: {type: linear_regression, params: {}}
  cost:
    target_column: cost
    model_name: "{catalog}.{metadata_schema}.cost_model{resource_suffix}"
    model: {type: ridge_regression, params: {alpha: 0.5}}

The model_set block in inference.yml owns complete-set activation and output storage; choose its output mode as described in model sets. Individual component aliases are not the set's release mechanism. Branches do not compete against each other: they predict different targets. A failed branch leaves earlier immutable candidates available but produces no complete successful set.

For the generated graph, MLflow parameters, evaluation charts and SHAP reports, see training reports. Configure classification decision thresholds separately from quality gates.

docs.title: Check edits before training
docs.text:
Run from the generated project with the matching Core installed:

uv pip install -r deployment/train-requirements.txt
python src/tools/smoke.py
python src/tools/preview.py --action train --catalog workspace --input-schema demo --output-schema demo --metadata-schema demo
python src/tools/refresh_training_graph.py

Replace the preview bindings with the intended target's values; see the local tools reference for every flag and default. Preview does not read deployment/targets.yml for you. After changing model names, candidates or branch count, refresh the graph and validate/deploy it before running the job. Scoring source/model selector/model-set settings remain in the existing inference.yml; update them to the intended trained names and concrete versions. The training file alone is not a complete deployment or scoring configuration.

Smoke checks configuration/source syntax; preview resolves trusted recipe builders and displays each candidate/branch's effective model, inputs, window, CV and metric. Neither fits a model or reads Delta data. Expect one model preview, two competition candidates or two target branches for the examples above. Use a real fit/save/predict check on representative rows before production.

If a pre-split recipe reads the target, choose scoring behavior before preview: in config/scoring.yml set skip_target_pre_split_steps: true to retain feature-only reuse while skipping target-reading filters, or choose mode: custom for separately defined scoring eligibility. Mixed target/feature filters are skipped whole. An imputer does not override a scoring eligibility exclusion; excluded outcomes retain their keys and null predictions.

Error or surprising result Action Unknown/duplicate key or multiple owners Correct the exact field or remove the competing declaration; values are not merged silently. Recipe missing/default recipe absent Add a default recipe and select an existing named list in the matching phase file. Target-reading pre-split recipe blocks preview Choose the explicit scoring switch/mode above; the examples' empty pre-split recipe needs neither change. First-champion approval requires a bound Set quality_threshold before training and create a new candidate with saved matching evidence. Automatic policy lacks quality_threshold Supply a domain-appropriate absolute bound before training. Window controls active in the wrong mode Omit/null inactive calendar/day/event/result fields; choose the intended window and split independently. No tuning intended but search runs Remove tuning mapping, rather than leaving an empty one. Budget exceeded Deliberately reduce the eligible source/sample or review a larger limit; prediction never samples automatically. Model/params changed but scoring is unchanged Train a new version, select/activate it deliberately, and run scoring; old artifacts keep their saved state.

Continue to preprocessing recipes for node choices, SDK workflows for Python use, and the operator walkthrough for actual run/task inspection and copyable approval/rollback fields.

docs.title: Select training rows, time windows and holdout
When you need it
docs.text: Choose the population and evaluation split before training. Snapshot version, observation window, label availability, sample, split and job schedule are separate choices. These rules apply to single-model, competition and model-set projects.

docs.title: Prepare the source table
docs.text:
Skyulf reads existing tables; it never creates or repairs them. Before the first training run, make sure the training and scoring sources meet these rules:

Requirement Why Unity Catalog Delta table Training pins a Delta snapshot version; scoring reads Delta changes. Change Data Feed on the scoring source, before new rows arrive Incremental scoring reads new rows from the change feed. The default first score processes existing rows; initial_scoring: from_now checkpoints without predictions. Scoring explains the starting choice, updates and deletes. Record key columns of type STRING or BIGINT, nonnull and unique Keys identify each prediction. Date or timestamp keys are not supported. Keys kept out of input_columns Keys are copied to the output, not learned from. A nonnull target for every eligible training row Skyulf does not create labels. Use result availability for delayed outcomes. The same key and input columns, with the same types, in training and scoring sources The saved pipeline expects the training input schema. The scoring source needs no target. Date columns stored consistently Declare their type and parsing as described in source date formats.

To enable Change Data Feed on an existing table you own:

ALTER TABLE my_catalog.my_schema.customer_observations
SET TBLPROPERTIES (delta.enableChangeDataFeed = true);

For a worked example table, see the end-to-end guide.

docs.title: Spark DECIMAL model values
docs.text:
At the Spark-to-model boundary, Skyulf converts selected DECIMAL(p,s) model inputs, numeric targets and weights to DOUBLE / float64. Bounded training, batch prediction, Spark worker inputs and the serving job's smoke sample use the same rule. Nulls remain missing values for the fitted preprocessing. Record keys, grouping identities and time controls retain their declared types. Use supported STRING or BIGINT record keys. Serving refuses a DECIMAL key that cannot be represented by its saved JSON contract; it does not round the key to float.

For example, an amount DECIMAL(17,6) input becomes float64 in the fitted pipeline, double in its MLflow signature and DOUBLE in the generated SQL scoring function. REST callers send JSON numbers or null, rather than Python decimal.Decimal objects. Converting DECIMAL to float64 may lose precision beyond roughly 15–17 significant digits.

The completed training report and training_data.json list the observed conversions:

{
  "source_column_conversions": [
    {"column": "amount", "source_dtype": "decimal(17,6)", "target_dtype": "float64"}
  ]
}

The saved model's manifest.json records conversions for its fitted inputs; a model set retains these in each component manifest. The default offline preview cannot inspect a table's physical types. Use its source-validation action for planned casts on the current schema, and the training report for casts actually performed on the pinned snapshot. Older artifacts without this field have no recorded conversion evidence.

Native Feature Engineering lookup reads its own source/feature tables after Skyulf's projection. Its model-value columns must already use DOUBLE; persist the converted column and retrain before logging or serving that native lookup model. Its existing admission check rejects DECIMAL storage with an actionable message.

If an older champion learned a DECIMAL input as object or string, the new float64 candidate has a different input contract. Follow the schema migration steps before switching consumers; a runtime-recovery flag does not override schema validation.

docs.title: Choose a table layout
docs.text:
A project reads data in three roles. A layout only decides how many physical tables hold them:

Role What it holds Who reads it Training data Inputs and the known answer (target) for past rows The train job, to fit the model Scoring input Rows to predict, without a target The score job, which writes the predictions table Actual outcomes (labels) The real answer for a predicted row, learned later: record key, target and the time it became known (available_at) Monitoring, to compare predictions with reality; training too, when training_label_table is set

A label is the actual answer. A prediction is made before the answer is known, so the scoring input has no target; the answer is inserted into the outcomes table when it arrives.

The score job never writes to its input table. It reads only the record keys and input columns, so a target column in the scoring input is ignored, and it writes each prediction as a row of the separate prediction table (see Tables in your workspace). Even with one input table, a project therefore has at least two tables: the input and its predictions.

Quick and detailed setup both ask for source_layout. single_table is the default and uses embedded training targets. separate_outcomes connects one feature source to a separate actual-outcome table for both training and monitoring. separate_all asks for a distinct scoring source and keeps targets in the training table. The separate layouts require an outcome table and its availability column. Existing answer files with an explicit scoring-table override retain that override even when no layout answer was supplied.

Check or create your source tables walks through the check, the table contract and its error messages.

Each generated project includes SOURCES.md and a read-only validation command. The optional config/sources.sql starter is generated only when setup selects include_source_sql: "true" (default "false"). Existing tables need no SQL starter:

python src/tools/preview.py --action sources --profile YOUR_PROFILE --warehouse-id YOUR_WAREHOUSE_ID --catalog my_catalog --input-schema my_schema --output-schema my_schema --metadata-schema my_schema

The check reads Delta metadata, CDF settings, required columns, compatible input types, unique/non-null keys and the declared outcomes. Key probes may scan the full table; no data or settings are changed. It validates the calling identity's access to current tables. It cannot prove future inserts or another run-as identity will satisfy the same contract. Supply --label-table and --label-available-at-column when target overrides differ from setup answers. Fetched Feature Store outputs are not required in raw tables. The report warns that lookup-table permissions, point-in-time joins and fetched feature types still require the training checks. The SQL starter deliberately leaves unknown types as TYPE_FOR_column: replace these and namespace placeholders with your real schema before running.

Training, scoring and monitoring each read a table you name: training_table in config/training.yml, the scoring source in config/inference.yml, and monitoring_label_table in deployment/targets.yml. They may be the same table or different ones. Choose by how your actual outcomes arrive:

Layout Use it when Configure One append-only table Each row is complete when it is inserted (inputs, target and the time the outcome became known) and is never updated afterwards. Point all three settings at the same table. Training selects its window with start/cutoff and keeps rows whose outcome is available; scoring reads newly inserted rows. Measurements plus a separate outcomes table The outcome is known only later. New measurements are inserted without a target; outcomes are inserted into a second table keyed by the same record key. separate_outcomes sets both training_label_table and monitoring_label_table; training joins a pinned outcome snapshot. Training and scoring share the measurement source. A raw table plus derived tables or views Your raw source receives updates or deletes, such as late corrections or outcomes written into existing rows. Keep the raw table for your own processes, and give Skyulf insert-only derived tables: one for training, one for scoring inputs, one for outcomes. source_layout Tables Use it when single_table One: inputs, target and available_at Each row arrives complete with its answer and is never updated afterwards separate_outcomes Two: measurements without a target, and actual outcomes The answer arrives later; the most common case separate_all Three: training with targets, scoring input, actual outcomes Training and scoring data come from different places, as in the real_data examples

In every layout the score job works in batches: each run predicts the rows inserted since the previous run, found through Delta change data feed. It does not predict a row the moment it arrives; use a serving endpoint for that.

The generated source_layout choices map to these tables and jobs:

flowchart LR
    subgraph ONE["single_table"]
        O1[("observations: inputs, target, available_at")]
        O1 --> T1["train"]
        O1 -- "new inserts" --> S1["score"]
        O1 -- "outcomes" --> M1["monitoring"]
        S1 -- "predictions" --> M1
    end
    subgraph TWO["separate_outcomes"]
        F2[("measurements: inputs only")]
        L2[("outcomes: key, target, available_at")]
        F2 --> T2["train"]
        L2 -- "pinned join on the record key" --> T2
        F2 -- "new inserts" --> S2["score"]
        L2 -- "outcomes" --> M2["monitoring"]
        S2 -- "predictions" --> M2
    end
    subgraph THREE["separate_all"]
        A3[("training table: inputs, target")]
        B3[("scoring source: inputs only")]
        L3[("outcomes: key, target, available_at")]
        A3 --> T3["train"]
        B3 -- "new inserts" --> S3["score"]
        L3 -- "outcomes" --> M3["monitoring"]
        S3 -- "predictions" --> M3
    end

In separate_all, training keeps the targets embedded in its own table: new labelled rows must reach that table upstream, unless you also configure training_label_table. Only separate_outcomes joins the outcomes into training by default.

Three behaviours decide which layout works:

  • Incremental scoring accepts inserts only. For a single model or a competition, an UPDATE or DELETE in the scoring source fails the score job with Source updates and deletes require an explicit rescore policy. Model sets alone can opt into on_source_change: rescore_all; see source changes. Writing an outcome into an existing scoring row is an update, so use a separate outcomes table instead.
  • Choose whether to score existing rows. The default initial_scoring: full_snapshot includes historical training rows when the source is shared; that first population is an in-sample observation. Set initial_scoring: from_now in config/inference.yml before the first score to record a zero-row checkpoint and score only later inserts. The choice is fixed for that prediction target. Rebuilds preserve the starting boundary using saved prediction keys and recent CDF. Only CDF-expiry recovery needs the original starting snapshot to remain readable. See start with new records only. If you keep full_snapshot, run the first score on its own UTC day and ignore that day's performance window; the policy cannot filter out training rows.
  • Monitoring needs to know when an outcome became available. The outcomes table must contain the saved record keys, the target and a UTC timestamp for when the actual value was known (monitoring_result_available_at_column); see delayed labels.

The single-table air-quality walkthrough trains on summer rows, then appends individual winter days to the same input table and scores them with Spark. Outcomes stay in a separate table, so retrying a partial load never updates the scoring source. It also explains why loading two historical days today does not create two daily performance-policy windows.

Tables in your workspace shows these tables next to the ones the jobs create. The prepared examples use the second layout: observations_train, observations_score and labels, with no column ever updated. When new data arrives, insert it: new measurements into the scoring source, measured outcomes into the outcomes table. These prepared examples keep embedded training targets, so they also need newly labelled rows in the training source before retraining. With training_label_table, insert new feature rows into the training source and actual targets into the outcome table instead; the join supplies the labels.

docs.title: Train from separate outcomes
docs.text:
Use a read-only join when new feature rows arrive before their actual target. The separate_outcomes layout generates this configuration; you can also add it explicitly to defaults or a model entry in config/training.yml:

training_table: "{catalog}.{input_schema}.measurements"
training_table_version: null
training_label_table: "{catalog}.{input_schema}.outcomes"
training_label_table_version: null
record_key_columns: [record_id]
input_columns: [temperature, humidity]
target_column: demand
filter_unavailable_results: true
result_available_at_column: available_at
result_availability_lag_hours: 0
# result_cutoff is resolved at invocation when omitted.

The outcomes table supplies record_id, demand and the UTC available_at. Its target and availability values are authoritative; same-named columns in the feature table are ignored. Both sources need unique, non-null keys with exactly matching types. A duplicate outcome fails instead of choosing an arbitrary latest row. Missing joins and outcomes after the availability cutoff are excluded by the existing availability policy. An available row with a null target still needs an explicit target-missing policy; joining does not invent labels or silently relax target validation.

At invocation, both Delta versions and the outcome table's immutable identity are pinned. Saved training specifications, dataset identity and MLflow input provenance include that binding. Replaying the saved model uses those versions, even if outcomes have since arrived. A replaced same-name outcome table fails the identity check. training_label_table_version: 12 explicitly selects version 12; leave it null for new training runs to see later outcomes. No source rows are written or merged back into Delta.

The same join is used for pandas/Polars training and Spark retraining freshness checks. It can recognize new eligible labels when the feature table has not changed. In separate_all, rows arriving only in the scoring source still need to reach the configured training feature source upstream. Model-set branches may share one outcome table with multiple targets; each branch keeps its own target and availability policy.

docs.title: Local input limits
docs.text:
max_rows bounds the rows read into the local process before train/test splitting. Without sampling it applies after any observation-window selection, but before result-availability filtering. An overflow fails; the reader never silently truncates data. Explicit sampling is available as described below.

Quick setup uses max_rows: 10000 and max_input_mb: 64. Detailed setup also asks for training_sample_rows; null means no sampling. Overflow errors show the configured limit and the setting to edit. A bounded read reports at least the observed number of rows, not a fabricated count of the entire table.

max_input_mb is required; setup writes 64. One unit is 1 MiB (1,048,576 bytes). It bounds measured decoded input/serialized row sizes and local frames; it does not cap Spark's scan, total process RAM, preprocessing expansion or model training RAM. The existing scoring services also check bounded prediction frames. Row count alone cannot predict size: wide numeric tables and long strings cost more.

max_rows: 100000
max_input_mb: 256

These are illustrative limits, not a claim that every 100,000-row dataset fits 256 MiB. Training, scoring and approval convert this value to bytes internally. Approval may tighten but never relax the saved training budget. The lower-level Python SDK accepts max_bytes; Bundle settings use only max_input_mb. In an answer file use "max_input_mb": "64"; the generated config/training.yml stores the number 64.

docs.title: Record identity and result availability
docs.text:
Keys must be non-null STRING or BIGINT values and uniquely identify records across the initial data and later inserts. Initialization accepts customer_id, observation_id and emits an ordered array. For repeat observations of a customer, choose a composite key before deployment. Keep keys out of input_columns; the Bundle does not create IDs or turn them into model features.

Reference Role training_table Existing labeled source, pinned to a Delta snapshot for training score_source_table Existing CDF-enabled source for predictions prediction_table Output table, or active view in full-rebuild mode model_name Unity Catalog registered model, not a table

Training and scoring default to the same existing source. Separate them when labeled examples and new prediction requests have different lifecycles. The initial score processes existing source rows, including historical labeled rows if you retain that default. A prediction keeps its keys, so it can be queried:

SELECT customer_id, prediction, model_version
FROM catalog.schema.predictions
WHERE customer_id = 'C123';

config/training.yml uses the following names:

record_key_columns: [customer_id, observation_id]
event_column: observation_date
target_column: claim_amount
result_available_at_column: result_confirmed_at

The key columns identify a source record and are copied to prediction output. They do not create an ID, become features, or implicitly define CV groups. event_column names the source observation timestamp; start, holdout_start and cutoff are boundaries applied to that column. result_available_at_column names each row's actual result-availability timestamp. Different rows can have different availability dates. With filter_unavailable_results: true, exclude unknown results and results later than the independent result_cutoff. Skyulf does not invent those timestamps or fill them with the job's execution time.

Use record_key_columns and result_available_at_column in answer files. The default example identity column is entity_id. Date columns you do not answer are omitted from the generated YAML, which means null. Initialization does not create columns or generate timestamps. The same names are used throughout the library and saved training settings.

docs.title: Choose the evaluation split and result availability
docs.text:
The default split_strategy: "random" needs only existing keys, features and a nonnull target. training_table_version pins the source Delta snapshot; it is unrelated to dates. Leave it null to resolve latest once at run start, or set a nonnegative integer to pin that version. This example shows the training-related part of the generated config/training.yml defaults. Generation omits keys whose value is null, such as event_column, start or result_cutoff:

defaults:
  training_table_version: 12
  record_key_columns: [customer_id]
  input_columns: [income, age]
  target_column: claim_amount
  split_strategy: random
  training_window_mode: full_snapshot
  test_size: 0.2
  random_state: 42
  stratify: false
  filter_unavailable_results: false
Split Availability filter Required date settings Random Disabled None; all supplied targets must be known. Random Enabled result_available_at_column; explicit result_cutoff or invocation time minus lag; source parsing rules when needed. Temporal Disabled event_column; start, holdout_start, cutoff for fixed_window, or rolling_calendar or rolling_days settings; source parsing rules when needed. Temporal Enabled Both sets above; observation and result cutoffs are independent.

For random splitting with delayed outcomes, keep the event fields null and set filter_unavailable_results: true, result_available_at_column: "confirmed_at" and an aware result_cutoff, for example 2026-09-15T00:00:00+00:00, or leave it null to derive invocation time minus result_availability_lag_hours. Each row is eligible only if its own result date is known and no later than that instant. A future snapshot/cutoff can admit results that became available later. Null availability is excluded; a known, eligible result with a null target fails. With filtering disabled, any null target fails: Skyulf does not manufacture labels.

Core DataSplitter selects the random holdout after sorting by the complete record key. The same snapshot, keys, seed and split settings retain membership when input row order changes. stratify: true is for classification; insufficient class counts or an impossible partition fail instead of silently disabling it. A different snapshot may produce different membership even with the same seed. The final holdout never fits preprocessing or the model.

Saved training settings include the split policy and a holdout-key digest. holdout_membership.json records the key-column names, count and digest without labels. Approval replays the saved snapshot and verifies that membership before comparison; changing today's workflow cannot silently replace the evaluation set. See training CV and the independent source-window controls below.

Inactive fields must stay null/default: full-snapshot selection rejects event fields; random splitting rejects holdout_start. A random split can use an explicit event window without becoming a temporal split. A result column with availability filtering disabled is rejected. Missing temporal dates never switch training to random. Initialization hides irrelevant prompts but preserves explicitly supplied values so validation can identify conflicts. The examples folder contains date-free-init.example.json, random-delayed-results-init.example.json and temporal-delayed-results-init.example.json. Replace their table/feature names and snapshot before using them. Their date examples assume native timestamp instants; edit parsing rules for other source types. In answer-file JSON, test_size, random_state, stratify and filter_unavailable_results are strings; the generated YAML stores numbers and booleans.

docs.title: Explicit training sampling
docs.text:
training_sample_rows: 10000
training_sample_seed: 42
max_rows: 10000
max_input_mb: 64

training_sample_rows: null keeps the full selected input and fails on budget overflow. When enabled, Spark selects up to the requested number of eligible records using a seeded SHA-256 ordering of complete record keys. Selection occurs before local transfer, after window and result-availability filtering. Changing partition layout does not change the sample. A different seed or source snapshot may change it. The requested count must be 4 through max_rows.

The count includes the final holdout: a 10,000-row sample with test_size: 0.2 produces 8,000 training and 2,000 test rows. Sampling is without replacement and is not class-balanced; split/CV class-count guards still apply. For temporal splits it samples within the chosen window; both partitions must remain usable. It never samples inference rows. Record keys must be nonnull and unique across the selected source, and eligible targets must be nonnull before sampling.

training_selection.json records source/eligible/selected counts, seed, algorithm and membership digest. Saved training evidence pins both sample and holdout membership; approval replays those choices. Row/memory budgets remain enforced. Sampling bounds transfer, not Spark scans: validation, counts and hash ordering can scan the selected source several times.

docs.title: Source windows are independent of splitting and scheduling
docs.text:
training_window_mode Source selection Settings full_snapshot All eligible rows from the pinned snapshot Random split; event fields, lookback and window timezone null. fixed_window Explicit [start, cutoff) observations Event column and boundaries; random or temporal split; lookback and window timezone null. rolling_calendar Completed calendar months, derived at every train invocation Event column, explicit window_timezone and monthly_lookback_months; random or temporal split. rolling_days Preceding elapsed UTC days, ending at invocation time Event column, lookback_days; temporal uses holdout_days, random uses test_size. Calendar-only fields stay null.

With training_window_mode: auto, setup writes full_snapshot for random projects and an editable rolling_calendar with four months and window_timezone: "UTC" for temporal projects. Every train invocation resolves latest once when training_table_version is null or missing; an explicit version is honored regardless of trigger. rolling_calendar and rolling_days derive new observation boundaries, including for manual runs. Fixed windows stay fixed even if a job runs again a month later.

Sampling fields participate in the saved dataset identity even when sampling is disabled.

For example, window_timezone: "Europe/Vilnius" uses Vilnius month boundaries, including the correct seasonal UTC offsets. Four months includes the temporal holdout month: three months for fit, the last completed month for final test. Random splitting instead divides the selected four-month data by test_size and leaves holdout_start null. Temporal lookback is 2-120 months; random is 1-120. Source parsing timezone, window timezone and cron timezone serve different purposes. Neither the cron day nor the source timestamp format determines the calendar implicitly. When availability filtering is enabled, an explicit result_cutoff is honored; null derives invocation time minus result_availability_lag_hours, equally for manual and scheduled runs.

flowchart LR
    Source["Pinned Delta source"] --> Window["Full, fixed or rolling selection"]
    Window --> Sample["Optional eligible-row sample on Spark"]
    Sample --> Split["Random or temporal outer split"]
    Split --> Train["Training rows"]
    Split --> Test["Protected final holdout"]
    Train --> CV["Optional CV and search with fold-local preprocessing"]
    CV --> Fit["Final pipeline fit with fixed or tuned parameters"]
    Train --> Fit
    CV --> Report["MLflow CV report"]
    Fit --> Evaluation["Final evaluation and champion comparison"]
    Test --> Evaluation

docs.title: Source date formats and timezones
docs.text:
Column names and time boundaries serve different purposes. event_column selects the source column; event_time_parsing explains its values. The start, holdout_start and cutoff boundaries are timezone-aware instants. They do not need to use the same UTC offset as source values.

Edit these settings in the generated config/training.yml defaults. Calendar and day-window fields are omitted because fixed_window does not use them:

defaults:
  split_strategy: temporal
  training_window_mode: fixed_window
  filter_unavailable_results: true
  event_column: observation_date
  event_time_parsing: {format: "%d/%m/%Y %H:%M:%S", timezone: Europe/Copenhagen, date_only: reject}
  result_available_at_column: result_confirmed_at
  result_time_parsing: {format: "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z", timezone: null, date_only: reject}
  start: "2026-06-01T00:00:00+00:00"
  holdout_start: "2026-08-01T00:00:00+00:00"
  cutoff: "2026-09-01T00:00:00+00:00"
  result_cutoff: "2026-09-15T00:00:00+00:00"

In this example 01/08/2026 02:00:00 in Copenhagen and 2026-08-01T03:00:00+03:00 represent the same instant: August 1 at 00:00 UTC. An event at that instant belongs to the holdout. The window includes start and excludes cutoff; the holdout includes holdout_start.

Source values Parsing settings Native Spark TIMESTAMP instants Keep defaults: format: null, timezone: null, date_only: "reject"; the stored instant is retained. Native TIMESTAMP_NTZ or naive local datetimes Set the source IANA timezone; leave format: null. Strings containing UTC offsets Set an explicit format with %z; leave timezone: null. Strings containing local clock times Set an explicit format and source timezone. Native DATE or date-only strings Set date_only: "midnight" and source timezone; strings also need a date format.

Formats use Python numeric directives: %Y, %m, %d, %H, %M, %S, %f and %z, with literal separators. A complete four-digit year, month and day are required. They are not Spark/Java patterns such as yyyy-MM-dd. The same parser handles formatted source values and local validation, so pandas and Polars training receive the same instants. Precision is limited to microseconds; submicrosecond pandas timestamps are rejected. Local month names, missing years and guessed day/month order are not supported. An explicit %d/%m/%Y resolves day/month order; a string without a format does not.

Date-only values are not automatically interpreted as UTC. For example, 2026-08-01 with date_only: "midnight" and Europe/Copenhagen means July 31 at 22:00 UTC, before the holdout boundary above. Ambiguous or nonexistent local times at daylight-saving transitions fail; supply an offset-bearing source timestamp to make the intended instant explicit.

Source dates are normalized in Spark before filtering. Invalid/null event values fail validation even if a window filter would otherwise hide them. A null result-availability value remains unavailable, while a malformed value fails. Normalized instants cross the Spark/Python boundary as integer microseconds; session and process timezone settings do not reinterpret them. The local row/byte limits still apply after filtering. Date validation may scan the pinned source snapshot in Spark; these limits bound driver materialization, not the amount of distributed source validation.

Keep driver, worker and replay environments' timezone data aligned. Saved rules record zone identifiers, not a copy of the IANA timezone database.

Parsing rules are saved with the candidate's training specification and dataset identity. Approval replays those saved rules. The job's cron timezone only controls when it runs; it does not define the source timestamps' timezone. For Python APIs, use TrainingDateSpec in the Python SDK training guide. The supported format vocabulary is a subset of Python's strptime directives; source timezone rules use IANA zoneinfo.

training_table_version defaults to null, resolving latest once at the start of each train invocation. Set an explicit version for a repeatable snapshot. Date boundaries default to null and are required only for fixed_window; rolling_calendar and rolling_days derive them at invocation. Scoring and saved-evidence actions do not require a new training window.

docs.title: The command
docs.text:
Edit config/training.yml defaults or the selected model entry, then inspect the resolved request:

python src/tools/preview.py --action train
databricks bundle validate --strict -t test --profile YOUR_PROFILE

Preview validates configuration, not real source values. After deployment, run train; it pins the source and checks actual keys, dates, labels and budgets before fitting.

docs.title: What you should see
docs.text:
Inspect training_data.json, training_selection.json when sampling is configured, and holdout_membership.json in the model-producing MLflow run. They identify the source and saved selection; training reports explain the run graph and Inputs view.

Saved-artifact holdout evaluation uses sequential joblib prediction so parallel Random Forest tree summation does not introduce last-bit metric differences into exact approval evidence. This affects evaluation only: model hyperparameters and normal training/batch inference parallelism are retained. Arbitrary numerical runtimes may still be nondeterministic and must pass replay checks.

docs.title: Common errors and fixes
docs.text:
Symptom Fix Row/byte budget exceeded Choose an explicit sample or a smaller source window; there is no silent truncation. Temporal boundaries are missing Supply a fixed window or valid rolling_calendar or rolling_days settings; training does not switch to random. Null labels remain Enable a valid availability filter if labels are delayed; eligible rows still need a real target. A date parses in the wrong timezone Declare its source format and zone; cron timezone only schedules the job. Approval cannot replay a candidate Restore access to its saved source version and evidence; today's configuration cannot replace its holdout.

For CV and search on the selected training rows, see tuning. For delayed labels arriving after predictions, see monitoring outcomes.

docs.title: Read training reports, evaluation charts and explanations
When you need it
docs.text: Use this page to inspect a completed or failed training invocation, locate its MLflow evidence, and enable bounded evaluation charts or SHAP explanations. Start with the training walkthrough to run a project. Lifecycle decisions explain approval, rejection and rollback; this page explains the reports that support them.

docs.title: What to edit
docs.text:
Set evaluation_charts, explainability and save_preprocessing_diagnostics under defaults or the supported named-model override in config/training.yml. The field reference lists allowed values. Generated optional report tasks and their pinned dependencies must be present: changing a setting cannot create an omitted notebook or update a deployed graph. Use project upgrades when adding those resources.

Keep workflow_contract: "3" in generated notebook parameters. It is distinct from workflow JSON config_version: 1 and companion YAML version: 1.

docs.title: The command
docs.text:
From the generated project, using its pinned training requirements:

uv pip install -r deployment/train-requirements.txt
python src/tools/smoke.py
python src/tools/preview.py --action train
databricks bundle validate --strict -t test --profile YOUR_PROFILE
databricks bundle deploy -t test --profile YOUR_PROFILE
databricks bundle run train -t test --profile YOUR_PROFILE

Substitute your target and profile. Smoke and preview do not read source data or fit models. Preview bindings can be passed explicitly with --catalog, --input-schema, --output-schema, --metadata-schema and --resource-suffix. Do not execute explanations.py directly: the normal fit saves its report.

docs.title: What you should see
docs.text:
Open Jobs > your run > the task > Output. Generated notebooks print STARTED, then either COMPLETED with elapsed time or FAILED with the task name, exception type, message, source file and line. Available job/run/model identifiers appear beside the start message. Failure diagnostics preserve the original exception and traceback; they do not convert a failed task to success. Inspect the failing task's inputs and saved effects before retrying.

After a successful training run (lifecycle_action=train), the final training_report starts with Where to look, one row per fitted model. Approve, reject and rollback runs show only the action result. The index links to existing evidence rather than recomputing reports:

Column What to inspect Model / run The exact MLflow fitting run; a registered UC version where one exists. Competition losers have runs but no registered winner version. Training data Saved table and Delta version, available source/train/holdout counts and pre-split removals; links to the underlying JSON evidence. Preprocessing probe Saved diagnostic status and artifact, or off when confirmed by the saved config. SHAP Saved explanation status and JSON/HTML link, or an enablement link. Evaluation charts The saved Charts run if ready. Off when saved settings disable charts. Winner only; see the selected model for a competition candidate that was not selected. Otherwise check generate_charts > Output. Decision threshold Saved threshold mode/values and evidence; absence is reported explicitly.

The decision, quality comparison and receipts follow this index. Single models, competition winners and model sets show the same operator blocks: Available action: approve, Available action: reject and If rollback is needed. Copy parameter values from those blocks; the operator steps explain each one. A model set ends with Decision details (JSON). Missing/unreadable evidence is unavailable, not proof that a check passed. Off is shown only when saved settings establish it. The summary uses the fitting run's saved configuration, not today's edited YAML.

Artifact links open that run's Artifacts tab; select the filename shown in the link. Threshold previews show at most ten entries and shorten long labels or values. Open decision_threshold.json for the complete saved mapping.

Chart leaves run independently and can still be running when this final report renders. Their eventual task state is in the job graph. A requested child score run starts after training_report, so it cannot have a child-run link in that report yet; open the later run_batch_scoring task. If lifecycle finalization fails, its existing exception remains authoritative and the final summary may not render. Inspect the failed task and fitting runs directly.

Other task outputs retain their labeled text or specialized reports. Notebook JSON and task values remain available for automation.

The final-report notebook (training_report.py or models_report.py) passes Databricks displayHTML to the renderer. Without it, the task prints a plain text summary and no Where to look table. The training_report task also needs the base parameter workspace_host: ${workspace.host} in resources/train.job.yml. Without it, the table renders but every link is plain text. Project upgrades show how to add both to an existing project.

Project generation writes the selected model entries in config/training.yml and optional set settings in config/inference.yml. It includes only the job notebooks of the selected graph, including optional SHAP/charts/recovery. Reinitialize a separate project when changing layout or enabling a feature whose notebook was omitted, then review and merge the required resources and files. Do not only toggle a resource flag and reference a missing notebook.

docs.title: Optional evaluation charts
docs.text:
Detailed Bundle initialization asks evaluation_charts_enabled (default: false). Choosing true adds a separate generate_charts task after model evaluation, plus matplotlib==3.10.0 in the training environment. Charts do not retrain models.

Layout Images and destination Single Saved model diagnostics in a Charts child of its training run Competition CV leaderboard and selected model diagnostics share a Charts child of the parent training run; final holdout is never used to rank candidates Model set Each component has its own Charts child; a separate Charts child of the set parent contains the overview

Regression includes actual versus predicted, residuals and error distribution. Classification includes raw/normalized confusion matrices and per-class metrics; ROC/PR and calibration require model probabilities. Tree models expose native feature importance; linear models expose signed coefficients when available. Saved CV folds, tuning trials and training loss are plotted only when present. Full-holdout metric summaries use existing scalar values and separate metric scales.

Open the Charts tab using the links printed by generate_charts. Images are indexed in dedicated Charts child runs with no training parameters, so MLflow's image-grid header does not repeat the long parameter list. The original training run retains all parameters, metrics and model artifacts. Its skyulf.charts.run_id tag links to the latest successful chart run.

MLflow can automatically create image cards from logged image keys. If a card is missing from your saved layout, choose Add chart -> Image grid and select a key such as single_actual_vs_predicted or competition_leaderboard. The task output is plain text: created image keys grouped under their MLflow Charts links. Sample counts, skipped diagnostics and charts_run_id remain in evaluation_charts/report.json on the parent training run. Component reports keep the source run_id and the separate chart destination_run_id.

config/training.yml > defaults controls the saved sample and display budgets:

evaluation_charts:
  enabled: true
  max_rows: 2000
  max_features: 20
  max_classes: 20

Enabling charts saves a deterministic bounded sample of actual heldout predictions, probabilities and labels in the evaluated model's MLflow artifacts, subject to the experiment's access and retention policies. Raw features and record keys are excluded. Sampling happens after full-holdout evaluation, preserving temporal feature context. Maximums are 10,000 rows, 50 displayed features and 50 classes; each sample has a 16 MiB budget. Pairwise coefficient outputs are capped at 20 boundaries. Sample diagnostics are labelled with their row count; full-holdout scalar metrics are never overwritten. Missing classes or unavailable model capabilities are reported explicitly.

If the saved output includes scoring_status, prediction diagnostics plot only rows marked predicted. Excluded rows remain in the original uniform sample; their null predictions are not turned into zeros. Each component report records sample_scored_rows, sample_excluded_rows and sample_excluded_by_reason. Chart captions and task output show how many sampled rows were accepted or excluded. These are sample counts, not the full holdout's exclusion counts. Fewer than two predicted sample rows skip prediction diagnostics; available model and training evidence charts can still be shown. Sampling, saved labels and evaluation metrics are unchanged, and malformed predictions still raise an error.

The task is an independent leaf with no retries. A chart failure can mark the overall job failed but does not undo model decisions or repeat training. Inspect the chart task and skyulf.charts.status; do not repair an old lifecycle invocation. Setting enabled to false disables an already deployed chart task. Adding charts to a project generated without them also requires adding the generated task and Matplotlib dependency, then redeploying; the flag alone cannot change a job graph.

docs.title: Optional SHAP explanations
docs.text: Quick setup leaves SHAP off and skips its questions. Detailed setup can add the config, pinned dependencies and separate shap_model/shap_<name> leaves. The SHAP explanation guide shows how to add those files to an existing project, where reports are saved and how to read them. Computation uses bounded training inputs during fit; the leaf displays the saved report without retraining. Unavailable or disabled SHAP does not replace the model's evaluation metrics.

docs.title: Training graph and notebook files
docs.text:
Each train_<name> performs a real fit and retains its split, preprocessing, model, CV and tuning information. Its shap_<name> task is a separate leaf: it displays that exact run's saved report and has no outgoing dependencies. SHAP computation still happens during the fit; the leaf does not retrain the model. Unavailable explanations show their saved reason. A report-task failure is visible in the job but does not prevent model selection or set assembly.

SHAP tasks display saved explanation charts. Training, scoring and monitoring report tasks also render readable summaries where available. Structured JSON and saved artifacts retain the machine-readable results; task values and downstream job handoffs use those results, not the HTML presentation.

Each diagram starts after initialize_run and choose_action select training. The single-model main path is:

flowchart LR
    A["load_data"] --> B["prepare_dataset"]
    B --> C["train_and_tune"]
    C --> D["validate_model"]
    D --> E["register_model"]
    E --> F["evaluate_model"]
    F --> G["model_decision"]
    G --> H["training_report"]

The competition shares the prepared dataset and fans out into named fits. Selection uses training-side CV, adopts the fitted winner without retraining and retains loser runs without registering them:

flowchart LR
    A["load_data"] --> B["prepare_dataset"]
    B --> C["train_name: each candidate"]
    C --> D["select_best_model"]
    D --> E["register_model"]
    E --> F["evaluate_model"]
    F --> G["model_decision"]
    G --> H["training_report"]

The multi-target model set has separate source/split/fit work inside each branch. It packages every pinned component, checks the saved quality policies and applies one set-level decision. The model set guide explains the set:

flowchart LR
    C["train_name: each target"] --> D["register_model_set"]
    D --> E["evaluate_model_set"]
    E --> F["model_decision"]
    F --> G["training_report"]

train_name represents each concrete train_<name> key in the generated graph. These diagrams show the training paths, not every condition or optional leaf. Manual approve/reject/rollback skip fitting and use model_decision. training_report uses ALL_DONE to attempt finalization even after a failure; that does not make the failed invocation successful. Optional SHAP leaves depend only on their own fitting task; chart generation is another independent branch. After a successful final report, the verified scoring handoff can start the separate score job. Model-set aliases belong to the set, while components remain pinned.

The graph uses meaningful model names; notebook implementation is shared:

File in src/jobs Responsibility initialize_run.py Pin single/competition source, recipes and champion initialize_models.py Pin every multi-model recipe, source version and set baseline load_data.py, prepare_dataset.py Load and split the shared single/competition dataset train_and_tune.py Fit a single model train_model.py Fit the named competition candidate or multi-model branch shap_report.py Display one training task's saved SHAP report select_best_model.py Select the complete competition's winner from training-side CV validate_model.py Verify the single fitted candidate before registration register_model.py, evaluate_model.py, model_decision.py Existing single-model registration and alias controls register_model_set.py Package the complete set and nominate its challenger evaluate_model_set.py Evaluate every component against its quality policy and pinned champion model_set_decision.py Apply set promotion policy or an explicit approve/reject/rollback action training_report.py, models_report.py Final single/competition or multi-model status score.py, score_models.py Saved single-model or model-set scoring

Changing parameters or a recipe keeps the graph unchanged. After adding, removing or renaming entries in config/training.yml > models, run:

python src/tools/refresh_training_graph.py
databricks bundle validate --strict --target test
databricks bundle deploy --target test

The refresh script preserves schedules, compute and operator settings. A changed model list with an old deployed graph is rejected before any model is trained. Tasks can run concurrently when compute permits; each task's row/byte/search limits still apply separately. Existing serialized job admission, frozen receipts and no-repair/no-retry rules remain in effect.

docs.title: Training parameters in MLflow
docs.text:
After training, open the model's MLflow experiment run and select Parameters. Competition candidates and multi-target branches each record their own settings:

Parameter Meaning tuning_strategy, tuning_model_type Search strategy and selected model family tuning_requested_metric, tuning_metric Requested objective and resolved scorer tuning_requested_trials, tuning_trials Configured trial budget and actual Core trial count tuning_random_state, tuning_timeout, tuning_n_jobs Search seed, timeout and workers tuning_strategy_params, tuning_search_space Strategy controls and effective search space tuning_best_params.<name> Each parameter selected by the final search

Large parameter previews point to the complete tuning.json artifact. Existing cv_* parameters remain alongside these fields; tuning_best_score is a metric. With nested CV, Parameters shows the final search on all training rows; individual outer-fold selections remain in tuning.json.

Fixed and tuned models also expose their fitted configuration in Parameters:

Parameter Meaning model_type, model_params.<name> Model family and actual constructor settings, including defaults and tuned values ensemble.base_models, ensemble.strategy Ordered member names and voting/stacking strategy ensemble.voting, ensemble.weights Applicable voting type and weights in member order ensemble.final_estimator, ensemble.cv Stacking meta-model and its internal folds, separate from workflow CV split_strategy, split_test_size, split_random_state, split_stratify Active random holdout controls, separate from CV and tuning seeds split_start, split_holdout_start, split_cutoff, split_event_column Temporal holdout boundaries and clock column; inactive random controls are omitted preprocessing_recipe, pre_split_recipe Selected recipe or declared builder default; inline means no project recipe metadata preprocessing_steps, pre_split_steps Ordered step names for each phase

training_parameters.json retains complete summaries when a preview exceeds the display limit. Non-JSON constructor objects are described by type; their nested constructor settings are separate entries, and the fitted artifact retains the actual objects. builder_default means the builder has no named recipe default; none means that optional builder is absent. Previously saved artifacts without recipe metadata still work.

docs.title: Task outputs and saved input evidence
docs.text:
The train job has one active run, with queued training and operator actions:

Task Purpose initialize_run Validate settings and pin source version, recipe and expected champion choose_action Select training or an explicit approve/reject/rollback action load_data Read the bounded pinned source and save its verified dataset prepare_dataset Apply fixed cleanup and eligibility rules, then save training/holdout partitions train_and_tune Fit preprocessing inside training folds, run configured CV/tuning, and save the fitted pipeline validate_model Verify the single fitted candidate select_best_model Show the competition leaderboard and selected winner register_model Check heldout evaluation before registering and nominating the candidate evaluate_model Compare the registered candidate with the pinned champion on the same holdout model_decision Apply promotion policy or execute an explicit approve/reject/rollback action training_report Finalize the run and publish verified results and next actions register_monitor Enroll the activated model, competition winner or model-set components before scoring scoring_requested Check whether scoring was requested run_batch_scoring Invoke the existing score job

The separate score job has the score task. With CDF expiry recovery enabled, recovery_needed routes recognized expiry to recover_predictions, and scoring_report shows the actual scoring or recovery result. Open training_report for metrics, the decision and ready-to-copy next_actions. Search details are in train_and_tune; champion comparison is in evaluate_model. Score results are in the child or independent score run. Manual actions skip data and training and use model_decision directly. Finalization can run after failure; that does not imply a successful result.

The score job's monitor_model task invokes the separate monitoring job after its preparation checks succeed. In that monitoring job, monitor_model measures enrolled models, monitoring_report displays saved drift and performance evidence, and evaluate_retraining applies the configured retraining guards. These are monitoring operations, not fitting tasks in the train graph.

prepare_dataset applies only fixed transformations and filters. Learned preprocessing and feature engineering stay inside train_and_tune so each CV fold learns from its own training rows. With tuning disabled, that task fits the configured model directly. With training_layout=model_competition, each named candidate is fitted and select_best_model verifies the complete shared-CV leaderboard before the winner reaches registration. Other candidates remain inspectable MLflow runs without registered versions.

Bounded source and split datasets are saved as Parquet artifacts under the MLflow run's lifecycle/data/. Downstream training verifies their saved digests and preserves split membership without rereading the source. These artifacts contain training data: apply the experiment's access and retention policy. Registration and approval retain their source/evidence replay checks.

docs.title: Preprocessing diagnostics
docs.text: With defaults.save_preprocessing_diagnostics: true, each fitting run saves preprocessing_probe.json; the fitting task's Output (train_and_tune or train_<name>) shows the result. The preprocessing diagnostics guide explains the check and every status.

docs.title: Common errors and fixes
docs.text:
Symptom Check and fix A report task/notebook is missing Regenerate the selected optional capability separately, review its notebooks/dependencies/resources, and redeploy the matching graph. SHAP says unavailable Read the saved reason; check transformed feature width, supported model and installed pinned dependencies. max_features does not select columns. An evaluation chart is absent Inspect evaluation_charts/report.json; unavailable probabilities, missing classes or absent CV/tuning history can legitimately skip a chart. A chart task failed after a model decision Inspect skyulf.charts.status; the independent leaf does not undo decisions. Do not repair an old lifecycle invocation to recreate charts. Training report ran after another task failed Finalization reports the failure; a completed report does not establish a successful training run. Large MLflow parameter value is truncated Read training_parameters.json or tuning.json for the complete saved value. Preprocessing reports requires_context Supply the actual groups/history through the supported inference contract; the sample probe cannot certify worker or endpoint execution.

Reports describe the exact saved run and installed Core version. A local preview or the examples on this page do not establish cloud execution or model quality.

docs.title: Databricks project troubleshooting
docs.text:
Find the message from smoke.py, preview.py or the failed task below. The index points to the page that owns each fix. The three detailed diagnostics at the end come from the project validators. You can reproduce them locally without Spark, credentials or a deployed job. Use the Core release matching your generated project.

Each correction below is a change to an existing generated project, not a complete replacement configuration. Start a project with the walkthrough. See the glossary for the lifecycle and data terms.

docs.title: Find your message
docs.text:
Search this table for the start of your message. Values in angle brackets vary. The linked section explains the cause and the fix.

Message or symptom Where to fix it Pre-split step '<step>' reads target '<target>'. Set SKIP_TARGET_PRE_SPLIT_STEPS=True or SCORING_MODE='custom'. Below feature_lookup.lookups[<n>].table_name: Unity Catalog names must be catalog.schema.name; each part a simple identifier (letters, digits, underscore; not starting with a digit). Below feature_lookup.lookups[<n>] is not filled in: complete feature_lookup and online_features in config/training.yml, or regenerate with include_online_feature_lookup=false. Below Automatic promotion requires quality_threshold. Below AliasOutcomeUnknownError, or a pending alias event Lifecycle recovery Project and job definitions disagree; regenerate/redeploy the Bundle together. after a Core or template upgrade (workflow contract) Project upgrade The same message after changing follow_champion in config/inference.yml Redeploy the Bundle; see score handoff Training source has ... rows, exceeding max_rows=..., Training source observed size ... bytes exceeds max_bytes=... or Training source estimated size ... bytes exceeds max_bytes=... Training data: adjust max_rows / max_input_mb in config/training.yml, or set training_sample_rows to sample eligible rows before splitting. Training input has ... rows, exceeding max_rows=..., Training input size ... bytes exceeds max_bytes=... or Competition training data ... exceeds max_rows=... / max_bytes=... Python API: reduce the input size or adjust max_rows / max_bytes in fit_workflow or evaluate_competition_candidate. The frame training limit covers all splits together. Increase memory limits only when the process has enough memory. Initial scoring source exceeds the configured max_rows budget. or Source increment exceeds max_rows. Scoring <node>.apply on pandas: <reason>, for example project_scoring.apply on pandas: Custom scoring and reused pre-split rules are unsupported. (Spark admission) Distributed inference An online endpoint returns Encountered an unexpected error while evaluating the model. ... Error '' Online features: read the served model logs A Unity Catalog permission error in a job run Deployment; test the job's run_as identity Set both monitoring_catalog and monitoring_schema. Set both in deployment/variables.yml, or leave both blank with monitoring_enabled: "false". See if no destination is set Local artifact runtime mismatch for skyulf-core: requires ..., found ... or report reason champion_runtime_unavailable The model was produced by another runtime. Approve a reviewed replacement with allow_unloadable_champion=true, or run with the producing release. See champion from an older Core release. bundle init fails with ERROR_monitoring_schema_is_required_with_monitoring_catalog A monitoring catalog was answered without a schema. Answer both, or leave both blank to start without monitoring. See project setup. Spark reference is not prepared; run prepare_spark_monitoring_reference first. Monitoring enrollment Serving endpoint is not ready or its config update is pending. Serving

docs.text: Topic Typical symptoms Project setup Wrong schema in preview, missing columns or notebooks, monitoring destination Deployment REPLACE_* values, authentication, privileges, duplicate jobs Project upgrade Graph contract, missing notebooks, saved model runtime Training data Budgets, temporal boundaries, null labels, timezones Custom steps Factory paths, row count, source package and dependencies Custom pre-split filters Target-reading filters, non-Boolean masks Decision thresholds Too few classes, unknown manual class, threshold conflicts Training reports Missing report tasks, charts or SHAP, truncated parameters Explanations Missing SHAP tasks or artifacts, explanation status codes Model sets Replacement stays challenger, quality failures, Spark admission Approve, reject and roll back Missing quality threshold, changed champion, scoring after promotion Lifecycle recovery Uncertain alias changes Scoring Champion selection, eligibility, budgets, schema Monitoring overview Monitoring destination, nothing monitored, old dashboard results Monitoring store setup Store permissions and upgrades Monitoring enrollment Enrollment and references Delayed labels Label columns, timestamps, duplicate keys, classes Drift no_data, degraded, large PSI without drift Performance Unknown policy fields, missing baseline, failure streaks Retraining Why no new train run appeared Monitoring dashboard Issues to investigate, missing links Serving Endpoint readiness and privileges Online features Missing and stale online features Serving monitoring awaiting_logs, failed, blank counts or latency Daily rollout Retries, stops and recovery of traffic updates Remove a project Unexpected deletions, shared dashboard, endpoints left running

docs.title: A pre-split step reads the target
docs.text:
Example message, where the step name and target depend on your recipe:

Pre-split step 'dropmissingrows' reads target 'churn'. Set SKIP_TARGET_PRE_SPLIT_STEPS=True or SCORING_MODE='custom'.

Cause. The selected config/pre_split.yml recipe filters or edits churn, the actual target. That can be appropriate when choosing labeled training rows. The default scoring mode also reuses this recipe, but prediction requests do not contain the actual target. Project loading resolves the saved scoring policy, so this can fail during the training preview, before fitting or scoring.

Fix. Decide the scoring policy in config/scoring.yml before preview and training. To reuse the feature checks while omitting target-dependent rules, set:

version: 1
mode: pre_split
skip_target_pre_split_steps: true
eligibility: []
outputs: []
combined: []

A filter reading both target and feature columns is skipped as a whole. Split it into separate target and feature checks if the feature check must still apply to scoring. Fixed edits can instead be projected onto the selected input columns.

Alternatively, select mode: custom with skip_target_pre_split_steps: false and define the required eligibility and output rules in the same file. Custom mode does not reuse pre-split rules; the generated custom lists start empty. Do not select it expecting the commented examples to become active. The training pre-split recipe still runs in either case. These choices are saved with the newly fitted model; editing the file does not change an already registered version's scoring policy.

Check. From the project root, run:

python src/tools/smoke.py
python src/tools/preview.py --action train
python src/tools/preview.py --action score

Confirm the selected recipe and scoring mode, then train a new model version. Read pre-split admission and scoring and scoring eligibility.

docs.title: A feature lookup table name is incomplete
docs.text:
Example message for the second lookup:

feature_lookup.lookups[1].table_name: Unity Catalog names must be catalog.schema.name; each part a simple identifier (letters, digits, underscore; not starting with a digit).

Cause. feature_lookup.lookups[N].table_name is blank, contains an unresolved placeholder, has fewer than three parts or has invalid identifier syntax. The index is zero-based: [0] is the first list entry and [1] is the second. A completely blank generated entry (no table_name, lookup_key or feature_names) reports feature_lookup.lookups[N] is not filled in: ... instead: fill the entry, or regenerate the project with include_online_feature_lookup=false. These checks validate names locally; passing them does not prove the table exists or that the job can read it.

Fix. In config/training.yml, find the effective feature_lookup under defaults or the model override and repair the indexed entry's table_name. For example, replace an empty second table name with this field value:

table_name: "{catalog}.{input_schema}.balances"

Here catalog and input_schema come from the selected project bindings. A concrete workspace.features.balances also works. Use your own existing feature table name and simple identifiers. Preserve the entry's lookup_key, feature_names and any timestamp lookup settings; ensure they match the table's keys and the model's declared inputs. A model override replaces the complete lookup mapping, so check the effective model entry rather than repairing only a shadowed default. The syntax correction does not create or merge a feature table.

Check. Run the three local checks above with the intended catalog/schema bindings. The expanded table name should resolve without this message. Then verify table existence, feature metadata and permissions in the chosen workspace before training. See feature tables and lookup choices and the training reference.

docs.title: Automatic promotion has no quality threshold
docs.text:
Automatic promotion requires quality_threshold.

Cause. The effective model configuration has promotion_policy: automatic and a missing or null quality_threshold. A relative improvement requirement or additional quality_gates does not replace the primary absolute threshold. The validator stops before remote training and registry work.

Fix. In config/training.yml, set a numeric threshold under defaults or the affected model entry, using the units and direction of its metric. For an existing regression model, this is a fragment illustrating an RMSE upper bound:

defaults:
  promotion_policy: automatic
  metric: heldout_rmse
  quality_threshold: 5.0

The value 5.0 is an example, not a recommended business limit. Choose your acceptance criterion: lower RMSE is better, while classification accuracy/F1 needs a minimum acceptable score. Check model overrides for a null that masks the default. Keep any additional gates and min_improvement requirements appropriate to the same target and task. Choosing manual_approval allows a pending candidate without this automatic-policy check; first-champion activation still needs an explicit quality threshold and passing saved evidence.

Check. Run smoke.py and preview.py --action train again. Passing validation only confirms a complete policy. After training, inspect the saved held-out metric and every gate in training_report before accepting the candidate. Read the quality fields and registry lifecycle.

docs.title: If your message is different
docs.text: Keep the full traceback, task key, model/branch name, concrete model version and the effective configuration for the failing action. Inspect the first failing task; excluded conditional tasks are often expected. Retry only after checking whether training, alias changes or prediction publication already committed. Approve, reject and roll back explains saved results and operator actions; scoring recovery covers the recognized CDF-expiry path. This page does not enumerate every validator or imply that a local preview verifies cloud execution.

docs.title: Databricks Bundle tuning and ensembles
docs.text:
Choose an estimator in the model catalog, then choose how to search its parameters here. This guide describes the generated Bundle's config/training.yml contract. The training reference owns the complete workflow field list; Core tuning describes the Python API. The Bundle accepts a bounded subset of the underlying sklearn and Optuna APIs.

Strategy Use when Candidate selection grid A small, deliberate set of combinations covers the question. Every Cartesian-product combination. random Several axes make a full grid too expensive. Up to n_trials sampled combinations. halving_grid A small grid has a useful cheap training budget. Full initial grid, then fewer candidates at larger resources. halving_random A large space has a useful cheap training budget. Sampled initial candidates, then successive elimination. optuna Adaptive trial selection or supported pruning is useful. TPE, random or CMA-ES sampling. 
flowchart LR
    A["Choose estimator and fixed params"] --> B["Choose search space"]
    B --> C["grid / random / halving / optuna"]
    C --> D["Training-side CV and budget"]
    D --> E["Select parameters and refit"]
    E --> F["Separate heldout evaluation"]

Search selection uses training-side validation. The final holdout measures the selected fitted model; it does not choose the winning trial.

docs.title: Where settings belong
docs.text:
Use models.<name>.model.params for fixed constructor values and models.<name>.tuning.search_space for searched values. For example, keep fit_intercept: true fixed and search alpha: [0.1, 1.0, 10.0]. Do not also fix alpha: 1.0: a conflicting explicit axis is rejected. A matching singleton axis is allowed, but adds no search. Defaults inherited from defaults are shallow overrides: a model's tuning mapping replaces the shared mapping.
