Missing and values outside the outer edges have no bin unless missing label mode is enabled. Label mode produces strings in Polars, including ordinal code strings, while pandas can retain numeric codes alongside a string sentinel in object dtype. Duplicate edges and mismatched custom-label counts must be resolved; fit failures and output-name collisions raise. All-missing columns have no learned edges. Do not assume the number of bins always equals the requested count.

docs.title: GeneralBinning
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: Create numeric bins with learned or per-column fixed edges; five equal-width bins put 10 and 90 in opposite end bins for 0–100 data.

File: config/preprocessing.yml.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes columns list[string]/null null Existing numeric columns; [] selects none. Select features; omitted selection uses numeric detection. output_suffix string _binned String. Name output as source plus suffix. drop_original boolean false true, false Remove successfully binned source columns. label_format string ordinal ordinal, bin_index, range Emit numeric codes or interval labels; valid custom labels take precedence where supported. include_lowest boolean true true, false Include the lowest edge in the first interval; intervals are right-closed. precision integer 3 Nonnegative. Choose range-label display precision, retaining exact labels if rounding merges bins. missing_strategy string keep keep, label Keep missing/out-of-range bin results missing or label them. missing_label scalar Missing Compatible scalar/string. Supply label-mode missing value. strategy string equal_width equal_width/uniform, equal_frequency, kmeans, custom, kbins Choose how edges are obtained. n_bins integer 5 Positive; sklearn kbins needs at least 2. Set base bin count. equal_width_bins, equal_frequency_bins integer n_bins Positive. Override count for the corresponding strategy. duplicates string drop drop, raise Handle repeated equal-frequency edges. kbins_n_bins integer n_bins At least 2. Override sklearn bin count. kbins_strategy string quantile quantile, uniform, kmeans; equal_width/equal_frequency aliases. Choose sklearn edge fitting. custom_bins mapping {} Column→numeric edge list. Set per-column fixed edges for custom strategy. custom_labels mapping {} Column→labels; count must match intervals. Override code/range labels. column_strategies mapping {} Column→strategy/count/duplicates/kbins/custom options. Override fit settings per column.

Minimal YAML:

- name: generalbinning
  transformer: GeneralBinning
  params: {columns: [age], strategy: equal_width, n_bins: 5}

Common mistake: A requested bin count can shrink with repeated values; inspect the fitted output.

Details: Noncustom strategies save learned edges. For values 0–100 and five equal-width bins, 10 belongs to the first and 90 to the last. Unknown strategies and per-column fit failures raise instead of saving a partial fit. All-missing columns still have no learned edges. Saved artifacts keep their fitted edges at apply time. The runtime default is equal_width, despite older metadata saying uniform (these two select the same width strategy).

docs.title: CustomBinning
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: Apply one fixed edge list; with [0, 18, 65, 120], 18 is in the first interval and 19 in the second.

File: config/preprocessing.yml.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes columns list[string]/null null Existing numeric columns; [] selects none. Select features; omitted selection uses numeric detection. output_suffix string _binned String. Name output as source plus suffix. drop_original boolean false true, false Remove successfully binned source columns. label_format string ordinal ordinal, bin_index, range Emit numeric codes or interval labels; valid custom labels take precedence where supported. include_lowest boolean true true, false Include the lowest edge in the first interval; intervals are right-closed. precision integer 3 Nonnegative. Choose range-label display precision, retaining exact labels if rounding merges bins. missing_strategy string keep keep, label Keep missing/out-of-range bin results missing or label them. missing_label scalar Missing Compatible scalar/string. Supply label-mode missing value. bins list[number]/null null At least two distinct numeric edges; sorted at fit. Use one fixed edge list for every selected column; absent/empty is no-op.

Minimal YAML:

- name: custombinning
  transformer: CustomBinning
  params: {columns: [age], bins: [0, 18, 65, 120], label_format: range}

Common mistake: Use GeneralBinning custom strategy when columns need different edges or custom labels.

Details: One sorted edge list applies to every selected column; absent/empty bins is no-op. At least two distinct edges are needed. Shares output options above but does not expose GeneralBinning's per-column fit strategy. For these edges, 18 belongs to the first interval and 19 to the second. Saves fixed edges; automatic column selection can still depend on training values. Use GeneralBinning custom strategy for different edge/label lists per column.

docs.title: KBinsDiscretizer
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: Learn quantile, uniform or kmeans bin edges and replay them at prediction.

File: config/preprocessing.yml.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes columns list[string]/null null Existing numeric columns; [] selects none. Select features; omitted selection uses numeric detection. output_suffix string _binned String. Name output as source plus suffix. drop_original boolean false true, false Remove successfully binned source columns. label_format string ordinal ordinal, bin_index, range Emit numeric codes or interval labels; valid custom labels take precedence where supported. include_lowest boolean true true, false Include the lowest edge in the first interval; intervals are right-closed. precision integer 3 Nonnegative. Choose range-label display precision, retaining exact labels if rounding merges bins. missing_strategy string keep keep, label Keep missing/out-of-range bin results missing or label them. missing_label scalar Missing Compatible scalar/string. Supply label-mode missing value. n_bins integer 5 At least 2. Choose sklearn bin count. strategy string quantile quantile, uniform, kmeans; equal_width/equal_frequency aliases. Choose learned edges. kbins_n_bins integer 5 At least 2; an explicit n_bins takes precedence. Set forwarded bin count when n_bins is absent. kbins_strategy string quantile quantile, uniform, kmeans; an explicit non-kbins strategy takes precedence. Set forwarded strategy when strategy is absent. column_strategies mapping {} Same per-column fit options as GeneralBinning. Override individual column strategies. equal_width_bins, equal_frequency_bins integer n_bins Positive; relevant to corresponding per-column overrides. Set overridden strategy counts. duplicates string drop drop, raise Handle repeated edges in equal-frequency overrides. custom_bins, custom_labels mapping {} Column→edges or labels; relevant to custom per-column overrides. Configure forwarded custom strategies.

Minimal YAML:

- name: kbinsdiscretizer
  transformer: KBinsDiscretizer
  params: {columns: [age], n_bins: 5, strategy: quantile}

Common mistake: The sklearn encode option is not exposed; use label_format to control this wrapper’s output.

Details: This wrapper routes to GeneralBinning's kbins strategy; it also accepts its shared output and per-column override options. Saves learned edges, not a new estimator fit at inference. Quantile bins seek similar training population sizes; repeated values can reduce the number of distinct bins. Encoding is ordinal internally; public label_format controls final rendering, not sklearn's sparse one-hot encode setting (which is not exposed).

docs.title: Missing values, cleaning and types
docs.text:
Back to the preprocessing catalog

These steps fill missing values, drop incomplete rows or columns, clean text, replace values and cast types. Seven of them are also admitted in config/pre_split.yml; each card names the file it belongs in. The last section shows a complete fixed-normalization recipe for config/pre_split.yml.

YAML blocks are list fragments to paste under a selected recipe unless a card marks them as standalone Core configuration. Shared column, row and runtime rules are in read the step cards.

docs.title: SimpleImputer
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: [2, null, 4] with mean becomes [2, 3, 4].

File: config/preprocessing.yml.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes columns list[string]/null null Existing columns; mean/median require numeric; [] selects none. Select features; omitted selection uses strategy-appropriate detection. strategy string mean mean, median, most_frequent (mode), constant Choose learned statistic or fixed fill. fill_value scalar/null null Used by constant; specify text/Boolean fills explicitly. Numeric default is 0; object defaults differ by engine.

Minimal YAML:

- name: simpleimputer
  transformer: SimpleImputer
  params: {columns: [income], strategy: mean}

Common mistake: Do not expect mean imputation to fill an all-null training column; choose an explicit constant.

Details: Mean/median need numeric input; other modes can select text. State saves selected columns and one fill value per column. Apply replaces null/NaN in place; mean/median can promote integer columns to float. A learned all-null fill remains unavailable; use explicit constant filling for such columns. Most-frequent ties use the smallest comparable value. Context: row. Dependencies: base. Native Spark accepts numeric mean and compatible constant fills (text/Boolean need explicit matching values), not all local strategies.

Schema preview preserves known double-precision targets with numeric-compatible fills. It returns an unknown schema for automatic selection, non-double targets or constants whose output can depend on values and the engine. This includes nullable float32 mode/constant fills and Boolean constants in double columns. Explicit empty or missing-only selections remain a no-op. Fitted values and native apply dtypes are unchanged.

For local pandas/Polars fits, an explicit text fill_value is converted for each selected integer, floating-point or Boolean column, including pandas Arrow dtypes. Text columns retain the literal text. Use an explicit Casting step for Decimal, date and other unsupported scalar types. Integer conversion preserves exact values above 2**53 and rejects fractional or out-of-range constants. Boolean columns accept true or false (case-insensitive), never general text truthiness or numeric Boolean strings. Nonfinite numeric constants fail during fit with the column name. The artifact stores the resolved values, so inference does not reinterpret request dtypes. Existing saved fills remain unchanged. Canvas keeps the input as text to avoid JavaScript rounding large integers before fitting.

docs.title: GroupImputer
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: missing income in group A receives A's training mean; an unseen group receives the global training mean.

File: config/preprocessing.yml.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes group_by string/list[string] required One existing column or a nonempty ordered list of distinct columns. Select the group lookup keys. columns list[string]/null null Empty/omitted selects eligible columns automatically. Choose columns to fill; group key and target are excluded. strategy string mean mean, median, most_frequent, mode Learn per-group fills and global fallbacks. fallback string global global, hierarchical For a list of keys, optionally try successively shorter prefixes before the global training value.

Minimal YAML:

- name: groupimputer
  transformer: GroupImputer
  params: {columns: [income], group_by: segment, strategy: mean}

Common mistake: Do not recompute group means on scoring rows; the saved lookup and global fallback are reused.

Details: Automatic selection excludes group key and target and selects numeric columns for mean/median, all eligible columns for mode. State stores group/value pairs and global fallbacks. Missing group keys, unseen groups and groups without a usable statistic fall back to the saved global value; an entirely unobserved column can remain missing. Replaces selected missing cells, preserves observed values, and uses floating values for numeric statistics. Context: row after fit, not request-time group aggregation. Dependencies: base. No native Spark fit/apply claim.

An explicit list opts into versioned tuple keys. With group_by: [region, industry] and fallback: hierarchical, an unseen pair tries the region's training statistic before the global value. A null component skips its level; [known_region, null] can still use the region. Every prefix learns its statistic directly from training rows, including for median and mode. The global statistic includes observed values from rows with missing group keys. Key order matters: [industry, region] falls back to industry instead. fallback: global uses only the complete tuple and the global value.

The saved list-based state contains group_key_version: 1, ordered levels, and global fill_values. Canonical tuple components preserve exact integers and distinguish Boolean, numeric, text and missing values. Existing string group_by configurations and saved single-key artifacts retain their original representation. Canvas keeps old graphs unchanged until multiple group columns are enabled and shows controls for reordering the selected keys.

- name: regional_income
  transformer: GroupImputer
  params: {columns: [income], group_by: [region, industry], strategy: median, fallback: hierarchical}

docs.title: KNNImputer
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: fill a missing numeric feature from nearby training observations measured on their shared observed features.

File: config/preprocessing.yml.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes columns list[string]/null null Existing numeric columns; [] selects none. Select features; omitted selection uses numeric detection. n_neighbors integer 5 Positive. Choose the number of training neighbors. weights string uniform uniform, distance; callable is Python-only. Weight neighbor contributions.

Minimal YAML:

- name: knnimputer
  transformer: KNNImputer
  params: {columns: [income, age], n_neighbors: 5, weights: uniform}

Common mistake: Do not send text categories into numeric neighbor distances; encode or exclude them first.

Details: State stores the fitted sklearn imputer and training reference matrix. All-missing training columns are removed from its imputation matrix and left untouched in the output, with a warning. The full frame retains its columns. Outputs numeric fills, including float promotion for nullable integers; null/NaN are missing. Empty apply preserves fitted output width. Context: row against saved training neighbors. Dependencies: base/sklearn. Distances use sklearn's nan_euclidean metric over jointly observed features. No metric option is exposed: sklearn's other metric extension is a Python callable, which is not a portable YAML or Canvas setting.

docs.title: IterativeImputer
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: model each incomplete numeric column from the other selected columns, then replay the fitted chained models.

File: config/preprocessing.yml.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes columns list[string]/null null Existing numeric columns; [] selects none. Select features; omitted selection uses numeric detection. max_iter integer 10 Nonnegative. Limit chained imputation rounds. estimator string BayesianRidge BayesianRidge, DecisionTree/decision_tree, ExtraTrees/extra_trees, KNeighbors/knn. Choose the fitted predictor; unknown names fail during fit with the supported choices listed. random_state integer/null 0 Integer seed or null. Control estimator randomness.

Minimal YAML:

- name: iterativeimputer
  transformer: IterativeImputer
  params: {columns: [income, age], max_iter: 10, estimator: BayesianRidge, random_state: 0}

Common mistake: Use DecisionTree, not DecisionTreeRegressor, as the configured estimator name.

Details: All-missing columns are excluded from the fitted matrix and remain unchanged in the frame. Saves the fitted imputer, selected columns and estimator choice; replaces missing cells with numeric predictions without refitting. Empty apply preserves width. Context: row using saved models. Dependencies: base/sklearn.

docs.title: MissingIndicator
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: income [10, null] adds income_missing=[0, 1].

File: config/preprocessing.yml.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes columns list[string]/null null Empty/omitted selects columns missing at fit. Choose columns receiving flags. flag_suffix string _missing Nonempty string; null/empty uses default. Name appended 0/1 flags.

Minimal YAML:

- name: missingindicator
  transformer: MissingIndicator
  params: {columns: [income], flag_suffix: _missing}

Common mistake: A newly missing scoring column gets no flag unless it was selected during fit.

Details: Saves the selected columns; apply appends integer 0/1 flags for null/NaN and preserves original columns. Generated-name collisions raise. A column first becoming missing at prediction gets a flag only if selected at fit. Context: row. Dependencies: base.

docs.title: DropMissingColumns
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: remove unused columns or columns too incomplete in training, retaining that same drop set at prediction.

File: config/preprocessing.yml.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes columns list[string] [] Existing names; unknown names ignored. Drop these columns explicitly. missing_threshold number/null null 0–100 percent; 0/null disables automatic selection. Also drop columns at or above this missing percentage. target_column string/null null Existing label name; paired y can supply the label. Identify the supervised target, normally supplied by the pipeline.

Minimal YAML:

- name: dropmissingcolumns
  transformer: DropMissingColumns
  params: {columns: [unused_clock], missing_threshold: null}

Common mistake: The threshold is a percentage, not a 0–1 fraction; an explicit drop can remove the target.

Details: Explicit drops and learned drops are unioned; unknown names are ignored. Saves that union and removes those columns on apply, never remeasuring request missingness. Context: row. Dependencies: base.

docs.title: DropMissingRows
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: rows with a missing required label are removed.

File: config/preprocessing.yml, or config/pre_split.yml under the narrower admission rules. Training-only row changes need an explicit scoring decision.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes subset list[string]/null null Core empty/missing/nonmatching means all columns; pre_split requires explicit existing names. Choose required cells. how string any any, all Drop on any missing value or only all missing, if no threshold is set. threshold integer/null null Minimum present count; pre_split validates subset range. Overrides percentage and how in Core. missing_threshold number/null null 0–100 percent; do not combine with threshold in pre_split. Maximum allowed missing percentage.

Minimal YAML:

- name: dropmissingrows
  transformer: DropMissingRows
  params: {subset: [churn], how: any}

Common mistake: A filter reading the target needs an explicit scoring decision before preview; set the skip switch for this tutorial.

Details: Null and floating NaN count as missing, empty strings do not. No learned statistics; saves the policy. Removes rows and paired targets by position while preserving survivor order. Context: row; ordinary prediction skips this training filter. Dependencies: base.

docs.title: Deduplicate
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: two matching business records retain the first, last, or neither, as configured.

File: config/preprocessing.yml, or config/pre_split.yml under the narrower admission rules. Training-only row changes need an explicit scoring decision.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes subset list[string]/null null Core: all columns; pre_split: nonempty case-insensitively distinct existing names. Define a business duplicate. keep string/boolean first first, last, none, false Keep one representative or remove every duplicate.

Minimal YAML:

- name: deduplicate
  transformer: Deduplicate
  params: {subset: [segment, age, income], keep: first}

Common mistake: Do not use this to repair duplicate record keys or conflicting target labels; Bundle validation rejects those inputs.

Details: Comparisons include missing values according to the dataframe duplicate semantics. Saves the policy, not a global deduplication database. Filters paired targets with the same positions and preserves survivor order. Bundle additionally rejects conflicting labels and validates original record-key uniqueness. Context: global within the supplied population. Dependencies: base. Not an independent-request uniqueness guarantee.

docs.title: TextCleaning
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: " ACME " becomes "acme".

File: config/preprocessing.yml, or config/pre_split.yml under the narrower admission rules.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes columns list[string]/null null Core: automatic text selection; pre_split: explicit names. Choose text columns. operations list[mapping] [] Ordered trim, case, remove_special or regex rules; options below. Apply fixed edits; empty list changes nothing.

Minimal YAML:

- name: textcleaning
  transformer: TextCleaning
  params:
    columns: [segment]
    operations: [{op: trim}, {op: case, mode: lower}]

Common mistake: Declare operations in the intended order; cleaning does not cast non-text columns.

Details: Operation options:

op Options and defaults trim mode: both (default), leading, trailing. case mode: lower (default), upper, title, sentence. remove_special mode: keep_alphanumeric (default), keep_alphanumeric_space, letters_only, digits_only; replacement string default "". regex mode: custom (default), collapse_whitespace, extract_digits, normalize_slash_dates; custom requires nonempty pattern; repl string default "".

Saves fixed operations and selection. Nulls remain null; explicit non-text columns are preserved rather than converted into strings. Replacement is in place. Python-compatible regex semantics are retained across local engines; invalid patterns fail validation. Pre-split rejects unsupported operation keys/modes. Context: row. Dependencies: base.

docs.title: AliasReplacement
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: known text aliases normalize to one label; "ACME Inc." can become "ACME" with a custom map.

File: config/preprocessing.yml, or config/pre_split.yml under the narrower admission rules.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes columns list[string]/null null Core: automatic text selection; pre_split: explicit names. Choose columns to normalize. alias_type string boolean boolean, country, custom, punctuation Select normalization rules. custom_map mapping {} Normalized alias to replacement; required and nonempty for pre_split custom mode. Supply custom aliases; other pre_split modes reject this map. mode string/null null Core compatibility alias; normalize_boolean/canonicalize_country_codes also recognized. Used when alias_type is absent; not admitted in pre_split. custom_pairs mapping/null null Core map fallback; not admitted in pre_split. Compatibility input for custom aliases.

Minimal YAML:

- name: aliasreplacement
  transformer: AliasReplacement
  params: {columns: [company], alias_type: custom, custom_map: {acmeinc: ACME}}

Common mistake: Boolean alias normalization produces canonical values; use Casting when you need Boolean dtype.

Details: Matching lowercases text and removes punctuation/spaces; custom map keys are normalized the same way. Unknown aliases and non-text/null values remain unchanged. Punctuation mode only removes punctuation, preserving case/spaces. Custom pre-split mode requires a nonempty custom_map; other pre-split modes reject one. Core compatibility inputs mode (used when alias_type is unset), normalize_boolean/canonicalize_country_codes mode names and custom_pairs as a map fallback exist; Pre-split only accepts columns, alias_type, custom_map and canonical modes. State saves rules; output replaces selected cells. Context: row. Dependencies: base. Use Casting separately for actual Boolean dtype.

docs.title: ValueReplacement
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: "unknown" becomes null before imputation.

File: config/preprocessing.yml, or config/pre_split.yml under the narrower admission rules.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes columns list[string]/null [] Existing explicit names; empty/omitted selects none. Choose replacement scope; pre_split requires explicit names. mapping mapping/null unset Old→new map, or column→map. Declare replacements in mapping form. replacements list[mapping]/null unset Each item has old and new. Declare replacements as pairs; Core gives this mode precedence. to_replace scalar unset Nonnull old value for pre_split scalar mode. Select scalar mode when no pair/map mode is active. value scalar/null unset JSON-safe in pre_split. Supply the scalar replacement, including null.

Minimal YAML:

- name: valuereplacement
  transformer: ValueReplacement
  params: {columns: [segment], to_replace: unknown, value: null}

Common mistake: Use exactly one replacement mode in pre_split, and cast integers before fractional replacements.

Details: Defaults are unset; no active rule means no replacements. Core resolves pairs before mapping before scalar mode; Bundle pre-split requires exactly one mode and explicit columns. Pre-split also requires lossless JSON values, forbids colliding old values such as numeric 1 and "1", and requires a nonnull scalar old value in scalar mode. Matched cells are replaced, unmatched/null cells otherwise remain. Numeric replacement preserves integer precision; fractional/out-of-range replacement of an integer column requires an explicit cast first. Saves rules only. Context: row. Dependencies: base.

For a numeric missing-value marker, replace it with YAML null before imputation:

- name: missing_measurements
  transformer: ValueReplacement
  params: {columns: [co_gt], mapping: {-200: null}}
- name: fill_measurements
  transformer: SimpleImputer
  params: {columns: [co_gt], strategy: mean}

On pandas and Polars, a floating co_gt column remains floating after replacement; existing nullable storage is preserved. The imputer learns its mean from the remaining training values and reuses that mean when scoring. Other columns and unmatched values remain unchanged. Text and object columns retain their native replacement semantics; use Casting if a text column must become numeric.

docs.title: InvalidValueReplacement
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: an income outside fixed bounds becomes missing.

File: config/preprocessing.yml, or config/pre_split.yml under the narrower admission rules.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes columns list[string]/null null Existing numeric columns; [] selects none. Select features; omitted selection uses numeric detection. rule string/null null negative, negative_to_nan, zero, custom_range; Core also zero_to_nan, percentage_bounds, age_bounds. Select a fixed invalid-value rule; pre_split allows negative/zero/custom_range only. replace_inf boolean false true, false Replace positive infinity. replace_neg_inf boolean false true, false Replace negative infinity. min_value, max_value number/null null Inclusive bounds; pre_split custom_range needs at least one finite bound. Mark values outside the range invalid. replacement scalar/null missing null or a compatible finite scalar in pre_split. Set invalid cells to this value. value scalar/null null Nonnull value overrides replacement. Compatibility replacement alias. mode string/null null Core alias for rule; not admitted in pre_split. Compatibility rule input.

Minimal YAML:

- name: invalidvaluereplacement
  transformer: InvalidValueReplacement
  params: {columns: [income], rule: custom_range, min_value: 0, max_value: 1000000, replacement: null}

Common mistake: Use rule: custom_range, not outside_range; pre_split requires explicit columns and JSON-safe replacements.

Details: Supported named rules are negative/negative_to_nan, zero, and custom_range (values strictly outside the specified inclusive bounds). Boundary comparisons are fixed, not fitted quantiles. Core also normalizes zero_to_nan, percentage_bounds (0–100), age_bounds (0–120), with explicit bounds overriding presets. Pre-split allows only negative, zero, custom_range or null with an infinity flag; custom_range needs a finite lower or upper bound. A nonnull value overrides replacement. Replaces invalid selected numeric cells in place, preserves existing missing values and exact integer values where representable. Cast before fractional replacement in integer columns. Pre-split accepts only its fixed allowlisted fields, requires explicit columns and JSON-safe replacement (null, not NaN/Infinity). State stores rules only. Context: row. Dependencies: base.

docs.title: Casting
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: text "12" becomes numeric 12; invalid numeric text becomes null with coercion enabled.

File: config/preprocessing.yml, or config/pre_split.yml under the narrower admission rules.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes columns list[string] [] Existing names paired with target_type. Apply a common type to selected columns. target_type string required with columns Portable types listed below. Override the same columns in column_types. column_types mapping {} Column→type. Set individual output types. coerce_on_error boolean true true, false Convert invalid input to missing, or request failure.

Minimal YAML:

- name: casting
  transformer: Casting
  params: {column_types: {age: float64, active: boolean}, coerce_on_error: true}

Common mistake: Category casts learn a vocabulary and are not admitted in pre_split.

Category values follow native engine semantics: numeric pandas categories keep numeric labels, while Polars categories are strings. For matching text labels across engines, cast to string first, then category, and refit; an existing fitted category vocabulary is not rewritten.

Details: Supported cross-engine names: float32, float64 (float, double, numeric); int32, int64 (int, integer); string (str, text); boolean (bool); datetime64[ns] (datetime, date, datetime64); category (categorical). Extra native dtype spellings are engine-specific and not portable Bundle pre-split contracts. Boolean text accepts true/yes/1/on/y/t and false/no/0/off/n/f, case-insensitively. Numeric and nullable dtype conversion can change precision; use explicit float widths. Category casting learns and saves the vocabulary, with unseen categories missing on replay; therefore Pre-split rejects it. Other casts save only the fixed type map. Columns are replaced in place; missing values use the destination's nullable representation. Context: row. Dependencies: base.

docs.title: Fixed normalization followed by eligibility
docs.text:
This pre_split.yml recipe fragment demonstrates explicit text and type normalization before target completeness and business deduplication. Replace names and rules for your data; do not include record keys in the write columns.

clean_known_labels:
  - name: textcleaning
    transformer: TextCleaning
    params: {columns: [segment], operations: [{op: trim}, {op: case, mode: lower}]}
  - name: casting
    transformer: Casting
    params: {columns: [age], target_type: float64, coerce_on_error: true}
  - name: dropmissingrows
    transformer: DropMissingRows
    params: {subset: [churn]}
  - name: deduplicate
    transformer: Deduplicate
    params: {subset: [segment, age, income], keep: first}

Deduplicate is not a target-conflict resolution rule: conflicting labels in one subset group fail. If you need a business tie-breaker or cross-table join, prepare that upstream with explicit lineage. Unseen text does not automatically map to an alias; null produced by Casting still needs a deliberate missing-value policy. Select the recipe with pre_split_recipe: clean_known_labels.

docs.title: Custom factory contracts and ready functions
docs.text:
Back to the preprocessing catalog

These cards cover the Core function wrappers behind custom factories and the ready factories shipped in a generated project. For writing your own factory, see custom steps and custom pre-split filters.

YAML blocks are list fragments to paste under a selected recipe unless a card marks them as standalone Core configuration. Shared column, row and runtime rules are in read the step cards.

custom: preprocessing.log_feature calls a top-level factory in the captured src/features/preprocessing.py with YAML params as keyword arguments. The factory returns one valid step dictionary. It is not passed a DataFrame. The returned step later calls the calculation/learning functions with real rows. A raw def transform(df) returning a frame, a sklearn transformer, a list of steps, a lambda or a closure is not a valid factory. Use one YAML entry per factory and wrap calculations with the existing helpers below.

Callbacks receive a private pandas frame, also when the surrounding model uses Polars; their output is restored to the original engine. Column callbacks must return one value per input row and declared output, preserving index/order. An array follows row position; a pandas Series/frame must retain the index. Empty and null handling belong to the callback, so define and test them. Learning functions return a dict with string keys and JSON-compatible finite values; NaN/Infinity and nonstring mapping keys are rejected. Apply never sees y. Keep I/O out of imports and factories; package dependencies explicitly.

docs.title: ColumnFunction
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: a fixed calculation adds or replaces columns. The registry ID is code-only; select the factory in Bundle YAML:

File: config/preprocessing.yml. Select a custom factory; the parameter table describes its Python helper, not literal YAML callback values.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes name string required Nonempty step name. Label the returned step. output string/list[string] required Nonempty unique names. Declare output columns. replace boolean false true, false Allow replacement of existing output names, excluding hidden target. params JSON mapping/null {} String keys and finite JSON values. Pass fixed callback arguments. inference_context string/null null (unknown) row, group, window or global declaration accepted by the helper. Declare actual callback context; declaration is still validated. function Python callable required Top-level captured function; not a YAML value. Compute output columns.

Minimal YAML:

- custom: preprocessing.log_feature
  params: {column: income}

Common mistake: Put Python callbacks in a top-level factory and select custom in YAML; raw functions are not YAML transformer parameters.

Details: Python helper: column_step(name, function, *, output, replace=False, params=None, inference_context=None). Required name string, top-level function, output string or nonempty unique string list; replace bool default false; params JSON mapping default {}; inference_context optional row/group/window/ global declaration (default unknown). Callback is function(df) when params empty, or function(df, params) otherwise. Saves function reference/config, no learned state. Output names must be new unless replace is true; overwriting the hidden target is prohibited. Context depends on actual code, not the helper name. Dependencies: base plus callback imports. No blanket worker/REST admission.

docs.title: FittedFunction
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: learn frequencies from training rows, then replace categories using the saved lookup.

File: config/preprocessing.yml. Select a custom factory; the parameter table describes its Python helper, not literal YAML callback values.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes name string required Nonempty step name. Label the returned step. output string/list[string] required Nonempty unique names. Declare output columns. replace boolean false true, false Allow replacement of existing output names, excluding hidden target. params JSON mapping/null {} String keys and finite JSON values. Pass fixed callback arguments. inference_context string/null null (unknown) row, group, window or global declaration accepted by the helper. Declare actual callback context; declaration is still validated. learn Python callable required Top-level captured function. Learn a JSON dict from training df and y. apply Python callable required Top-level captured function. Compute outputs from df and saved state, without y.

Minimal YAML:

- custom: preprocessing.frequency_encoding
  params: {columns: [segment]}

Common mistake: A saved state does not prove row independence; declare the context your callback actually requires.

Details: Python helper: fitted_step(name, learn, apply, *, output, replace=False, params=None, inference_context=None). Same name/output/replace/params/context fields as column_step; required top-level learn and apply functions replace the single callback. Calls learn(df, y) → JSON dict, and apply(df, state) → outputs; nonempty params adds the params argument last to both. The target is available only to learn, separate from the feature frame. Saves state once per fit/fold; apply cannot learn from prediction rows by using the helper alone, but user code must still honor that intent. Context depends on the callback; saved state is not proof of row independence. Dependencies: callback-specific.

docs.title: RowFilterFunction
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: retain rows whose age is inside a declared range.

File: config/pre_split.yml, through a captured project factory. The parameter table describes the Python helper used by the factory.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes name string required Nonempty step name. Label the returned step. function Python callable required Top-level captured fixed filter. Return an aligned nonmissing Boolean Series. columns list[string] required Nonempty unique required source names. Declare columns read by the filter. params JSON mapping/null {} String keys and finite JSON values. Supply fixed callback arguments. inference_context string/null null (unknown) Fixed row-local context required for pre_split admission. Declare actual callback behavior.

Minimal YAML:

- custom: pre_split.value_range
  params: {column: age, minimum: 0, maximum: 120}

Common mistake: An arbitrary custom transformer is not admitted before splitting; use the fixed-filter helper and preserve source values.

Details: Python helper: filter_step(name, function, *, columns, params=None, inference_context=None). Required name, top-level function and nonempty unique string columns list; params/context follow the helpers above. Callback returns a pandas Boolean Series aligned to the input index, one nonmissing value per row; explicitly fill ambiguous mask values. Saves a function reference/rule and a declaration with effect: filter, required_columns and learns_from_data false. Bundle admission checks that captured registration and declaration, JSON-safe params and unchanged source values/dtypes. It does not admit arbitrary custom transformers before splitting. Filters must be fixed and row-local for pre-split; do not calculate means, deduplication or request-sized ranks in the callback. Rows/y are filtered consistently, never edited. Dependencies: callback-specific; context unknown unless explicitly declared, and still subject to validation.

docs.title: preprocessing.log_feature
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: Add a nonnegative log feature: [-1, 0, 3, null] becomes [0, 0, log(4), null].

File: config/preprocessing.yml.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes column string required Existing numeric column. Add log_ without replacing input.

Minimal YAML:

- custom: preprocessing.log_feature
  params: {column: income}

Common mistake: This clips negatives to zero before log1p; it is not the same rule as SimpleTransformation log.

Details: Adds log_<column> without replacing the source, using log1p(max(value, 0)). Thus [-1, 0, 3, null] produces [0, 0, 1.386294..., null]; positive infinity remains infinity and nonnumeric text needs casting first. Output is floating. Saves fixed code/params, no learned state; mathematically row-local, although the shipped factory does not explicitly declare diagnostic context. Base NumPy/pandas dependencies.

docs.title: preprocessing.frequency_encoding
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: Use training category frequency as a numeric feature; [A, A, B, null] learns A=0.5 and B=0.25.

File: config/preprocessing.yml.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes columns list[string] required Nonempty unique names; use string categories for JSON lookup keys. Replace categories with saved training shares.

Minimal YAML:

- custom: preprocessing.frequency_encoding
  params: {columns: [segment]}

Common mistake: Null contributes to the denominator but not a category count; unseen/null scoring values become 0.

Details: Fits value_counts / number_of_training_rows; null is excluded from counts but included in the denominator. Training [A, A, B, null] stores A=0.5, B=0.25; prediction [A, NEW, null] becomes [0.5, 0, 0]. Replaces selected columns with floats; empty training raises, empty apply retains columns. Saves one lookup per column, never recomputes scoring frequencies. Mathematically row-local apply; the shipped factory has no explicit context declaration. Base dependencies.

docs.title: preprocessing.rare_categories
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: Combine rare and unseen categories while preserving missing values.

File: config/preprocessing.yml.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes column string required Existing category column; string categories recommended. Choose values to group. min_share number 0.05 Strictly between 0 and 1. Keep categories at or above this training share. other JSON scalar Other Compatible replacement value. Replace rare and unseen nonnull categories.

Minimal YAML:

- custom: preprocessing.rare_categories
  params: {column: segment, min_share: 0.05, other: Other}

Common mistake: An original category already named Other is not escaped and becomes indistinguishable from grouped values.

Details: Fits category shares using all training rows as denominator, saving category strings with share at least the threshold. Apply keeps known common values and nulls; rare/unseen values become other. A 2% category and an unseen category both become Other at a 5% threshold. It replaces the original column (object on pandas). An original value already equal to Other is not reserved or escaped, so it becomes indistinguishable from grouped values. Use string categories to avoid stringification ambiguities. Saves common values; no request refit. Empty training produces an empty keep set, not a useful learned vocabulary. Mathematically row-local, undeclared diagnostic context in the shipped factory.

docs.title: pre_split.minimum_completeness
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: Keep rows with enough observed inputs; [1, null] passes min_present 1 but fails 2.

File: config/pre_split.yml, through a captured project factory.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes columns list[string] required Nonempty unique existing names. Choose cells counted for completeness. min_present integer 1 1 through number of selected columns; Boolean rejected. Require this many nonmissing cells.

Minimal YAML:

- custom: pre_split.minimum_completeness
  params: {columns: [age, income], min_present: 1}

Common mistake: Empty text and infinity count as present; completeness is not a value-validity check.

Details: Keeps rows with that many nonmissing cells. Null/NaN are missing; empty text and infinity count as present. [1, null] stays at 1 and is removed at 2. No learned state; fixed row-local filter, preserves survivor values/order and y alignment. Empty apply remains empty. Base dependencies.

docs.title: pre_split.value_range
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: Keep values within fixed inclusive limits while preserving missing values.

File: config/pre_split.yml, through a captured project factory.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes column string required Existing comparable column. Choose eligibility value. minimum comparable scalar required Compatible with column and no greater than maximum. Set inclusive lower bound. maximum comparable scalar required Compatible with column and no less than minimum. Set inclusive upper bound.

Minimal YAML:

- custom: pre_split.value_range
  params: {column: age, minimum: 0, maximum: 120}

Common mistake: Missing values survive this rule; add a completeness filter when missing input is ineligible.

Details: Keeps values in the closed interval or missing values. [35, -1, 130, null] keeps 35 and null. It does not validate away missing inputs: combine completeness when that is required. Reversed/incompatible bounds are not a useful rule; validate them before training. Saves rule only; row-local filter, empty apply stays empty. Base dependencies.

docs.title: pre_split.allowed_values
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: Keep listed categories, for example NL and DE, and remove other rows.

File: config/pre_split.yml, through a captured project factory.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes column string required Existing column. Choose eligibility category. values sequence required Configured allowed values; empty sequence admits no rows. Keep matching values without case normalization.

Minimal YAML:

- custom: pre_split.allowed_values
  params: {column: country, values: [NL, DE]}

Common mistake: NL and nl are different unless normalized first; an ordinary nonnull list removes missing values.

Details: Empty values allow no rows. Uses membership in the configured values, without case normalization: NL is kept, FR removed. Null is removed for ordinary nonnull allowed lists; explicitly placing a null-like value in the list follows pandas membership behavior, so omit null to require a known category. Saves rule only; row-local filter with original survivor values/order. Base dependencies.

docs.title: Asset-backed factories
docs.text:
preprocessing.city_region and pre_split.allowed_countries are commented examples, not active shipped factories. To use one:

  1. Create its UTF-8 JSON asset under src/features/assets/, for example countries.json containing ["NL", "DE", "BE"].
  2. Add its relative filename to src/features/assets.json, for example {"files": ["assets/countries.json"]}, retaining the existing manifest's required fields and other entries.
  3. Uncomment the matching import, callback and factory in the phase Python file.
  4. Add custom: pre_split.allowed_countries (no params) to the selected pre-split recipe, or custom: preprocessing.city_region to the preprocessing recipe for the city→region lookup.
  5. Run smoke/preview and retrain. The asset is captured with the model; changing the live file does not change an existing model version.

The country callback filters on country; the region callback reads city and adds region, with unmapped cities missing. Both use read_project_asset from the captured package. A raw filesystem path, uncaptured network service or feature-group function is not a substitute for this saved asset contract.

docs.title: Categorical encoding
docs.text:
Back to the preprocessing catalog

These steps turn categorical columns into numbers with one-hot, ordinal, label, hash, frequency, target and weight-of-evidence encoders. Rare-category grouping combines infrequent text values before encoding. The saved mapping fixes the output columns; new categories at scoring time do not extend it.

YAML blocks are list fragments to paste under a selected recipe unless a card marks them as standalone Core configuration. Shared column, row and runtime rules are in read the step cards.

Except LabelEncoder's target-oriented default, omitted columns uses categorical auto-detection and explicit [] yields no feature transformation. Select columns explicitly when numeric categories or Boolean values should be encoded. Encoder state fixes the output schema/mappings; new scoring categories do not extend it. All cards in this section use config/preprocessing.yml (LabelEncoder also has standalone target use), never pre-split. Dependencies are base/sklearn unless stated otherwise.

Automatic categorical detection leaves homogeneous pandas Decimal object columns as numeric inputs, matching native Polars Decimal. Explicit column selection is unchanged; no implicit conversion of numeric values occurs.

Schema previews for explicit selections advertise Label/Hash int64, Ordinal float32, and WOE or binary/continuous Target float64 outputs. Automatic category selection, multiclass Target expansion and Hash widths above the signed 64-bit range use runtime schema discovery. Label/Ordinal target-only selections retain their existing target behavior; no runtime values or saved mappings change.

docs.title: FrequencyEncoder
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: Replace each category with its training frequency or count.

File: config/preprocessing.yml.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes columns list[string]/null null Existing categorical columns; [] selects none. Select features; target is excluded. mode string frequency frequency, count Emit float64 shares or int64 counts in place. 
- name: category_frequency
  transformer: FrequencyEncoder
  params: {columns: [segment], mode: frequency}

Counts include missing values; the frequency denominator includes all training rows. For [A, A, null, B], saved frequencies are A=0.5, null=0.25 and B=0.25. Unseen values become zero. Missing values share a canonical key across None, NaN, pandas NA and Polars null, distinct from the literal string "nan". Apply uses saved counts without measuring the scoring batch. Empty apply retains the output dtype; fitting selected columns with zero rows raises an error.

docs.title: RareCategoryGrouping
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: Keep frequent text categories and group rare or unseen values under a replacement label. Output columns remain nullable strings.

File: config/preprocessing.yml.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes columns list[string]/null null Existing text/category columns; [] selects none. Select features; target is excluded. min_count integer 2 At least 1; booleans rejected. Minimum training count to retain a category. min_share number 0.0 Finite value in [0, 1]. Minimum share of all training rows to retain a category. replacement string Other Nonempty text. Label for rare and unseen values. 
- name: group_rare
  transformer: RareCategoryGrouping
  params: {columns: [segment], min_count: 2, min_share: 0.01, replacement: Other}
- name: fill_missing_category
  transformer: SimpleImputer
  params: {columns: [segment], strategy: constant, fill_value: Missing}
- name: encode_groups
  transformer: OneHotEncoder
  params: {columns: [segment], max_categories: null}

A category must meet both thresholds; equality passes. Missing values are counted as one category: frequent missing stays null, while rare missing and unseen values become the replacement. Impute retained missing values before learned OneHot encoding so pandas nullable strings are supported. An existing literal Other label can intentionally merge with grouped values.

Non-null values must be text, including textual pandas/Polars categorical values. For numeric category codes, add explicit Casting to string first. Saved membership is never recomputed on inference batches. Empty apply retains the string dtype; fitting selected columns with zero rows raises an error. In Canvas, use Rare Category Grouping in the existing Encoding panel.

docs.title: OneHotEncoder
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: Turn categories into fitted numeric indicator columns, for example segment_A and segment_B.

File: config/preprocessing.yml.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes columns list[string]/null null Existing categorical columns; [] selects none. Select feature columns; omission uses categorical detection. handle_unknown string ignore ignore, error Use all-zero indicators or fail for unseen categories. drop_first boolean false true, false Omit the first fitted category indicator. max_categories integer/null 20 At least 2; null disables cap. Limit fitted category width through infrequent grouping. prefix_separator string _ String. Retained compatibility option; generated names use _. drop_original boolean true true, false Remove selected source columns. include_missing boolean false true, false Represent missing values using an escaped category sentinel. categories mapping/null null Each selected column maps to an ordered, nonempty list of unique strings. Fix the vocabulary, including levels absent from training. Requires explicit columns, max_categories: null and include_missing: false. column_names string sklearn sklearn, slug Keep original category text or produce lowercase ASCII category names.

Minimal YAML:

- name: onehotencoder
  transformer: OneHotEncoder
  params: {columns: [segment], handle_unknown: ignore, max_categories: null}

Common mistake: Set max_categories: null when the default cap of 20 is not intended.

The default cap remains available for local execution. Independent Spark workers and endpoint admission require max_categories: null and include_missing: false; the admission error lists these supported settings. Choose them explicitly before fitting a pipeline intended for those runtimes.

Details: Learns sklearn categories/infrequent grouping and output names. A/B produces segment_A, segment_B; output is dense numeric indicators. Unknown categories with ignore are all-zero. Dropping the first category can produce no output for a constant column. Missing-category behavior depends on fitted categories and include_missing; enabling it uses an escaped sentinel so literal sentinel text and null do not collide. Target selection is excluded. Retained-name collisions raise. Context: row for the supported fitted configuration.

Fixed vocabulary: Keys must match columns exactly. Category list order fixes output order; drop_first: true removes the first listed level. Inputs must be string or categorical columns; numeric values are not converted to strings. With handle_unknown: ignore, both unknown values and nulls produce zeros. With error, either raises, so impute missing values first when needed.

- name: fixed_city
  transformer: OneHotEncoder
  params:
    columns: [city]
    categories:
      city: ["Øl", "Åben", "Zürich"]
    column_names: slug
    max_categories: null
    include_missing: false
    handle_unknown: ignore

This emits city_oel, city_aaben, city_zurich even when training omits a listed city. slug also works with learned categories. It folds æ/ø/å/ß to ae/oe/aa/ss, removes accents, lowercases and replaces punctuation with _. Empty or duplicate generated names fail clearly. Existing artifacts without the new options keep their original names and encoding.

In ML Canvas, select Use fixed categories and enter one category per line for each selected column. Spaces, commas and order are preserved. The form disables the category cap and missing-category option for fixed vocabularies.

docs.title: DummyEncoder
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: Create one fitted dummy column per category with all-zero output for unseen categories.

File: config/preprocessing.yml.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes columns list[string]/null null Existing categorical columns; [] selects none. Select feature columns; omission uses categorical detection. drop_first boolean false true, false Omit the first fitted category indicator.

Minimal YAML:

- name: dummyencoder
  transformer: DummyEncoder
  params: {columns: [segment], drop_first: false}

Common mistake: The OneHotEncoder category-cap and unknown-error options are not exposed here.

Details: Saves observed category lists, replaces selected original columns with fitted dummy columns named from column and category. A/B becomes one indicator per category; unknown values produce zeros, and missing values do not invent a new category. Output schema stays fixed on empty apply. Unlike OneHotEncoder, no category cap, separator, unknown-error, include-missing or drop-original options are exposed. Context: row.

docs.title: OrdinalEncoder
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: Replace categories with ordered numeric codes; unknown categories can receive -1.

File: config/preprocessing.yml.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes columns list[string]/null null Existing categorical columns; [] selects none. Select feature columns; omission uses categorical detection. handle_unknown string use_encoded_value use_encoded_value, error Choose how unseen categories are handled. unknown_value number -1 Must not collide with assigned codes. Choose the unseen-category code. categories_order string/list[string]/null null Multiline string or list of comma-separated strings, one line per column. Set category order; malformed explicit orders raise an error. target_column string/null null Existing label name; paired y can supply the label. Identify the supervised target, normally supplied by the pipeline.

Minimal YAML:

- name: ordinalencoder
  transformer: OrdinalEncoder
  params: {columns: [segment], handle_unknown: use_encoded_value, unknown_value: -1}

Common mistake: categories_order expects comma-separated strings, not nested YAML lists.

Details: Saves category lists and sklearn encoders. Replaces A/B with float32 0/1; unseen values use the unknown policy. Newly fitted feature keys distinguish nulls, numeric categories and literal strings; a missing category observed at fit can get its own code. Can also encode paired y under the target contract; avoid using it unintentionally to rewrite model labels. Context row for current feature artifacts; legacy pandas string-based states can depend on the batch. An explicit order must have the matching number of lines; malformed shapes and unsupported handle_unknown policies raise an error at fit. Use comma-separated lines, not nested YAML lists. Empty orders retain automatic ordering.

docs.title: LabelEncoder
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: Encode explicitly selected category columns as integer labels, or encode the target in standalone Core use.

File: config/preprocessing.yml.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes columns list[string]/null null Explicit features; absent/empty selects y when available. Choose features or use the target-oriented default. missing_code integer -1 Integer. Encode missing/unseen feature values. target_column string/null null Existing label name; paired y can supply the label. Identify the supervised target, normally supplied by the pipeline.

Minimal YAML:

- name: labelencoder
  transformer: LabelEncoder
  params: {columns: [segment], missing_code: -1}

Common mistake: Omitting columns targets y rather than auto-detecting feature columns.

Details: Absent/empty columns do not auto-detect feature columns: they fit y when available; with no y there may be no-op state. Explicit feature selection learns one encoder per column; y can be encoded when selected by its name. Saves vocabularies and target routing. Replaces categories with integer labels; missing/unseen feature values use the saved missing code unless represented in the learned vocabulary. Legacy/string-normalization semantics are retained by old artifacts. Use OrdinalEncoder for multi-feature encoding with an explicit unknown policy. Context depends on fitted state and engine; no worker/REST promise for target-changing use.

docs.title: HashEncoder
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: Replace each category column with one integer hash bucket without learning a vocabulary.

File: config/preprocessing.yml.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes columns list[string]/null null Existing categorical columns; [] selects none. Select feature columns; omission uses categorical detection. n_features integer 8 Positive integer; booleans and floating values are rejected. Set the number of possible integer buckets per source column.

Minimal YAML:

- name: hashencoder
  transformer: HashEncoder
  params: {columns: [segment], n_features: 8}

Common mistake: n_features is the bucket range; it does not create that many output columns.

Details: Saves selection, bucket count and normalization version, not a fitted category vocabulary. Replaces each selected column in place with an integer bucket in [0, n_features); it does not append n_features columns. Collisions are expected, so different categories can share a bucket. Unknown categories are hashable without refit. Current numeric normalization avoids changing keys because another row contains null. The target is excluded. Context: row for current supported scalar state. Previously saved encoders keep their saved bucket count and assignments, including the earlier default of 10; the default of 8 applies only to new fits.

docs.title: TargetEncoder
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: Replace categories with smoothed target statistics, using cross-fitted training values in the pipeline.

File: config/preprocessing.yml.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes columns list[string]/null null Existing categorical columns; [] selects none. Select feature columns; omission uses categorical detection. target_column string/null null Existing label name; paired y can supply the label. Identify the supervised target, normally supplied by the pipeline. target_type string auto auto, continuous, binary, multiclass Choose target interpretation. smooth string/number auto auto or nonnegative number. Smooth category statistics toward the global mean. cv integer 5 At least 2; booleans rejected. Requested maximum cross-fitting folds, capped by available rows/class counts. shuffle boolean true true, false Shuffle rows before assigning cross-fitting folds. random_state integer/null 42 0 through 2^32-1, or null. Reproducible shuffling; ignored when shuffle is false.

Minimal YAML:

- name: targetencoder
  transformer: TargetEncoder
  params: {columns: [segment], target_type: binary, smooth: auto}

Common mistake: Keep this step inside training folds; do not precompute encodings on the entire dataset.

Details: Requires a usable target during fit. Saves sklearn target/category statistics and global target mean. Binary or continuous encoding replaces a column with its smoothed target mean; multiclass drops it and emits segment_cls0, segment_cls1, etc. Unseen categories use the global mean; missing categories can be learned. New fits use the same key for None, NaN, pandas NA and Polars null, distinct from literal strings such as "nan". The saved key version makes this stable across engine changes; older artifacts retain their original sklearn categories. Collision checks protect multiclass output names. This wrapper fits saved mappings and applies them; pipeline training separately cross-fits training encodings so a row's own target does not enter its feature; heldout/prediction uses the full training map. The fold count is bounded by cv and sample/class counts. Defaults remain five folds, shuffle enabled and seed 42. With shuffle disabled the sklearn seed is unset; this does not implement grouped or forward-time CV. A null seed permits nondeterministic shuffled folds. Saved estimators replay their learned maps without refitting or adopting new CV settings. Too few examples for safe cross-fitting fail. Keep the entire step inside training folds too. Context: row against saved maps.

docs.title: WOEEncoder
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: Replace categories with learned binary log-odds evidence; unseen keys use 0.

File: config/preprocessing.yml.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes columns list[string]/null null Existing categorical columns; [] selects none. Select feature columns; omission uses categorical detection. target_column string/null null Existing label name; paired y can supply the label. Identify the supervised target, normally supplied by the pipeline. regularization number 0.5 Numeric smoothing strength; zero requires both classes in every category. Stabilize category class-count logarithms.

Minimal YAML:

- name: woeencoder
  transformer: WOEEncoder
  params: {columns: [segment], regularization: 0.5}

Zero smoothing is supported when each learned category contains both target classes. This must also hold in every cross-fitting training complement; a valid full-data map alone is insufficient. Otherwise fitting raises a clear ValueError recommending positive regularization before computing an undefined ratio or logarithm. Saved valid mappings replay unchanged.

Common mistake: Use exactly two target classes; missing labels or any other class count raise an error at fit.

Details: Requires binary target labels and finite usable class counts; use smoothing to avoid zero-count logarithms. Learns category log-odds/evidence maps and information value. Replaces selected columns with floats; an unseen key uses saved default 0.0 (not an exposed fit-time default knob). Missing categories have their own learned key. Current scalar keys distinguish numbers from literal strings; older artifacts retain older string-key semantics. Pipeline training cross-fits training encodings and saves full-training maps for heldout/prediction. Absent target input still warns and returns no-op state; a supplied target must have exactly two complete classes. Context: row for saved-map apply.

docs.title: Feature generation and selection
docs.text:
Back to the preprocessing catalog

These steps add interaction, polynomial and formula features, or keep a subset of columns by variance, correlation, univariate scores or a model.

YAML blocks are list fragments to paste under a selected recipe unless a card marks them as standalone Core configuration. Shared column, row and runtime rules are in read the step cards.

docs.title: FeatureInteraction
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: income 10 and tenure 3 add income_x_tenure=30.

File: config/preprocessing.yml.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes columns list[string] [] Existing column names. Select explicitly; no automatic detection. degree integer 2 2, 3, 4 Generate products of exactly this degree. interaction_only boolean true true, false Exclude repeated inputs/powers when true. include_bias boolean false true, false Add interaction_bias=1.

Minimal YAML:

- name: featureinteraction
  transformer: FeatureInteraction
  params: {columns: [income, tenure], degree: 2}

Common mistake: This generates exactly the selected degree; use PolynomialFeatures for all terms up to a degree.

Details: Generates products of exactly the chosen degree; false interaction_only permits repeated columns/powers. Saves combinations and names, adds float columns joined in sorted-name order with _x_, and optionally interaction_bias=1. Original columns remain. Null products stay missing; generated-name conflicts raise. Context row; base dependencies. For terms up to a degree, use PolynomialFeatures.

docs.title: PolynomialFeatures
docs.text:
Aliases: PolynomialFeaturesNode selects this same owner.

Purpose and effect: x=2, y=3 adds squared and cross terms 4, 6, 9.

File: config/preprocessing.yml.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes columns list[string] [] Existing column names. Select explicitly; no automatic detection. auto_detect boolean false true, false Detect numeric columns when none are selected, excluding target_column. target_column string/null null Existing label name. Exclude the target from automatic discovery; the pipeline supplies this name. degree integer/pair[integer] 2 Nonnegative degree or ordered [min_degree, max_degree]. Set generated term degrees. interaction_only boolean false true, false Exclude repeated-input powers when true. include_bias boolean false true, false Add a constant term. include_input_features boolean false true, false Append copied degree-1 terms; original columns already survive. output_prefix string poly String. Prefix generated names.

Minimal YAML:

- name: polynomialfeatures
  transformer: PolynomialFeatures
  params: {columns: [income, tenure], degree: 2, output_prefix: poly}

Common mistake: High degrees can create many columns; include_input_features does not control preservation of original inputs.

Details: Saves layout/configuration. Appends terms up to degree, with names such as poly_income_pow_2, poly_income_tenure; original columns remain. Optional bias is a constant term. Numeric finite input is required by sklearn; impute before expansion. Empty apply derives the same layout. Generated-name collisions raise. Context row; base/sklearn dependencies. Degree can grow output width rapidly.

docs.title: FeatureGeneration
docs.text:
Aliases: FeatureGenerationNode, FeatureMath select this same owner.

Purpose and effect: two numeric columns can add a sum, ratio or saved group statistic; fixed arithmetic and fitted group operations can share one list.

File: config/preprocessing.yml.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes operations list[mapping] [] Ordered operations described below. Generate new features, allowing later operations to read earlier outputs. epsilon number 1e-9 Small numeric guard. Protect division near zero. allow_overwrite boolean false true, false Overwrite named outputs, or suffix collisions. operations[].operation_type string arithmetic arithmetic, ratio, similarity, datetime_extract, group_agg Choose calculation family. operations[].input_columns list[string] [] Existing inputs appropriate to the operation. Supply primary operands, the numerator or grouping key. operations[].secondary_columns list[string] [] Existing inputs appropriate to the operation. Supply secondary operands, the denominator or grouped value. operations[].method string Operation-dependent Choices in the operation table below. Choose arithmetic, similarity or aggregate behavior. operations[].output_column string/null null Optional explicit name. Name the output; datetime operations may expand it for multiple sources/features. operations[].output_prefix string/null null Optional prefix. Prefix automatically generated output names. operations[].round_digits integer/null null Integer. Round numeric output. operations[].constants list[number] [] Arithmetic only. Add numeric operands. operations[].fillna scalar/null Effective 0 Arithmetic only. Fill missing numeric operands. operations[].datetime_features list[string] [] Calendar choices below. Choose extracted datetime components.

Minimal YAML:

- name: featuregeneration
  transformer: FeatureGeneration
  params:
    operations:
      - {operation_type: arithmetic, method: add, input_columns: [income, bonus], output_column: total}
      - {operation_type: group_agg, input_columns: [segment], secondary_columns: [total], method: mean, output_column: segment_mean}

Common mistake: A fitted group aggregate reuses training lookups. Unseen groups yield missing for existing aggregate methods; deviation uses the saved global training mean.

Details: Additional fields and choices:

Operation Input and options arithmetic method: add, subtract, multiply, divide; constants numeric list default []; fillna scalar/null default effective 0. Numeric inputs/secondary columns and constants participate in configured order. ratio Sums input columns as numerator and secondary columns as denominator; near-zero/missing denominator uses signed epsilon. similarity First input and first secondary (or second input); method ratio, token_sort_ratio or token_set_ratio. Backend is selected and saved at fit, not a user-supplied artifact field. datetime_extract datetime_features list default []: year, quarter, month, month_name, week, day, day_name, weekday, is_weekend, hour, minute, second, season, time_of_day. group_agg First input is group key, first secondary is numeric value; method default mean, also sum, min, max, count, std, median, deviation.

The fitted artifact also stores these fields inside each operation. They are created during fit, not configurable YAML parameters. Supplying them in a recipe does not override fitting: fit replaces them with its own values.

Saved field Type and values How it is created and used operations[].similarity_backend rapidfuzz or difflib Similarity fitting selects rapidfuzz when installed, otherwise difflib. Apply reuses the saved choice; a saved rapidfuzz model requires that dependency. With difflib, all method names use its sequence ratio, not rapidfuzz token matching. operations[].group_agg_mapping Mapping or null Group fitting saves group_column, parallel keys/values lists and null_value for the missing-key group. Null records an unresolved fit operation. Apply maps incoming keys to saved numbers; it does not aggregate the request batch.

Operations run in order; later operations can read earlier outputs. A group aggregate learns a training lookup (including missing-key group) and reuses it; an unseen group yields missing for ordinary aggregate methods. There is no request-time refit. Default generated names use <operation_type>_<index> with optional prefix; datetime outputs use source/feature names, expanding a supplied name when multiple sources/features are requested. Existing names receive a numeric suffix unless overwrite is true. New fits validate operation types, named methods and calendar choices before publishing state; errors while evaluating supported operations propagate. polynomial is not a supported operation_type: use PolynomialFeatures. Similarity uses optional rapidfuzz when available, otherwise difflib; a saved rapidfuzz artifact requires that package on replay. Null/empty string pairs score 100 when both empty, 0 when one empty. Context is row for supported numeric/group lookup operations; pandas similarity can be global due to string rendering. Other dependencies: base.

New fits save operation_contract_version: 1. Numeric datetime_extract outputs use nullable Int64 on both local engines, including invalid dates, singletons and empty batches. Missing numeric calendar values remain missing. Unversioned saved artifacts retain their historical dtypes and logged-skip behavior; refit to adopt the checked operation contract. Arithmetic zero/null defaults and signed-epsilon division are unchanged.

For method: deviation, each output is the source value minus its group's training mean. Unseen groups and groups with no usable mean use the global training mean. A learned missing-key group keeps its own mean; a missing source value stays missing. All outputs are floating point. For example, training values [2, 4] in group A produce mean 3, so a later value 8 produces 5 even when scored alone. The saved mapping adds category_key_version: 1 and global_value; typed group keys distinguish Boolean, numeric and text values. This extends the existing operation; old saved aggregate methods retain their lookup representation and behavior.

- name: income_deviation
  transformer: FeatureMath
  params:
    operations:
      - {operation_type: group_agg, method: deviation, input_columns: [segment], secondary_columns: [income], output_column: income_deviation}

docs.title: VarianceThreshold
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: remove a constant numeric feature with threshold 0.

File: config/preprocessing.yml.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes columns list[string]/null null Numeric candidates, including binary; [] also auto-selects. Choose candidate features; target is excluded. threshold number 0.0 Nonnegative. Retain variance strictly above this value. drop_columns boolean true true, false Remove rejected candidates, or record selection only.

Minimal YAML:

- name: variancethreshold
  transformer: VarianceThreshold
  params: {columns: [age, constant_flag], threshold: 0.0, drop_columns: true}

Common mistake: If every candidate is constant or all-missing, every candidate can be removed.

Details: Learns training variance/retained columns and saves that set. False records selection but does not remove columns. Unselected unrelated columns remain; target is excluded. NaNs are ignored for variance estimation; all-missing candidates are rejected. If no candidate clears the threshold, all candidates are removed when drop_columns is true. This does not impute values. Apply never remeasures variance. Context row; base/sklearn dependencies.

docs.title: CorrelationThreshold
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: remove one of two strongly correlated inputs.

File: config/preprocessing.yml.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes columns list[string]/null null Numeric candidates, including binary; [] also auto-selects. Choose candidate features; target is excluded. threshold number 0.95 Normally 0–1. Choose correlation strength for removing a redundant input. correlation_method string pearson pearson, spearman, kendall Choose fitted correlation measure. drop_columns boolean true true, false Remove rejected candidates, or record selection only.

Minimal YAML:

- name: correlationthreshold
  transformer: CorrelationThreshold
  params: {columns: [income, income_copy], threshold: 0.95, correlation_method: pearson}

Common mistake: Candidate column order can determine which of a correlated pair survives.

Details: Saves correlated columns chosen for removal from training correlations. Column order matters when choosing which redundant feature survives. Constant/missing correlations do not establish strong correlation. Apply drops the saved set only, or no columns when drop_columns is false. Context row; base dependencies.

docs.title: UnivariateSelection
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: keep the two numeric inputs most associated with y.

File: config/preprocessing.yml.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes columns list[string]/null null Numeric candidates, including binary; [] also auto-selects. Choose candidate features; target is excluded. target_column string/null null Existing label name; paired y can supply the label. Identify the supervised target, normally supplied by the pipeline. method string select_k_best select_k_best, select_percentile, select_fpr, select_fdr, select_fwe, generic_univariate_select; sklearn PascalCase aliases. Choose selection rule. score_func string/null auto f_classif, f_regression, mutual_info_classif, mutual_info_regression, chi2, r_regression. Choose association score. problem_type string auto auto, classification, regression Resolve default scorer. allow_missing_target boolean false true, false Allow configured missing-target fallback. drop_columns boolean true true, false Remove rejected candidates. k integer/string 10 Positive integer or all. Select-k-best feature count. percentile number 10 0–100. Select-percentile share. alpha number 0.05 Significance level for FPR/FDR/FWE. Set statistical threshold. mode string k_best k_best, percentile, fpr, fdr, fwe Choose generic selector mode. param number/string Mode-dependent Explicit override of k/percentile/alpha. Set generic selector parameter.

Minimal YAML:

- name: univariateselection
  transformer: UnivariateSelection
  params: {columns: [age, income, tenure], method: select_k_best, k: 2, problem_type: classification}
