Common mistake: For low-cardinality numeric regression targets, declare problem_type: regression instead of relying on auto.

Details: Statistical p-value selectors need a scorer returning p-values. chi2 uses nonnegative scaled values during fitting. Requires training y unless explicit missing-target behavior is selected; missing classification labels fail. Auto problem type uses a cardinality heuristic for numeric labels: declare regression for low-cardinality count targets. Saves selected/candidate columns and scores; apply only drops the saved rejected columns. Context row; base/sklearn dependencies.

docs.title: ModelBasedSelection
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: retain inputs with sufficient fitted importance or recursively eliminate inputs down to a requested count.

File: config/preprocessing.yml.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes columns list[string]/null null Numeric candidates, including binary; [] also auto-selects. Choose candidate features; target is excluded. target_column string/null null Existing label name; paired y can supply the label. Identify the supervised target, normally supplied by the pipeline. method string select_from_model select_from_model, rfe, rfecv, sequential_feature_selection Choose importance, recursive or sequential selection. estimator string auto auto, logistic_regression/logisticregression, linear_regression/linearregression, random_forest/randomforest. Choose fitted importance estimator. problem_type string auto auto, classification, regression Resolve suitable estimator. drop_columns boolean true true, false Remove rejected candidates. threshold number/string mean Sklearn threshold expression, such as mean, median or a multiplier. Select-from-model importance cutoff. max_features integer/null null Select-from-model only. Cap selected features. n_features_to_select integer/number/string/null RFE: null; sequential: auto RFE count/fraction/null; sequential count, fraction in (0,1), or auto. Set retained features; sequential auto selects half. k integer/null null Legacy RFE fallback when n_features_to_select is unset. Set retained feature count. step integer/number 1 Positive count or fraction for RFE/RFECV. Set elimination size. cv integer 5 At least 2; RFECV/sequential only. Set unshuffled cross-validation folds. scoring string/null null sklearn scorer name or estimator default. Choose the CV selection criterion. min_features_to_select integer 1 Positive; RFECV only. Set the smallest evaluated feature subset. direction string forward forward, backward; sequential only. Add or remove features greedily.

Minimal YAML:

- name: modelbasedselection
  transformer: ModelBasedSelection
  params: {columns: [age, income, tenure], method: select_from_model, estimator: random_forest, threshold: mean}

Common mistake: Supply training y or target_column; a missing target or unsupported estimator raises an error instead of disabling selection.

Details: Uses a resolved estimator suitable for the problem type. Unknown methods, estimators and problem types raise with supported choices; estimator fit errors propagate. Logistic regression is supported only for classification. Saves selected columns/importance evidence. Requires numeric inputs and training y; no candidate columns remains an empty no-op. Candidate NaNs are filled with zero for selection fitting only; output values are not imputed. Apply preserves unrelated columns and drops saved rejected candidates only. Context row; base/sklearn dependencies.

RFECV chooses the subset size by cross-validation. Sequential selection chooses each next feature using cross-validation; its separate n_features_to_select setting does not inherit the legacy RFE k. Integer CV uses sklearn's unshuffled stratified folds for classification and ordinary folds otherwise. Folds are not automatically reduced: small training populations must choose a valid lower cv. These methods repeat estimator fits and can be expensive on wide data. Saved inference only uses fixed selected names and does not repeat CV. Sequential selection has no fitted feature-importance report, so it saves an empty importance mapping instead of inventing scores.

- name: recursive_cv
  transformer: ModelBasedSelection
  params: {method: rfecv, cv: 3, min_features_to_select: 1, step: 1}

docs.title: feature_selection
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: Choose a concrete selection algorithm through a method field; it does not add another algorithm.

File: config/preprocessing.yml.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes method string select_k_best Aliases listed below. Dispatch to the corresponding concrete selector. threshold number/string, depending on selector Selected algorithm's default For variance, a nonnegative number (default 0.0); for correlation_threshold, a correlation limit (default 0.95). Other selectors define their own fields. Forwarded unchanged to the chosen calculator; it is not ignored by variance/correlation selection. Other fields See selected card See selected card VarianceThreshold, CorrelationThreshold, UnivariateSelection or ModelBasedSelection options. Forward configuration unchanged.

Minimal YAML:

- name: feature_selection
  transformer: feature_selection
  params: {method: variance, columns: [age, constant_flag], threshold: 0.0}

Common mistake: Use correlation_threshold, not correlation, as the dispatcher method.

Details: variance/variance_threshold route to VarianceThreshold; correlation_threshold to CorrelationThreshold; select_k_best, select_percentile, select_fpr, select_fdr, select_fwe, generic_univariate_select to UnivariateSelection; select_from_model, rfe, rfecv, sequential_feature_selection to ModelBasedSelection. The matching card defines required target, defaults, state, output and context. Unknown methods raise with supported choices. Existing saved artifacts still replay their fitted selection without resolving the fit method again. Prefer the concrete selector ID when readability is more valuable than a single dispatcher field.

docs.title: Bounds and outliers
docs.text:
Back to the preprocessing catalog

These steps apply fixed bounds, clip values or remove outlier rows during training. Read each card for whether it changes values or removes rows.

YAML blocks are list fragments to paste under a selected recipe unless a card marks them as standalone Core configuration. Shared column, row and runtime rules are in read the step cards.

ManualBounds removes rows; ClipValues changes values and preserves rows. The learned outlier filters below belong in training, never pre-split. Their appliers can remove rows. Saved pipeline scoring retains each request row and reports excluded rows with a null prediction and an outlier:<step> reason.

docs.title: ManualBounds
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: lower 0, upper 100 retains 0 and 100 and removes -1 and 101; missing values are retained.

File: config/preprocessing.yml, or config/pre_split.yml under the narrower admission rules. Training-only row changes need an explicit scoring decision.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes bounds mapping {} Column→{lower, upper}; each bound number/null. Filter rows outside fixed inclusive bounds. bounds.<column>.lower, upper number/null null pre_split requires at least one finite bound per column and lower ≤ upper. Set each side; omitted sides are unbounded.

Minimal YAML:

- name: manualbounds
  transformer: ManualBounds
  params: {bounds: {age: {lower: 0, upper: 120}}}

Common mistake: Missing values survive; combine with a completeness rule if they are ineligible.

Details: Saves fixed bounds. Rows violating any bound are filtered with paired targets and survivor order preserved. Context: row. Dependencies: base.

docs.title: ClipValues
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: [-1, 50, 200] with bounds 0–100 becomes [0, 50, 100].

File: config/preprocessing.yml.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes bounds mapping required Nonempty existing numeric column→{lower, upper}. Set clipping scope. bounds.<column>.lower, upper number/null null At least one finite bound; lower ≤ upper. Cap values while preserving rows.

Minimal YAML:

- name: clipvalues
  transformer: ClipValues
  params: {bounds: {income: {lower: 0, upper: 1000000}}}

Common mistake: ClipValues preserves rows and is not admitted in pre_split; use ManualBounds to filter there.

Details: Missing values pass through. Saves fixed bounds, replaces values in place, never filters rows. Integer bounds must be representable if the integer dtype is preserved; cast explicitly when fractional arithmetic is intended. Context: row. Dependencies: base. Not admitted in pre-split, despite using fixed values.

docs.title: IQR
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: remove observations outside training Q1/Q3 fences.

File: config/preprocessing.yml. Training-only row changes need an explicit scoring decision.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes columns list[string]/null null Existing numeric columns; [] selects none. Select features; omitted selection uses numeric detection. multiplier number 1.5 Numeric fence multiplier. Set distance beyond fitted Q1 and Q3.

Minimal YAML:

- name: iqr
  transformer: IQR
  params: {columns: [income], multiplier: 1.5}

Common mistake: This removes rows; ordinary prediction rejects row-count loss. Use Winsorize to retain rows.

Details: Saves Q1 − multiplier × IQR and Q3 + multiplier × IQR per column. Apply removes rows outside any learned fence while preserving missing values and aligning y. A zero IQR gives equal fences. No request-time quartile fit. Context: row against saved bounds. Dependencies: base.

docs.title: ZScore
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: remove observations farther than the configured number of fitted standard deviations from the training mean.

File: config/preprocessing.yml. Training-only row changes need an explicit scoring decision.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes columns list[string]/null null Existing numeric columns; [] selects none. Select features; omitted selection uses numeric detection. threshold number 3.0 Numeric standard-deviation threshold. Set allowed distance from the training mean.

Minimal YAML:

- name: zscore
  transformer: ZScore
  params: {columns: [income], threshold: 3.0}

Common mistake: Do not expect row-removing outlier filters to return one ordinary prediction per input.

Details: Saves mean/standard-deviation statistics and threshold; filters paired rows using those statistics. Missing values are preserved; unusable/zero scales cannot provide a meaningful outlier distance. No refit on heldout/request rows. Context: row. Dependencies: base.

docs.title: Winsorize
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: values beyond fitted 5th/95th percentiles are capped to the corresponding saved percentile, retaining every row.

File: config/preprocessing.yml.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes columns list[string]/null null Existing numeric columns; [] selects none. Select features; omitted selection uses numeric detection. lower_percentile number 5.0 0–100; no greater than upper_percentile. Learn the lower cap. upper_percentile number 95.0 0–100; no less than lower_percentile. Learn the upper cap. percentiles_by_column mapping omitted Selected column → {lower, upper}; both finite, ordered percentages required. Override the global tails for individual measurements.

Minimal YAML:

- name: winsorize
  transformer: Winsorize
  params: {columns: [income], lower_percentile: 5, upper_percentile: 95}

Different measurements can use different tails while other selected columns keep the global settings:

- name: measurement_tails
  transformer: Winsorize
  params:
    columns: [income, tenure]
    lower_percentile: 5
    upper_percentile: 95
    percentiles_by_column:
      income: {lower: 1, upper: 99}

Common mistake: Use percent values such as 5 and 95, not shares such as 0.05 and 0.95. Integer columns require finite, integral bounds within their dtype's range. Add an explicit Casting step to float64 before Winsorize when fractional percentile bounds are intended; the node does not silently round the bounds or promote integer values.

When columns is omitted, automatic numeric selection also includes integer IDs and counts. If a selected integer column has fractional percentile bounds, the whole fit raises. Set columns explicitly to keep IDs out of clipping. Cast only the measurements that should support fractional bounds, for example:

- name: fractional_income
  transformer: Casting
  params: {columns: [income], target_type: float64}
- name: cap_income
  transformer: Winsorize
  params: {columns: [income], lower_percentile: 5, upper_percentile: 95}

This recipe leaves a separate customer_id column unchanged, including integers above 2**53; it does not cast every numeric column to float.

Details: Saves bounds; applies clipping in place. Missing values remain missing, constant columns retain their constant. Integer 0th/100th-percentile endpoints remain exact; interpolated integer quantiles outside the exact float64 range also require explicit Casting. Automatic column selection follows the same precision rule. Context: row. Dependencies: base.

docs.title: EllipticEnvelope
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: remove observations classified as outside the fitted robust envelope.

File: config/preprocessing.yml. Training-only row changes need an explicit scoring decision.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes columns list[string]/null null Existing numeric columns; [] selects none. Select features; omitted selection uses numeric detection. contamination number 0.01 Greater than 0 and at most 0.5. Set expected outlier fraction. random_state integer/null 42 Integer seed or null. Control fitting randomness.

Minimal YAML:

- name: ellipticenvelope
  transformer: EllipticEnvelope
  params: {columns: [income], contamination: 0.01, random_state: 42}

Common mistake: This wrapper fits separate envelopes per column; it is not a multivariate covariance filter across all inputs.

Details: Fits a separate sklearn envelope for each selected column, rather than one multivariate envelope across all selected columns. Saves these models. Apply filters rows and paired y; missing values are handled separately from finite fit observations. Small or degenerate fits can be skipped with a warning. Context: row against saved models; training fit is population-dependent. Dependencies: base/sklearn.

docs.title: IsolationForest
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: fit one joint isolation forest across the selected features and exclude rows classified as outliers. This can detect unusual combinations that separate per-column filters miss.

File: config/preprocessing.yml; this learned node does not belong before the train/test split.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes columns list[string]/null null Numeric features; [] selects none. Select joint axes; implicit target excluded. contamination number/string 0.01 (0, 0.5] or auto. Set the learned outlier threshold. n_estimators integer 100 Positive integer. Set the number of isolation trees. max_samples integer/number/string auto Positive count, fraction in (0, 1], or auto. Set each tree's training population. random_state integer/null 42 Valid sklearn seed or null. Control training randomness. 
- name: joint_outliers
  transformer: IsolationForest
  params: {columns: [income, tenure], contamination: 0.01, random_state: 42}

Details: learns from complete finite training rows and requires at least two such rows. At training and apply, a row with a missing or infinite value in any selected column is retained without outlier screening, even if another selected value is extreme. Retention does not mean the detector judged that row normal. Normalize infinite values and impute missing values before this step if partially observed rows must also be screened. Fit failures propagate. Saved trees never refit on request data. Row filtering preserves paired targets and sample-weight positions, including duplicate indexes. Saved scoring publishes excluded outcomes in their original positions. Context: local row/filter; native Spark training is not supported. Worker execution still requires the existing artifact admission.

docs.title: LocalOutlierFactor
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: learn joint local-density outliers, then compare new rows with the fixed learned neighbor population.

File: config/preprocessing.yml; fit only on training data.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes columns list[string]/null null Numeric features; [] selects none. Select joint Euclidean-distance axes. contamination number/string 0.01 (0, 0.5] or auto. Set the learned outlier threshold. n_neighbors integer 20 Positive integer; sklearn caps to available neighbors. Set the local density neighborhood. 
- name: density_outliers
  transformer: LocalOutlierFactor
  params: {columns: [income, tenure], n_neighbors: 20, contamination: 0.01}

Common mistake: training rows and new rows use different sklearn scores. The pipeline training hook uses negative_outlier_factor_ against the learned offset. Saved apply uses novelty prediction for new data. Direct SDK callers should use fit_transform_train for their training representation; calling novelty apply on training rows is not equivalent.

Details: requires two complete finite training rows. At training and apply, a missing or infinite value in any selected column keeps the row without outlier screening; other observed values in that row are not checked separately. Normalize infinite values and impute missing values before this step if those rows must also be screened. Scale features when their units require it. The model retains its learned neighbor population, so saved artifacts grow with training size. Targets and sample weights follow the actual training mask; scoring preserves request positions and exclusion reasons. Context: local row/filter; worker admission remains explicit, with no native Spark fit support.

docs.title: Split, sampling and diagnostic Core nodes
docs.text:
Back to the preprocessing catalog

These cards cover the split nodes, training-only resampling and diagnostic nodes. Generated projects split through config/training.yml, not through these nodes.

YAML blocks are list fragments to paste under a selected recipe unless a card marks them as standalone Core configuration. Shared column, row and runtime rules are in read the step cards.

These cards complete the registry inventory. Generated Bundles own splitting through training configuration; do not insert split/target-split nodes into their phase recipes. Sampling is a training-only Core operation, not pre-split eligibility, and diagnostic nodes observe training without transforming features. The two split-node YAML examples are standalone Core entries. Sampling and diagnostic entries can accompany a preprocessing recipe; they do not replace training.yml split/model fields.

docs.title: TrainTestSplitter
docs.text:
Deprecated alias: Split.

Purpose and effect: partitions rows into training/test and optional validation datasets, rather than adding a feature.

File: Standalone Core configuration; not a generated project phase recipe. Use config/training.yml for generated project split/target settings.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes test_size number 0.2 Fraction leaving viable training rows. Choose test fraction. validation_size number 0.0 Nonnegative; test plus validation less than 1. Choose optional validation fraction. random_state integer/null 42 Integer seed or null. Control random partitioning. shuffle boolean true true, false Shuffle before splitting. stratify boolean false true, false; requires usable class labels and shuffle. Request class-balanced partitions. target_column string/null null Existing label name; paired y can supply the label. Identify the supervised target, normally supplied by the pipeline.

Minimal YAML:

- name: traintestsplitter
  transformer: TrainTestSplitter
  params: {test_size: 0.2, validation_size: 0.0, random_state: 42, shuffle: true, stratify: false}

Common mistake: Generated projects already split through training.yml; do not insert this node into their phase recipes.

Details: Fractions must leave viable training rows and test+validation must be less than 1. Saves split policy, then returns a SplitDataset; paired feature/target membership is aligned. Core warns and falls back to an unstratified split for an absent in-frame label or classes with fewer than two examples. Other impossible stratified sizes can fail; stratification cannot be combined with unshuffled random splitting. Generated Bundle split validation has its own stricter rules. Context global/training. Dependencies: base/sklearn.

docs.title: feature_target_split
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: {age, churn} becomes feature frame {age} plus y.

File: Standalone Core configuration; not a generated project phase recipe. Use config/training.yml for generated project split/target settings.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes target_column string/null required Existing label name; paired y can supply the label. Identify the supervised target, normally supplied by the pipeline.

Minimal YAML:

- name: feature_target_split
  transformer: feature_target_split
  params: {target_column: churn}

Common mistake: Generated projects already route their target; this is a standalone Core helper.

Details: Saves the name; separates that column from X into y without fitting statistics or changing row order/count. Missing target input cannot supply a training y; prediction paths use their saved target routing instead. This is not another holdout splitter. Generated Bundles already manage the target contract. Context row/routing; base dependencies.

docs.title: Oversampling
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: balances minority classes by duplication or synthetic numeric observations.

File: config/preprocessing.yml. Training-only row changes need an explicit scoring decision.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes method string smote random_over, smote, adasyn, borderline_smote, svm_smote, kmeans_smote, smote_tomek Choose training resampler. target_column string/null null Existing label name; paired y can supply the label. Identify the supervised target, normally supplied by the pipeline. sampling_strategy string/number/mapping auto imbalanced-learn strategy, binary float ratio or class-count map. Choose desired class balance; callable is Python-only. random_state integer/null 42 Integer seed or null. Control randomness. k_neighbors integer 5 Positive; relevant synthetic methods. Set minority-neighbor count. m_neighbors integer 10 Positive; borderline/SVM methods. Set danger/noise-neighbor count. kind string borderline-1 borderline-1, borderline-2 Choose BorderlineSMOTE variant. svm_estimator Python estimator/null null Python-only object; not a YAML mapping. Set SVMSMOTE estimator. out_step number 0.5 SVMSMOTE setting. Set extrapolation step. kmeans_estimator integer/Python estimator/null null Integer or null in YAML. Choose KMeansSMOTE clustering. cluster_balance_threshold number/string 0.1 Number or auto. Choose KMeansSMOTE cluster eligibility. density_exponent number/string auto Number or auto. Choose KMeansSMOTE density weighting. n_jobs integer -1 Only forwarded to compatible samplers. Control supported parallelism. synthetic_weight string unset class_mean, uniform; required for weighted synthesis. Assign class mean weight or 1 to synthetic rows.

Minimal YAML:

- name: oversampling
  transformer: Oversampling
  params: {method: random_over, sampling_strategy: auto, random_state: 42}

Common mistake: Synthetic methods need finite numeric data and enough minority neighbors; this is training-only, not eligibility.

Details: SMOTETomek also removes selected rows after synthesis. Only method-relevant fields act. Saves the sampling policy, not a prediction transform. Requires valid class y; SMOTE-family methods need finite numeric features and enough minority neighbors. Output row count/order changes with y kept aligned. Random over-sampling copies rows; synthetic modes do not preserve one-to-one source identity. Context global; optional dependency imbalanced-learn. A Python estimator object cannot be placed directly in YAML; configure supported scalar options or use a Python workflow.

docs.title: Undersampling
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: reduce majority-class rows while keeping sampled features/labels aligned.

File: config/preprocessing.yml. Training-only row changes need an explicit scoring decision.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes method string random_under_sampling random_under_sampling, nearmiss, tomek_links, edited_nearest_neighbours Choose training resampler. target_column string/null null Existing label name; paired y can supply the label. Identify the supervised target, normally supplied by the pipeline. sampling_strategy string/number/mapping auto imbalanced-learn strategy, binary float ratio or class-count map. Choose retained class balance. random_state integer/null 42 Integer seed or null. Control random sampling. replacement boolean false Random under-sampling only. Allow selected duplicates. version integer 1 1, 2, 3; NearMiss only. Choose NearMiss algorithm. n_neighbors integer 3 Positive; neighborhood methods. Choose neighbor count. kind_sel string all all, mode; edited nearest neighbours. Choose neighbor agreement rule. n_jobs integer -1 Only compatible samplers. Control supported parallelism.

Minimal YAML:

- name: undersampling
  transformer: Undersampling
  params: {method: random_under_sampling, sampling_strategy: auto, random_state: 42}

Common mistake: Resampling changes training rows and y together; do not use it in pre_split or ordinary prediction.

Details: Neighborhood modes need numeric data and enough observations. Saves policy; removes/selects training rows, including potential duplicates when replacement is true; corresponding y and supported weights are selected consistently. Context global; optional imbalanced-learn dependency.

docs.title: DatasetProfile
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: Inspect training counts, dtypes, missingness and numeric summaries without changing features.

File: config/preprocessing.yml.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes None — — No configuration fields. Collect training profile metadata; apply passes through.

Minimal YAML:

- name: datasetprofile
  transformer: DatasetProfile
  params: {}

Common mistake: This is a saved training profile, not a fresh prediction-batch drift test.

Details: Fit saves row/column counts, dtype names, missing counts and numeric summary statistics (including binary, constant and all-missing numeric columns). For [1, null, 3], missing count is 1. Apply is passthrough; it does not recompute a prediction-batch profile. Metric names differ between pandas and Polars descriptions. Fit context global, apply context row/passthrough. Dependencies: base. This is not a distribution-drift decision.

docs.title: DataSnapshot
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: Capture a small training-row preview without changing features.

File: config/preprocessing.yml.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes n_rows integer 5 Nonnegative. Save the first n training rows as records.

Minimal YAML:

- name: datasnapshot
  transformer: DataSnapshot
  params: {n_rows: 5}

Common mistake: The artifact stores actual row values; choose intentionally whether sample data should be retained.

Details: Fit records the first n training rows as records; apply passes data through unchanged. If only three rows exist, the snapshot has three records. Stores actual input values, not just statistics; choose whether those values belong in your model artifact. Fit depends on input ordering, apply is row/passthrough. Dependencies: base.

docs.title: Scaling and numeric transformations
docs.text:
Back to the preprocessing catalog

These steps rescale numeric columns or apply fixed and fitted numeric transformations. They fit on training rows and reuse the saved state at prediction time.

YAML blocks are list fragments to paste under a selected recipe unless a card marks them as standalone Core configuration. Shared column, row and runtime rules are in read the step cards.

StandardScaler, MinMaxScaler, MaxAbsScaler and RobustScaler replace selected numeric columns and save the fitted statistics. columns is an optional list with numeric auto-detection when absent and no selection for []. Constant scales use 1 instead of dividing by zero; NaN is not an imputed value. State and column order stay fixed on apply. Use an imputer first if the model cannot accept missing values. Dependencies: base; context: row. Each is for config/preprocessing.yml only.

docs.title: StandardScaler
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: Center and scale numeric inputs; [1, 3] becomes [-1, 1] with both options enabled.

File: config/preprocessing.yml.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes columns list[string]/null null Existing numeric columns; [] selects none. Select features; omitted selection uses numeric detection. with_mean boolean true true, false Subtract the saved training mean. with_std boolean true true, false Divide by the saved training scale.

Minimal YAML:

- name: standardscaler
  transformer: StandardScaler
  params: {columns: [income], with_mean: true, with_std: true}

Common mistake: Scaling does not impute NaNs; fill them first if the estimator requires finite inputs.

Details: Saves population mean and scale; apply computes (x - mean) / scale with disabled operations omitted. For [1, 3], output is [-1, 1]. The two flags false preserve numeric values (conversion may still affect dtype). Native Spark supports its explicitly validated numeric contract, with finite statistics and portable-state checks; this does not extend Spark support to the other scalers or arbitrary downstream steps.

docs.title: MinMaxScaler
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: Put numeric inputs on a chosen scale; training [10, 20] becomes [0, 1].

File: config/preprocessing.yml.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes columns list[string]/null null Existing numeric columns; [] selects none. Select features; omitted selection uses numeric detection. feature_range pair[number] [0, 1] Lower strictly less than upper. Map training extrema to this range. clip boolean false true, false Clip scoring output to the saved feature range.

Minimal YAML:

- name: minmaxscaler
  transformer: MinMaxScaler
  params: {columns: [income], feature_range: [0, 1]}

Common mistake: Future values can lie outside the requested range when clip is false.

Details: Saves fitted minima and scale. Training values [10, 20] become [0, 1]; a future 30 becomes 2 by default, or 1 with clip: true. Clipping uses the fitted range and preserves missing values. Previously saved artifacts without this option remain unclipped. Constant columns use a nonzero denominator. No native Spark fit/apply declaration for this node.

docs.title: MaxAbsScaler
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: Scale by maximum absolute training value; [-4, 2] becomes [-1, 0.5].

File: config/preprocessing.yml.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes columns list[string]/null null Existing numeric columns; [] selects none. Select features; omitted selection uses numeric detection.

Minimal YAML:

- name: maxabsscaler
  transformer: MaxAbsScaler
  params: {columns: [income]}

Common mistake: This is not centering: use StandardScaler if the mean should become zero.

Details: Saves maximum absolute values; [-4, 2] becomes [-1, 0.5]. There is no centering, clipping or feature-range parameter. Future values may exceed absolute 1. Zero columns remain zero.

docs.title: RobustScaler
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: Center on the median and scale by a quantile span to reduce the influence of extreme observations.

File: config/preprocessing.yml.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes columns list[string]/null null Existing numeric columns; [] selects none. Select features; omitted selection uses numeric detection. quantile_range pair[number] [25.0, 75.0] Ordered percentiles in 0–100. Choose the fitted spread. with_centering boolean true true, false Subtract the fitted median. with_scaling boolean true true, false Divide by the fitted quantile span. unit_variance boolean false true, false Adjust the saved scale for unit variance on normally distributed data.

Minimal YAML:

- name: robustscaler
  transformer: RobustScaler
  params: {columns: [income], quantile_range: [25, 75], with_centering: true, with_scaling: true}

Common mistake: Percentiles use 0–100. unit_variance targets normally distributed data; it does not guarantee variance one for every input distribution.

Details: Saves medians and quantile spans. The fitted median becomes 0 when centered; an observation one fitted interquantile span above it becomes 1. With unit_variance: true, sklearn adjusts the learned scale using the corresponding standard-normal quantile span. Apply reuses that adjusted scale without relearning it. Old artifacts without the option retain their saved numerical behavior.

docs.title: QuantileTransformer
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: Map each numeric feature's training distribution to uniform values in [0, 1] or a standard-normal marginal distribution. This is a nonlinear transformation and can change distances and correlations between features.

File: config/preprocessing.yml; also available in the Canvas Scaling method menu.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes columns list[string]/null null Existing numeric columns; [] selects none. Select features; automatic detection excludes target_column. n_quantiles integer 1000 Positive integer, not boolean. Requested distribution landmarks; fitted count is capped at training rows. output_distribution string uniform uniform, normal Choose the output marginal distribution. subsample integer/null 10000 Positive integer or null. Limit rows used to estimate quantiles; null disables subsampling. random_state integer/null 42 Integer seed or null. Control deterministic subsampling; null permits random sampling.

Minimal YAML:

- name: income_quantiles
  transformer: QuantileTransformer
  params: {columns: [income], n_quantiles: 100, output_distribution: normal}

Common mistake: The configured n_quantiles cannot exceed a non-null subsample, even when the eventual fitted count would be capped by a small training set.

Details: Fits a real sklearn transformer and persists its learned quantiles and reference probabilities. Apply uses that saved transformer, never scoring-batch ranks. Values beyond the learned range reach distribution endpoints; normal output uses sklearn's finite endpoint limits. Missing values are ignored when estimating quantiles and remain missing at apply. Selected outputs are float64; names, other columns, row order and labels remain unchanged. Local pandas/Polars replay has row context; native Spark fitting is not declared. Dependencies: base/sklearn.

docs.title: Normalizer
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: Normalize each row across the selected feature vector. With L2 normalization, [3, 4] becomes [0.6, 0.8].

File: config/preprocessing.yml; also available in the Canvas Scaling method menu.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes columns list[string]/null null Existing numeric columns; [] selects none. Define the feature vector; automatic detection excludes target_column. norm string l2 l1, l2, max Divide each row by its absolute sum, Euclidean length or maximum absolute value.

Minimal YAML:

- name: normalize_vector
  transformer: Normalizer
  params: {columns: [x, y], norm: l2}

Common mistake: Fill missing values first; sklearn rejects NaN and infinity. Selecting a single feature usually reduces nonzero values to their sign.

Details: Rows containing only zeros remain zero. Fit validates the feature width and saves sklearn's normalizer; apply uses the saved norm and selected columns without learning population statistics. Outputs are float64, preserving other columns, row order and labels. Missing fitted feature columns raise. Empty requests keep the same schema. Local pandas/Polars replay has row context; native Spark fitting is not declared. Dependencies: base/sklearn.

docs.title: SimpleTransformation
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: square replaces 3 with 9; log replaces 3 with log(4).

File: config/preprocessing.yml.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes transformations list[mapping] [] Ordered rules. Apply the fixed calculations below. transformations[].column string required Existing numeric or coercible column. Choose the column replaced by the rule. transformations[].method string required log, sqrt/square_root, cube_root, reciprocal, square, exp/exponential. Choose fixed math; log means log1p. transformations[].clip_threshold number 700 Used by exp. Clip before exponentiation.

Minimal YAML:

- name: simpletransformation
  transformer: SimpleTransformation
  params:
    transformations: [{column: income, method: log}]

Common mistake: Use transformations; the old func/columns metadata does not configure this node.

Details: Rules run in order and replace their columns. Numeric text is coerced; invalid text becomes missing. Negative log/sqrt inputs and zero reciprocals become missing; cube root supports negatives; exp clips above its threshold. Unknown methods fail during fit with the supported choices listed; missing source names are skipped. Previously saved rules retain their replay. Saves rules only; context row. Dependencies: base. The registry's old func/columns metadata does not configure this node: use the actual transformations list above.

docs.title: GeneralTransformation
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: ordered fixed math plus learned per-column power normalization, for example square then Yeo–Johnson.

File: config/preprocessing.yml.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes transformations list[mapping] [] Ordered SimpleTransformation rules, box-cox or yeo-johnson. Apply fixed math and optionally learn power transforms. transformations[].column string required Existing input column. Choose the replaced column. transformations[].method string required All SimpleTransformation methods plus box-cox and yeo-johnson. Choose fixed or fitted math. transformations[].clip_threshold number 700 Used by exp. Clip before exponentiation. transformations[].standardize boolean true Used by power rules. Standardize the power-transformed values.

Minimal YAML:

- name: generaltransformation
  transformer: GeneralTransformation
  params:
    transformations:
      - {column: income, method: yeo-johnson, standardize: true}

Common mistake: Box–Cox requires positive values; inspect warnings when a power rule leaves a column unchanged.

Details: Each rule fits on the result of prior rules. Saves lambdas and optional standardization statistics, never refits in apply. Box–Cox requires strictly positive usable values. A failed power transform is logged and leaves that column unchanged; this fallback can depend on the batch, so context is global when power rules are present, row for fixed rules only. Use PowerTransformer when you want a dedicated power step. Dependencies: base/sklearn.

docs.title: PowerTransformer
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: learn a monotonic transform making skewed numeric features more nearly Gaussian.

File: config/preprocessing.yml.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes columns list[string]/null null Existing numeric columns; [] selects none. Select features; omitted selection uses numeric detection. method string yeo-johnson yeo-johnson, box-cox Choose the learned power family. standardize boolean true true, false Center and scale transformed values.

Minimal YAML:

- name: powertransformer
  transformer: PowerTransformer
  params: {columns: [income], method: yeo-johnson, standardize: true}

Common mistake: Do not choose Box–Cox for zero or negative inputs.

Details: Saves fitted lambdas and scale statistics, replaces selected columns with floats. Yeo–Johnson accepts negative values; Box–Cox requires positive values. Missing values remain missing and degenerate/all-null fitting needs a usable training population; inspect warnings and the resulting state. Context is determined by the fitted operation and its failure behavior; do not assume worker admission from this mathematical description. Dependencies: base/sklearn.

docs.title: Text and embeddings
docs.text:
Back to the preprocessing catalog

These steps tokenize text, build count, TF-IDF or hashed term features, or add sentence embeddings.

YAML blocks are list fragments to paste under a selected recipe unless a card marks them as standalone Core configuration. Shared column, row and runtime rules are in read the step cards.

These steps use config/preprocessing.yml, not config/pre_split.yml. columns is an explicit list default []; absent, empty or wholly absent names give no-op state, not text auto-detection. The target is excluded. Count/TF-IDF default to column_mode: joined: selected columns become one document per row with spaces and a source-name prefix joined by _. Opt into per_column for independent vocabularies and source prefixes. Hashing and embeddings remain joined; Hashing has no learned vocabulary or per-column vocabulary option. Tokenizer processes each source separately. Null text becomes empty text. Text outputs are attached to the original engine; sklearn operations can cross through bounded NumPy/pandas data. Output-name collisions raise.

docs.title: tokenizer
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: Produce normalized tokens and optional token counts; Blue sky becomes blue sky with count 2.

File: config/preprocessing.yml.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes columns list[string] [] Existing column names. Select explicitly; no automatic detection. analyzer string word word, char, char_wb Choose tokenization unit. lowercase boolean true true, false Lowercase before tokenization. stop_words string/list[string]/null null english, custom word list, null Remove stop words. ngram_range pair[integer] [1, 1] Positive ordered [min, max]. Choose token sequence lengths. drop_original boolean false true, false Remove selected source text columns. add_token_count boolean false true, false Add an integer token count per source.

Minimal YAML:

- name: tokenizer
  transformer: tokenizer
  params: {columns: [description], analyzer: word, add_token_count: true}

Common mistake: The token output is a space-joined string, not a list; default word tokenization excludes one-character words.

Details: Saves rules only. Adds string <source>__tokens (space-joined tokens, not a list) and optionally integer <source>__token_count. "Blue sky" becomes "blue sky" with count 2; null becomes empty tokens/count 0. Word tokenization uses sklearn's default token pattern, so one-character words are normally excluded. Context row for text input; non-text string rendering may be engine/context-dependent. Dependencies: base/sklearn, no NLP model download.

docs.title: count_vectorizer
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: Learn a token vocabulary and append dense counts; blue blue contributes count 2 for blue.

File: config/preprocessing.yml.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes columns list[string] [] Existing column names. Select explicitly; no automatic detection. column_mode string joined joined, per_column Learn one shared vocabulary or a separate vocabulary per source. min_df integer/number 1 Integer count or share in [0, 1]. Remove tokens rarer than this training frequency. max_df integer/number 1.0 Integer count or share in [0, 1]. Remove tokens more common than this training frequency. max_features integer/null null Positive; falsy 0 is treated as unset. Limit vocabulary size. ngram_range pair[integer] [1, 1] Positive ordered [min, max]. Choose token sequence lengths. lowercase boolean true true, false Lowercase before tokenization. stop_words string/list[string]/null null english, custom word list, null Remove stop words. binary boolean false true, false Clip each count to presence/absence. drop_original boolean false true, false Remove selected source text columns.

Minimal YAML:

- name: count_vectorizer
  transformer: count_vectorizer
  params: {columns: [description], max_features: 1000, drop_original: true}

Common mistake: max_df: 1 is a count, while max_df: 1.0 is a share; choose the intended YAML type.

Details: Shares must be in [0,1], counts nonnegative and ordered thresholds viable for the training corpus. Saves vocabulary and fitted vectorizer. Adds dense <prefix>__count__<token> counts (binary clips presence to 1); "blue blue" has count 2 for blue. Unknown tokens add nothing. Empty/stopword-only training vocabulary in joined mode produces no useful vectorizer (inspect the warning/state). In per_column mode each source learns its own vocabulary, emits <source>__count__<token> columns, and applies max_features independently. N-grams cannot cross sources. If any selected source has no usable vocabulary, fitting raises with its name. Missing fitted sources also raise at inference. Null text is an empty document; empty apply preserves learned width. Context row for text inputs. Base/sklearn.

docs.title: tfidf_vectorizer
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: Weight token counts by saved inverse document frequencies to reduce common-word influence.

File: config/preprocessing.yml.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes columns list[string] [] Existing column names. Select explicitly; no automatic detection. column_mode string joined joined, per_column Learn shared vocabulary/IDF or independent vocabulary/IDF per source. min_df integer/number 1 Integer count or share in [0, 1]. Remove tokens rarer than this training frequency. max_df integer/number 1.0 Integer count or share in [0, 1]. Remove tokens more common than this training frequency. max_features integer/null null Positive; falsy 0 is treated as unset. Limit vocabulary size. ngram_range pair[integer] [1, 1] Positive ordered [min, max]. Choose token sequence lengths. lowercase boolean true true, false Lowercase before tokenization. stop_words string/list[string]/null null english, custom word list, null Remove stop words. sublinear_tf boolean false true, false Use logarithmic term-frequency scaling. drop_original boolean false true, false Remove selected source text columns.

Minimal YAML:

- name: tfidf_vectorizer
  transformer: tfidf_vectorizer
  params: {columns: [description], max_features: 1000, sublinear_tf: true, drop_original: true}

Common mistake: binary, norm, use_idf and smooth_idf are not exposed by this wrapper.

Details: Saves vocabulary, inverse-document frequencies and vectorizer. Adds dense floating <prefix>__tfidf__<token> values; frequent words across the training corpus receive less inverse-document weight. Unknown tokens are ignored; empty text is the zero vector. Normalization follows the wrapped sklearn default L2; norm, use_idf and smooth_idf are not exposed here. With per_column, each source has independent IDF statistics and normalization, emits <source>__tfidf__<token> columns, and gets its own max_features limit. Empty-vocabulary/empty-apply behavior follows count_vectorizer. Context row for text inputs; base/sklearn.

docs.title: hashing_vectorizer
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: Append fixed-width numeric hash vectors without learning a vocabulary.

File: config/preprocessing.yml.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes columns list[string] [] Existing column names. Select explicitly; no automatic detection. n_features integer 1024 Positive. Choose dense hash-vector width. norm string/null l2 l2, l1, null Normalize each output vector. alternate_sign boolean true true, false Use signed hashing contributions. lowercase boolean true true, false Lowercase before tokenization. stop_words string/list[string]/null null english, custom word list, null Remove stop words. drop_original boolean false true, false Remove selected source text columns.

Minimal YAML:

- name: hashing_vectorizer
  transformer: hashing_vectorizer
  params: {columns: [description], n_features: 1024, norm: l2, drop_original: true}

Common mistake: The final output is dense; a very large n_features value consumes dense memory.

Details: No public ngram_range or vocabulary field. Saves fixed configuration/vectorizer, not corpus statistics. Adds dense float <prefix>__hash__0 through n_features-1; new words hash into the same width and collisions are expected. Empty documents produce zero vectors. Large widths consume dense memory even though sklearn's intermediate result is sparse. Context row for text inputs; base/sklearn.

docs.title: sentence_embedder
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: Append pretrained semantic vectors; similar text should have similar representations.

File: config/preprocessing.yml.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes columns list[string] [] Existing column names. Select explicitly; no automatic detection. model_name string all-MiniLM-L6-v2 Pretrained sentence-transformers model; empty uses default. Choose the captured encoder. normalize boolean true true, false Normalize embeddings. drop_original boolean false true, false Remove selected source text columns.

Minimal YAML:

- name: sentence_embedder
  transformer: sentence_embedder
  params: {columns: [description], model_name: all-MiniLM-L6-v2, normalize: true, drop_original: true}

Common mistake: Local embedding success does not establish Spark-worker or REST admission; the packaged snapshot and dependencies matter.

Details: Appends float <prefix>__emb__<index> features whose width comes from the selected pretrained encoder. Semantically similar text should have similar vectors; exact values depend on that captured model. No task-specific fine-tuning occurs. Fit may download the model on a cold cache and saves its weights, tokenizer/settings, SHA256 and exact dependency versions; modern apply restores the saved CPU snapshot rather than fetching changed model weights. Snapshot size is bounded (256 MiB) in addition to model-package budgets. Load only trusted producer artifacts because native PyTorch serialization is executable. Null text is encoded as empty text, not automatically a zero vector. Context is the pretrained encoder's supported local apply contract; floating tolerances and dependency pins matter. Requires optional sentence-transformers/PyTorch stack; base installation alone is insufficient. No Spark-worker/REST certification is implied by successful local embedding.

docs.title: Time and geography
docs.text:
Back to the preprocessing catalog

These steps add calendar features, lags and rolling aggregates, distances and H3 cells. Lags and rolling aggregates depend on ordered history; read the history section before scoring them.

YAML blocks are list fragments to paste under a selected recipe unless a card marks them as standalone Core configuration. Shared column, row and runtime rules are in read the step cards.

docs.title: DateFeatures
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: a timestamp adds calendar components such as event_time_year=2026 and event_time_month=10.

File: config/preprocessing.yml.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes columns list[string] [] Existing column names. Select explicitly; no automatic detection. features list[string] [year, month, day, dayofweek] year, month, day, dayofweek, dayofyear, quarter, weekofyear, hour, minute, second, is_weekend, is_month_start, is_month_end; hour_sin/hour_cos, dayofweek_sin/dayofweek_cos, month_sin/month_cos, dayofyear_sin/dayofyear_cos. Choose calendar parts or cycles; null/empty uses default, unknown names fail during fit with supported choices listed. drop_original boolean false true, false Remove source date columns. epoch_unit string/null null s, ms, us, ns; required for numeric epochs. Interpret numeric timestamps. timezone string UTC IANA name, such as Europe/Istanbul or Europe/Copenhagen. Extract parts and cycles in the selected local calendar.

Minimal YAML:

- name: datefeatures
  transformer: DateFeatures
  params: {columns: [observation_time], features: [year, month, dayofweek], drop_original: true}

Common mistake: Numeric epochs require epoch_unit; new artifacts normalize timestamp interpretation to UTC before converting to the selected timezone. A naive local clock string must carry its offset if it represents a non-UTC instant.

Details: Newly fitted artifacts interpret naive dates and numeric epochs as UTC, then convert each instant to timezone; offset-aware dates describe the same instant regardless of their written offset. DST jumps and repeated hours follow that conversion without localizing an ambiguous wall clock. The fitted state stores the timezone and calendar selections. Adds <column>_<feature> values, with null features for unparseable timestamps; dtype representation of nullable calendar values can differ across engines. dayofweek is Monday=0. Empty apply retains generated columns. Context row. Base dependencies. Legacy artifacts retain their old timestamp interpretation when their saved state lacks a timezone, until the whole pipeline is refitted. Existing artifacts with timezone: UTC retain UTC.

The explicit _sin and _cos options emit Float64 values using sin(2*pi*position/period) and cos(2*pi*position/period). Hour uses integer hours 0–23 and period 24; weekday uses Monday=0 and period 7. Month subtracts one (January=0) and uses period 12. Day-of-year subtracts one (January 1=0) and uses 365 or 366 according to each row's local calendar year. These are calendar components, so minutes do not contribute a fractional hour. Select both members of a pair to preserve circular position; each output can also be selected alone.

- name: local_calendar
  transformer: DateFeatures
  params:
    columns: [observation_time]
    timezone: Europe/Copenhagen
    features: [second, hour_sin, hour_cos, dayofweek_sin, dayofweek_cos]
    drop_original: true

docs.title: LagFeatures
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: ordered values [10, 20, 30] and lag 1 add [null, 10, 20].

File: config/preprocessing.yml.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes columns list[string] [] Existing column names. Select explicitly; no automatic detection. lags integer/list[integer] [1] Positive; normalized to sorted distinct integers. Choose previous-row offsets. drop_na boolean false true, false; carry rejects true. Remove rows with missing lag output. group_by string/list[string]/null null Existing grouping columns; use a list in carry mode. Maintain separate entity sequences. sort_by string/null null Existing numeric/typed datetime clock for carry. Order observations; absent uses batch input order. history_mode string batch batch, carry Use the current batch or a bounded saved training tail. history_max_rows integer 10000 Positive; carry only. Bound stored history rows. history_max_bytes integer 1048576 Positive; carry only. Bound stored history bytes.

Minimal YAML:

- name: lagfeatures
  transformer: LagFeatures
  params: {columns: [income], lags: [1], group_by: [entity], sort_by: observation_time}

Common mistake: Sorting can reorder rows; independent batches do not share history unless you manage continuation explicitly.

Details: Appends <column>_lag_<n> and keeps original columns. Missing previous observations produce missing lags; drop_na filters rows with missing lag values and aligns y. Without sort_by, input order is the sequence. Batch mode sorts stably when requested and can reorder rows/y. State saves configuration, plus bounded seed observations in carry mode. Context window; base dependencies. Target lags require careful availability handling and are forbidden in carry mode; use only prediction-available inputs in Bundle features.

Schema preview retains known shift-stable types, including nullable integers, Boolean extensions, strings and floats. Native integer and Boolean labels can change when missing lags are inserted, so ambiguous types return an unknown schema. Apply keeps the engine's native behavior, including empty batches.

docs.title: RollingAggregate
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: [10, 20, 30] with window 2 and mean adds [10, 15, 25]: the current row is included.

File: config/preprocessing.yml.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes columns list[string] [] Existing column names. Select explicitly; no automatic detection. window integer 3 Positive. Set rolling row-count window. aggregations string/list[string] [mean] mean, sum, min, max, std, median. Choose summary features; unknown names fail during fit with supported choices listed. min_periods integer 1 No greater than window. Require enough nonmissing observations. group_by string/list[string]/null null Existing grouping columns; use a list in carry mode. Maintain separate entity sequences. sort_by string/null null Existing numeric/typed datetime clock for carry. Order observations; absent uses batch input order. history_mode string batch batch, carry Use the current batch or a bounded saved training tail. history_max_rows integer 10000 Positive; carry only. Bound stored history rows. history_max_bytes integer 1048576 Positive; carry only. Bound stored history bytes.

Minimal YAML:

- name: rollingaggregate
  transformer: RollingAggregate
  params:
    columns: [income]
    window: 2
    aggregations: [mean, max]
    min_periods: 1
    group_by: [entity]
    sort_by: observation_time

Common mistake: The current row is included; rolling the known target would leak its label and is rejected.

Details: Unknown aggregation names fail during fit. Adds <column>_roll_<aggregation>_<window> columns, keeping originals. Missing observations affect min_periods; sample std needs enough observations. Rolling the known target is rejected to prevent same-row label leakage. Batch mode may reorder rows/y through sorting. Saves rules and optionally bounded training history. Context window; base dependencies.

Pandas rolling outputs are double precision. Polars can retain float32 and integer types for some aggregates. Schema preview predicts only known double outputs: double inputs, or integer mean/median/std. Other combinations return an unknown schema; this does not change their fitted or native apply behavior.

docs.title: Carry history for LagFeatures and RollingAggregate
docs.text:
Both accept history_mode string batch default or carry, history_max_rows positive int default 10000, and history_max_bytes positive int default 1048576. Use a list for grouped carry history, such as group_by: [entity]. Carry requires explicit columns, a nonempty sort_by, a numeric or typed datetime clock, and nonmissing unique entity/time keys; parse text clocks first. It rejects drop_na and target leakage. It saves the required tail per entity within both budgets; budget overflow fails instead of silently discarding entities. New observations must follow saved history. Apply does not mutate the model. Successive requests need caller-owned continuation state if they should see one another; repeating apply without it reuses the training seed. See preprocessing context for TemporalHistorySession and publication of state with predictions.

- name: rollingaggregate
  transformer: RollingAggregate
  params:
    columns: [income]
    window: 5
    aggregations: [mean]
    group_by: [entity]
    sort_by: observation_time
    history_mode: carry
    history_max_rows: 1000
    history_max_bytes: 48000
- name: dropmissingcolumns
  transformer: DropMissingColumns
  params: {columns: [observation_time], missing_threshold: null}

In a Bundle, observation_time must be an actual model input available at scoring, distinct from protected split event metadata when necessary. Drop the raw clock after generating features if the estimator cannot consume it. Do not split ordered history across arbitrary Spark partitions or independent REST requests and expect batch-equivalent results.

docs.title: GeoDistance
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: identical coordinate pairs produce distance 0.

File: config/preprocessing.yml.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes lat1_col string required Existing numeric latitude column in degrees. Latitude of the first point; an empty name fails. lon1_col string required Existing numeric longitude column in degrees. Longitude of the first point; an empty name fails. lat2_col string required Existing numeric latitude column in degrees. Latitude of the second point; an empty name fails. lon2_col string required Existing numeric longitude column in degrees. Longitude of the second point; an empty name fails. method string haversine haversine, euclidean Choose spherical or flat-plane approximation. unit string km km, mi Choose output distance unit. output_column string geo_distance_ Explicit name, or empty/unset for generated name. Name the appended/replaced distance column.

Minimal YAML:

- name: geodistance
  transformer: GeoDistance
  params: {lat1_col: latitude, lon1_col: longitude, lat2_col: store_lat, lon2_col: store_lon, unit: km}

Common mistake: Validate coordinates upstream; this step is not a general coordinate-cleaning rule.

Details: Euclidean uses the flat-plane approximation for coordinates. Saves configuration, appends/replaces the named float output. Null coordinates produce missing distance; validate geographic ranges upstream rather than assuming this is a coordinate-cleaning step. Context row. Base dependencies.

docs.title: H3Index
docs.text:
Purpose and effect: nearby lat/lon observations map to string H3 cell IDs at the chosen grid resolution.

File: config/preprocessing.yml.

Parameter Type Default Allowed values What it changes lat_col string required Existing numeric latitude column in degrees. Latitude used to compute the H3 cell. lon_col string required Existing numeric longitude column in degrees. Longitude used to compute the H3 cell. resolution integer 9 0–15. Choose H3 grid resolution. output_column string h3_index String. Name the appended/replaced cell column.

Minimal YAML:

- name: h3index
  transformer: H3Index
  params: {lat_col: latitude, lon_col: longitude, resolution: 9, output_column: h3_index}

Common mistake: Install the h3 extra in both fit and apply environments; missing/invalid coordinates produce null.

Details: Saves only configuration; appends/replaces the output column, keeps inputs and row order. Missing/invalid coordinates and latitude outside ±90 or longitude outside ±180 produce null. Context row. Optional dependency h3 (geo extra) must be installed in fit and apply environments. For example, uv pip install "skyulf-core[geo]".

docs.title: Build preprocessing with YAML
docs.text:
Configure a generated Databricks project's preprocessing by editing YAML. This walkthrough uses built-in steps: the shipped src/features/ Python files can stay unchanged. It covers fixed eligibility, missing values, categorical encoding, scaling, outlier exclusion and saved prediction. The examples use the preprocessing additions in Skyulf Core 0.9.4.

Use the preprocessing catalog for every step's parameter types, defaults, allowed values and output contract. The complete list below links all registered names, including operations that require custom Python or standalone use.

docs.title: 1. Start from a generated project
docs.text:
Generate a single-model classification project using the Bundle setup guide. Keep its source table, record keys, registry, training split and deployment settings. This walkthrough replaces two complete recipe files and updates selected fields in config/training.yml. It does not create a Delta table or deploy an endpoint by itself.

File What belongs here When it runs config/pre_split.yml Fixed input normalization and eligibility, such as an age range. Before splitting training data; the generated scoring policy reuses feature-only rules. config/preprocessing.yml Imputation, learned category maps, scaling, feature selection and learned outlier detection. Fitted on training rows; fitted again inside training folds when cross-validation fits a fold. Saved state is replayed at prediction. config/training.yml Input columns, target, model and the names of the two selected recipes. Selects what a training run builds.

A recipe is an ordered list of steps. Only the named recipe runs. default: [] and none: [] below deliberately do nothing; defining four recipes does not combine them. Each built-in step has a unique name, a case-sensitive transformer and its params mapping.

Use a table with these illustrative rows and columns. customer_id is the record key, outside model inputs. The tiny dataset demonstrates the contracts; it is not a benchmark or a recommendation for production split sizes.

14,32,2200,2,A,1
15,42,-200,3,A,0
16,52,4200,4,B,1
17,62,5200,5,B,0
18,72,6200,6,B,1
19,27,1700,2,A,0

23,67,5700,6,C,0

All labels are present. For delayed or separate labels, configure training outcomes rather than fabricating labels in an imputer. Load your table separately, and use enough labeled rows for the split and CV settings you retain from the generated project.

docs.title: 2. Apply fixed rules before the split
docs.text:
Replace config/pre_split.yml with this complete file:

version: 1
recipes:
  default: []
  none: []
  eligible:
    - name: income_marker
      transformer: ValueReplacement
      params: {columns: [income], to_replace: -200, value: null}
    - name: age_range
      transformer: ManualBounds
      params: {bounds: {age: {lower: 0, upper: 120}}}

The marker -200 becomes a missing measurement; it is not included in the mean learned later. The fixed age rule removes row 32 before the training split. Bounds are inclusive. ManualBounds retains missing values; use an explicit missing-value rule if a missing age should be ineligible rather than imputed.

Both rules read features only. The generated mode: pre_split policy in config/scoring.yml can reuse them without editing Python or enabling a target-skip switch. At scoring time an out-of-range age keeps its result row with scoring_status=excluded, an empty prediction and exclusion_reason=pre_split:age_range.

Pre-split accepts a restricted set of fixed operations: DropMissingRows, ManualBounds, Deduplicate, ValueReplacement, TextCleaning, AliasReplacement, InvalidValueReplacement and Casting. Each has additional pre-split constraints. Learned means, quantiles and outlier boundaries belong in preprocessing, not before the split. If a rule reads the target, follow the explicit target-filter policy instead of copying the feature-only policy in this example.

docs.title: 3. Define alternative fitted recipes
docs.text:
Replace config/preprocessing.yml with this complete file. The recipes share the same raw input columns, so switch between them by changing one recipe name in training configuration.

version: 1
recipes:
  default: []
  none: []
  customer:
    - name: fill_numeric
      transformer: SimpleImputer
      params: {columns: [age, income, tenure], strategy: mean}
    - name: rare_segments
      transformer: RareCategoryGrouping
      params: {columns: [segment], min_count: 3, replacement: Other}
    - name: segment_frequency
      transformer: FrequencyEncoder
      params: {columns: [segment], mode: frequency}
    - name: numeric_quantiles
      transformer: QuantileTransformer
      params:
        columns: [age, income, tenure]
        n_quantiles: 16
        output_distribution: uniform
        subsample: null
        random_state: 42
    - name: numeric_row_norm
      transformer: Normalizer
      params: {columns: [age, income, tenure], norm: l2}
  fixed_categories:
    - name: fill_numeric
      transformer: SimpleImputer
      params: {columns: [age, income, tenure], strategy: mean}
    - name: scale_measurements
      transformer: StandardScaler
      params:
        columns_regex: '^(age|income|tenure)$'
        dtype: numeric
        exclude_columns: [customer_id]
    - name: fixed_segments
      transformer: OneHotEncoder
      params:
        columns: [segment]
        categories: {segment: [A, B, C]}
        column_names: slug
        max_categories: null
        include_missing: false
        handle_unknown: ignore
  isolation:
    - name: fill_numeric
      transformer: SimpleImputer
      params: {columns: [age, income, tenure], strategy: mean}
    - name: unusual_measurements
      transformer: IsolationForest
      params:
        columns: [age, income, tenure]
        contamination: 0.1
        n_estimators: 40
        random_state: 42
    - name: segment_frequency
      transformer: FrequencyEncoder
      params: {columns: [segment], mode: frequency}
  local_density:
    - name: fill_numeric
      transformer: SimpleImputer
      params: {columns: [age, income, tenure], strategy: mean}
    - name: scale_measurements
      transformer: StandardScaler
      params: {columns: [age, income, tenure]}
    - name: unusual_measurements
      transformer: LocalOutlierFactor
      params: {columns: [age, income, tenure], n_neighbors: 5, contamination: 0.1}
    - name: segment_frequency
      transformer: FrequencyEncoder
      params: {columns: [segment], mode: frequency}

Choose the recipe for the behavior you need; these are alternatives, not an instruction to stack every available transform:

Recipe What happens What the saved model remembers customer Impute numeric inputs, group rare segments, encode group frequency, transform each numeric column by its quantiles, then normalize each row's numeric vector. Training means, frequent-category membership, group frequencies and quantile maps; the selected columns and normalization rule. fixed_categories Impute and standardize numeric measurements; emit exactly segment_a, segment_b, segment_c. Numeric means/scales and the explicit vocabulary/order, including levels absent from training. isolation Impute, exclude rows outside the learned IsolationForest boundary, and frequency-encode segment for surviving training rows. The fitted detector and downstream category map. local_density Impute, scale numeric distances, exclude rows using the fitted LocalOutlierFactor detector, then encode segment. Numeric scales, the novelty detector and downstream category map.

Quantile transformation changes each column's distribution. L2 normalization then makes each nonzero selected row vector have length one; it does not standardize columns. They are shown together to demonstrate both operations. For a random forest neither is automatically necessary; compare validation results before retaining extra steps.

Rare grouping sends an unseen segment to Other. The next frequency encoder uses the saved frequency of that group, or zero if no such group was learned. Frequency encoding alone sends an unseen category to zero. Neither recomputes frequencies from the scoring request.

Fixed one-hot requires explicit string vocabularies, max_categories: null and include_missing: false. Here NEW or a null segment produces three zeros; changing handle_unknown to error rejects them instead. column_names: slug normalizes output names; conflicting normalized names are rejected at fit.

Outlier filtering changes the training population. At prediction, the scoring workflow preserves an outlier's row and reports exclusion_reason=outlier:unusual_measurements. The first exclusion reason wins: an age already rejected by the fixed rule keeps pre_split:age_range. contamination: 0.1 controls the fitted cutoff; it does not promise that exactly 10% of future requests will be excluded. Review the exclusion counts as well as the model metric before choosing a detector.

docs.title: 4. Select and inspect the recipe
docs.text:
Merge this fragment into the generated config/training.yml. Keep its table, record keys, registry, split, resource and quality settings. Select a classification quality metric and remove an existing tuning block if you want only the fixed model below. Use the generated model key if it differs from main.

version: 1
defaults:
  task: classification
  input_columns: [age, income, tenure, segment]
  target_column: churn
  pre_split_recipe: eligible
  preprocessing_recipe: customer
models:
  main:
    model:
      type: random_forest_classifier
      params: {n_estimators: 40, max_depth: 6, n_jobs: 1, random_state: 42}

Change preprocessing_recipe to fixed_categories, isolation or local_density to train that alternative. A model entry can override the defaults. Competition candidates can use different preprocessing recipes while sharing pre-split eligibility and holdout membership; independent-target models can select their own recipes. Follow the generated layout for your project type.

Run from the generated project directory:

python src/tools/smoke.py
python src/tools/preview.py --action train
python src/tools/preview.py --action score
python src/tools/preview.py --list-preprocessors

Preview resolves the configuration without training the model. Inspect the selected recipes and input columns, then use your project's generated training and scoring commands. The registry listing shows metadata defaults; the parameter cards below explain the full accepted configuration. Successful preview does not prove that a particular input dataset or serving configuration will be admitted.

docs.title: Select columns once, at fit
docs.text:
The fixed_categories scaler demonstrates three shared selector options:

Option Effect in the example columns_regex: '^(age\|income\|tenure)$' Select these exact names; matching uses a regular-expression search, so anchors matter. dtype: numeric Require numeric feature columns as well as a matching name. exclude_columns: [customer_id] Keep identifiers out even if a broader pattern is used later. The key is already outside model inputs here.

The rules combine with AND and resolve once from training features. Saved prediction uses the resulting explicit names. An empty selection raises an error. These rules apply to preprocessing steps that accept columns; they do not apply to pre-split rules or directly to Calculator calls. Native Spark training uses explicit names. The Canvas uses its explicit column picker. See the selection contract for dtype details and the interaction with an explicit columns list.

docs.title: 5. Check saved prediction behavior
docs.text:
Send raw model inputs in their recorded types; do not manually reproduce the mean, scale or category columns in a client. For example:

customer_id,age,income,tenure,segment
101,40,3000,3,A
102,40,,3,NEW
103,150,3000,3,A
104,40,10000000,5000,B
105,40,-200,3,A

The source record key associates each result with its input; it is not a model feature. With customer or fixed_categories, rows 101, 102, 104 and 105 are predicted, while 103 is excluded by the age rule. Missing income and the marker are imputed using the training mean. The two detector recipes can also exclude 104 for its extreme measurements. Their learned boundaries, and therefore other accepted rows, depend on the training split.

The published scoring table keeps excluded rows, their status and reason, with null predictions. This is different from asking a bare preprocessing applier to remove rows. Use the complete saved scoring workflow for that contract. See scoring and incremental inputs for output columns.

Training saves fitted transformations and the selected project rules with the model. Editing YAML affects the next training run; it does not change an existing registered version. Load and replay the saved artifact to check the behavior you intend to deploy.

Execution path What must be checked pandas / Polars The selected configuration, input dtypes, missing values and saved replay on the chosen native engine. Spark worker scoring Admission of the fitted artifact for independent batches, its input/output schema and worker dependencies. This is not distributed training of the estimator. Serving endpoint Admission of the complete serving workflow, its raw input contract, saved rules and dependencies. A working local pipeline alone does not establish endpoint support. Lag or rolling features Ordered history must be supplied through the supported context workflow. A model does not fetch prior customer records by itself.

The recipes use saved state plus individual request rows during prediction. In contrast, history-dependent operations require additional observations. Use preprocessing diagnostics and the Spark guide for artifact-specific checks. Do not infer support for every configuration from the existence of a registry entry.

docs.title: New nodes and additions to existing nodes
docs.text:
The six new registered operations are FrequencyEncoder, RareCategoryGrouping, QuantileTransformer, Normalizer, IsolationForest and LocalOutlierFactor. In the Canvas they are choices within the existing Encoding, Scaling and Outlier panels, not six separate palette cards.

Other additions are parameters or operations within existing nodes:

Existing operation Addition and where to read the complete configuration OneHotEncoder Fixed string vocabularies and slug output names. GroupImputer Multiple group keys and hierarchical fallback. An unknown full key can fall back to a shorter key, then the saved global statistic. FeatureGeneration Group deviation subtracts a saved group reference from a value. DateFeatures Local timezone and cyclic date features, such as month sine/cosine. count_vectorizer / tfidf_vectorizer Per-column vocabularies separate text fields instead of joining them. Winsorize Per-column percentile bounds. ModelBasedSelection RFECV and sequential feature selection, with their own CV and feature-count controls. TargetEncoder Cross-fitting fold count, shuffle and seed. Training encodings remain separate from full-training maps used for prediction. MinMaxScaler / RobustScaler Clipping and unit-variance adjustment. Steps accepting columns Pattern, dtype and exclusion selectors in Core pipelines and YAML.

docs.title: Find every step and its parameters
docs.text:
Each linked family contains per-step parameter tables with type, default, allowed values, effect, minimal YAML and saved-state behavior. There are 73 registered names and 69 distinct implementations, including four aliases. The following inventory includes standalone and custom-only operations; registration is not a promise that every name can be pasted into a Bundle recipe.
